356: A step is activated from an intake sufficient to reconstruct its governing
357: relations without conversation history, commentary or a prior actor's memory
358: (P0, actor-change premise). The intake names:
359: 
360: - the governed outcome or decision: the selected outcome, admitted
361:   prerequisite or experiment it serves (P2);
362: - the exact workspace subject and basis, and the inputs it may acquire,
363:   each by identity and hash or by an input commit;
364: - the evaluation or evaluation family the step performs and its result
365:   algebra: the core of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) or
366:   a refinement mapped into it (§3);
367: - the bounded affected relation set and the applicable governing
368:   invariants;
369: - the accepted transformation-admission relations the step relies on (§4);
370: - the selected computational or common-library dispositions: which
371:   shared machinery serves the step and under what binding (FOUNDATIONS §4,
372:   shared machinery);
373: - the construction and assessment authority: the applicable frame-set,
374:   semantic, evaluation, operation where material, and decision authority
375:   (FOUNDATIONS §2, authority kinds), and the grant: the operations
376:   permitted, the territory that may change, and the decisions reserved to
377:   others (P6);
378: - the available actor capability envelopes;
379: - the conditions that make the result stale or out of scope, and the
380:   conditions that require re-entry at an owning relation;
381: - where the governed question is a cost claim, the allowance and how
382:   spend will be measured (§6).
383: 
384: Implementation folklore is not an intake source. Where a design profile
385: applies, its bounded-frame conservation, transformation-admission
386: completeness, invariant-reconstruction sufficiency and
387: computational-realisation projection laws supply the affected set, the
388: admission relations, the invariants and the computational dispositions;
389: this section consumes those laws and creates no second design package
390: ([DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md)). Conserves
391: [UP-020 intake](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#sufficient-execution-intake),
392: [UP-018](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#invariant-reconstruction-sufficiency-stdo-up-018)
393: and the engagement basis (rc.2 RF #establish-the-evaluation-basis).
394: 
395: ### Execution unit
396: 
397: The execution unit is the smallest coherent causal dependency cone capable
398: of delivering working behaviour while preserving every affected governing
399: relation. It need not coincide with one function, file, module, ticket
400: field or design document (P0, P4b; provenance rc.2 SPEC_METHOD
401: #bounded-causal-construction). A seam whose far side can causally affect,
402: or be affected by, the action is inside the cone unless the basis
403: establishes that it cannot participate. Unrelated incompleteness outside
404: the cone is recorded as repricing input and does not block the bounded
405: claim. The cone is the seed set Z of §2; the context is its projection.
406: 
407: ### Admission
408: 
409: Drafting a step's contract and admitting it are distinct relations, even
410: inside one invocation that drafts, validates, admits and executes; no
411: separate turn, carrier or approval ceremony is implied by the distinction.
412: A contract carries at minimum the states drafted, admitted, rejected and
413: superseded ([TICKETS §5](TICKETS.md#execution-contract-admission)).
414: Execution begins only after deterministic admission or an
415: explicit human override of the exact contract. The drafting actor never
416: infers admission from its own draft, from the presence of a carrier
417: (ticket, sprint entry, work contract), from lane placement or from an
418: `active` label. The admitted result identifies the admission mechanism and
419: its authority, the exact contract identity or digest, the decision and the
420: evidence, including any human override; absent those coordinates the
421: contract stays drafted or rejected, and prose asserting admission is not
422: admission evidence (P6; the actor cannot self-certify its own execution
423: basis). Admission validates the contract against its cited outcome,
424: prerequisite or experiment basis; it does not admit that basis, and
425: drafting, admitting or retaining a contract creates or renews no authority
426: its owner has not admitted (P6, P2;
427: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
428: creates no authority). Only an admitted contract activates a step: no
429: result, child completion, tool output, model response, shared actor or
430: lateral handoff activates another step or authorises continuation by
431: itself, and a profile that routes results names its instances of this
432: rule. Purpose and material relation: a profile and a template each stated
433: this list for one configuration, so the generic rule had no owner (P6).
434: The admitted contract names one
435: durable result and evidence surface; every result, withheld closure and
436: residual obligation is recorded there before return, a conversation return
437: alone is not durable evidence, and if no such surface is authorised and
438: available, admission refuses (P4b). Absent or rejected admission returns
439: the missing work authority without execution, as `admission_refused` with
440: its cause ([§3 Admission and activation](#admission-and-activation)).
441: Provenance:
442: [work-carrier-to-execution rule](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/TICKET_METHOD.md#work-carrier-to-execution-rule)
443: and
444: [execution contract admission](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/TICKET_METHOD.md#execution-contract-admission);
445: the selection of the carrier (ticket, sprint entry, run-scoped contract)
446: is tier-2 law in the [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) member, which disposes those rows.
447: 
448: ### Applicability
449: 
450: The owning evaluation and scope declarations determine which frame
451: obligations apply to the exact subject. Their declared predicates are
452: evaluated from sufficient basis-bound facts: a true predicate requires the
453: applicable evaluation and its result; a false predicate excludes only that
454: obligation, under its cited authority; a missing or ambiguous premise
455: leaves applicability unresolved, not false. A supported inapplicability
456: of a conditional obligation is recorded as such, apart from any result
457: value, and waives no criterion of the member's acceptance (P5, P6; new
458: law carried at iteration 4 from the common construction contract's
459: conformance case on inapplicability). A frame name, an available
460: tool or a listed family triggers no activation by itself. Where
461: applicability needs residual semantic judgment, that judgment and its
462: evidence are retained as a judgment, never represented as a computed fact
463: (P6, P1). A required result that is absent, stale, bound to another subject
464: or basis, or incapable of establishing its claim cannot satisfy a dependent
465: conjunction ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results));
466: unresolved applicability withholds the dependent claim until
467: sufficient evidence or the owning decision resolves it; other applicable
468: constraints stay in force even if only one evaluation detects them (P4b,
469: P5). Qualification of an applicability rule distinguishes true, false and
470: unknown premises, required results that are missing or bound to the wrong
471: subject, and a sufficient positive result, under a finite declared fixture;
472: a rule that always skips or always activates cannot satisfy those distinct
473: expected outcomes (EVALUATION §7; rc.2 RF
474: #applicability-and-required-results).
475: 
476: Exclusion and the core. Deciding applicability is an evaluation of the
477: predicate "the obligation applies to the exact subject", and its result is
478: a core value of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): a true
479: predicate is `satisfied`; a false predicate is `falsified`, the
480: basis-bound fact that makes it false being the counterexample; a missing
481: or ambiguous premise is `indeterminate`, or `out_of_frame` where the
482: premise needs a relation the frame does not declare, and never
483: `falsified`. An exclusion is the state of the excluded obligation after a
484: `falsified` applicability result: it is no result, the obligation's own
485: evaluation is not performed and maps to no core value, and the obligation
486: leaves the required coverage of a dependent conjunction under the cited
487: authority of that applicability result. An obligation whose applicability is
488: unresolved stays in that required coverage. A predicate that its owner
489: declares as a disjunction that includes non-application, such as "meets
490: the axiom or does not apply", may be `satisfied` because the obligation
491: does not apply; that `satisfied` is for the declared disjunction only and
492: never counts toward the predicate that the obligation holds
493: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
494: Predicates travel). Members, profiles and projects refer to this
495: paragraph for exclusions and do not decide them again (P5, P6, P1).
496: Purpose and material relation: an exclusion read as a result of the
497: excluded obligation, or a "does not apply" counted toward that obligation,
498: would report a skipped obligation as met; an unresolved premise read as an
499: exclusion would drop an obligation that may apply.
500: 
501: ### Output
502: 
503: The step's output is a candidate plus its step-produced facts: judgments with
504: their evidence, residuals, observations, authority decisions, provenance, and
505: one stop state, a value of construction availability (§3). The actor's
506: internal path is not part of the output
507: and is not governed (FOUNDATIONS §2, work boundary; provenance
508: [Probabilistic Work Boundary](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#probabilistic-work-boundary)).
509: 
510: ### Configuration
511: 
512: A configuration allocates a task's responsibilities and information
513: exchanges to frames; activation binds an actor to each frame (§2). It
514: spans the task's work. The active frame configuration of
515: [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects) is the part of it used for
516: one evaluation or decision (P0, P6).
517: 
518: Allocation. The allocation is derived from the task's operations, the
519: dependencies among them, the capabilities of the available actors and the
520: required assurance. These conditions constrain a configuration without
521: determining it. One frame or several, fixed or adaptive allocation, a
522: hierarchy, peer coordination, or an arrangement that changes as actors
523: allocate work within their contracts may each be adequate. The method
524: prescribes no role inventory, hierarchy, coordinator or actor sequence
525: (P0, P2; [RF-016](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-016-implementation-neutrality)).
526: 
527: Explanation. The design that selects a configuration explains its
528: allocation, including the material resource limits it assumes, such as
529: context, attention, time and spend, each declared as §6 Resource limits
530: states, and its assumptions about failure. The
531: explanation is recorded in the existing design, frame declarations and
532: work records; no separate configuration carrier is required. It is
533: proportional (§6): for a direct entry, the intake states it, its
534: capability envelopes carrying the resource limits and its stale,
535: out-of-scope and re-entry conditions the failure assumptions (P2, P6).
536: 
537: Direct entry. A one-frame configuration is lawful. One directly
538: authorised task that fits a sufficient frame may be entered directly, as
539: Roles and delegation below states, subject to any separately required
540: assessment (P0, P2).
541: 
542: Evaluation of a configuration. A configuration is evaluated against the
543: task, its dependencies, the actors' limits, the authority it applies and
544: the required assurance. Its labels, its topology, and the presence or
545: absence of a coordinator or of familiar roles neither accept nor reject
546: it (P1, P6).
547: 
548: Distinct relations. Within a configuration, the relation structures that
549: [RF-009](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-009-no-assumed-hierarchy) lists as
550: distinct stay distinct; RF-009 owns that list and the rule, and this
551: section adds no structure to it and drops none. Naming or selecting a
552: frame grants no authority
553: ([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
554: creates no authority): each activation binds its subject, result algebra,
555: actor capability and admitted authority through its intake (Intake above)
556: and its activation (§2).
557: 
558: Admission of a configuration. A configuration is admitted by the smallest
559: existing authority that owns the material decision the configuration
560: makes. One configuration may derive from several governing owners; each
561: keeps its own decision, and admitting the configuration creates no new
562: authority over them. An explicitly bounded proxy admits a configuration
563: only inside its existing grant (FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds, Proxy
564: limit). Which authority owns which decision is a binding of the method or
565: profile that applies this rule; the executive configuration's binding is
566: [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §16](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#existing-authority-selects-the-configuration),
567: which refers here for the rule (P6, P2; provenance
568: [Existing Authority Selects The Configuration](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#existing-authority-selects-the-configuration)).
569: Purpose and material relation: a configuration allocates authority-bearing
570: responsibilities, so admitting one by an authority that does not own the
571: decision would move authority with position in the decomposition; the
572: rule holds for every configuration, so it is stated here and not only in
573: an optional profile.
574: 
575: Reconfiguration. The allocation, and every reconfiguration, preserves the
576: material dependencies, the outstanding obligations, the effects,
577: including those of uncertain completion, the admitted authority and the
578: required independence. A reconfiguration is any change of allocation
579: during the work, including actors redistributing work among themselves
580: and the changes §4 Reconfiguration selects after a result. An outstanding
581: obligation and the results that depend on it move with the work. An
582: effect of uncertain completion is resolved sufficiently for the next
583: dependent action before that action (§3 Effects, §5). Required
584: independence keeps its authorship and evidence conditions
585: ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), which a fresh
586: context alone does not meet. An adaptive or self-organised arrangement is
587: exempt from none of these conditions (P4b, P5, P6).
588: 
589: Coordination across tasks. Where a configuration separates carrying out a
590: bounded change from managing delivery across successive tasks, the frame
591: that manages delivery, a coordinator, keeps the longer-term outcome. It
592: decides from a sufficient bounded view of the closed results of the task
593: frames (§7), not from their working context. When a decision needs
594: information that view lacks, the coordinator acquires it through its
595: permitted frame inputs or requests a further bounded evaluation. Missing
596: information is never assumed favourable. A task result never omits a
597: blocker material to delivery: a compact result keeps every residual and
598: stop material to delivery, and its size is no evidence that none exists
599: (P0, P4b, P6).
600: 
601: Optimality. Adequacy and optimality are separate claims. A claim that a
602: configuration is optimal is relative to stated objectives, constraints and
603: comparison scope, and rests on evidence for that comparison. Familiarity,
604: persistence or self-organisation is no such evidence. Different
605: objectives or actor models can favour different configurations (P2, P6).
606: 
607: Example. The executive configuration, which the
608: [executive baseline profile](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md) defines, is one
609: configuration, for task-based work in which a bounded change and delivery
610: across tasks need separate attention. It allocates construction,
611: assessment and disposition (Roles and delegation below) to three frames: a
612: Worker frame, specialised as Writer for documents and records, constructs;
613: a Reviewer frame assesses; an Executive frame keeps the longer-term
614: outcome, selects the next work and disposes within its decision grant, and
615: mutates nothing. That profile owns its frames, their grants, limits and
616: prohibitions, and its explanation; they apply where it is selected. It is
617: not the method's default. A configuration with other frames, names or
618: topology is evaluated as Evaluation of a configuration above states.
619: 
620: Purpose and material relation: finite context and attention bound each
621: responsibility (P0); dependencies between tasks require exchanges and
622: compatible results (P4a); and fallible actors with incomplete knowledge
623: require checking and recovery (P5, P6). These conditions constrain a
624: configuration without determining it, so the method states what every
625: allocation preserves and leaves the arrangement to the design. A
626: coordinator that decides from a bounded view relies on what the view
627: holds, so a blocker missing from a task result would be read as absent
628: (P4b). The material relation is whether an allocation or a reallocation
629: can drop an obligation, an effect or a required independence, move
630: authority with position in a decomposition, or hide a blocker from the
631: decision that needs it. This law is new in this corpus.
632: 
633: ### Roles and delegation
634: 
635: Roles are relations over steps that a configuration allocates
636: (Configuration above), not kinds of actor and not a fixed inventory.
637: Where a configuration's operations include construction, assessment or
638: disposition, this member names the responsibility for each: a
639: constructor owns the bounded implementation and its self-review; an
640: assessor evaluates a frozen candidate independently; a decision owner
641: disposes. A configuration may allocate other responsibilities. Where
642: independent assessment supports promotion, the assessor evaluates the
643: exact live subject, its authority paths, proof and installed state, not
644: the constructor's summary (EVALUATION §3). This preserves the
645: independent-review relation and prescribes no actor count: one actor may
646: occupy different roles across different claims when independence for the
647: assessed claim is preserved; no role name confers an operation
648: ([RF-016](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-016-implementation-neutrality);
649: P6; provenance rc.2 SPEC_METHOD #construction-assessment-and-delegation).
650: 
651: The governing authority relation declares whether a bounded proxy may
652: accept and advance routine actions. Inside a step, a proxy so declared may
653: accept preservation, require local repair, reject a violating candidate
654: and advance to the next already-authorised action; what it cannot change,
655: and the re-entry such a change requires, is the proxy limit of
656: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), which
657: this paragraph applies and does not restate. Human ceremony is not
658: required at every transition when the governing basis, the affected cone,
659: the decision envelope and the re-entry conditions are already accepted;
660: this delegation does not weaken direct human acceptance where the
661: governing product or release law requires it (P6).
662: 
663: When one capable context has sufficient existing work authority, exact
664: intake and operation grant, it may enter directly as constructor. No
665: coordinating activation is required solely to appoint that constructor.
666: The applicable configuration (Configuration above) selects
667: coordination when material contexts, authority, capability or required
668: independence need it; a role or frame name alone does not create that
669: need. Direct entry preserves
670: execution-contract admission (Admission above), the smallest lawful
671: carrier, the required assessment and the reserved decisions; it permits
672: bounded work and condition-based result recording, not self-acceptance at a
673: boundary owned elsewhere (P0, P6).
674: 
675: Recording a result without review. Where the applicable law requires no
676: independent assessment and reserves no acceptance, the constructor that
677: holds the grant may record the satisfied bounded result, with the conditions
678: it found satisfied and their evidence, in the existing durable result
679: surface (Admission above), without adding a carrier, coordinating
680: appointment, review or recreated design view solely to mark completion. The
681: recording waives no condition that actually applies, states only
682: conditions that were evaluated, as an actor cannot report an evaluation it
683: did not perform
684: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed), and is
685: no disposition at a boundary owned elsewhere
686: (§3 Disposition). Where an assessment or a reserved acceptance does apply,
687: it stays required, and an insufficiency found during the work withholds
688: the dependent effect and returns the question to its owner. Carriers and
689: profiles refer to this paragraph and add only their own carrier binding
690: (P0, P2, P6; provenance rc.2 SPEC_METHOD
691: #construction-assessment-and-delegation). Purpose and material relation:
692: requiring a review or a ceremony that no law requires adds reasoning cost
693: without removing ambiguity (§6), while recording a satisfied result where
694: a review or acceptance is required would read construction as acceptance.
695: 
696: One bounded operation grant may cover its declared construction, status and
697: checkpoint sequence. Actual role transitions are recorded in the existing
698: work carrier; a status change alone requires neither a new grant nor
699: rehashing an unchanged subject. A material change to the operation, the
700: subject, the territory, the authority or the validity conditions requires
701: the affected binding to be resolved before effect. Where the selected
702: configuration restricts its coordinating role from mutation, as the
703: executive configuration (Configuration above) restricts its Executive,
704: the restriction that the coordinating role mutates nothing remains
705: applicable; an operation grant covering the sequence does not lift it
706: (P6, P3).
707: 
708: ## 2. Context construction under an envelope
709: 
710: Given a seed set Z (the subject, outcome and affected relations named in the
711: intake), a relation family R (the dependency relations whose change can
712: alter the result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency or authority), and
713: the actor's envelope B:
714: 
715: 1. Compute the material closure of Z under R (AC-010,
716:    [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-010-material-closure);
717:    provenance rc.2 AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS #ac-010-material-closure).
718:    If Z, R, the required-edge semantics, the basis or the scope is not
719:    exact, or the closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis,
720:    activation returns `closure_unresolved` (§3, Admission and activation)
721:    and no step proceeds; it does not guess.
722: 2. Project the closure to the selected context, recording its boundary: the
723:    excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive
724:    seams (AC-011,
725:    [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-011-projection);
726:    provenance rc.2 AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS #ac-011-projection).
727:    If the projection returns a gap or refusal, activation returns
728:    `closure_unresolved` and no step proceeds.
729:    Material not in the closure stays out; adjacent material does not enter
730:    because it exists
731:    ([RF-004](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-004-irrelevance-exclusion)).
732: 3. Test fit against B. This step owns the size measurement and the fit
733:    test for the context dimension. Where B declares a context capacity,
734:    the size of the selected context is measured before the actor reads it,
735:    in the unit the capacity is declared in (bytes or tokens) and over the
736:    boundary that the selected execution binding states for it (§6), and is
737:    compared with that capacity. The measurement, the capacity and the
738:    outcome of the comparison are recorded before the read. A fit holds
739:    only for the measured boundary: context outside it is recorded as not
740:    measured, and no fit claim covers it. The fit claim for a measured
741:    boundary and the step's fit judgment are distinct: the judgment is
742:    established from the recorded complete active inputs, or from a
743:    supported upper bound that includes any host-supplied context; where
744:    neither exists it is `indeterminate`, unless a counterexample, such as
745:    a measured excess, establishes `falsified`. A correct task result keeps
746:    its own bounded standing and does not satisfy a missing fit judgment
747:    (P0, P5; new law carried at iteration 4 from the common construction
748:    contract's Limits). The measurement applies wherever B declares a
749:    context capacity, whatever question the step governs, because without
750:    it a fit claim against that capacity is an assertion, and a context
751:    that exceeds it would be cut without record
752:    ([RF-014](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-014-capability-fit)). It applies only
753:    there, because a resource control applies only through a selected frame
754:    and its owning scope
755:    ([REFERENCE_FRAME §4](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#frame-set-selection)), and a
756:    declared capacity is such a control: the measurement tests that
757:    capacity, is no budget, and is not a universal measurement gate (P0,
758:    P2). Where B declares no context capacity, no measurement is
759:    required, and the other conditions of
760:    [RF-002](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-002-finite-attention) still apply. The size
761:    shows fit and nothing else: whether the actor attends adequately to a
762:    context that fits is decided by actual-use evidence under
763:    [EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification). The envelope's
764:    other dimensions are fitted as RF-014 states; time, spend and other
765:    resource limits follow [§6 Resource limits](#resource-limits), which
766:    this step refines for the context dimension.
767:    If the context fits, activate. If it does not, one or more of these, in
768:    combination: refine the outer contract into steps whose contexts fit
769:    (§4); sequence activations; apply a lawful compression that preserves the material
770:    distinctions and failure detections the evaluation needs
771:    ([RF-017](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-017-proportional-compression));
772:    select another actor whose envelope fits; or return `out_of_frame`
773:    ([§3 Admission and activation](#admission-and-activation)). Silent
774:    omission to fit is never one of them
775:    ([RF-014](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-014-capability-fit)).
776:    None of these options silently reduces the required predicate: the
777:    obligations the step preserves stay bound
778:    ([§1 Transitions](#transitions)), a narrowing of them is a destination
779:    change under its owning authority (§1, Destination change), and what
780:    the selected context leaves undecided stays an explicit unknown.
781:    Within its grant a step selects refinement, sequencing and compression
782:    itself; selecting another actor or enlarging the envelope re-enters the
783:    owner of the grant or envelope, who may delegate that choice in the grant
784:    (RF-014 vests the selection in human authority; a grant is that authority
785:    exercised in advance). Whether a compression preserved what the
786:    evaluation needs is a claim with the standing of any other (EVALUATION
787:    §1): the compressing step records the compression and its preservation
788:    argument, and the claim is assessed independently only where the
789:    promotion it serves needs independent assessment (EVALUATION §3).
790: 4. Acquire declared inputs by their exact identity. A declared input absent
791:    from the actor's materialised view is neither licence to read elsewhere
792:    nor evidence that it is absent.
793: 
794: Acquisition. Acquisition is the read-only observation of the material a
795: step needs (its frame, its subject and its declared inputs) within the
796: inputs its intake permits it to acquire (§1 Intake). It is not an admission and not a further
797: actor stage; effectful work still needs its admitted contract (§1
798: Admission), and acquiring material grants no role, operation or decision
799: ([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
800: creates no authority). A derived surface is material derived from owning
801: sources by copying, projection or compression, such as a projected frame
802: for a task; it names its sources and owns no determination. Where a
803: current interpretation of the subject in `a_c` exists, the constraint
804: surface it yields for the task is such a derived surface, under the
805: conditions of
806: [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §9 Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).
807: Where a derived surface whose sources
808: are current serves the task, the actor acquires it. For another task, or
809: where the derived surface is stale ([Staleness of derived surfaces](#staleness-of-derived-surfaces)),
810: missing or insufficient for a named unresolved question, the actor acquires the deciding owner sections
811: directly: the owning sections that decide the task's questions, which are
812: declared inputs of the selected basis. Only material in the exact selected
813: basis is acquired: where that basis has no derived surface for the task,
814: its exact owner sections are used, and a candidate source, a version-line
815: selector or another basis is no substitute for it
816: ([FOUNDATIONS §2 Product lineage objects](FOUNDATIONS.md#product-lineage-objects)).
817: The actor reads the selected material and the actual subject, and follows
818: the material source and coupled-obligation references the task needs
819: (step 2; [RF-003](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-003-material-sufficiency));
820: presence of the corpus is no reason to read it (step 2;
821: [RF-004](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-004-irrelevance-exclusion)). No frame,
822: derived surface or acquisition carries a universal sufficiency claim:
823: sufficiency is decided for the named question against the task's
824: material relations, never for the corpus or the frame as a whole
825: ([RF-003](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-003-material-sufficiency)). Before any dependent action, a missing binding is returned with
826: its outcome of [§3 Admission and activation](#admission-and-activation),
827: naming what is missing: where no available frame declares what the
828: evaluation needs, `out_of_frame`; where the basis the step requires is
829: absent, or cannot be verified as the exact basis named, the basis cannot
830: support the step, and the outcome is `admission_refused(basis)` at
831: admission or `activation_refusal(basis)` at activation. Coupled material that does not fit is handled under
832: step 3 (P0, P6, P3).
833: 
834: Activation. The actor or the assigning authority selects one frame or one
835: declared active frame configuration capable of the evaluation. Activation
836: binds each reusable frame declaration to the exact subject and basis and
837: loads the declared material relations and evidence sources, never an
838: undifferentiated workspace dump; what the actor receives is the packet of
839: REFERENCE_FRAME §11. When no available frame and actor pairing can lawfully
840: perform the evaluation, activation returns `out_of_frame` where no such
841: pairing declares a material relation or capability the evaluation needs,
842: and otherwise the `activation_refusal` whose cause holds
843: ([REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions)); both are
844: outcomes of §3 Admission and activation. Work does not proceed through
845: implied context (P0, P5; rc.2 RF #select-and-activate).
846: 
847: Evaluation. The evaluator applies the activated frame's declared
848: invariants, evidence rules and result algebra. It distinguishes semantic
849: law, observed evidence, inference and decision, and records every
850: assumption whose failure could change the result (P6; rc.2 RF #evaluate).
851: 
852: Standalone scope. A derived surface or projected frame decides standalone
853: only the questions that its own source members own. It refuses to close a
854: question owned by another member, or one that joins the law of several
855: owners; the evaluation of that question returns `out_of_frame`
856: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) naming the owning
857: members, and
858: the question is decided from those members at their current digests or
859: from a derived surface whose declared sources include every owner of it
860: (P6, P1; provenance rc.2 authority_compressions/stdo_compressed.md,
861: spec_method.compressed.md and design_module_method.compressed.md, a claim
862: no rc.2 body states).
863: 
864: Prompt construction. A prompt is rendered contract over typed authority;
865: it is not source law. Prompt text must project the current authority
866: references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations and
867: fallback conditions the step needs. A prompt body must not carry
868: historical workaround prose unless the current requirement, design,
869: runtime or test still needs that constraint. Construction starts from the
870: highest live authority surface the question needs. If the prompt needs an
871: upstream ambiguity resolved, it names the unresolved authority gap before
872: fallback context is read. The prompt projects the material that
873: Acquisition above selects, including the raw owning members where
874: Acquisition falls back to them (P6, P0, P5; provenance rc.2
875: authority_compressions/stdo_compressed.md and spec_method.compressed.md, a
876: claim no rc.2 body states). The design, ODD, UX and ticket
877: specialisations are
878: [DESIGN_MODULE §11](DESIGN_MODULE.md#11-review),
879: [ODD §11.5D](ODD.md#115d-constructive-evaluation-and-yield-loop) A5 and
880: [§11.7A](ODD.md#117a-conforming-agentic-development),
881: [UX §7](UX.md#7-carrier-binding) and
882: [TICKETS §5](TICKETS.md#5-from-carrier-to-execution) and
883: [§7](TICKETS.md#7-authority-judgment-closure-and-state) (P6).
884: 
885: The operation that joins AC-010, AC-011 and RF-002, RF-003, RF-004,
886: RF-014 and RF-017 into one procedure is new in this corpus (P0); each of
887: those laws is applied here from its successor section in
888: [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-010-material-closure) and
889: [REFERENCE_FRAME §3](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#3-laws), and a `stdo://` route in
890: this section is provenance only. The method does not require proving
891: that no undiscovered material relation exists
892: ([RF-003](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-003-material-sufficiency)).
893: The size measurement of step 3, with the condition under which it
894: applies, and Acquisition are also new. Purpose and material relation:
895: finite context makes fit necessary (P0), so a fit against a declared
896: capacity is measured rather than asserted, while fit and attention stay
897: separate claims (P6); and an actor without a derived surface for its task
898: still reaches the sections that decide it, from the exact basis, without
899: reading the corpus or substituting a stale or mutable copy (P3, P6). The
900: material relation is whether a context larger than the declared capacity
901: is read as if it fit, a fit is taken as adequate attention, or a decision
902: rests on material other than its deciding owners at the selected basis.
903: 
904: ### Staleness of derived surfaces
905: 
906: This subsection owns when a derived surface (Acquisition above) is current
907: and when it is stale, for any method and any carrier (P3, P5, P6):
908: 
909: - A derived surface names the exact identity, such as the path and
910:   digest, of each source it was derived from and of each source whose
911:   change can change its content.
912: - It is current for a selected basis only while every source identity it
913:   names equals the identity of that source in the selected basis. A change
914:   to any of them makes it stale.
915: - A stale derived surface is not used as current for any question. It
916:   becomes current again only by regeneration from the sources at the
917:   selected basis, or by an explicit re-acceptance that records the new
918:   source identities and the finding that its content still matches them;
919:   until then the actor acquires the deciding owner sections directly
920:   (Acquisition above).
921: - Matching source identities establish only that the surface was derived
922:   from those sources. They establish neither its fidelity to them nor its
923:   sufficiency for a question; a surface found insufficient for a named
924:   question is handled as Acquisition above states.
925: - The owning sections at the selected basis remain the deciding source.
926:   Whether a current surface is insufficient for a question, or decides
927:   beyond its own sources, is judged against them (Standalone scope above);
928:   a derived surface never decides that about itself.
929: 
930: A packaging or installation carrier refines this rule with its own
931: identities and re-acceptance procedure, and names this subsection as its
932: owner; [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §11](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#11-one-constitutional-surface-and-version-boundary)
933: does so for the method's released carriers. Provenance: rc.2
934: authority_compressions/README.md and stdo_bootstrap.md step 5, a claim no
935: rc.2 body states. Purpose and material relation: an actor that relies on a
936: derived surface after one of its sources has changed decides from material
937: that no longer matches its owners, and a matching digest read as fidelity
938: would let a faithful-looking but wrong surface decide; the material
939: relation is whether a decision rests on a surface whose sources are not
940: those of the selected basis. This rule is new in tier 1; it was stated
941: only for packaging carriers before.
942: 
943: ## 3. Step results and disposition
944: 
945: A step returns its results in the core algebra of
946: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): each evaluation it
947: performed returns one core value with its predicate and domain outcome,
948: and an evaluation it did not perform has no result. The outcomes of
949: admitting and activating a step, and the step's own outcomes, answer other
950: questions than its evaluations do. This section owns them as five
951: refinements of the core. Each names the question it answers and the
952: predicate its mapping is for, and maps each of its values to exactly one
953: core value; the predicate travels with the value, so no refinement's
954: `satisfied` counts toward another predicate
955: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).
956: Purpose and material relation: admission, work, decisions and effects
957: stand in the one core (P5, P6), so a consumer that combines them cannot
958: read a refused activation as a step's stop, availability as fitness or
959: acceptance, a carried ambiguity as resolved, or an unknown effect as none.
960: 
961: | Refinement | Question | Predicate of the mapping |
962: |---|---|---|
963: | admission and activation | may the step begin | the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject and basis |
964: | construction availability | did the step yield its output | a candidate is available |
965: | disposition | what the decision owner does with an assessed candidate | the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary |
966: | ambiguity outcome | what happened to a declared ambiguity | the declared ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis |
967: | effects | did an intended external effect occur | the intended effect occurred |
968: 
969: A profile that refines these values for its own units maps each of its
970: values to exactly one core value under FOUNDATIONS §4 Results and adds no
971: core value.
972: 
973: ### Admission and activation
974: 
975: A step exists only after its contract is admitted (§1, Admission) and its
976: frame is activated on the exact subject and basis (§2). The outcomes of
977: admission and of context construction are owned here; each maps for the
978: predicate "the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact
979: subject and basis", and its cause selects its value (P5, P6; RF-005 for
980: the basis causes). The outcomes of frame activation are the `activate`
981: refinement of [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions),
982: which owns their causes, their predicate and their core values. Because
983: this predicate requires activation, a refused activation decides it with
984: the value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 gives; the table names those outcomes and
985: maps none of them again:
986: 
987: | Outcome | Cause | Core value |
988: |---|---|---|
989: | `activated` | the contract is admitted with its admission evidence (§1), Z, R, the required-edge semantics, the basis and the scope are exact and the material closure is finite and unique (§2, step 1), its projection returns a selected context (§2, step 2), and activation returns `activated_frame` | satisfied |
990: | `admission_refused(authority)` | the work authority the step needs is not admitted: no admission mechanism or explicit human override admits the exact contract, or no durable result and evidence surface is authorised and available; the outcome names the missing authority or surface and its owner | out_of_frame |
991: | `admission_refused(basis)` | the contract's cited outcome, prerequisite or experiment basis, or the exact subject and basis it names, cannot support it; the outcome names that basis | invalid_basis |
992: | `closure_unresolved` | the seed set Z, the relation family R, the required-edge semantics, the basis or the scope is not exact, or the material closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis (§2, step 1; AC-010), or the projection of the closure returns a gap or refusal (§2, step 2; AC-011); the outcome names the condition that fails and the basis coordinates that leave it open | invalid_basis |
993: | `out_of_frame` | no available frame and actor pairing declares a material relation or capability the evaluation needs (§2, Activation), or no fit option of §2 step 3 fits the selected context to an actor's envelope | out_of_frame |
994: | `activation_refusal` with its cause | a cause REFERENCE_FRAME §5 states | the core value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 maps that cause to |
995: 
996: These outcomes are not values of construction availability and are not
997: results of a step. A refused admission or activation creates no step, no
998: activation of the step's frame and no work result, the closed output of a
999: constructing actor to its consumer; the outcome returns to the assigning
1000: authority or the declared result carrier, and no consumer records it as a
1001: step's stop state. [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §5](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#work-result)
1002: applies this rule to the Worker (provenance
1003: [work result](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#work-result)).
1004: Purpose and material relation: a mismatch known before the step begins is
1005: reported with its cause in the one core, so it is neither mistaken for a
1006: step that stopped nor for one that ran.
1007: 
1008: ### Construction availability
1009: 
1010: A step's output is a candidate until evaluated (FOUNDATIONS §3, P0): the
1011: constructed subject of a constructing step, or the closed results of an
1012: assessing step. Construction availability records whether that output
1013: exists (P5, P6; provenance
1014: [work result](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#work-result)):
1015: 
1016: | Value | Core value | Ground |
1017: |---|---|---|
1018: | `candidate_ready` | satisfied | an exact candidate and its transition evidence are available |
1019: | `refused` | falsified | lawful activation occurred, and a governing prohibition or an owner-valid construction refusal defeats the requested construction; the prohibition or refusal is the counterexample |
1020: | `incomplete` | falsified | the lawfully activated step stopped without its output, because an evaluation the output needs was not performed or could not be decided on the admissible evidence, or bounded execution ended first; the stop basis is the counterexample, and it and the residuals name which |
1021: | `re_entry_requested(authority)` | out_of_frame | a material decision the step needs lies outside its grant; the value names the owner of that decision |
1022: | `re_entry_requested(basis)` | invalid_basis | the activated basis can no longer support the work |
1023: 
1024: The mapping is total and exclusive after lawful activation: the cause of
1025: the stop selects the value, and payload wording, stop timing or actor
1026: preference cannot select another. A mismatch known during admission or
1027: activation is no value of this refinement, because no step exists; it
1028: takes its outcome under Admission and activation above.
1029: 
1030: `satisfied` here establishes availability only and never counts toward the
1031: candidate's fitness or acceptance (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results).
1032: 
1033: `incomplete` maps to `falsified` only for "a candidate is available", never
1034: to `indeterminate`. The step's evaluations keep their own results: each
1035: evaluation it performed returns its core value, `indeterminate` where the
1036: admissible evidence could not decide; each evaluation it planned and did
1037: not perform has no result, and its work state (§5) carries it as a
1038: residual with the capability or the execution left unfinished
1039: (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, the third case of the boundary). An evaluation
1040: not performed thus stays distinct from one whose evidence cannot decide
1041: (P5, P6).
1042: 
1043: An assessing step that ends `incomplete` leaves each criterion it did not
1044: evaluate not performed: no result, never `falsified`. The `falsified` of its
1045: availability concerns its own output, never the subject under assessment
1046: (P6).
1047: 
1048: The cause of a re-entry request is part of its value, because a re-entry
1049: request without its cause would map to `out_of_frame` or to
1050: `invalid_basis` according to that cause, and a refined value maps to
1051: exactly one core value (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Refinements). A stop
1052: with both causes records both and takes `re_entry_requested(basis)`,
1053: because a decision cannot be taken on a basis that cannot support it (P5,
1054: P3).
1055: 
1056: ### Disposition
1057: 
1058: The decision owner disposes an assessed candidate with one of four
1059: semantic dispositions (§1, Roles and delegation; P6, P5; provenance rc.2
1060: SPEC_METHOD #proportional-disposition). An assessor may recommend one; the
1061: recommendation is evidence for the decision owner, never a disposition
1062: ([EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results)). The disposition is the
1063: acceptance result: it consumes the candidate's availability and assessment
1064: results and stays separate from both (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results). Each maps
1065: to the core for the predicate "the candidate is accepted at its declared
1066: boundary":
1067: 
1068: | Disposition | Condition | Core value |
1069: |---|---|---|
1070: | `accept` | the candidate closes its declared cone and preserves every affected governing relation | satisfied |
1071: | `local_repair` | implementation or proof is locally defective while the governing relation remains coherent | falsified |
1072: | `re_enter` | the governing outcome, a requirement, an identity, a lifecycle, an authority, a public contract or the accepted design must change | invalid_basis |
1073: | `reject` | the candidate violates a governing relation or leaves an undisposed competing truth path | falsified |
1074: 
1075: For `local_repair` the local defect, and for `reject` the violated relation
1076: or the competing truth path, is the counterexample to accepting this
1077: candidate; a repaired candidate is a new candidate with its own results.
1078: For `re_enter` the governing basis the candidate was built and assessed on
1079: must change, so that basis cannot support acceptance; the change re-enters
1080: at its owning relation (§4). The core values are new; they place
1081: acceptance in the one core, as FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires, so that a
1082: consumer combining results cannot take availability or assessment as
1083: acceptance (P6).
1084: 
1085: Global correctness means conserving every global relation affected by the
1086: bounded action; it does not require proving the whole product inside every
1087: local action (P4b). Repeated rejection against one unchanged boundary
1088: requires reassessment of the frame altitude, the causal cone, the common
1089: components, the design-versus-code placement and the authority
1090: sufficiency. The method sets no rejection-count threshold, mandatory
1091: review-round count or review state machine; it prohibits repeating an
1092: unchanged failed construction relation as if iteration alone could close
1093: it (P2).
1094: 
1095: ### Ambiguity outcome
1096: 
1097: A declared ambiguity is resolved, carried, escalated or blocked, and the
1098: outcome is recorded either way (§4, which also names the hard stops;
1099: [SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle)
1100: applies this to the method's chain of authority surfaces). Each outcome
1101: maps to the core for the predicate "the declared ambiguity is resolved on
1102: the exact basis" (P5, P6):
1103: 
1104: | Outcome | Core value | Ground |
1105: |---|---|---|
1106: | `resolved` | satisfied | a decision was taken under the policy that permits lawful probabilistic processing, or by human adjudication, and recorded |
1107: | `carried` | falsified | policy permits work to continue with the ambiguity open; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and it stays a recorded residual that names the evidence or decision that would resolve it |
1108: | `escalated` | out_of_frame | policy or risk appetite reserves the decision to human adjudication, an authority the step does not hold; the value names that authority |
1109: | `blocked` | falsified | the ambiguity stays unresolved, and policy or a hard stop (§4) halts work at it; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and the value names the halting condition and what would lift it |
1110: 
1111: An open ambiguity is a known state of the exact basis, so `carried` and
1112: `blocked` decide the predicate false; neither is `indeterminate`, whose
1113: evidence cannot decide the predicate. Each keeps its domain outcome with
1114: the value: `carried` with what would resolve the ambiguity, `blocked` with
1115: the halting condition and what would lift it (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
1116: Recording). No outcome other than `resolved` maps to `satisfied`, so a
1117: dependent claim cannot rest on a carried, escalated or blocked ambiguity
1118: as if it were resolved. The mapping is new; it places ambiguity outcomes
1119: in the one core, which FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires of every outcome
1120: (P5, P6).
1121: 
1122: ### Effects
1123: 
1124: An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
1125: mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
1126: declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
1127: admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
1128: premise, P6):
1129: 
1130: | Value | Core value | Ground |
1131: |---|---|---|
1132: | `completed` | satisfied | evidence about the subject establishes that the intended effect occurred in full and that the effect has ended |
1133: | `not_effected` | falsified | evidence about the subject establishes that the declared outcome is not attained and that no later completion of the effect can attain it, for example where no effect began, the effect ended short, an interval that the declared outcome bounds has closed with part of it not done, or the part already done has itself made the declared outcome unattainable, as when it destroyed what the outcome needed; any part that did occur is named with the value |
1134: | `completion_unknown` | indeterminate | neither of the other values is established: the evidence cannot decide whether the intended effect has occurred or will occur, as for a request whose response was lost with no counterexample observed; or the evidence shows the intended effect in full while the effect may still be acting, and the outcome stays undecided until what the effect leaves on the subject is settled; its residual names the observation that would decide |
1135: 
1136: `not_effected` requires evidence about the subject. A lost response, an
1137: absent record, or an actor's context that holds no trace of the effect is
1138: not that evidence, and the value stays `completion_unknown`.
1139: `completion_unknown` never maps to `completed` or to `not_effected`.
1140: 
1141: Whether the effect has ended is a second question beside the predicate
1142: above, and it enters the value only as a conjunct of `completed`. An
1143: effect has ended where evidence about the subject establishes
1144: that it no longer acts on the subject or that it never began. Where an
1145: effect began and the evidence does not establish its end, the end is not
1146: established, and that is recorded beside the value as a residual naming
1147: the observation that would establish it. The end never decides a
1148: `not_effected` value and is never folded into one: when an interval that
1149: the declared outcome bounds has closed with part not done, the value is
1150: `not_effected` while the effect may still be acting. The residual does
1151: not weaken the counterexample, and the counterexample does not resolve
1152: the residual. `completed` alone requires the end established, so a
1153: counterexample stands without proof that the effect has ended, while
1154: success is never claimed for an effect that may still be acting
1155: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing).
1156: 
1157: An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
1158: `completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
1159: established. §5 reconciles it, sufficiently for the next dependent
1160: action, before any repetition or dependent action. A `not_effected`
1161: value licenses neither treating the effect as absent nor repeating it
1162: while its end is not established.
1163: 
1164: The refinement is new. Its material relation is whether an action whose
1165: external effect may have occurred is repeated or relied on; §4 names a
1166: lost post-effect response as a case that no added core value solves, and
1167: this refinement records it in the existing core. Keeping the end of the
1168: effect beside the value keeps two facts that one value would merge: a
1169: counterexample already established for the declared outcome, and an
1170: effect that may still be acting.
1171: 
1172: ## 4. Totality and refinement
1173: 
1174: Next moves after any non-satisfied result are named in advance: continue
1175: within the current contract when supported; refine; recover; yield; re-enter
1176: the owning relation; terminate. Each admitted condition class has a declared
1177: next move, including an explicit unknown class. Total handling does not
1178: claim that every external condition is recognised, that an invoked provider
1179: terminates, or that every request can be completed. A hanging external call,
1180: an unsatisfiable demand and a lost post-effect response are three different
1181: cases and none is solved by adding a value to the algebra.
1182: 
1183: Which outcome of [§3 Ambiguity outcome](#ambiguity-outcome) a declared
1184: ambiguity takes is decided by the applicable ambiguity policy and its risk
1185: appetite, an added choice; for this method the owner of the default
1186: policy is [SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle),
1187: and this section states none. The outcome is recorded either way.
1188: 
1189: Hard stops. Some conditions are not optional ambiguity decisions and
1190: remain hard stops regardless of risk appetite. Typical hard-stop classes
1191: include: a violated invariant or guarantee; an absent required authority
1192: surface; a missing declared capability for an executional or operational
1193: stage; an undeclared irreversible side effect; and an explicit policy gate
1194: requiring human approval. A hard stop halts the work at its condition whatever the policy:
1195: for a declared ambiguity, with the §3 Ambiguity outcome `blocked`;
1196: otherwise, as a stop of [§1 Transitions](#transitions), Stops. This
1197: section owns the hard stops;
1198: [SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle)
1199: applies them to the method's chain of authority surfaces (P6, P5;
1200: provenance rc.2
1201: [Ambiguity Governance Rule](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#ambiguity-governance-rule)).
1202: 
1203: Reconfiguration. An out_of_frame, invalid_basis, repeated indeterminate or
1204: incompatible result causes one of: supply the missing admissible evidence;
1205: select another actor inside the frame's capability envelope; activate
1206: another existing frame; refine or extend a frame declaration; revise the
1207: frame set (REFERENCE_FRAME §10); change the evaluation; or re-enter the
1208: governing product or method relation. The next move follows the cause; a
1209: difficult evaluation alone does not prove that another frame is required
1210: (P5, P2; rc.2 RF #reconfigure-when-necessary).
1211: 
1212: ### Refinement
1213: 
1214: An outer transformation T: A → X with success predicates P₀ … Pₙ
1215: is faithfully refined by steps Tᵢ when each admitted input satisfying Pᵢ
1216: yields an output satisfying Pᵢ₊₁, retains every applicable invariant, exposes
1217: other outcomes without coercion, and each output satisfies the next step's
1218: declared domain and preconditions, as typed composition requires (P4a;
1219: [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5 AC-016](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-016-typed-composition)).
1220: The step and end-to-end preservation obligations this refinement discharges, and what a completion-only relation leaves unclaimed, are [FOUNDATIONS §4 Preservation through construction](FOUNDATIONS.md#preservation-through-construction); this section applies them to refinement. Then a successful composite of exact steps carries P₀ to Pₙ by induction;
1221: a composite that contains an approximate step carries only what its
1222: end-to-end bound states (Exact and approximate steps below). A refinement
1223: carries an earlier output to a later step other than the next only through
1224: a declared adapter, itself a step composed under AC-016, or a declared
1225: specialised contract, in either case one whose declared domain names what
1226: is carried; a specialised contract is declared under its owner's exact
1227: authority, context, basis, scope, preservation, loss, refusal and
1228: invalidation law (P4a, P4b; provenance rc.2
1229: [AC External Imports And Specializations](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#external-imports-and-specializations)).
1230: Coverage of the outer obligations, correctness of the local
1231: implications and legitimate authority are premises, not conclusions; "each
1232: step passed" is weaker than "the outer contract was conserved". Required
1233: coupled relations must fit together in some step; unrelated obligations stay
1234: outside the selected context. Every seam crossing the affected set includes
1235: its far side or states why it cannot participate
1236: ([UP-017](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#bounded-frame-conservation-stdo-up-017)).
1237: Admission of a material transition is one semantic commit of the complete
1238: transition within its enclosing relation, or none (the law below). This
1239: generalises ODD
1240: [graph functions](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/ODD_METHOD.md#graph-functions),
1241: which refine one outer vector into a small inner workflow, to any
1242: realisation; PROFILES §2 keeps the ODD binding.
1243: 
1244: Preservation and licensing. A refinement step decomposes a transformation
1245: into steps, as above. A rewrite step replaces a representation, a step or
1246: a composite by another that is claimed to keep its meaning, for example
1247: by partitioning, regrouping, reordering, merging or substituting parts.
1248: Each refinement layer, the steps that refine one transformation, states
1249: what it preserves of the layer above, the transformation it refines, and
1250: discharges that obligation (P4a, P6). A refinement or rewrite step is
1251: admissible only under the laws declared for its subject. Its licensing law is the declared
1252: law that permits it, such as an associativity, commutativity or
1253: equivalence law that the subject's owner declares for the subject. Where
1254: no law is declared for the subject, only universally valid steps are
1255: admissible: steps that hold whatever laws the subject has. A step that
1256: is neither licensed nor universally valid, such as a partition or
1257: regrouping that no declared law permits, is inadmissible, and so is a
1258: refinement or rewrite that relies on it (P4a, P1).
1259: 
1260: Exact and approximate steps. An exact step preserves meaning: under the
1261: subject's declared interpretation, its output means what the material it
1262: replaces means, and an exact refinement step carries Pᵢ to Pᵢ₊₁ without
1263: approximation (P1). Faithful refinement, defined above, requires exact
1264: steps. An approximate step does not preserve meaning exactly. It
1265: states its adequacy relation, which says how close its output must be to
1266: the exact result to be close enough for the outer contract, and the
1267: composite that contains it states an end-to-end bound, which limits how
1268: far the whole composite may depart from the outer obligation and is
1269: argued for that composite. Such a composite is not faithful; it is
1270: adequate within its end-to-end bound and establishes nothing beyond that
1271: bound. A fixed tolerance at each step does not compose into an
1272: end-to-end bound, because deviations that each stay within the tolerance
1273: can accumulate across steps, so the induction above applies to exact
1274: steps only. A step that is neither exact nor approximate with its
1275: adequacy relation and an end-to-end bound for its composite is
1276: inadmissible: a composite that relies on it is neither faithful nor
1277: adequate within a bound (P4a, P6).
1278: 
1279: Purpose and material relation: a decomposition or rewrite that changes
1280: meaning, or approximations whose deviations accumulate, would let a
1281: composite whose every step passed violate the outer contract (P4a, P1,
1282: P6). The material relation is whether the composite still meets the outer
1283: obligations. Preservation per layer, licensing laws and the per-step law
1284: for exact and approximate steps, including the inadmissibility of a step
1285: that is neither, are new in this corpus; the obligation to state an
1286: adequacy relation and a composition bound, and the end-to-end obligations
1287: of a composition, are
1288: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Preservation through construction](FOUNDATIONS.md#preservation-through-construction),
1289: which this section applies to refinement steps.
1290: 
1291: ### Complete enclosing-relation admission
1292: 
1293: For a material transition, each admission owner is independently
1294: responsible for deriving and validating the complete enclosing relation
1295: from authoritative inputs (P4b, P6; provenance
1296: [UP-021](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#complete-enclosing-relation-admission-stdo-up-021)).
1297: The relation contains every participant and equality join whose identity,
1298: validity, authority, currentness or transition can affect or be affected by
1299: admission; each crossing seam includes its relevant far side or
1300: authoritatively establishes that the far side cannot participate. Caller or
1301: owner assertions of completeness, validity, prior admission or authority do
1302: not establish truth.
1303: 
1304: An owner may consume established facts when their exact subject, basis,
1305: scope, provenance and validity remain applicable to its relation. Their
1306: production and invalidation are recoverable; an unsupported assertion of
1307: prior success is not such a fact. A function, component, role,
1308: conversation or status boundary alone invalidates none of those coordinates
1309: and requires no repeated derivation. Material mutation, rollback, changed
1310: authority or basis, expired validity and an actual trust boundary trigger
1311: the applicable validation before reliance or effect. Reuse does not
1312: transfer the owner's admission responsibility, omit a participant or
1313: satisfy a separately required independent judgment (§7).
1314: 
1315: Derivation and validation bind one exact admission-valid authoritative
1316: basis identity through admission. If validity or currentness can advance
1317: after preflight, admission remains conditional on the declared predecessor
1318: and currentness law for that basis, or re-enters derivation and validation
1319: without effect. Participating owners bind an equal basis or a
1320: design-declared coherent composite basis; independently valid mixed-basis
1321: judgments cannot combine (FOUNDATIONS §2, Basis).
1322: 
1323: Every participant and join is validated before any transition effect.
1324: Internal evaluation order and lawful reuse are implementation-owned, and no
1325: participant subset or nested constituent becomes admitted truth. Admission
1326: is one semantic commit of the complete transition, bound to its exact basis
1327: identity; failure or interruption admits the complete transition or none,
1328: never a subset. No realisation mechanism or participant count is
1329: prescribed. Direct and every supported composite or nested boundary
1330: preserve this law: a partial result cannot substitute for an owner's
1331: derivation and validation, and a competing same-scope path cannot establish
1332: the transition outside the governing admission relation. Fresh
1333: reconstruction and replay over the same basis reproduce the enclosing
1334: relation, the basis identity and the complete outcome or refusal exactly at
1335: semantic altitude (P3, P5).
1336: 
1337: The law is false if completeness is asserted rather than derived; a
1338: relevant participant, join or seam is omitted; validation and admission use
1339: an unidentified, stale or incoherently mixed basis; currentness can
1340: advance without a commit condition or effect-free re-entry; any effect
1341: precedes complete validation; failure or interruption exposes a subset;
1342: fresh reconstruction differs; or competing same-scope authority remains.
1343: 
1344: ### Standing structural qualification
1345: 
1346: Qualification of the admission law is instantiated for every admission
1347: owner and supported boundary declared by accepted design (P6; provenance
1348: rc.2 SPEC_METHOD #standing-structural-qualification). Case applicability
1349: follows the supported input, state and operating or threat model. An
1350: excluded threat alone cannot create an acceptance predicate or require
1351: defensive work; a proposed scope expansion returns to its owning authority.
1352: Supported malformed inputs, stale state and effect boundaries retain their
1353: required checks:
1354: 
1355: | Form | Required observation |
1356: |---|---|
1357: | direct | the complete direct relation is derived, validated and admitted once |
1358: | supported composite or nested | every supported constituent and owning boundary satisfies the same law; unsupported forms have a design-grounded `not_applicable` disposition and no weaker or competing path |
1359: | forged | forged identity, membership, equality or authority reachable within the supported operating or threat model is refused without effect; exclusion requires its owning authority, not a helper's inability to construct the case |
1360: | ambiguous enclosing relation | unresolved participant, join, seam or relation identity ambiguity is refused without effect |
1361: | stale or advanced basis | stale input is refused, and basis advancement between preflight and admission causes effect-free re-entry rather than mixed-basis admission |
1362: | incoherent multi-owner basis | owner judgments on bases that are neither equal nor joined by a design-declared coherent composite basis cannot combine and are refused without effect |
1363: | competing same-scope admission authority | an undisposed competing same-scope path cannot establish the transition |
1364: | reconstructed or fresh-process | the same basis reconstructs the same relation, basis identity and outcome or refusal |
1365: | exact replay equality | replay over the same basis reproduces exactly the enclosing relation, basis identity and complete outcome or refusal |
1366: | atomic publication failure | after validation succeeds, failure or interruption is observed at every materially distinct commit or publication boundary capable of exposing a subset, followed by fresh reconstruction showing the complete transition or none; named representative observations suffice only under a design-declared dominance or equivalence proof covering the complete partial-failure surface |
1367: 
1368: For an indivisible commit unit the atomic test establishes that boundary
1369: and observes failure immediately on both sides. Final-participant
1370: validation failure does not substitute for post-validation atomic-failure
1371: evidence. A standing claim is false if an owner or supported boundary is
1372: omitted, a materially distinct partial-failure boundary lacks an
1373: observation or a declared coverage proof, a case uses a weaker helper or a
1374: manufactured refusal, or fresh reconstruction does not compare the complete
1375: semantic result (EVALUATION §1).
1376: 
1377: ## 5. Work state and restart
1378: 
1379: Work state is the tuple of: the current persistent workspace; the governing
1380: basis; the applicable closed results and judgments with their invalidators;
1381: the residuals; and the known uncertainty over external effects. It is an
1382: object (P3); its carrier (files, an event stream, another admitted owner) is
1383: a profile or realisation choice. Resumption, checkpointing and the
1384: progress account of this section are generic procedures
1385: ([SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding)): they require
1386: no particular carrier (P1, P6).
1387: 
1388: Resumption is re-entry of the same method over the current work state,
1389: starting from the current material state, by a possibly different actor.
1390: It recovers applicable progress, re-checks the invalidators of each reused
1391: result (§7), reopens only affected support, and reconciles uncertain
1392: external effects, sufficiently for the next dependent action, before any
1393: repetition or dependent action. Resumption does not imply idempotence: an
1394: action whose external effect may have occurred is not repeated blindly;
1395: the lawful next moves are reconciliation, yield or stop.
1396: 
1397: Checkpoint. Acceptance binds one exact checkpoint. The next
1398: already-authorised bounded action may begin without renewed human approval;
1399: acceptance does not widen the selected outcome or the affected relation set
1400: (P6, P2). A preservation checkpoint may retain unfinished or unaccepted
1401: work under an existing exact operation grant; it identifies its parent or
1402: predecessor, the included territory, the concurrent-writer disposition and
1403: the durable evidence location, and it is neither acceptance, promotion nor
1404: publication. A proposed restart, which reconstructs from less than the
1405: retained work, identifies why repair of retained work is insufficient,
1406: which obligations and evidence survive, and which causal assumptions
1407: change; reconstructability alone does not select reconstruction. Conserves
1408: [UP-020 checkpoint and continuation](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#checkpoint-continuation-progress-and-churn);
1409: the generic work-state object, the reconciliation of uncertain external
1410: effects and the non-idempotence rule are new (P0, P5 with the open-world
1411: premise).
1412: 
1413: Progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome;
1414: prerequisite work names the obligation it enables; preservation and
1415: repeated proof are evidence, not new progress; rejected or superseded
1416: construction is churn; discovering previously hidden distance revises the
1417: forecast and is not negative progress. Paperwork, code volume, test count,
1418: commit count and review count are not progress by themselves. These are
1419: semantic categories, not a numeric progress algorithm; a consumer may
1420: derive its own progress and churn projections from them (P2). A member,
1421: profile or project that distinguishes finer categories for its own
1422: outcome states them as a refinement of these, naming this paragraph and
1423: mapping each of its categories to one of progress, prerequisite work,
1424: evidence that is not new progress, churn or forecast revision; a category
1425: it cannot map is a change to this owner, not a parallel category (P2, P6).
1426: 
1427: The execution protocol of §1, §3 and this section is false if execution
1428: proceeds from unreconstructable context; if a constructor's report
1429: substitutes for required independent live evidence; if a bounded proxy
1430: changes a governing relation outside its delegation; if unrelated
1431: incompleteness blocks a closed causal cone; if a same-process test is used
1432: to prove materially cross-process authority (§7); or if rejected activity
1433: is reported as accepted progress.

1467: ### The workspace and an actor's account
1468: 
1469: The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations and
1470: are the continuing truth surface of the work: the surface whose current
1471: material state decides what the work has and has not done. An actor's
1472: context is an account of that state. It is bounded, because it is a
1473: projection of the state (§2); revisable, because an observation can
1474: correct it; and disposable, because a step records its closed results and
1475: step-produced facts before it returns (§1 Admission; P4b). An account is
1476: never a second truth surface, and no later activation needs a prior
1477: actor's context: its intake reconstructs the governing relations without
1478: it (§1 Intake) (P0, P3, P6).
1479: 
1480: Acquisition ([§2](#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)) observes the
1481: current subject and its authoritative inputs. Where they materially
1482: disagree with a cached belief, a retained summary or a prior result, the
1483: actor reconciles the disagreement: current evidence corrects the account,
1484: and what the evidence cannot decide stays an explicit unknown. A stored
1485: belief, a summary or a successful prior result never overrules contrary
1486: current evidence. A prior result is relied on only after its
1487: applicability and invalidators are checked against the current subject
1488: and inputs (§7). The actor corrects its account within its grant; where
1489: resolving the disagreement needs an operation, a territory or a decision
1490: outside the grant, the step stops with `re_entry_requested(authority)`,
1491: naming the owner of what it needs (§3 Construction availability) (P5,
1492: P6).
1493: 
1494: Discarding an actor's private context resets nothing: the workspace, the
1495: applicable valid work and the outstanding obligations remain as the work
1496: state records them. A missing trace in a context, a memory or a summary is
1497: no evidence about the subject. It shows neither that work was not done
1498: nor that an external effect did not occur, nor that it ended; an effect
1499: of uncertain completion keeps the value `completion_unknown`, or its end
1500: stays not established beside its `not_effected` value, until evidence
1501: about the subject decides it (§3 Effects) (P5).
1502: 
1503: Work that an interruption left partly written is part of the current
1504: material state from which resumption (above) starts, and is assessed as
1505: it stands; an assessment that was not performed has no result and is
1506: never recorded as performed
1507: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results); §3 Construction
1508: availability). The method imposes no universal reset and no obligation to
1509: replay the complete history. The recovery contract that applies, which is
1510: the resuming step's intake with the work state, determines which
1511: observations and which effect reconciliations the next dependent action
1512: needs. Handoff between actors is by closed results, which carry no private
1513: working context and keep their validity and independence conditions (§7)
1514: (P0, P4b).
1515: 
1516: Purpose and material relation: finite context (P0) means an actor's
1517: context ends or is replaced while the work continues, and discarding it is
1518: safe only because the step-produced facts the outer contract needs are
1519: recorded (P4b). Treating the account as the truth surface would let a
1520: stale account overrule the workspace; treating a discarded account as a
1521: reset would erase progress or repeat an effect that occurred (P5, P6). The
1522: material relation is whether a decision relies on an account that current
1523: evidence contradicts, or reads a missing record as undone work or an
1524: absent effect. This subsection is new in this corpus. The workspace, the
1525: work state and the closed results carry it, and no further carrier is
1526: required.
