1528: ## 6. Cost and proportionality
1529: 
1530: Proportionality is the relation between semantic ambiguity removed and
1531: effective reasoning complexity introduced. A method obligation is
1532: proportional when its contraction of the admissible interpretation space
1533: justifies the additional concepts, relations, projections and evidence an
1534: actor must hold together to reach a correct decision (P2, P0; conserves
1535: [UP-014](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#proportional-method-and-delivery-stdo-up-014),
1536: [UP-005](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#boundary-and-governance-cost-stdo-up-005)).
1537: 
1538: Effective reasoning complexity includes independent concepts and authority
1539: surfaces, cross-document joins, exceptions and branching, states and
1540: transitions, duplicated representations requiring reconciliation, and the
1541: detail required to decide the governed question. It is not raw line count,
1542: artifact count or context-window size. A detailed algebra or semantic
1543: design view may be highly proportional when it eliminates rival
1544: interpretations; a short additional ticket, receipt or summary may be
1545: disproportionate when it creates another truth surface without reducing
1546: uncertainty.
1547: 
1548: A proportional method deliberately constrains the admissible reasoning and
1549: realisation space. Each constraint identifies the semantic ambiguity it
1550: removes and contracts enough of the admissible interpretation space to
1551: justify the reasoning complexity it introduces. Rival authority,
1552: uncertainty over failure classification and evidence uncertainty count only
1553: where they leave materially distinct admissible semantic, authority,
1554: outcome or acceptance interpretations; they measure or evidence the same
1555: interpretation space removed and are not independent proportional
1556: benefits. The method does not prescribe an internal decomposition, search,
1557: collaboration, tool or synthesis procedure when variation in that procedure
1558: cannot affect a governed semantic, authority, evidence, safety or release
1559: property. Increased actor capability may enlarge the bounded relation an
1560: actor can resolve; it grants no authority, an instance of
1561: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
1562: creates no authority, and it weakens no invariant and waives no
1563: acceptance (P6). The owning law may justify one coherent constraint
1564: family once; no rationale field, receipt or repeated audit is required for
1565: every clause or consumer application.
1566: 
1567: For symbolic design, materially divergent implementation paths, runtime
1568: states, tests, reviews and reconciliation joins are counterfactual evidence
1569: of the semantic alternatives the design contracts; they are not an
1570: independent numerator. When one bounded symbolic model can resolve those

1638: ### Resource limits
1639: 
1640: A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
1641: attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
1642: resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
1643: no value (P0, P2, P5, P6):
1644: 
1645: - Declaration. A limit applies to an activation only where its intake,
1646:   its actor's capability envelope or the selected execution binding
1647:   declares it, because a resource control applies only through a selected
1648:   frame and its owning scope
1649:   ([REFERENCE_FRAME §4 Frame-set selection](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#frame-set-selection)).
1650:   A declared limit states its unit and the boundary over which it is
1651:   measured: which inputs, actors, processes and repeated reads it counts.
1652:   No universal quota, budget or measurement gate follows.
1653: - Measurement. A declared limit is measured in its unit over its boundary
1654:   where the obligation it serves needs the measurement; consumption
1655:   outside the boundary is recorded as not measured, and no claim against
1656:   the limit covers it. A context limit bounds the material held in active
1657:   context at once, including material acquired during the activation, so
1658:   the bytes supplied at its start, the cumulative bytes it acquires,
1659:   counting repeated reads, and the bound on what it holds at once are
1660:   reported separately; §2 step 3 refines this for the measurement of the
1661:   selected context before it is read. Measures that answer different
1662:   questions, such as the cost components of Cost is selected above, are
1663:   reported separately.
1664: - Exhaustion. Pressure on a declared limit never licenses omitting or
1665:   truncating a material obligation or input. Before a limit would be
1666:   exceeded, the activation refines the task, sequences activations,
1667:   reassigns the work to an actor whose limits fit, or stops with the
1668:   applicable value of §3, naming the limit, such as `incomplete` where
1669:   bounded execution ends first; a stop keeps the unresolved outcome
1670:   ([§1 Transitions](#transitions), Stops). Enlarging a limit re-enters the
1671:   owner of the grant or binding that set it.
1672: - Values. The value of each limit, and the units and boundaries the
1673:   selected environment can measure, are set by the selected execution
1674:   binding, which binds this law; for a build tenant that binding is the
1675:   one [SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding) defines.
1676:   A value is stated before the activation it limits.
1677: - Standing. An activation that stays within its limits is not thereby
1678:   adequate, and an actor's larger limits grant no authority and waive no
1679:   invariant (P2, P6).
1680: 
1681: Purpose and material relation: the configuration (§1), context
1682: construction (§2) and frame qualification
1683: ([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification)) rely on resource
1684: limits, so the law for declaring, measuring and honouring them is stated
1685: once in tier 1, and only their values are left to the execution binding.
1686: The material relation is whether an undeclared, unmeasured or exceeded
1687: limit is read as fitting, or forces a silent omission. This subsection is
1688: new in this corpus; its parts carry RF-014's prohibition of silent
1689: omission, REFERENCE_FRAME §4's rule that a resource control applies only
1690: through a selected frame, and UP-014's selection rule.
1691: 
1692: ## 7. Closed result and reuse
1693: 
1694: A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the
1695: basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual
1696: uncertainty and the invalidation conditions (the minimal shape is
1697: REFERENCE_FRAME §13). The frame's internal working context need not be
1698: transferred when the closed result and its provenance are sufficient for
1699: the consuming decision; it may still be attached, for audit or otherwise,
1700: without changing the result. Independent evaluations may share valid
1701: mechanical evidence under the declared independence conditions of
1702: [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment), which owns that
1703: permission (P4b, P0; rc.2 RF #return-a-closed-result).
1704: 
1705: The selection of affected results after a change and the conditions for
1706: retaining evidence on a new subject are
1707: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse);
1708: this section applies them to closed results and handoffs, and the three
1709: invalidators below are kinds of change Δ, and a closed result is affected
1710: when its dependencies `D*(t)` meet the impact cover `I(Δ)` (P3, P6).
1711: 
1712: A closed result is reused by an unchanged consumer that checks exact
1713: applicability; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates
1714: nothing. An invalidator invalidates the affected result before reliance,
1715: even where the subject's own bytes are unchanged, preserving its
1716: predecessor/successor relation and any demonstrably independent surviving
1717: results. Invalidation withdraws the result from direct reliance; whether
1718: its evidence is retained on the new basis is decided by `retain_applicable`
1719: of FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse, and the changed
1720: coordinate alone establishes neither that the claim fails nor that it
1721: holds. The invalidators are three:
1722: 
1723: - a material input change: a change to the result's subject or to an
1724:   input it rests on, including the admissible evidence that bears on its
1725:   predicate; newly acquired or changed admissible evidence is such a
1726:   change when it is material to the result as
1727:   [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology) defines material, that is,
1728:   when it could change the result's value;
1729: - a changed basis: a change to any coordinate of the basis the result
1730:   binds (FOUNDATIONS §2, Basis);
1731: - a declared revising observation: an observation that the result or
1732:   judgment itself names as one that would revise it, once it occurs.
1733: 
1734: A changed source, task or actor condition is a changed basis where the
1735: basis binds it, and otherwise a material input change; a role change that
1736: alters a required actor condition is such a change, while a role,
1737: conversation or resumption change that alters none of these invalidates
1738: nothing (P3, P6).
1739: 
1740: Judgment continuity names the basis and the evidence; Return A Closed
1741: Result names inputs and the observation. A member, profile or project
1742: that names a trigger for its own domain, such as a changed projection,
1743: rule or configuration, names it as an instance of one of these three and
1744: states no parallel list (P3, P4b, P6). A reused judgment does not
1745: satisfy a separately required independent judgment; the independent assessor
1746: acquires its own evidence and supplies its own judgment. Conserves
1747: [Return A Closed Result](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#return-a-closed-result),
1748: [judgment continuity](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/TICKET_METHOD.md#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity),
1749: whose "changed material evidence" is the evidence case of the first
1750: invalidator. Purpose and material relation of naming the three kinds once
1751: and of the instance rule: the predecessor stated its invalidators in
1752: several differing lists, so a consumer had to take their union; one list
1753: with named instances gives every consumer the same triggers, and the
1754: material relation is whether a result is relied on after a change that
1755: could alter it (P3, P6). Whether a revision of a frame needs a new
1756: revision coordinate is
1757: [REFERENCE_FRAME §10](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#revision-actions)'s question;
1758: whether a result it touches stays valid is this section's.
1759: 
1760: ### Transition evidence
1761: 
1762: A reviewable transition identifies the exact candidate, the affected
1763: relations, the changed realisation paths, the authority paths added or
1764: removed, the retained and open seams, the focused proof, any required
1765: integration proof, the explicit non-changes, and, where an assessor was
1766: activated, the assessor's recommended disposition, with the decision
1767: owner's disposition beside it once one is made (§3). Consumers
1768: choose the representation. Transition evidence is a read
1769: model; it does not become specification, design or admission authority
1770: (P6, P4b; provenance rc.2 SPEC_METHOD
1771: #transition-evidence-and-proof-cadence).
1772: 
1773: Construction uses the cheapest focused proof capable of falsifying the
1774: active relation. Expensive whole-candidate qualification occurs at a
1775: declared candidate boundary rather than after every local edit, unless the
1776: affected risk makes whole-candidate proof necessary (§6). A durable or
1777: reconstructable authority claim is not established solely by a same-process
1778: proof when loss of incidental process state is a material counterexample:
1779: the proof destroys or excludes the incidental authority and compares the
1780: reconstructed semantic outcomes (P5, P6).

38: ## 1. Verification layers
39: 
40: Each layer of the chain ([SPEC_METHOD §2 Constitutional chain](SPEC_METHOD.md#constitutional-chain)) preserves a distinct kind of truth
41: (P2, P6; rc.2 #verification-layers):
42: 
43: | Layer | What it preserves | Primary question answered |
44: |---|---|---|
45: | Requirements | invariant truth | what must be true? |
46: | Design | structural choice | how is that truth realised? |
47: | Scenarios | operational meaning | can the realised system actually do the claimed thing? |
48: 
49: Without scenarios a capability can appear covered because the words exist
50: in requirements and design. Scenarios force the sharper question: can the
51: product really do the thing? A requirement can name a reusable composable
52: unit and a design record can describe the types that realise it, but only
53: a scenario asks whether a user can build such a unit and apply it twice
54: (P6).
55: 
56: Scenarios are the product-owner layer: concrete, end-to-end use cases that
57: validate the chain from intent to realised behaviour. While no scenario
58: for a capability can be written, its operational meaning is unverified;
59: that alone does not show whether its governing claim is inadequate or the
60: means to state or observe its expected outcome is missing, and diagnosis
61: under [ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation)
62: locates the cause. When a scenario fails, its observed outcome disagrees
63: with the scenario's expected outcome, which no comparison of the
64: specification's words with its other words could show. That report is an
65: observation, so it shows that actual behaviour disagrees only where its
66: observation binding is supported
67: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation)).
68: The failure alone does not show whether the realisation, the governing
69: claim, the scenario's expected outcome or its observation is wrong;
70: [§12 Counterexample localisation](#12-counterexample-localisation) locates
71: the cause as far as the evidence supports (P2, P6).
72: 
73: Scenarios do not replace requirement categories. They primarily validate
74: capability claims and other behaviour with concrete operational meaning.
75: Constraints, governance rules and verification-infrastructure requirements
76: may require different evidence in addition to, or instead of, end-to-end
77: scenarios (P2).
78:

141: ## 2. Testing strategy taxonomy
142: 
143: This member owns the product-assurance bounded context,
144: `urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-assurance`, under the selected complete
145: STDO basis, and within it the Product-level test-authority taxonomy.
146: Module-derived unit-proof law stays owned by the design profile (the
147: DESIGN_MODULE member); the shared context does not merge the two authority
148: sources (P6; rc.2 #testing-strategy-taxonomy).
149: 
150: Every executable proof surface declares its authority source (P6). For
151: ticketed work the immediate proof authority is the admitted ticket and its
152: triage path: tests derive from the ticket's lawful re-entry point
153: (SPEC_METHOD §4) and from the governing constitutional or realisation-law
154: surfaces it cites; they never derive expected results from current
155: implementation behaviour (P6, P2).
156: 
157: Authority source is not execution breadth. A test may be small or broad,
158: fast or slow, deterministic or live, and still derives from one of two
159: primary authorities (P6, P1):
160: 
161: 1. design or module conformance tests; and
162: 2. UAT, or acceptance, tests.
163: 
164: Design or module conformance tests derive from realisation authority: the
165: governing design, module ownership, the carrier inventory the design
166: declares (the design profile's irreducible architectural carrier set,
167: [DESIGN_MODULE §6](DESIGN_MODULE.md#irreducible-architectural-carrier-set),
168: or an equivalent), structural carrier diagrams where present, and boundary-local
169: fail-closed law. They answer one question: did the implementation realise
170: the module or design boundary correctly? Unit tests are design or module
171: conformance tests. Module integration tests, negative tests and
172: fail-closed tests may also be, when their proof target is a designed module
173: boundary rather than a user scenario (P6).
174: 
175: UAT or acceptance tests derive from constitutional user or product
176: authority: requirements, acceptance criteria, declared scenarios or use
177: cases, and product-level release or qualification claims. They answer one
178: question: does the composed product satisfy the claimed requirement or
179: scenario? (P6, P2)
180: 
181: Under this method only sandbox tests, or an explicitly equivalent isolated
182: composed-product proof lane, may be called UAT or acceptance tests. A
183: sandbox test exercises the deployed, installed or otherwise runnable
184: product form through declared application, public, runtime or control
185: surfaces, and is driven by a requirement-sourced scenario or acceptance
186: case. Direct source-level unit tests, helper tests and module integration
187: tests may be valuable proof; they are not UAT and cannot close user
188: acceptance by themselves (P6; EVALUATION §1, the weaker property never
189: substitutes for the claimed one).
190: 
191: Sandbox UAT has two lawful execution modes (P6, P1):
192: 
193: - harnessed sandbox UAT exercises the full composed product path with a
194:   deterministic, fake, recorded or injected worker or result surface; and
195: - live sandbox UAT exercises the full composed product path with a real
196:   configured worker, tool, agent, service or other external probabilistic
197:   transport where the product depends on that live boundary.
198: 
199: Harnessed sandbox UAT proves composition, orchestration, control,
200: projection, archive and scenario wiring without relying on live
201: probabilistic execution; it is the lane for deterministic reproducibility.
202: Live sandbox UAT proves that the same scenario can cross the real external
203: probabilistic boundary and return evidence through the declared result,
204: evaluation, provenance and projection surfaces. Where a product or release
205: claim depends on live probabilistic compute, semantic green, unit green,
206: module-integration green and harnessed-sandbox green are necessary and not
207: sufficient for live acceptance (P6, P5).
208: 
209: Terminology (P1):
210: 
211: - `unit` names module or design conformance scope, not user acceptance;
212: - `integration` names execution breadth, not authority source;
213: - `sandbox` names composed-product acceptance execution;
214: - `harnessed`, `fake`, `recorded` or `deterministic` name non-live sandbox
215:   execution; and
216: - `live` is reserved for real external worker or transport execution; a
217:   status projection named "live" is not live UAT unless it crosses that
218:   real boundary.
219: 
220: A project that uses other local filenames or runner labels still maps each
221: executable lane back to this taxonomy before claiming closure (P1, P6).
222: 
223: ### Fixture and proof portability
224: 
225: Required closure lanes are reproducible from the declared source boundary
226: (P3, P6; rc.2 #fixture-and-proof-portability-rule). A unit, semantic or
227: module-design conformance lane does not depend on an undeclared local path,
228: a sibling workspace, an operator home directory or a mutable external
229: fixture.
230: 
231: Where a proof needs external project evidence, one of these holds:
232: 
233: - a minimal fixture is checked into the source boundary;
234: - a fixture manifest declares the external source, version and
235:   acquisition or binding rule; or
236: - the test is classified as harnessed sandbox, live sandbox, reference
237:   comparison or optional local evidence rather than required semantic
238:   closure.
239: 
240: A missing external fixture fails with a governed diagnostic that names the
241: fixture authority and the lane; it never masquerades as a product semantic
242: failure (P5, P6).
243: 
244: ## 3. Test authority
245: 
246: Every live requirement has written test-case authority (P6; rc.2
247: #test-authority-rule). That authority may include scenario bundles,
248: ordered test-case sequences, negative or control cases and other explicit
249: evidence cases appropriate to the kind of truth being proved; it exists in
250: written form and is traceable. Written authority includes the assertion
251: provenance of each expected result: the owning obligation, its
252: interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies, and
253: whether the asserted predicate is the obligation, a necessary condition of
254: it or part of a sufficient conjunction
255: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation),
256: [Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance))
257: (P6). No live requirement is fully proved on
258: informal operator confidence, ambient habit or an unlabelled test corpus
259: (P6; EVALUATION §5, green labels are not acceptance). The derivation of
260: each test case from admitted work authority is
261: [TICKETS §7 Test case authority](TICKETS.md#test-case-authority).

METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/ASSURANCE.md member_sha256=e33a6e39e1e93d38dbd3ea212d8d9f0d2f44a366a9345fda762d2481c254d0bf lines=317-594
317: ### Terms
318: 
319: A testing frame is a frame (REFERENCE_FRAME §1) whose evaluation executes
320: or observes a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim through an
321: explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification
322: condition. A test file, suite, runner, fixture, scenario label, coverage
323: percentage or actor does not become a testing frame by existing. A testing
324: frame's authority is bounded by the claim actually exercised; test count,
325: assertion count, source coverage, runtime duration and framework category
326: do not widen it (P6, P1; provenance rc.2 STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE
327: #testing-frame).
328: 
329: An authoritative Product path is the declared ordinary causal composition
330: from a supported user or public entry, through the exact selected
331: interfaces, owners, state transitions, effects, persistence and recovery
332: boundaries, to the outcome projection the Product claim requires.
333: Producing an expected output through a bypass, an obsolete executor, a
334: test-only seam, an undeclared fallback or a competing authority falsifies
335: path conformance even when the output value is equal (P6, P3; provenance
336: #authoritative-product-path).
337: 
338: Material combinatorial complexity is the claim-relative population of
339: independent dimensions and interactions whose combinations can change an
340: outcome, violate an invariant, select another authority path or expose a
341: failure. At unit altitude it includes module-owned laws, behaviour at the
342: public module contract included, with their algebraic operators,
343: calculation regimes, states, transitions, boundary classes and failure
344: cases. Cross-participant interface, Product, persistence, configuration and
345: user-role combinations belong to the integration, end-to-end or
346: user-acceptance frames; they are not mocked away and counted as unit
347: evidence (P2, P6; provenance #material-combinatorial-complexity).
348: 
349: ### The set
350: 
351: Where the governing frame configuration (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7) or the
352: admitted work authority selects testing frames for a Product promotion,
353: closure or release-assurance claim, testing is configured as a
354: claim-relative set of testing frames. Placement in this member makes the
355: set, and the law of §8 to §13 that serves it, available; it adopts nothing,
356: and each activation is decided by ACTIVATION §1 (Applicability). The kind
357: of runner does not select the frame; the evaluated claim, subject, path,
358: population, oracle and falsification boundary do (P6, P2; provenance
359: #derived-product-testing-frame-set). Each frame's `invalidation` row,
360: here and in §13, lists named instances of the material input change or
361: the changed basis of
362: [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse); it adds no
363: other kind of invalidator. The ordinary configuration holds four
364: distinct frames:
365: 
366: - user acceptance evaluates the Product outcome from the user's supported
367:   frame;
368: - end to end evaluates the complete runnable causal realisation of that
369:   outcome;
370: - integration evaluates one material composition boundary and its
371:   interaction population; and
372: - unit evaluates one module-owned law; internal combinatorial complexity
373:   decides the proportional size and strategy of that evidence, not whether
374:   the law is eligible for unit proof.
375: 
376: They add no role, stage, authority or testing hierarchy. Their ordinary
377: evidence topology assigns each claim to its congruent frame (P6, P4a;
378: provenance #canonical-compression):
379: 
380: ```text
381: Product and accepted design
382:   |- user-outcome claims -> user-acceptance frames
383:   |- runnable causal-path claims -> end-to-end frames
384:   |- composition-boundary claims -> integration frames
385:   `- module-owned laws -> unit frames
386: 
387: bound results -> declared conjunction -> Product or release disposition
388: ```
389: 
390: The fan-out assigns claims to evidence; it is neither an authority
391: hierarchy nor a claim that one frame decomposes into another. Evidence
392: may relate through declared conjunction
393: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),
394: translation (REFERENCE_FRAME §6), falsification and re-entry (P4a). A
395: broader frame cannot make a module-owned
396: law true, and any number of narrower green frames cannot establish an
397: unevaluated Product composition or user outcome (EVALUATION §1, the weaker
398: property never substitutes for the claimed one).
399: 
400: The frames may overlap, and one execution may supply evidence to several of
401: them; every result stays bound to its own claim. A label such as `UAT`,
402: `E2E`, `integration` or `unit` has no assurance value without the
403: corresponding frame declaration (P1, P6). Each frame below is given in the
404: shape of a frame declaration (REFERENCE_FRAME §13); "core result", here
405: and in §13, is a value of the core result algebra of
406: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), recorded with the
407: predicate the frame's claim states.
408: 
409: ### User-acceptance frame
410: 
411: (P6, P2; provenance #derived-user-acceptance-frame)
412: 
413: | Frame element | User acceptance |
414: |---|---|
415: | evaluation family | Can a declared user, with the user's admitted capability and information, obtain the exact Product-defined outcome through the supported ordinary Product surface? |
416: | subject and basis | the exact deployed, installed or otherwise runnable Product form the claim names; current Product, requirement, UX, identity, policy and acceptance authority; the declared user role, environment, and harnessed or live sandbox mode (§2) |
417: | material manifold | user goal, supported entry surfaces, permissions, inputs, Product configuration, ordinary dependencies, any declared external-worker or transport substitution boundary, user-visible state and outputs, refusal and recovery behaviour, and the acceptance interval |
418: | coordinates | exact Product and artifact identity, install, user role, capability, configuration, dependency realisation, harnessed or live mode, data, workspace, invocation, time, outcome and scenario identity |
419: | governing invariants | the applicable Product and requirement outcomes; supported-interface, identity, UX, safety, persistence and release law; RF-001 to RF-017; EVALUATION §1, §2, §3, §6 and §7 (proof target, evidence separation, assurance-boundary congruence, freeze and post-exposure revision, comparison, method qualification) |
420: | authority | bounded evaluation only; the frame mints no Product meaning or acceptance authority, and an automated actor does not become the human or Product acceptance owner |
421: | evidence | actual supported-surface requests and responses, user-visible projections, durable side effects where claimed, refusals, recovery observations, scenario records, exact-subject identity, and the declared live or substituted dependency identity |
422: | capability envelope | ability to operate the Product as the declared user would, perceive the material outcome and refusal surfaces, and distinguish hidden setup or unsupported assistance |
423: | exclusions | source imports, private APIs, direct Product-state injection, test-only endpoints, hidden administrator capability, undeclared fixtures or substitutes, a test double at a boundary claimed as real or live, compatibility bypasses, and internal success substituted for the user outcome |
424: | result | one core result bound to the exact user-outcome claim, with witnessed paths, counterexamples, residual user populations and invalidation conditions |
425: | invalidation | a material change of Product, supported interface, user role, capability, configuration, dependency or substitution mode, data contract, runnable subject, acceptance meaning or ordinary path |
426: 
427: User acceptance is the primary Product-outcome evidence frame when the
428: claim is that a user can use the Product. It may be automated only when the
429: automation faithfully occupies the declared user frame and gains no path or
430: capability that user lacks. Automation can execute acceptance evidence; it
431: cannot assume acceptance authority (P6; EVALUATION §5).
432: 
433: Where harnessed sandbox UAT is admitted (§2), a deterministic, fake,
434: recorded or injected external worker or transport limits the result to the
435: composed Product relations actually exercised; it does not prove that the
436: live external boundary works. When a Product or release claim depends on
437: real external compute or transport, live sandbox UAT is mandatory for that
438: claim; unit, integration, semantic and end-to-end evidence that uses the
439: substitute, and harnessed UAT green, are not sufficient (P6, P5).
440: 
441: ### End-to-end frame
442: 
443: (P6, P3; provenance #derived-end-to-end-frame)
444: 
445: | Frame element | End to end |
446: |---|---|
447: | evaluation family | Does the exact Product subject realise the claimed outcome through the complete authoritative Product path, including every material interface, owner, state transition, effect, persistence, continuation, recovery and projection boundary? |
448: | subject and basis | the exact deployed, installed or otherwise runnable Product form, the composition design, the supported entry, the selected owner and dependency set, the ordinary runtime configuration and the Product claim |
449: | material manifold | the complete causal producers and consumers from entry to outcome; interface contracts; authority transitions; state, event, persistence, process, continuation, retry, recovery and projection relations; competing paths |
450: | coordinates | artifact and installed-tree identity, entry, operation, selected definition and owner, path and edge identities, process, event prefix, state, configuration, dependency, result, replay and scenario identity |
451: | governing invariants | Product and accepted-design composition law; exact-subject and assurance congruence; path singularity where required; lifecycle, authority, persistence, replay, recovery and release law |
452: | authority | bounded evaluation only; observation may expose internal evidence but may not bypass, repair, replace or reinterpret the Product path |
453: | evidence | supported entry invocation, the observed semantic path and authority edges, owner receipts, durable events, state transitions, outputs, replay or reconstruction where claimed, installed artifact identity, and negative-path observations |
454: | capability envelope | ability to execute and observe the complete Product path without changing it, to tell the authoritative path from rival paths, and to reproduce material state and failure relations |
455: | exclusions | source-only substitutes for runnable-Product claims, direct invocation below the supported entry, test doubles at claimed real boundaries, test-only routing, hidden retries or repair, omitted persistence or fresh-process boundaries, and equal output without path evidence |
456: | result | one core result bound to the exact end-to-end claim, with the exercised composition edges, unexercised material paths, counterexamples and residual combinations |
457: | invalidation | a material change of artifact, install, dependency, configuration, interface, owner, path, lifecycle, persistence, recovery, projection, test semantics or evidence population |
458: 
459: The expected output is necessary and not sufficient. Reaching it through a
460: forbidden or obsolete path falsifies the end-to-end claim. A test is not end
461: to end because it starts and finishes in one process, crosses many lines or
462: carries an end-to-end label (P6, P1).
463: 
464: ### Integration frame
465: 
466: (P6, P4a; provenance #derived-integration-frame)
467: 
468: | Frame element | Integration |
469: |---|---|
470: | evaluation family | Do the actual participants at one declared material composition boundary satisfy their joint contract across the combinations of state, authority, configuration, timing, failure and recovery that can change the boundary result? |
471: | subject and basis | the exact interface or composition declaration, the actual participating implementations or exact substitutes the bounded claim admits, the governing Product, requirement and design law, and the interaction population |
472: | material manifold | both sides of the boundary, shared carriers, preconditions, postconditions, authority and ownership, ordering, state, configuration, failure, retry, recovery, translation and competing participants |
473: | coordinates | participant and version identities, interface and carrier revision, state, configuration, dependency, interaction case, input, output, failure and evidence identity |
474: | governing invariants | declared interface and composition law, complete participant admission, atomicity and reconstruction where applicable, and the exact assurance boundary (EVALUATION §1) |
475: | authority | bounded boundary evaluation only; no integration result establishes an unevaluated Product outcome or authorises a substitute participant |
476: | evidence | actual exchanges, admitted carriers, state transitions, contract verdicts, failures, retries, recovery observations, interaction combinations and participant identities |
477: | capability envelope | competence and access to exercise and observe the real composition seam, identify participant substitution and vary every material interaction dimension |
478: | exclusions | mocks or stubs that hide the claimed real contract, one-sided contract assertions, happy-path-only exchange, helper-call equivalence, flattened versions or states, and projection of a boundary result to the whole Product without a governing relation |
479: | result | one core result for the declared integration claim, with covered combinations, counterexamples, omitted interactions and invalidation conditions |
480: | invalidation | a material change of participant, interface, carrier, state, configuration, dependency, timing, failure, recovery or interaction population |
481: 
482: A substitute or test double may support a deliberately narrower claim only
483: when its equivalence boundary and exclusions are explicit. Its result
484: cannot be promoted to evidence that the real participant or Product
485: composition was exercised (P6, EVALUATION §1).
486: 
487: ### Unit frame
488: 
489: (P6, P2; provenance #derived-unit-test-frame)
490: 
491: | Frame element | Unit |
492: |---|---|
493: | evaluation family | Does one module-owned law hold across its material combinations of algebraic operator, calculation regime, state, transition, public or private boundary class, and failure case? |
494: | subject and basis | one exact module boundary, the accepted ontology and design, the active carrier inventory the design declares, module-owned requirements and public contracts, the implementation, and a module-bounded decidable oracle |
495: | material manifold | module-owned public contracts, algebras, calculations, parsers, reducers, state machines, transition functions, combinators, admission predicates, conservation laws, invariants, numerical boundaries and failures |
496: | coordinates | module and implementation revision, owned law, operator or function family, module state, input class, boundary class, expected relation, generated case, mutation and result identity |
497: | governing invariants | the design profile's module-ownership and unit-proof law (DESIGN_MODULE); the accepted ontology, carrier inventory, domain, sequence, state, algorithm and error relations material to the module |
498: | authority | bounded local evidence only; a unit result has no Product, installed, integration, user-acceptance, architecture, path-selection or release authority |
499: | evidence | law-derived examples, equivalence classes, finite exhaustive cases where available, property-based or generative cases, metamorphic relations, calculation or algebra oracles, boundary cases and killed internal mutations |
500: | capability envelope | competence to derive an oracle independently from the owned law, identify the module-bounded combination population, and tell an invariant violation from an implementation restatement |
501: | exclusions | Product outcomes, cross-module composition, supported user paths, packaging or installation, real external participants, orchestration topology, mocked-away interface behaviour, incidental branches, private helper layout, assertion count, and source coverage used as broader assurance |
502: | result | one core result limited to the exact module-owned law and the module-bounded population, with counterexamples, residual combinations and invalidation conditions |
503: | invalidation | a material change of ontology, carrier inventory, module boundary, owned law, algorithm, state space, numerical regime, implementation, oracle, generator or module-bounded population |
504: 
505: Unit testing is deliberately module-bounded. Every coded module requires
506: the module-derived unit lane the design profile owns; public module
507: contracts are valid unit-proof subjects. Internal combinatorial complexity
508: decides the proportional size and strategy of that evidence. Its highest
509: discriminating value is often in algebras, calculations, transformations,
510: parsers, reducers, state machines, decision tables, admission predicates,
511: conservation relations and bounded algorithms with strong independently
512: derived oracles. A unit test whose oracle repeats the implementation, or
513: whose cases follow incidental code branches, gives weak or circular
514: evidence (P6, P2).
515: 
516: Modules whose material complexity lies mainly in composition,
517: orchestration, configuration, persistence, ownership or user interaction
518: need integration, end-to-end or user-acceptance evidence at that actual
519: boundary. Mocking those relations into a unit test does not turn their
520: complexity into unit evidence (P6).
521: 
522: This frame does not waive the module-derived unit lane. It binds the lane
523: to module-owned law and the smallest congruent evidence population. Low
524: internal combinatorial complexity justifies a small lane, not omission and
525: not hundreds of implementation-shaped tests. Unit-test volume has no
526: independent closure value (P2).
527: 
528: No Product, user-outcome, installed-path, cross-module composition or
529: release claim may be closed from unit evidence, whatever the test count,
530: assertion count, source coverage, mutation score, runtime or historical
531: pass rate. Treating unit green as broader assurance is a frame error (P6,
532: EVALUATION §1).
533: 
534: ## 8. Combinatorial coverage and testing value
535: 
536: Testing value is indexed first by the material combinations a frame can
537: discriminate for its exact claim, not by test, assertion, file, line,
538: branch, mock, snapshot or runner count (P2, P6; provenance
539: #combinatorial-coverage-and-testing-value-index). For one claim, the
540: testing-value index considers at least:
541: 
542: 1. congruence between the claim and the evaluated subject;
543: 2. the number and materiality of independent claim dimensions;
544: 3. the interaction strength actually covered among those dimensions;
545: 4. the exactness of the authoritative path;
546: 5. oracle independence and precision;
547: 6. sensitivity to realistic faults, rival paths and historical failures;
548: 7. observability, reconstruction and reproducibility of the result; and
549: 8. explicit residual combinations and invalidation conditions.
550: 
551: No universal scalar is required. A project may define one only through
552: Product, requirement or accepted-design authority, and keeps the
553: underlying coverage coordinates rather than flattening them into a score
554: (P1, P6). A project-defined scalar is a quantified claim under
555: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Quantified assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#quantified-assurance)
556: and keeps its model and limits explicit (P6).
557: 
558: At unit altitude the relevant dimensions are module-bounded. Unit-testing
559: value normally rises with the internal combinatorial complexity of an
560: algebra, calculation, state machine, transition relation or other
561: module-owned closed domain, because local tests can cheaply discriminate
562: many meaningful combinations against a precise oracle (P2).
563: 
564: At integration, end-to-end and user-acceptance altitude, testing value can
565: be multiplicative rather than additive: each material interface composes
566: preconditions, postconditions, authority, state, configuration, failure and
567: recovery with every other traversed boundary. The value comes from the
568: interactions actually discriminated, not from touching many interfaces on
569: one sunny path (P4a, P2). Material Product factors commonly include:
570: 
571: - user role and capability;
572: - supported operation and Product composition;
573: - selected definition, owner, implementation and dependency;
574: - lifecycle and persisted state;
575: - configuration and version combination;
576: - process, continuation, retry, re-entry and recovery mode;
577: - success, refusal, malformed result, partial failure and competing-path
578:   case;
579: - fresh-process, replay, reconstruction and migration condition; and
580: - user-visible outcome and projection.
581: 
582: The activated frame declares the finite interaction population and why its
583: covering set is adequate. Pairwise or other covering-array reduction is
584: lawful only where the basis explains why the omitted higher-order
585: interactions cannot change the claim, or keeps them as residuals.
586: High-consequence authority, persistence, concurrency, recovery, migration
587: and historically failure-prone relations normally need explicit
588: higher-strength combinations (P5, P2; REFERENCE_FRAME §8, interaction and
589: failure coverage).
590: 
591: Source, line, branch and function coverage may diagnose whether code was
592: visited. They do not establish semantic combination coverage,
593: authoritative path selection, user-outcome coverage or the absence of a
594: rival path (P6, P1).
