596: ## 9. Legitimate path and technical-debt erasure
597: 
598: Every Product path claim needs two-sided evidence (P6, P3; provenance
599: #legitimate-path-and-technical-debt-erasure):
600: 
601: 1. required-path reachability: each required authoritative composition has
602:    an exact witness in the deployed, installed or otherwise runnable
603:    Product form through the supported ordinary path; and
604: 2. forbidden-path exclusion: each material superseded, duplicate,
605:    fallback, bypass or otherwise forbidden production path is absent,
606:    unreachable or refused at its declared boundary.
607: 
608: A successor passing does not prove the predecessor removed. Technical-debt
609: erasure evaluates two distinct, finite, subject-relative graphs (P3, P6):
610: 
611: 1. production closure: the exact deployed, installed or otherwise runnable
612:    Product form and configuration, with its transitive imports, exports,
613:    package paths, configuration switches, registries, fallbacks, consumers,
614:    generated runtime artifacts, recovery paths and fresh-process
615:    reconstruction. No obsolete, bypass, fallback or rival production path
616:    may remain reachable inside this graph for the claimed scope; and
617: 2. assurance/source closure: the source consumers, fixtures, proof
618:    scripts, generators, mutations and assurance tooling relied on for the
619:    claim. No obsolete assurance consumer may falsely supply closure
620:    evidence or reintroduce the removed production path into the Product
621:    graph.
622: 
623: A test-only seam is lawful when it is isolated from the Product
624: distribution, excluded from ordinary-path evidence and declared in the
625: assurance subject. Its presence outside the production graph is not a
626: production-path failure. A retained obsolete test or proof consumer stays
627: an assurance defect when it can falsely establish the claim or reintroduce
628: the removed path (P6).
629: 
630: Where proportionate and safe, assurance includes path-sensitive mutation or
631: sabotage (P5, P2):
632: 
633: - disabling the selected authoritative path prevents the Product scenario
634:   from succeeding;
635: - forcing or restoring a rival path causes refusal or a detected
636:   counterexample rather than silent success;
637: - corrupting a material interface or owner result is detected at the
638:   owning boundary; and
639: - removing an asserted obsolete path does not change the accepted Product
640:   outcome except through the declared deletion relation.
641: 
642: A Product outcome reached through a forbidden path is a falsified path
643: claim, not a passing Product test. A negative-path test that mutates the
644: exact subject without isolation, restoration and subject revalidation
645: invalidates its own assurance basis (P6, P3).
646: 
647: ## 10. Testing evidence composition
648: 
649: One execution may provide several bound results. A supported user scenario
650: may supply user-acceptance evidence for the outcome, end-to-end evidence for
651: the runnable causal path, integration evidence for selected seams and unit
652: counterexamples for a module-owned algebra. Those claims stay distinct and
653: combine only through the declared relations of REFERENCE_FRAME §6, whose
654: result conjunction is
655: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)
656: (P4a, P6;
657: provenance #testing-evidence-composition). Each bound result states which
658: predicate it establishes; a result over a necessary condition does not
659: establish the obligation, and the sufficiency of a conjunction is a claim
660: of its own ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation))
661: (P6).
662: 
663: The default proof responsibilities are (P6, P2):
664: 
665: - user acceptance proves the outcome from the user's supported frame;
666: - end to end proves the complete authoritative runnable Product path;
667: - integration proves material participant composition; and
668: - unit proves module-owned laws, with evidence size and strategy
669:   proportional to their internal combinatorial complexity.
670: 
671: User acceptance alone may leave internal path singularity unevaluated.
672: End-to-end success alone may leave unselected user populations or
673: combinations unevaluated. Integration and unit results cannot stand in for
674: either broader claim. When the Product claim requires all of them, a
675: conflict or a missing result stays visible to the decision owner's
676: disposition and cannot be hidden by aggregate green status (P5, P6;
677: FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results, Survival; REFERENCE_FRAME §8,
678: operational full coverage item 6).
679: 
680: ## 11. Assurance subject acquisition and evaluation
681: 
682: Acquiring the assurance subject and evaluating it are distinct relations
683: (P6, P1; provenance #assurance-subject-acquisition-and-evaluation). Where a
684: claim depends on owner-issued Product, runtime, lifecycle, admission,
685: replay or projection truth, the testing frame acquires that truth through
686: the exact runnable owner surface, validator, projection, receipt or
687: reconstruction relation. A harness, fixture, expected-value builder, proof
688: script, assurance evaluator or assessor does not reconstruct a parallel
689: owner state from raw payloads, events, logs, filenames, labels or
690: implementation fragments and then evaluate that self-authored state as if
691: it were the Product subject. Where the acquired observation cannot
692: separate two admissible subjects on which the assessed predicate takes
693: opposite truth values, the frame returns further evidence, a justified
694: narrower scope or `indeterminate`. The binding of the
695: observation itself needs support
696: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation),
697: Observation sufficiency) (P1, P6).
698: 
699: After lawful acquisition, an independently derived oracle may evaluate the
700: governing claim. Generic assurance mechanics may compute bytes, digests,
701: ordering, equality, set membership, completeness and conjunction over
702: owner-issued evidence. Those mechanics stay evidence evaluators: they
703: cannot mint owner carriers, choose the current history, select the
704: authoritative path, interpret domain lifecycle or admission meaning, or
705: become a runtime fallback (P6; EVALUATION §2).
706: 
707: The rule does not require an evaluator to trust the implementation under
708: test as its semantic oracle; the oracle derives from Product, requirement
709: and accepted-design law. It requires the assurance subject to be the actual
710: owner-issued subject rather than a second implementation of the owner's
711: runtime meaning. If the required owner projection or observable seam is
712: absent, the result keeps a named assurance or design gap; the proof harness
713: does not fill it with rival semantics (P6, P5).
714: 
715: ## 12. Counterexample localisation
716: 
717: A testing counterexample is returned to its earliest supported causal
718: frontier on the declared path. The frontier holds the causally minimal
719: violated owner relations or seam coordinates the evidence establishes;
720: earliest means minimal under the declared causal relation, not first in log
721: or clock order (P5, P6; provenance #counterexample-localization).
722: 
723: The localisation result represents exactly one of (P5, P1):
724: 
725: - one unique violated locus;
726: - a jointly established set of incomparable earliest violated loci whose
727:   combined violation is necessary to the supported causal explanation;
728: - unresolved alternative frontiers, when the evidence supports several
729:   possible causal explanations but cannot establish which occurred; or
730: - `indeterminate`, when the evidence cannot support a bounded frontier.
731: 
732: The four forms are a refinement of the core under the rule of
733: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), for the predicate "the
734: evidence establishes the counterexample's earliest violated loci on the
735: declared path". One unique violated locus and a jointly established set
736: map to `satisfied`. Unresolved alternative frontiers map to
737: `indeterminate`, naming the alternatives that further evidence must
738: decide between. The fourth form is the core value `indeterminate` itself,
739: naming the evidence a bounded frontier needs. The form travels with the
740: value as the domain outcome, so a joint set stays distinct from a unique
741: locus and unresolved alternatives stay distinct from an unbounded
742: frontier. Purpose and material relation: a localisation combines with
743: other results in the one core, and an unresolved causal explanation is
744: never read as an established one (P5, P1, P6).
745: 
746: Localisation records the subject, basis, frontier form and members, causal
747: evidence, expected relations, the observed counterexample and the
748: downstream claims it invalidates. It does not collapse a jointly
749: established set into one arbitrary owner, and it does not report
750: unresolved alternatives as a joint cause (P5, P4b).
751: 
752: A localised frontier does not itself authorise broader test expansion,
753: compatibility repair, another controller or a reinterpretation of unchanged
754: upstream meaning. A resulting scope or design change follows the existing
755: re-entry relation (SPEC_METHOD §4; P6).
756: 
757: ## 13. End-to-end interface integration frame
758: 
759: `urn:stdo:reference-frame:end-to-end-interface-integration:v1` is a
760: composite refinement whose identity resolves in
761: `urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation` (owned by
762: REFERENCE_FRAME) under the exact selected basis; its assurance law is
763: stated here. It relates the evaluation of public boundaries, design,
764: operators, owners and proof to the integration, end-to-end and
765: user-acceptance frames of §7. Like the set, it is available and is
766: activated only where the governing frame configuration or admitted work
767: authority selects it. It adds no fifth testing type, role or
768: universal activation gate (P2, P3; provenance
769: #derived-end-to-end-interface-integration-frame).
770: 
771: | Frame element | End-to-end interface integration |
772: |---|---|
773: | evaluation family | Does one outcome stay constructable, understandable and correctly realised across its material interface chain, with sufficient participant context and conserved meaning, authority and cause? |
774: | subject and basis | one Product outcome and an independently stated oracle; the governing requirements and design basis, exact source or workspace checkpoint, contracts and finite case population; for design claims, the declared participant roles, functional path, dependencies, configuration and capabilities; for claims over their realisation, the actual participants, callable selection, supported entry and exit, and the exact runnable artifact or install |
775: | material manifold | the producers, consumers, transformations and effect owners, as declared for design claims or actually selected for realised claims; at each material seam, the functional preconditions and postconditions, value and reference domains, lifecycle and time, supplied context, mutable subject, refusals, observations and user-visible result |
776: | coordinates and equality | distinct Product, artifact or install, workspace, observation, invocation, candidate, admitted result and evidence identities; exact revisions, domain, units, cardinality, ordering, empty, null or default meaning and validity interval; equal shape or output implies no equal meaning, provenance or authority |
777: | governing invariants | the selected Product, requirement, design and interface law; REFERENCE_FRAME declaration and translation law; the conjunction of results of FOUNDATIONS §4; the claim boundaries and obligations below; the existing testing and assurance owners keep their laws |
778: | authority | existing owners keep semantic, operation, admission and reserved decision authority; the activation grants bounded evaluation, with construction only under its existing exact operation grant; the declared decision consumer disposes the closed result |
779: | evidence | source-linked contracts and both selected sides; for design claims, design relations and explicitly unresolved realisation facts; for claims over realised relations, the actual supplied request, context and response, callable and configuration identity, owner validation, effect and observation records and the ordinary caller's outcome; independently derived expected relations and disclosed substitution limits |
780: | capability envelope | competence in the outcome, functional composition, domain and lifecycle semantics, participant capabilities and causal diagnosis; sufficient access to the exact subject and evidence without altering a reviewed subject; required independence stays claim-relative |
781: | exclusions | hidden context or privilege, rival contract truth, inferred authority, undeclared substitutes, private or test-only paths for ordinary-path claims, candidate output treated as admission, fixture success treated as real user evidence, and unsupported whole-Product or all-future-case conclusions |
782: | result and relations | each activated claim returns a core result with its exact evidence, coverage, causal findings and residuals; shared evidence is referenced once; mandatory claims compose only through a declared same-basis or lawful-translation conjunction (FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results) to the named decision consumer |
783: | invalidation | a material change of contract, domain, participant, prompt or context, capability, callable path, configuration, translation, relevant workspace observation, lifecycle, oracle or evidence population invalidates the affected conclusions; unchanged valid evidence and owner rulings stay reusable |
784: | qualification | the representative sensitivity and refusal cases below, bound to actual subjects, actor envelopes and independently stated expected relations; mechanical source checks supply no semantic or live-user qualification |
785: 
786: ### Claim boundaries
787: 
788: (P6, P1; provenance #interface-integration-claim-boundaries)
789: 
790: | Claim | Evaluation and evidence boundary |
791: |---|---|
792: | contract sufficiency | Can each participant determine and perform its responsibility from the declared interface and the available context? Source-grounded design evaluation may establish this claim without an implemented runtime; unresolved realisability or actor-context questions stay explicit. |
793: | boundary congruence | Do the actual selected producers, transformations and consumers preserve the declared domains, meanings, lifecycle and authority? An actual-composition claim acquires both sides and their exchanges; design correspondence alone proves no implementation behaviour. |
794: | path realisation | Does the exact runnable subject use the authoritative entry-to-outcome path through its material state, effect and observation boundaries? Matching output through another path is insufficient. |
795: | user usability | Can the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtain the selected outcome using only its declared context, access and supported surface? Internal success or validator-aware fixtures cannot establish this claim. |
796: 
797: The activation selects claims from the work's applicability (ACTIVATION §1)
798: and states the scope reason for each unselected claim; an unselected claim
799: has no result. Design-only work
800: does not require unavailable runtime evidence and does not report runtime or
801: UAT satisfaction. An unknown material condition keeps its dependent claim
802: unresolved: the claim's result is never `satisfied` and names the
803: condition as what would decide it
804: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing); omission
805: cannot close it. A full end-to-end usability claim
806: needs all four distinct results and their explicit conjunction
807: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),
808: in which an unselected claim is uncovered coverage. Transport,
809: parse, admission, semantic satisfaction, operation completion and user
810: success are not interchangeable (P5, P6).
811: 
812: ### Obligations
813: 
814: Existing truth surfaces are reused. The working record adds only missing
815: cross-interface relations; schemas, prompts, adapters, indexes and tests do
816: not become another contract owner (P6, P2; provenance
817: #interface-integration-obligations). For each material seam:
818: 
819: 1. Bind the functional input domain, producer success postconditions,
820:    consumer preconditions, permitted effects, refusals and observable exit.
821:    Direct successful handoff requires the producer's guarantees to meet the
822:    consumer's preconditions. An interface may instead emit candidates:
823:    candidate output, later admission and semantic assessment stay distinct
824:    declared stages. A normal model refusal or an inadmissible candidate does
825:    not by itself falsify an adequately declared candidate interface; the
826:    exact promised outcome and refusal behaviour are evaluated (P4a, P5).
827: 2. Make material actor obligations and domains available through the
828:    actual interface or context, or through an exact locator the actor can
829:    lawfully resolve. Bind the LLM role, instructions, supplied context,
830:    tools and model or transport configuration where material. Generic
831:    governance access does not replace the Product-specific contract or
832:    authorise inference of hidden validator rules. Existing deterministic
833:    owners compute the available facts and expose their owned relation to
834:    context and validation by reuse or a proven equivalent projection.
835:    Semantic actors judge meaning within that domain; reserved owner
836:    rulings, eligibility, authority and admission are not inferred from an
837:    actor response or a frame label (P0, P6, P1).
838: 3. Preserve domain and temporal meaning through serialisation, parsing,
839:    normalisation and adaptation. A lawful translation binds source and
840:    target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance,
841:    governing owner and refusal conditions. Distinguish proposed, admitted,
842:    assessed and completed states; active input from historical context;
843:    current validity from mere byte availability. Equal wire shape is no
844:    translation proof (P1, P3; REFERENCE_FRAME §6).
845: 4. Observe the relevant current mutable workspace for each later
846:    operation, and bind that observation separately from immutable
847:    authority, artifacts, history and prior candidates. Changed support
848:    invalidates dependent conclusions; unaffected accepted work stays
849:    reusable. A snapshot does not replace the current subject, and a change
850:    of actor alone is no reason to repeat still-valid work (P3, P4b;
851:    ACTIVATION §7).
852: 5. Follow the actual callable path and the existing effect owners through
853:    the selected exit and any required fresh observation. A hidden fallback,
854:    state injection, manually repaired output, private entry or undeclared
855:    retry cannot support an ordinary real-path claim. A pure function
856:    acquires no new event lifecycle because this frame evaluates it (P6,
857:    P3).
858: 6. Preserve diagnostic cause through wrappers and projections. Apply §12:
859:    report the supported causal frontier, not merely the first log or clock
860:    occurrence. Keep the originating seam, bounded field or path, expected
861:    domain or basis, observed mismatch and evidence locator where available,
862:    with downstream symptoms, successful work and the declared continuation
863:    or block. Preserve joint causes, alternative frontiers and
864:    indeterminacy; do not invent a unique cause. Product redaction rules
865:    still govern sensitive content. Missing required diagnostic evidence
866:    stays a named gap. Return the smallest supported owner or re-entry;
867:    diagnosis grants no repair or retry (P5, P4b, P6).
868: 
869: Evidence acquisition follows §11: owner facts are acquired through existing
870: surfaces and evaluated with an independent contract-derived oracle.
871: Computed facts, contextual judgments and reserved owner rulings keep their
872: distinct owners and validity scopes (P6).
873: 
874: For an LLM-interface usability claim, clean-room LLM UAT is used, with the
875: ordinary supplied context and permitted tools and without private
876: implementation knowledge or fixture assistance. Expected outcomes are
877: recorded before responses are inspected. The sunny case and the ordinary
878: ambiguity and negative cases material to the claim are included.
879: Substitutes are disclosed; replayed or fabricated responses prove only
880: their stated narrower relation, not live-provider usability. Responses are
881: not edited, and nothing is silently retried until green. Live claims need
882: live evidence under §2, not a new universal live-provider requirement
883: during design (P6, P5; EVALUATION §3, expectations before exposure).
884: 
885: An early sunny thread can establish bounded evidence while the unexercised
886: claims stay open (the sequencing heuristic of SPEC_METHOD §8). This frame
887: adds no exhaustive-hardening prerequisite, scenario quota, controller,
888: runtime, generator, routine human approval, new ledger or automatic extra
889: agent. Existing authority selects proportionate assurance and any further
890: operation. The result returns, for each of the four claims, its core
891: result or the scope reason it was not selected, the exact
892: exercised subject and path, the supported mismatch, retained work,
893: substitutions, residuals and invalidators in the existing work carrier; it
894: is neither acceptance nor a grant of the next action (P2, P6; ACTIVATION
895: §6).
896: 
897: ### Computational whole-path evaluation
898: 
899: For material computational composition or recurrence work, the selected
900: interface claims are composed with evaluations of the path's operators,
901: owners, reused foundations and proof, to evaluate one complete
902: producer-to-consumer path under the design profile's computational
903: realisation and recurrence law (DESIGN_MODULE). The evaluation binds fact
904: establishment, each consumer, validity and invalidation, effects, retained
905: alternatives and accumulated work. It evaluates equivalent computation
906: across different domain names without assuming semantic equivalence.
907: Qualification challenges the design's declared workload and operational
908: assumptions, and preserves the independent scope, freshness and effect
909: checks that serve distinct supported obligations (P4a, P1, P2; provenance
910: #computational-whole-path-evaluation).
911: 
912: An identifiable complete-path result and its evidence return to the
913: declared decision consumer; a collection of local successes cannot replace
914: that result. Design-only evidence establishes only the design claim; claims
915: about actual work need observations on the selected path. Valid unchanged
916: results are reused, and affected reassessment is activated on a material
917: change of path, basis or workload. This is a bounded composition of
918: existing frames, not a permanent actor, an extra frame family, a per-helper
919: review or a separate accounting ledger (P4b, P2).
920: 
921: ### Qualification
922: 
923: These are representative source-contract discriminators: not an executed
924: trial, a universal test quota or whole-Product qualification. Each selected
925: case binds its own exact subject, oracle, evidence and claim scope (P6,
926: P5; provenance #interface-integration-qualification; EVALUATION §7).
927: 
928: | Case | Required discrimination |
929: |---|---|
930: | empty and non-empty eligible domains | Ordinary context makes both domains usable; a universal empty-value workaround cannot replace the governing domain. A hidden required rule defeats contract sufficiency even when the validator correctly refuses. |
931: | adequate candidate contract and rejected response | Legitimate refusal or admission filtering is told apart from an inadequate interface or a violated success guarantee; model variability alone is no frame failure. |
932: | same-response or historical-only reference | Eligibility and lifecycle come from the owning domain; available or equal-looking references are not automatically current admissible inputs. |
933: | individually valid but temporally mismatched carriers | Different observations or admission states can falsify boundary congruence despite matching shapes. |
934: | meaning-changing translation | Loss of units, default, identity or ordering is detected against the independent outcome oracle, even when both shapes validate. |
935: | fixture knows a hidden rule | Mechanical success leaves user usability unproved; it cannot hide missing ordinary actor context. |
936: | expected output through a forbidden path | Path realisation is falsified; equal output does not discharge the actual-path obligation. |
937: | changed workspace and reusable accepted work | Affected context and dependent evidence are refreshed while unaffected valid work is kept; history does not stand in for the current subject. |
938: | wrapped or ambiguous failure | The supported originating causal frontier and its uncertainty are kept, not replaced by a downstream symptom or an invented unique cause. |
939: | design-only sufficient contract | A bounded contract result can close while runtime and user claims stay unclaimed or unresolved according to their applicability; no runtime or UAT satisfaction is inferred. |
940: 
941: ## 14. Design-to-module evidence route
942: 
943: For a new or materially changed realisation boundary governed by a design
944: profile (DESIGN_MODULE, tier 3, whose binding of the objects named here is
945: declared in that profile), the canonical evidence relation is (P6, P4b;
946: provenance rc.2
947: DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD #6a-design-to-module-to-implementation-unit-tests-evidence-route):
948: 
949: ```text
950: constitutional WHAT and owning requirements
951:   -> accepted ontology, the carrier inventory the design declares,
952:      target design, and the design's domain, sequence and state evidence
953:   -> implementation and module-derived unit tests
954:   -> reconciliation and acceptance
955:   -> promotion and design-method closure
956: 
957: implementation and module-derived unit tests
958:   -> evidence, counterexample or falsification input
959:   -> affected ontology or design relation
960: ```
961: 
962: The first chain is semantic derivation. The second is evidence feedback
963: and cannot select or accept the affected semantic answer (P6). The two
964: chains are this member's instance of parallel derivation: expected results
965: carry assertion provenance from the first chain and executions carry
966: execution provenance from the second; agreement between them is
967: compatible with a shared error, and disagreement requires diagnosis
968: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance))
969: (P6, P1). When the
970: design's co-evolution condition holds, the two chains may proceed together
971: without making implementation semantic authority; design still owns the
972: structural HOW. Where the design is not decision-complete, the relation is
973: design-gated at the smallest causally closed affected decision set and
974: retained implementation follows its acceptance. An unchanged
975: `realization_refactor` (SPEC_METHOD §4 Change classes) cites the accepted
976: relation and proves no material semantic-boundary delta; it does not
977: recreate the evidence (P2, P6).
978: 
979: Where construction is probabilistic or agentic, the execution relation of
980: ACTIVATION §1 governs the handoff from this accepted design basis into
981: bounded construction, assessment, disposition, checkpoint and
982: continuation. The design profile supplies the governing-frame,
983: transformation-admission, invariant-reconstruction,
984: computational-realisation and module evidence that relation consumes; it
985: does not define a second execution protocol (P0, P6).
986: 
987: Completeness requires (P6, P4b):
988: 
989: - the final implementation is traceable to the accepted ontology;
990: - the final implementation is traceable to design and module boundary
991:   assets;
992: - unit tests are traceable to module ownership, not only to helper
993:   layout;
994: - implementation-first discoveries are reconciled into the ontology and
995:   the design's domain, sequence and state evidence before promotion or
996:   closure; and
997: - implementation may not compensate for an unrealised declared
998:   constructor by introducing a hidden controller or alternative authority
999:   path.
1000: 
1001: Unit tests may be discovered from implementation behaviour, but the
1002: closure proof is re-expressed against module ownership rather than code
1003: helper shape. The module boundary is the intermediate reasoning surface
1004: that lets implementation and unit tests be audited against the same
1005: ownership cut; it does not outrank constitutional truth or ratified design
1006: (P6).
1007: 
1008: The minimum complete evidence chain is (P6, P4b):
1009: 
1010: 1. constitutional WHAT;
1011: 2. accepted ontology;
1012: 3. target design;
1013: 4. target module boundary assets and the ontology-derived carrier
1014:    inventory;
1015: 5. accepted domain, sequence and state projections with axiom evaluation;
1016: 6. implementation; and
1017: 7. unit tests derived from the same ontology and module boundary.
1018: 
1019: Where a reference realisation exists, the complete evidence chain becomes
1020: (P6, P4b):
1021: 
1022: 1. constitutional WHAT;
1023: 2. reference design;
1024: 3. accepted target ontology and reference-to-ontology mapping;
1025: 4. target design mapping;
1026: 5. target module boundary assets and the ontology-derived carrier
1027:    inventory;
1028: 6. accepted domain, sequence and state projections with axiom evaluation;
1029:    and
1030: 7. implementation and unit tests derived from the same ontology.
1031: 
1032: If a change jumps from design or code straight to tests and never
1033: reconstructs the module boundary, the proof surface is too weak (P6).
1034: 
1035: ## 15. Module-derived unit tests
1036: 
1037: Within the product-assurance bounded context of §2, the two authority
1038: sources stay distinct: the module-derived unit test and its proof relation
1039: derive from realisation authority, which the design profile owns
1040: (DESIGN_MODULE), and this section states that relation so both sources sit
1041: in one member; that ownership does not extend to Product-level UAT or
1042: acceptance meaning, which stays with Product authority under §2 (P6;
1043: provenance rc.2 DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD #6b-module-derived-unit-test-rule).
1044: 
1045: Unit tests under the design profile are module-owned proof lanes. They
1046: derive from module ownership evidence, not from code shape alone. A unit
1047: test should be traceable to (P6, P2):
1048: 
1049: - the accepted ontology and the applicable entity, lifecycle, authority,
1050:   function, effect or projection law;
1051: - the governing module design;
1052: - the active carrier inventory the design declares, or an equivalent
1053:   carrier inventory;
1054: - the module-bounded domain, sequence and state projections; and
1055: - the requirement families the module owns.
1056: 
1057: Unit tests are not authored primarily from helper function boundaries,
1058: private method layout, incidental branch structure, temporary
1059: implementation decomposition, or mock convenience that hides the real
1060: module contract. The required question is not "what functions exist to
1061: test?" but "what does this module own, and what proof does that ownership
1062: require?" This does not prohibit helper-level tests; it prohibits
1063: helper-level tests from becoming the canonical proof surface for a module
1064: boundary (P6, P1).
1065: 
1066: Canonical rule (P6): module-owned unit tests are authoritative for module
1067: proof; broader integration, scenario and sandbox lanes remain downstream
1068: proof families; transitional slice-gating tests may exist, but they do not
1069: replace module-derived unit proof. If a module has code but no
1070: module-derived unit test lane, the module is not closure-ready under the
1071: design profile. What such a lane claims, and what it never closes, is
1072: the unit frame of §7.
1073: 
1074: ## 16. Module lifecycle confirmation
1075: 
1076: Every designed module, function, application surface, runtime surface,
1077: plugin surface, public interface, data surface, and published function or
1078: module of a profile exists inside an operational lifecycle. Under the
1079: design profile that lifecycle signal is confirmed at the realisation
1080: boundary before design-method closure (P2, P6; provenance rc.2
1081: DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD #6c-module-lifecycle-confirmation-rule). The
1082: canonical operational lifecycle chain is SPEC_METHOD §2 Operational
1083: lifecycle sufficiency; this section consumes that chain and does not
1084: redefine its phases. The checklist is not a release plan and does not
1085: replace RELEASE; it is an ambiguity detector for ultimate intended use.
1086: 
1087: For each governed boundary, the design evidence states, or points to a
1088: surface that states (P6, P5):
1089: 
1090: - the upstream intent and requirement authority;
1091: - the build or realisation surface;
1092: - the assurance and proof surface;
1093: - the release or packaging posture;
1094: - the deployment or install posture;
1095: - the live usage or invocation posture;
1096: - the observed telemetry, projection or monitoring posture;
1097: - the retirement, revocation, supersession or decommission posture; and
1098: - the owner, source truth and authority boundary for the lifecycle
1099:   decisions.
1100: 
1101: Each lifecycle phase takes one of the three answers that
1102: [SPEC_METHOD §2 Operational lifecycle sufficiency](SPEC_METHOD.md#operational-lifecycle-sufficiency)
1103: owns, applied here to design evidence: answered by the active design,
1104: requirement, release, deployment or telemetry surface; declared not
1105: applicable with a reason; or recorded as a named `Gap:` or `Unanswered:`
1106: item, which in design evidence also names its owning follow-up. A phase
1107: list without answers, not-applicable reasons or named gaps is not
1108: design-method evidence (P5, P6). The three are declared states of the
1109: design evidence for a phase under that section, not result values; a
1110: named gap is a residual
1111: ([FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology)) that remains until its
1112: owning follow-up disposes it (P4b, P5).
1113: 
1114: Implementation proves the selected lifecycle path only within the
1115: authority it owns. Code, tests, generated artifacts or runtime fixtures may
1116: confirm that a lifecycle claim is real, but they may not invent lifecycle
1117: authority that the product, requirements, design, release or operational
1118: surface did not declare (P6). If the checklist exposes missing release,
1119: deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement truth, the module may still
1120: proceed only when that gap is explicitly governed; it may not close by
1121: relying on local convention, implementation precedent, mutable runtime
1122: state, prompt prose or test-only fixture behaviour (P6, P5).

METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md member_sha256=56d0c1ad9889ad8d09b1d1249ad4bae1fb1717af22d01bdf4190b2d0bf71500a lines=540-629
540: ### AC-007 Constraint and refusal
541: 
542: Each constraint names its governed subject, predicate, judgment kind,
543: latitude and refusal (§3, Constraint). The judgment of a constraint
544: returns one value of the core result algebra of
545: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), directly or through a
546: refinement that the owning signature declares and that maps each of its
547: values to exactly one core value. Under the no-coercion rule of
548: FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
549: invalid-basis result of a constraint follows that algebra and is never
550: coerced to satisfied (P5, P6; rc.2 #ac-007-constraint-and-refusal). The
551: core values, the rule that no mapping raises a result's standing and the
552: boundary among out_of_frame, indeterminate and an evaluation that was not
553: performed are FOUNDATIONS §4 Results'. This law applies them to the
554: judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this
555: member, and adds no core value.
556: 
557: Constraint results. The outcomes of a constraint's judgment map for the
558: predicate "the constraint's predicate holds for its governed subject on
559: the exact basis" (P5, P6):
560: 
561: | Outcome | Core value | Ground |
562: |---|---|---|
563: | holds | satisfied | the judgment establishes the predicate on the exact basis |
564: | failed | falsified | a counterexample defeats the predicate; the judgment names it |
565: | indeterminate | indeterminate | the admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate; the judgment names the evidence that would decide |
566: | out of scope | out_of_frame | the predicate is asked of a subject or relation outside the constraint's declared `applies_to`, context or scope, so deciding it needs a relation the constraint does not declare; the judgment names that relation, with its owner where the subject gives one |
567: | invalid basis | invalid_basis | the subject or basis cannot support the judgment; the judgment names the basis repair |
568: 
569: A missing result is no value of this refinement: a judgment that was not
570: performed has no closed result, is never `indeterminate`, and enters every
571: conjunction over it as a planned assessment without a closed result
572: (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed).
573: 
574: Operation outcomes. A closure (AC-010), a projection (AC-011), the
575: structural admission of a record, model or carrier, the application of a
576: transformation (AC-013) and an interpretation (§6) each end in their
577: declared result or in one of the stops `hold`, `gap` and `refusal` that
578: this member writes. Where this member says that a condition refuses, the
579: operation returns `refusal` naming the condition; the record, model or
580: carrier is not admitted, and nothing is dropped silently. Each outcome
581: maps for the predicate "the operation yields its declared result on the
582: exact basis" (P5, P6):
583: 
584: | Outcome | Core value | Ground |
585: |---|---|---|
586: | declared result | satisfied | the closure, the projection with its boundary, the admission, the proposed successor `M_b_prime*` or the proposed model `M_subject*` is returned on the exact basis; a proposed successor or model establishes that it is available, never its acceptance or admission (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results) |
587: | `hold` | indeterminate | the operation was applied and stops because evidence, an observation or a disposition it needs is not yet admitted, so the admissible evidence cannot decide whether it yields its result; its residual names what would decide |
588: | `gap` | invalid_basis | the result needs a member, reference, resolution or declaration whose resolution on the basis is still open: the declared relation that resolves it has not yet decided it, as for an external resolution not yet evaluated; the result is undefined on this basis until it is supplied. A reference evaluated to no target is dangling and refuses (AC-003): a local reference with no record in the model's closed population, and an external reference whose declared resolution has been evaluated and yields no target |
589: | `refusal(constraint)` | falsified | every refusal that is not `refusal(basis)`: the refusal names a demonstrated violation of a declared law of this member or a constraint of its signature by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment, including a missing record family (AC-001), a dangling reference (AC-003) and an application without its traversal (AC-015), or it names no condition of the basis; the violation or other defect it names is the counterexample |
590: | `refusal(basis)` | invalid_basis | the refusal names one or more conditions of the basis the operation acts on and no demonstrated violation of a declared law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment: a seed set, relation family, required-edge semantics, basis or scope that is not exact; a fixed point that is not finite and unique; an input model, subject or carrier whose exact identity, basis or admission is not established; or mixed bases with no composite-basis relation (AC-006) |
591: 
592: The cause is part of a refusal's value, because a refusal would otherwise
593: map to falsified or to invalid_basis according to its cause, and a refined
594: value maps to exactly one core value (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
595: Refinements). A refusal that names a demonstrated violation of a declared
596: law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or
597: application under judgment is `refusal(constraint)`, whatever condition of
598: the basis it also names. The basis condition is recorded with the refusal
599: and reported beside it as its own `invalid_basis` result, which names the
600: basis repair and answers the predicate of the evaluation that the
601: condition leaves without a supporting basis, never the operation-outcome
602: predicate that the refusal answers
603: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
604: Predicates travel). A refusal that names only conditions of the basis is
605: `refusal(basis)`. A violation inside an input that the operation acts on
606: as its basis is a condition of the basis for that operation, not a
607: violation by what it judges, as the projection below shows. Purpose and
608: material relation: a demonstrated violation is a known failure, which
609: survives every join only as a `falsified` result, so a basis condition
610: named beside it neither hides the failure nor discards its counterexample,
611: and the basis repair stays named (FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results,
612: Survival; P5, P6). A basis mismatch inside a model or a record, a
613: relation's qualifier record included, is mixed bases with no
614: composite-basis relation (AC-006): a coordinate of the model or record
615: binds, or a reference in it resolves on, a basis that the governing basis
616: relation does not admit, as a wrong-basis reference of AC-003 does. It is
617: a condition of the basis, in the structural admission that judges that
618: model or record as in every other operation, and never a violated
619: constraint of a signature, even where the signature declares the basis
620: relation; a refusal that names only such a mismatch is `refusal(basis)`.
621: One defect can bear on two predicates: a model that violates AC-001 is
622: `refusal(constraint)` in the structural admission that judges it and
623: `refusal(basis)` in a projection over it, and each outcome answers its own
624: predicate. An operation that was not applied has no outcome. A stop `gap`
625: is a closed result with the value invalid_basis; it is not the absence of
626: a result that
627: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)
628: records as a gap. A signature's stop contract and a traversal record map
629: stops of their own under §5.


METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md member_sha256=56d0c1ad9889ad8d09b1d1249ad4bae1fb1717af22d01bdf4190b2d0bf71500a lines=921-1039
921: ## 5. Traversals and functor kinds
922: 
923: A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6; rc.2
924: #traversals-and-functor-kinds):
925: 
926: ```text
927: v = {
928:   id,
929:   domain,
930:   codomain,
931:   context,
932:   owner,
933:   scope,
934:   basis,
935:   preconditions,
936:   postconditions,
937:   authority,
938:   evidence,
939:   provenance,
940:   stop_states
941: }
942: ```
943: 
944: The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
945: owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
946: equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
947: binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).
948: 
949: `a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):
950: 
951: ```text
952: F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
953: F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
954: F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
955: ```
956: 
957: Application notation is:
958: 
959: ```text
960: F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
961: ```
962: 
963: where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
964: `X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
965: its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
966: algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
967: core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
968: never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
969: `refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
970: value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
971: further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
972: stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
973: mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
974: may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
975: that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
976: `stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
977: to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
978: from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
979: `refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
980: different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
981: that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
982: one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
983: result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
984: traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
985: and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
986: constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.
987: 
988: - `F_D` classifies deterministic evaluation or proof over declared
989:   properties. It returns a judgment and does not perform the domain
990:   construction being judged (P6).
991: - `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
992:   proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
993:   admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
994:   or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
995: - `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
996:   authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
997:   grants no ambient authority (P6).
998: 
999: The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
1000: different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
1001: other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
1002: Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
1003: semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).
1004: 
1005: "Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
1006: not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
1007: categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
1008: [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
1009: every categorical claim (P6, P1).
1010: 
1011: ### AC-015 Functor classification
1012: 
1013: Every functor application binds exactly one functor kind and one traversal
1014: identity. Applying any `F_*` kind without the bracketed traversal identity
1015: `[v]` is incomplete (P3; rc.2 #ac-015-functor-classification). Such an
1016: application violates this law, and its outcome is `refusal(constraint)`
1017: under AC-007; this sense of incomplete is not the construction-availability
1018: value `incomplete` of a step
1019: ([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability)). Purpose and
1020: material relation: an application without its traversal has one core
1021: value, and the shared word does not let it be read as a step's stop (P5).
1022: 
1023: ### AC-016 Typed composition
1024: 
1025: Two traversals compose only when the first result type and judgment
1026: satisfy the second traversal's exact domain and preconditions (P4a; rc.2
1027: #ac-016-typed-composition):
1028: 
1029: ```text
1030: F_K2[w] compose F_K1[v]
1031: ```
1032: 
1033: Composition retains both traversal identities, intermediate results,
1034: judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states. It cannot
1035: flatten probabilistic proposal, deterministic evaluation and human
1036: decision into one undifferentiated operation. `a_c` prescribes no
1037: universal `F_P -> F_D -> F_H` sequence; each application owns its lawful
1038: topology (P4a, P4b, P6). FOUNDATIONS §3 P4a consumes this law.
1039:

1281: ### Application boundary
1282: 
1283: This member defines the generic relations `a_c.X` and `a_c.X.C`. It
1284: selects, constructs, accepts or releases no concrete interpretation or
1285: carrier. A downstream authority owns its exact subject population,
1286: interpretation, carrier, judgments and Product or release status. The
1287: downstream identity is never embedded back into the calculus or its
1288: publication basis (P2, P6; rc.2 #application-boundary).
1289: 
1290: ### External imports and specialisations
1291: 
1292: An application may declare a typed import, translation or specialisation
1293: of an `a_c` concept under that application's own exact authority, context,
1294: basis, scope, preservation, loss, refusal and invalidation law. Such a
1295: relation is external to the calculus. It neither changes `a_c` nor enters
1296: this member by being useful to an application (P6, P2; rc.2
1297: #external-imports-and-specializations). PROFILES §1 states the same
1298: rule from the profile's side as the declared-binding rule.
1299: 
1300: ### Constraint surfaces
1301: 
1302: A constraint surface states, for a declared subject and work boundary,
1303: the obligations and the permitted freedom of the work: its objects and
1304: their meanings, the predicates and dependencies that bear on it, the
1305: admissible operations, the required results, the authority, the evidence
1306: and the conditions still unresolved. It constrains the work without
1307: prescribing the worker's internal solution strategy beyond those
1308: obligations (P2, P6).
1309: 
1310: An interpretation of a subject in `a_c` (§6) yields the constraint surface
1311: of a task by projection. The task's declared subject and work boundary
1312: are the seed set `Z`, with the dependency relation family `R` the task
1313: declares, and the surface is `project(M_subject, Z, R)` (AC-011) over the
1314: material closure of AC-010. Its parts come from the records of this
1315: member:
1316: 
1317: | Part of the surface | Records and laws that supply it |
1318: |---|---|
1319: | objects and meanings | the semantic objects of `M_Z` (§3), with identity under AC-002 and provenance under AC-017 |
1320: | predicates and dependencies | the constraints (§3, AC-007) and typed relations (AC-004) in the closure; a premise shared by several constraints is one record, and the closure imposes no tree shape and no execution order |
1321: | admissible operations | the traversals and transformations in the closure (§5, AC-013), each with its preconditions and operation authority |
1322: | required results | each constraint's judgment kind and its outcomes, mapped to the core values of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) under AC-007 |
1323: | permitted freedom | the latitude records (AC-008); what no obligation fixes and a latitude admits is the worker's choice |
1324: | authority | the authority each record retains (AC-005); the surface grants none |
1325: | evidence | the judgments (AC-014) and the evidence, provenance and basis coordinates of the records (AC-006) |
1326: | unresolved conditions | the residuals in the closure (AC-009) and the seams recorded in `Boundary_Z` (AC-011) |
1327: 
1328: Conditions on its use:
1329: 
1330: 1. **Standing kept.** Each element keeps the standing the interpretation
1331:    records for it: premise, derived consequence, policy choice,
1332:    observation or unresolved claim. A policy choice keeps its owner, and a
1333:    preference is never read as an obligation. An element of the
1334:    construction or assurance relations also keeps the kind of support
1335:    the interpretation records for it, one of the five that
1336:    [FOUNDATIONS §4 Formal representation](FOUNDATIONS.md#formal-representation)
1337:    distinguishes: a stated formula is not read as discharged, and an
1338:    externally assessed predicate keeps the source, scope and evidence
1339:    that establish it.
1340: 2. **Unresolved blocks.** A residual, a `hold`, a `gap` or an external
1341:    predicate not yet established keeps its source and its required
1342:    acquisition, and it blocks every operation and result that depends on
1343:    it until its premise is established. A missing premise or an omitted
1344:    obligation never becomes permission or a satisfied result (AC-007,
1345:    AC-009).
1346: 3. **Routes, not observations.** The surface carries the constraints and
1347:    the acquisition routes of the material inputs the task needs. It
1348:    supplies no observation, effect grant or task context: a step acquires
1349:    those from the workspace and its selected authoritative inputs, at the
1350:    acquisition step of
1351:    [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
1352:    which is where a step uses a surface. The workspace stays the basis for
1353:    reacquisition.
1354: 4. **Exact subject and basis.** The surface binds the exact subject the
1355:    interpretation represents and, as a separate coordinate, the calculus
1356:    basis and signature used to represent it. A projection from an
1357:    interpretation bound to other subject bytes, or whose basis is not
1358:    established, returns `refusal(basis)`, which is `invalid_basis` (AC-006,
1359:    AC-011).
1360: 5. **A derived view.** The surface is a derived view of the owning prose,
1361:    not a second owner. A surface that changes the permitted or required
1362:    work is a fidelity defect (AC-017), repaired at the source or the
1363:    derivation that caused it. An approximate surface declares its
1364:    adequacy relation and its end-to-end bound.
1365: 6. **Separate claims.** Structural validity of a surface is a structural
1366:    claim that a checker may decide (AC-019); its fidelity is a semantic
1367:    judgment ([EVALUATION §2](EVALUATION.md#2-separation), AC-018); its
1368:    sufficiency for a task is shown only by actual use
1369:    ([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification)). A mechanical
1370:    projection runs only under a separately selected checking contract.
1371:    None of these claims grants operation or acceptance authority.
1372: 
1373: This section states how any interpretation yields a surface; under the
1374: Application boundary above it selects, constructs and accepts no
1375: interpretation. The downstream authority of a subject owns its
1376: interpretation and which interpretation is current. Ordinary entry
1377: selects the current exact interpretation with its limits, and an earlier
1378: interpretation is identified as historical. Purpose and material
1379: relation: an actor has to recover the constraints of one task within
1380: finite context and attention (P0, P2); the surface carries them from
1381: their owners with their dependencies, freedom and open conditions, so
1382: the actor neither loads the whole model nor loses an uncertainty (P4b,
1383: P5, P6). This is new law.


METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md member_sha256=9e2642d51d0b024a448fe7910dcb323fb3f3bb2a003ad33c27c39a5dda625220 lines=501-673
501: ### Proportional design sequencing
502: 
503: For one governed boundary `B`, let `M(B)` be its complete material-relation
504: set (decision-complete symbolic design, below) and `U(B)` the unresolved
505: members of that set (P2, P0; rc.2 #proportional-design-sequencing):
506: 
507: ```text
508: U(B) = unresolved(M(B))
509: decision_complete(B) iff
510:   U(B) = empty
511:   and M(B) is jointly satisfiable
512:   and every network admitted by M(B) is semantically equivalent under the
513:       governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations
514: co_evolution_admissible(B) iff decision_complete(B)
515: design_gate(B) =
516:   the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish
517:   decision_complete(B)
518: ```
519: 
520: Design sequencing follows `decision_complete(B)`, not one global authoring
521: order (P2, P6). Co-evolution is lawful only when `decision_complete(B)` holds:
522: design still owns the structural HOW, but design, implementation and tests
523: may evolve together and reconcile before promotion or closure.
524: Design-gated sequencing is required when implementation would otherwise
525: establish an unresolved or contradictory relation, or choose between
526: materially non-equivalent networks, with durable consequences for future
527: change: the affected design decision is accepted before retained
528: implementation establishes it. A disposable spike may supply evidence
529: without becoming the selected design.
530: 
531: Neither mode is the global default; the same proportionality relation
532: selects between them. Proportionality decides which relations are material
533: and bounds the smallest affected gate; decision completeness is the
534: resulting admissibility test (ACTIVATION §6). Where a bounded symbolic
535: model can contract the material semantic alternatives within effective
536: reasoning capacity, the code, runtime-state, test, review and
537: reconciliation space it removes is counterfactual evidence of that
538: contraction, not an independent reason for a design gate. Where no
539: material alternative remains, a separate prior gate adds ceremony without
540: disambiguation (P2).
541: 
542: The bidirectional design-and-implementation relation is an evidence
543: relation, not bidirectional semantic authority. Implementation may provide
544: a counterexample, falsify a constraint or expose hidden ambiguity. It may
545: not select the missing semantic answer, rewrite upstream truth to legalise
546: itself, or ratify a material design decision after establishing it (P6).
547: 
548: The selected relation and its basis belong in the existing work or design
549: carrier; this rule requires no separate artifact. If implementation
550: exposes previously hidden architectural ambiguity, the boundary switches to
551: design-gated sequencing at the smallest causally closed affected decision
552: set rather than retroactively invalidating unrelated work. Serial
553: implementation repairs do not establish design acceptance. Repeated or
554: cross-cutting material surprises are evidence for diagnosis under
555: [ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation),
556: not a diagnosis. Where the diagnosis establishes that the affected design
557: cut is underconstrained, so that `decision_complete(B)` fails, one bounded
558: `design_reframe` follows (SPEC_METHOD §4 Change classes), and retained code
559: remains provisional evidence until that reframe is accepted. Where the
560: accepted design is decision-complete and the realisation alone deviates
561: from it, the repair is a `realization_refactor`, however often the surprise
562: recurs (P6, P2).
563: 
564: This applies the governing proportionality law: a prior design gate is
565: warranted when it removes material semantic ambiguity whose alternatives
566: would establish materially different durable architecture, and that
567: contraction justifies its reasoning load. It is disproportionate when
568: upstream truth leaves no materially divergent architecture to adjudicate
569: and a separate prior acceptance would add no disambiguation. Design still
570: records and owns the resulting HOW before promotion or closure (P2, P6).
571: 
572: ### Decision-complete symbolic design
573: 
574: For one governed boundary `B`, the complete material-relation set is (P1,
575: P2; rc.2 #decision-complete-symbolic-design):
576: 
577: ```text
578: M(B) =
579:   entities + identities + relationships + cardinalities + invariants
580:   + authorities + authority transitions + functions
581:   + higher-order composition laws + topology
582:   + lifecycle states and transitions + public contracts
583:   + externally observable Product meaning
584:   + declared domains and admission conditions
585:   + failure and refusal routes + effect and closure laws
586:   + projections + module mappings + material algorithmic obligations
587: ```
588: 
589: A design boundary is decision-complete when `U(B)` is empty, `M(B)` forms
590: one jointly satisfiable constraint network, and every network admitted by
591: `M(B)` is semantically equivalent under the governing Product,
592: requirements and accepted design relations. This is the design gate's
593: acceptance criterion: a boundary is ready for retained implementation
594: without a prior gate exactly when it is decision-complete, and a gate that
595: cannot reach decision completeness has not closed (P2, P6).
596: 
597: Ontology, Prime contraction, IACS, target design, the domain, sequence and
598: state views, public contracts, module boundaries, implementation and tests
599: are projections of that one network at different reasoning altitudes.
600: Their presence, section names, individual plausibility or mechanical
601: validity does not establish decision completeness (P1, EVALUATION §1).
602: 
603: The boundary is underconstrained whenever `decision_complete(B)` is false,
604: including when implementation has to introduce a new material semantic
605: decision, projections contradict one another, or two materially
606: non-equivalent networks remain admissible. Local algorithm and layout
607: choices may remain open only when every admitted choice is semantically
608: equivalent under the accepted network. Contradictory projections make the
609: design unsatisfiable and block promotion (P1, P5): an unsatisfiable design
610: fails the design gate's acceptance criterion, so this block is a
611: precondition of the gate (§7 Gate and retrospective work), not a decision
612: on a review finding. Decision completeness
613: does not require another document: the constraint network may be expressed
614: through the existing Ontology, algebra, module mapping and views when those
615: surfaces jointly carry the complete relation (P2).
616: 
617: ### Bounded frame conservation (UP-017)
618: 
619: `M(B)` closes one governed boundary. A bounded local action is taken inside
620: a design frame that derives from other accepted frames, and its lawfulness
621: depends on relations the acting frame does not itself own (P4b, P0;
622: rc.2 #bounded-frame-conservation-stdo-up-017). Global and local are relative to
623: the selected frame. Each material design frame identifies:
624: 
625: - the governing frames and accepted relations from which it derives;
626: - the bounded affected relation set of the proposed action;
627: - the applicable inherited invariants;
628: - the authority and composition seams crossing that set; and
629: - the subordinate frames opened by unresolved material distinctions.
630: 
631: A frame may derive from more than one governing frame. A persistence
632: component belongs to an entity lifecycle boundary and an operational
633: consistency boundary; an admission function belongs to a domain transition
634: and a runtime-authority boundary; a shared callable may be consumed by
635: several sibling domains without becoming subordinate to one. A single
636: governing frame is lawful where the structure is genuinely hierarchical,
637: and is not required. Governing frames form a constraint network for the
638: same reason `M(B)` does (P4b, P6).
639: 
640: The seam rule is [ACTIVATION §1 Execution unit](ACTIVATION.md#execution-unit)
641: and [§4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement). Applied to a design
642: frame, it makes the declared set testable against its own declared seams without a closure algorithm or
643: recursive expansion through irrelevant relations (P0).
644: 
645: The result is evaluated against every affected governing frame, preserves
646: each applicable accepted relation, and updates only affected subordinate
647: projections. A bounded local action conserves governing truth; it does not
648: rewrite it. A result that changes a governing relation re-enters at that
649: relation before acceptance (P4b; FOUNDATIONS §3 P4b, frame instance). A
650: subordinate frame opens only when a material distinction cannot be
651: resolved at the governing altitude; this rule does not require recursively
652: documenting irrelevant descendants (P2). The law is false if a change is
653: locally valid inside the selected frame but violates, duplicates or
654: silently reinterprets an invariant in any affected governing frame.
655: 
656: Discovered functionality is evidence about required behaviour, not yet an
657: architectural operation. A discovered verb, screen action, endpoint,
658: command, ticket phrase or use case is not promoted directly into a public
659: operation identity, peer carrier, module or implementation function; it is
660: first derived through the Ontology (P6, P2). The derivation order:
661: 
662: ```text
663: constitutional functionality
664:   -> candidate Ontology
665:   -> logical completeness
666:   -> whole-family Prime contraction
667:   -> accepted Ontology basis
668:   -> Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set
669:   -> target design and domain, sequence and state projections
670:   -> public contract and adapter projections
671:   -> implementation and test projections
672: ```

809: ### Entity and lifecycle completeness
810: 
811: The Ontology enumerates the entities inside the active boundary, their
812: identities, relationships, cardinalities, invariants, lifecycle states and
813: authority owners (P3, P5; rc.2 #entity-and-lifecycle-completeness). For
814: each entity, design evidence provides this logical-completeness matrix or
815: an equivalent closed representation:
816: 
817: | Entity | Identity | Authority owner | Declare/create | Read/project | Update/transition | Delete/retire |
818: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
819: 
820: The matrix applies to identity-bearing entities and independently governed
821: value families (P3, P2). A Subordinate Payload or value object inherits the
822: lifecycle and authority of its owning entity unless it passes the
823: Promotion Test (§6); it does not require a ceremonial peer lifecycle row.
824: 
825: The lifecycle columns are completeness questions, not a mandate for
826: mutable CRUD: create may be declaration, construction, admission or
827: materialisation; read should normally be a typed projection over
828: authoritative truth; update should normally be an admitted transition or
829: new version rather than in-place semantic mutation; delete should normally
830: be retirement, revocation, decommission or supersession where history or
831: identity has to remain true (P3). Every cell identifies a lawful function,
832: declares `not_applicable` with a reason, or names a `Gap:` or
833: `Unanswered:` item and owner. Silence is not logical-completeness evidence
834: (P5, P6).
835: 
836: This entity lifecycle is distinct from the operational module lifecycle of
837: ASSURANCE §16: the Ontology describes what states and transformations
838: exist for domain entities; ASSURANCE §16 confirms how the resulting
839: realisation is built, released, deployed, observed and retired (P1).
840: 
841: ### Authority model
842: 
843: Authority is part of the Ontology, not metadata added to an operation
844: after its shape has been selected (P6; rc.2 #authority-model). For every
845: Ontology function or lifecycle transition that crosses a semantic,
846: authority, admission, effect, persistence or public boundary, design
847: evidence provides this authority matrix or an equivalent closed
848: representation:
849: 
850: | Function or transition | Proposer | Evaluator | Verifier | Admitter | Executor | Projector | Retirement owner |
851: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
852: 
853: The model distinguishes actor identity from authority; available
854: capability from authority admitted for the current basis; proposal from
855: evaluation, verification, admission, execution, projection and retirement;
856: attribution from permission; and ownership of domain meaning from
857: ownership of runtime effects (P6; FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds). One
858: owner may lawfully occupy more than one role only when the governing
859: authority explicitly says so; role coincidence is not inferred from
860: implementation convenience. Pure subordinate helpers inherit the authority
861: envelope of their owning Ontology function and do not require peer
862: authority rows unless they cross one of those boundaries.
863: 
864: What cannot create authority is stated once in
865: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
866: creates no authority. This paragraph applies its items on composition,
867: projection, labels, capability strings and payload shape to the Ontology's
868: functions and adds only these design instances (P6; IDENTITY §6).
869: Composition does not widen authority implicitly: a composed or
870: higher-order function has no more authority than the authority law
871: admitted for its inputs, constituent functions and current basis.
872: Delegation, elevation, transfer or retirement authority requires a named
873: typed transition and an owning admission boundary; these carry in the
874: design the explicit authority decision that FOUNDATIONS requires and do not
875: replace it. Projections cannot create authority, and downstream code
876: cannot reconstruct an authority witness from actor labels, capability
877: strings or payload shape.

879: ### Transformation admission completeness (UP-016)
880: 
881: The authority matrix names who admits; it does not by itself establish the
882: relation that decides which candidate transformation becomes durable
883: entity truth. Two designs can complete the matrix plausibly and still leave
884: two materially different ways to admit the same transformation (P6, P4b;
885: rc.2 #transformation-admission-completeness-stdo-up-016).
886: 
887: For every consequential entity-transition domain, design evidence contains
888: the complete transformation-admission relation over entity identity,
889: predecessor basis, authority scope, candidate family, decision
890: cardinality, admission predicate, resulting durable fact and supersession
891: law, through the authority matrix or an equivalent closed representation
892: (P6, P4b):
893: 
894: | Entity transition domain | Predecessor basis | Candidate family | Admission relation | Durable result | Competing-path disposition |
895: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
896: 
897: For every material admission relation, accepted design declares, in one
898: compact relation or equivalent representation (P6, P4b, P3):
899: 
900: - each admission owner and supported admission boundary;
901: - the exact admission-valid basis identity, predecessor and currentness
902:   continuity through admission, and any equal or coherent composite
903:   multi-owner basis;
904: - the complete enclosing relation, participant identities and equality
905:   joins;
906: - refusal and effect boundaries;
907: - the complete semantic commit unit and its decomposability: every
908:   materially distinct post-validation commit or publication boundary
909:   capable of exposing a subset, or a design-declared dominance or
910:   equivalence proof that named representative observations cover the
911:   complete partial-failure surface;
912: - reconstruction and the supported direct, composite and nested forms; and
913: - competing-path disposition.
914: 
915: The declaration binds the admission and standing-test semantics of
916: ACTIVATION §4 (Complete enclosing-relation admission; Standing structural
917: qualification), which solely owns them. Qualification is instantiated per
918: owner and supported boundary. Unsupported composite or nested forms use
919: `not_applicable` only when accepted domain or design excludes the form and
920: the boundary has no weaker or competing admission path (P6, P4b). This
921: obligation is false if a field, owner or supported boundary is missing or
922: invented downstream; if basis continuity, partial-failure boundary
923: coverage or its dominance or equivalence proof, or reconstruction is left
924: to implementation inference; or if non-applicability is established only
925: by a parser, helper or manufactured refusal.
926: 
927: Singularity attaches to the complete decision relation, not to one actor,
928: callable or component. Several actors, stages or implementations are
929: lawful as constituents or disjoint instances of that relation. A relation
930: may lawfully require one actor, several signatures, a quorum, a human
931: step-up, delegated proxy authority or jurisdictional partitioning, provided
932: its cardinality and adjudication law are declared (P6).
933: 
934: Competing-path disposition does not imply deletion. An equivalent path may
935: be a lawful constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent
936: realisation, provided its relationship to the singular admission law is
937: explicit. A superseded responsibility remains subject to SPEC_METHOD §7
938: Core interface migration: retention requires a distinct supported purpose,
939: not merely a path label or an existing test (P6, P2). A projection may
940: produce a candidate transformation, but projection status does not confer
941: admission authority; any consequential result re-enters the governing
942: admission relation against its explicit predecessor basis, and a
943: reconstructed projection state is not self-authenticating admission
944: evidence (P6; projection is an item of
945: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
946: creates no authority).
947: 
948: This law is false if any of the following holds (P6, P4b): two materially
949: non-equivalent admission relations remain reachable for the same governed
950: transition domain on the same entity identity, authority scope and
951: predecessor basis (disjoint scopes or identities are not a
952: counterexample); a materially equivalent competing implementation remains
953: reachable without being identified as a constituent, replica, replacement
954: or deliberately independent realisation; or a projection-triggered
955: reaction uses its own reconstructive state as self-authenticating
956: admission evidence.

958: ### Atomic functions and higher-order composition
959: 
960: The Ontology derives the smallest parameterised atomic function families
961: that make the entity lifecycles logically complete. Variation that changes
962: only an entity kind, projection kind, transition kind, policy or
963: subordinate payload should normally be a typed parameter or closed variant
964: of one function family, not another peer function (P4a, P3;
965: rc.2 #atomic-functions-and-higher-order-composition). The minimum
966: function-derivation evidence is:
967: 
968: | Discovered functionality | Entity | Atomic function or template | Higher-order composition | Effect class | Required authority | Disposition |
969: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
970: 
971: Every row is one of: derived through an admitted atomic function; derived
972: through a declared higher-order composition; deferred with an owner and
973: re-entry condition; excluded by current product authority; or unresolved
974: as a named gap (P5, P6).
975: 
976: Where the boundary has higher-order behaviour, the Ontology names the
977: governing composition and effect algebra. Typical categories include unit
978: or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold
979: or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and
980: projection. The design states the applicable identity, closure,
981: associativity, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws rather
982: than hiding them in controller flow (P4a, P6; FOUNDATIONS §4 Composition).
983: This does not require monadic or category-theory vocabulary
984: (SPEC_METHOD §2 Realisation shape). A product under the graph-execution
985: profile may bind the requirement to GTL composition and ABG
986: interpretation; another product may use another explicit algebra.
987: 
988: Composition, effects and implementation may be discovered iteratively only
989: when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds. Otherwise only a disposable spike
990: may supply evidence across the affected unresolved, contradictory or
991: materially non-equivalent relation before its design is accepted. Every
992: retained result is reconciled into accepted design before promotion or
993: design-method closure. No private helper, loop, adapter or endpoint may
994: become an undeclared constructor (P6, P2).
