996: ### Prime semantic atoms and admitted domain
997: 
998: A Prime semantic atom is one irreducible design relation: an atomic
999: function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation,
1000: topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot be expressed
1001: honestly by composing other accepted atoms while preserving the same
1002: meaning (P3, P1; rc.2 #prime-semantic-atoms-and-universal-domain).
1003: 
1004: Prime is decided at semantic-design altitude. A file, source function,
1005: class, schema record, public operation, diagram, module or owner category
1006: is not a Prime atom merely because it is small, typed, separately named or
1007: independently testable. One atom may project into several realisation
1008: units, and one realisation unit may implement several atoms, provided the
1009: mapping is explicit and introduces no rival meaning or authority. An
1010: atomic function is not proven Prime until the complete candidate family has
1011: been contracted (whole-family Prime contraction, below; P1, P6).
1012: 
1013: Every accepted Prime atom declares the admitted domain over which its law
1014: holds, and within that domain it governs every admitted instance. A later
1015: use case composes or parameterises the atom; it does not fork, shadow,
1016: specialise or reinterpret the atom locally. An out-of-domain case may
1017: justify proposing another candidate atom for design admission. An
1018: in-domain counterexample falsifies the shared atom and re-enters at that
1019: atom's design boundary rather than authorising a feature-local replacement
1020: (P3, P6). An atom without a declared admitted domain remains a candidate
1021: atom; it cannot supply Prime acceptance or Prime-conformance to a
1022: realisation projection.
1023: 
1024: ### Whole-family Prime contraction
1025: 
1026: Prime review evaluates the complete candidate semantic-atom family and
1027: every proposed realisation projection, not only functions, carriers or
1028: each atom in isolation. The family includes every proposed identity,
1029: authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, function, composition
1030: law, effect and closure law. A function-and-carrier-only pass does not
1031: establish whole-family Prime (P3, P2;
1032: rc.2 #whole-family-prime-contraction). Before promotion, review asks:
1033: 
1034: - can several proposed operations be typed parameters of one atomic
1035:   function?
1036: - are several commands lifecycle transitions over one entity?
1037: - are several reads projections over one source truth?
1038: - are several implementations applications of one higher-order function?
1039: - does the candidate introduce independent identity, authority, effect,
1040:   lifecycle, reuse or public pattern-match semantics?
1041: - has every candidate atom kind entered the same contraction?
1042: - does every realisation unit map explicitly to its accepted atom or
1043:   atoms?
1044: - does any realisation projection introduce, duplicate or reinterpret
1045:   meaning or authority?
1046: 
1047: A family of individually plausible functions is not Prime when one
1048: parameterised template plus closed variants carries the same meaning and
1049: authority. Recurrence is contracted during design when visible; the
1050: post-implementation recurrence rule (§10) is not a substitute for this
1051: prior pass (P2).
1052: 
1053: ### Recursive Prime and root conservation (UP-003)
1054: 
1055: At a material semantic boundary, Prime contraction applies to each
1056: candidate semantic atom and then to the complete family produced by those
1057: contractions. A locally irreducible atom is not globally Prime when the
1058: family duplicates identity, authority, function, lifecycle, topology,
1059: effect or projection meaning. Local Prime-conformance of realisation units
1060: does not prove the semantic family globally Prime (P3, P6;
1061: rc.2 #recursive-prime-and-root-conservation-stdo-up-003).
1062: 
1063: Contraction preserves root authority and every retained semantic relation.
1064: Reducing files, functions, operations or authoring surfaces cannot
1065: compensate for introducing another authority source or truth path (P6,
1066: P4b). Prime evidence states the complete candidate semantic-atom family;
1067: each atom's stable identity, irreducible relation, admitted domain and
1068: falsification condition; the whole-family contraction relation; retained
1069: meaning and authority before and after contraction; accepted loss; and the
1070: explicit total mapping from every proposed realisation projection to its
1071: accepted atom or atoms (P4b, FOUNDATIONS §4 Conservation accounting). Work
1072: inside an accepted boundary cites the existing Prime basis rather than
1073: recreating it (P2).
1074: 
1075: ### Ontology projection
1076: 
1077: The Ontology is one semantic truth (P1, P6; rc.2 #ontology-projection-law).
1078: These preserve it and do not become independent semantic authorities:
1079: class or domain diagrams; sequence diagrams; state and lifecycle diagrams;
1080: authority and effect matrices; the IACS; public APIs, operation registers,
1081: SDK and CLI surfaces; schemas, codecs, manifests and generated catalogues;
1082: target architecture and module design; implementation modules through
1083: accepted target design; and test and proof inventories through
1084: requirements and accepted design.
1085: 
1086: Each design projection identifies its Ontology source and the identity,
1087: relationship, lifecycle, authority, function or effect law it preserves.
1088: Any intentional omission or flattening declares accepted loss and a
1089: failure condition (FOUNDATIONS §4 Reference versus body). Target design
1090: may add structural HOW absent from the Ontology, but it may not originate
1091: rival semantic meaning. Implementation and tests trace through that
1092: accepted design rather than bypassing it (P1, P6).
1093: 
1094: If a public operation, sequence message, state transition, carrier or
1095: effect cannot be traced through accepted design to the accepted Ontology,
1096: it is ungrounded design and does not enter the active product line. An
1097: implementation branch or test expectation traces to requirements plus
1098: accepted design; it preserves, but need not be enumerated by, the
1099: Ontology (P6; SPEC_METHOD §2 Trace closure and anti-drift).

1312: ## 7. Ontology and three-view design gate
1313: 
1314: Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary carries
1315: one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view Mermaid design asset
1316: before the boundary is promoted or claims design-method closure (P6, P1;
1317: rc.2 #5e-ontology-and-three-view-behavioral-design-gate). When
1318: `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, design evidence, implementation and
1319: tests may develop together before that gate; otherwise the affected
1320: unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation is
1321: accepted before retained implementation establishes it. Unchanged
1322: boundaries cite their accepted basis; local realisation work with no
1323: material semantic-boundary delta does not recreate this gate (P2).
1324: 
1325: The asset contains all three views: a Mermaid `classDiagram` domain model;
1326: a Mermaid `sequenceDiagram` execution model; and a Mermaid
1327: `stateDiagram-v2` lifecycle model. A project may ratify another text-native
1328: diagram format only when it preserves the same three distinct views and the
1329: same cross-view checks. One broad flowchart does not substitute for the
1330: three models. The three views may be sections of one existing design
1331: surface and may share one acceptance decision; this rule does not require
1332: three files, three tickets, three reviews or three approval ceremonies
1333: (P2). The views are not decorative and are not peer truth surfaces: they
1334: are fidelity-checked projections of the accepted Ontology, and together
1335: the sign-off surface for domain identity, authority, behaviour, lifecycle
1336: and axiom conformance (P1, P6).
1337: 
1338: ### Ontology evidence
1339: 
1340: The design asset cites one accepted Ontology for the active boundary and
1341: includes or references its (P6; rc.2 #ontology-evidence): entity and
1342: relationship inventory; invariant and cardinality law; entity-lifecycle
1343: completeness matrix; authority matrix; atomic-function and
1344: higher-order-function derivation matrix; governing composition and effect
1345: algebra where applicable; whole-family Prime contraction, including every
1346: accepted atom's admitted domain and realisation-projection mapping; and
1347: explicit deferred, excluded and unresolved functionality.
1348: 
1349: The Ontology may be a boundary-bounded slice of a wider accepted product
1350: Ontology. The slice cites its parent and preserves parent identity,
1351: relationship, lifecycle, authority and function law. Copying selected rows
1352: into a new local model without that derivation creates another truth
1353: surface (P6, P3).
1354: 
1355: ### Invariant reconstruction sufficiency (UP-018)
1356: 
1357: The evidence above is not a documentation deliverable. It is the durable
1358: reasoning state a bounded actor needs, because the actor selecting a local
1359: action generally does not hold the reasoning that produced the governing
1360: frames. Dialogue, commentary, prior-agent memory and implementation
1361: folklore are not that state (P0, P4b;
1362: rc.2 #invariant-reconstruction-sufficiency-stdo-up-018). The general
1363: reconstruction rule is [ACTIVATION §1 Intake](ACTIVATION.md#intake); this
1364: clause states what design evidence supplies to it.
1365: 
1366: Given an accepted material-frame basis, as determined by the material
1367: semantic boundary definition (§5), and a proposed bounded action, the
1368: selected method basis together with the accepted design is sufficient to
1369: recover every governing relation in the action's causally closed affected
1370: set, and to decide whether the action preserves, changes, duplicates or
1371: violates each of those relations. The two inputs are distinct and neither
1372: substitutes for the other: the selected method describes which relations
1373: are required and how to reason about them; the accepted design supplies
1374: the concrete invariant values. A design that restates method decision law
1375: to satisfy this rule reproduces the local-method duplication this law
1376: exists to remove (P1, P6).
1377: 
1378: | Decision | The action, against a governing relation | Core value |
1379: |---|---|---|
1380: | preserves | leaves the relation intact and operates inside it | `satisfied` |
1381: | changes | alters the relation itself, and therefore re-enters at that relation before acceptance | `invalid_basis` |
1382: | duplicates | establishes an equivalent path that is explicitly disposed as a constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realisation | `satisfied` |
1383: | violates | contradicts the relation, or establishes an equivalent path that is left undisposed | `falsified` |
1384: 
1385: The boundary between changes and violates is the locus of acceptance, not
1386: the size of the delta: an otherwise lawful change accepted inside the
1387: acting frame rather than at the relation it changes is a violation. The
1388: boundary between duplicates and violates is disposition, not equivalence:
1389: an equivalent path is lawful when disposed and a defect when not (P4b,
1390: P6). Sufficiency is bound to a declared action and its affected set; it is
1391: not a claim over an unbounded space of possible future changes, and the
1392: performance of any particular reviewer is not evidence either way (P0).
1393: 
1394: The four decisions are a refinement of the core result algebra
1395: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)). They answer what the
1396: action does to one governing relation, and each maps to exactly one core
1397: value for the predicate "the action is admissible in the acting frame on
1398: the current governing basis"; the value travels with that predicate and
1399: with the decision, whose meaning stays here (P5, P6). `preserves` and a
1400: disposed `duplicates` leave the relation as accepted. For `changes`, the
1401: relation itself must change at its own locus before the action can be
1402: accepted, so the current governing basis cannot support accepting it in
1403: the acting frame, as for the disposition `re_enter` of
1404: [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#disposition). For `violates`, the
1405: contradiction or the undisposed equivalent path is the counterexample. An
1406: evaluation that reaches none of the four decisions returns the core value
1407: its cause selects, `indeterminate` where the admissible evidence cannot
1408: decide, naming what would decide (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results); where the
1409: cause is that the selected method basis and the accepted design do not
1410: suffice, the case falsifies this law, as stated below. The mapping is
1411: new in this corpus. Purpose and material relation: a lawful change is
1412: never read as a violation or as an action the acting frame may accept, and
1413: a violation is never read as a re-entry (P4b, P6).
1414: 
1415: This obligation adds no artifact. It is satisfied through the Ontology
1416: evidence, authority matrix, transformation-admission relation, frame
1417: declaration, views and module mapping already required, and is a property
1418: of that material rather than a separate package (P2). The law is false if,
1419: for a declared bounded action, the accepted design does not expose a
1420: governing relation in that action's causally closed affected set, or the
1421: preserve, change, duplicate or violate decision cannot be reached from the
1422: selected method basis and accepted design without conversation history,
1423: commentary, prior-worker memory or implementation folklore. Where the
1424: sufficiency of a boundary is tested, the test uses named cases with known
1425: governing relations and expected decisions, evaluated with conversation
1426: history, commentary, prior-worker memory and implementation folklore
1427: withheld (P6; EVALUATION §3).
1428: 
1429: ### Domain model
1430: 
1431: The `classDiagram` is the structural domain projection of the Ontology
1432: (P1, P3; rc.2 #domain-model). It shows, for the active boundary: domain
1433: identities and cardinalities rather than helper-class decomposition;
1434: entity ownership, invariants and lawful lifecycle relationships; atomic
1435: function families and their entity inputs and outputs where they cross the
1436: active boundary; higher-order composition relationships where they
1437: determine boundary shape; IACS carriers and their Prime-atom projection
1438: mappings; subordinate payloads; effect-edge-only payloads; downstream-only
1439: projections; deferred families outside the active slice; authoritative
1440: versus downstream role; public versus module-local visibility; and
1441: composition, containment, association and real variant-family structure.
1442: 
1443: The standard stereotype vocabulary is `<<prime-conformant>>`,
1444: `<<subordinate>>`, `<<effect-edge>>`, `<<deferred>>`, `<<authoritative>>`
1445: and `<<downstream>>`. The standard visibility vocabulary is `+` public or
1446: exported and `-` module-local or private. The standard relationship
1447: expectations are composition for owned subordinate payloads, association
1448: for downstream consumption, and inheritance only for real variant or
1449: outcome families (P1).
1450: 
1451: ### Sequence model
1452: 
1453: The `sequenceDiagram` is the behavioural projection of Ontology functions
1454: and authority (P1, P6; rc.2 #sequence-model). It shows the supported
1455: execution path from admitted input to result or truthful stop, and names
1456: the owner and required authority of every decision, admission, execution,
1457: projection and effect boundary. Where applicable it shows malformed input
1458: or output, retry, recursion, fan-out and fan-in, nested workflow and human
1459: escalation paths. Every participant exists in the domain model or is an
1460: explicitly external actor. Every message binds to a declared carrier
1461: transform, graph or computation constructor, interpreter action or
1462: effect-handler call; a private loop, service method, plugin, shell or
1463: script may not silently replace a declared workflow transition. Every
1464: message also binds to an Ontology function and its admitted authority
1465: role; actor identity or call reachability alone does not authorise a
1466: message (P6).
1467: 
1468: ### State model
1469: 
1470: The `stateDiagram-v2` is the lifecycle projection of Ontology entities
1471: (P3, P5; rc.2 #state-model). It shows the complete admitted lifecycle for
1472: the active boundary, including refusal, blocked, continuation, retry,
1473: escalation and terminal states that the boundary can produce. Every
1474: transition binds to an Ontology function and names its owning authority,
1475: admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection or external act.
1476: Controller-local memory is not a lawful source of lifecycle truth when the
1477: product declares replay, event, graph or carrier ownership (P6).
1478: 
1479: ### Cross-view axiom evaluation
1480: 
1481: The design pack evaluates every applicable product, graph, language,
1482: runtime, handler and module axiom with one of `pass`, `fail` or
1483: `not_applicable` with a reason (P1, P6; rc.2 #cross-view-axiom-evaluation).
1484: The minimum evaluation columns are:
1485: 
1486: | Axiom | Ontology evidence | Authority | Domain evidence | Sequence evidence | State evidence | Native enforcement | Admission/compiler enforcement | Verdict | Gap owner |
1487: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
1488: 
1489: The cross-view evaluation proves that: every element in each view derives
1490: from the accepted Ontology; every discovered functionality row has a
1491: derived, deferred, excluded or gap disposition; every sequence participant
1492: and lifecycle carrier exists in the domain model; every sequence message
1493: has a declared semantic or effect boundary; every lifecycle transition is
1494: derivable from admitted truth; every function and transition has an
1495: explicit authority path and composition does not widen that authority
1496: implicitly; every public operation is a projection of an Ontology function
1497: rather than an independently authored semantic peer; raw probabilistic
1498: output cannot transition directly to accepted or closed; handlers and
1499: plugins own interiors only when the runtime owns admission, events,
1500: continuation and closure; native types enforce locally decidable
1501: relations; and admission or semantic compilation owns global references,
1502: completeness and realisation gaps (P1, P6, P5).
1503: 
1504: For graph-native work, every batch, retry, recursion or nested workflow is
1505: visible through the product's declared graph or compute algebra. A
1506: relied-on `semantic_not_realized` constructor is a blocking gap; it may
1507: not be replaced by imperative glue in a plugin, shell, service, script or
1508: test harness (P6, P5).
1509: 
1510: Axiom verdicts. The three verdicts are a refinement of the core result
1511: algebra ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)). They answer
1512: what the design pack concludes about one axiom for the active boundary,
1513: and each maps to exactly one core value for the predicate "on the exact
1514: Ontology and design basis, the boundary's design meets the axiom, or the
1515: axiom does not apply to the boundary"; the value travels with that
1516: predicate and with the verdict, whose meaning stays here (P5, P6). This
1517: profile declares that predicate as a disjunction that includes
1518: non-application, the case that
1519: [ACTIVATION §1 Applicability](ACTIVATION.md#applicability), Exclusion and
1520: the core, permits and bounds. That paragraph decides what follows for the
1521: verdicts: `not_applicable` rests on a false applicability premise, an
1522: unresolved premise supports no `not_applicable`, and the `satisfied` of a
1523: `not_applicable` verdict counts toward this disjunction only, never toward
1524: the predicate that the design meets the axiom:
1525: 
1526: | Verdict | Ground | Core value |
1527: |---|---|---|
1528: | `pass` | the cited Ontology, view and enforcement evidence establishes that the design meets the axiom | `satisfied` |
1529: | `not_applicable` | the axiom's applicability premise is false for the active boundary on basis-bound facts, and the reason names those facts and the authority whose scope declaration excludes the axiom ([ACTIVATION §1 Applicability](ACTIVATION.md#applicability)) | `satisfied` |
1530: | `fail` | the axiom applies, and the evidence names an element, message, transition, authority path or enforcement that violates it; that is the counterexample | `falsified` |
1531: 
1532: The verdict, recorded with its value, keeps the distinction between not
1533: applying and meeting the axiom (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Recording). An evaluated axiom that reaches none of the three
1534: verdicts records in the Verdict column the core value its cause selects,
1535: with what would decide it: `indeterminate` where the admissible evidence
1536: cannot decide the predicate, as where the applicability premise is
1537: unresolved and the design does not meet the axiom; `out_of_frame` where
1538: the evaluation needs a relation or evaluator capability that the activated
1539: frame does not declare; `invalid_basis` where the Ontology or design basis
1540: cannot support it. An applicable axiom that the pack did not evaluate has
1541: no result (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed). None of these is
1542: `pass`. The mapping and the direct core values are new in this corpus.
1543: Purpose and material relation: a design gate that combines axiom verdicts
1544: with other results reads them in the one core, so an excluded axiom is
1545: never read as conforming or as failing, and an undecided or unevaluated
1546: axiom is never read as a pass or a fail (P5, P6).
1547: 
1548: ### Gate and retrospective work
1549: 
1550: For a new or semantically changed boundary, the Ontology and design
1551: verdict are both `accepted` before the affected implementation, public
1552: contract or semantic carrier is promoted or the work claims design-method
1553: closure. Any failed applicable axiom, missing functionality disposition,
1554: unresolved authority path or blocking realisation gap keeps the verdict
1555: non-accepted (P6; rc.2 #gate-and-retrospective-work).
1556: 
1557: The Ontology verdict and the design verdict are each an acceptance
1558: result: a decision that consumes the results of assessment, distinct from
1559: them. The decision owner is the
1560: design authority that accepts the Ontology (§5), and the verdict is its
1561: disposition of the Ontology or of the design pack at the design gate,
1562: under [ACTIVATION §3 Disposition](ACTIVATION.md#disposition), which owns
1563: the dispositions and their core values. `accepted` is the disposition
1564: `accept`, which maps to `satisfied` for "the candidate is accepted at its
1565: declared boundary", the candidate being the Ontology or the design pack
1566: and the boundary the design gate. A verdict that is not `accepted` is one
1567: of the other three dispositions, mapped there, or no disposition yet,
1568: which is no acceptance result. The verdict consumes the pack's availability
1569: and assessment results, among them the evaluation of decision
1570: completeness, which is the design gate's acceptance criterion
1571: ([§5 Decision-complete symbolic design](#decision-complete-symbolic-design)),
1572: the axiom verdicts and the cross-view proofs, and stays separate from both
1573: (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, availability, assessment and acceptance): a matrix in which every applicable axiom is
1574: `pass` is evidence for the design authority, never the verdict, and a
1575: step that produced the pack establishes neither. An axiom whose result
1576: is not `satisfied`, whether `fail` or a core value recorded directly, an
1577: applicable axiom with no result, or an axiom with no result whose
1578: applicability is not established false, keeps the verdict non-accepted
1579: as a failed axiom does, because a combination with a non-satisfied
1580: mandatory result or a gap is never `satisfied`
1581: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results))
1582: (P6, P5). The binding to ACTIVATION §3 is new in this corpus. Purpose and
1583: material relation: neither a passing matrix nor a produced design pack is
1584: read as acceptance, and the design gate's acceptance combines with other
1585: results in the one core (P6).
1586: 
1587: For an unchanged `realization_refactor`, the gate is proportional: cite
1588: the accepted Ontology and design basis, identify the touched projection
1589: set, and prove that entities, relationships, lifecycle, authority,
1590: functions, effects and public semantics have no delta. That proof reuses
1591: the existing verdict; it does not create a new Ontology or acceptance
1592: ceremony (P2; ACTIVATION §7).
1593: 
1594: When `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, implementation may precede or
1595: develop with design evidence and may be retained after reconciliation.
1596: Until the design gate is accepted it is provisional evidence: it does not
1597: author semantic truth, earn publication authority, or satisfy promotion or
1598: closure. Otherwise only a disposable spike may cross the affected
1599: unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation before
1600: design acceptance (P6, P2).
1601: 
1602: Existing implementation placed under retrospective review may continue to
1603: inform the affected design. Co-evolution remains lawful only while
1604: `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds; newly discovered material ambiguity,
1605: contradiction or a materially non-equivalent network makes
1606: `decision_complete(B)` false and activates the design gate for that
1607: decision. Promotion and design-method closure remain blocked until the
1608: required Ontology, three-view asset and axiom evaluation are accepted. The
1609: design evaluates the code against prior authority; it does not rewrite the
1610: Ontology or diagrams merely to rationalise an unlawful implementation
1611: shape (P6).
1612: 
1613: The asset stays boundary-bounded. It is a defect if it mixes an active
1614: semantic boundary with unrelated bootstrap, test-harness, projection or
1615: delivery shapes merely to look complete (P2). If the Ontology, any of the
1616: three views, the cross-view evaluation or either accepted verdict is
1617: absent, the boundary is not design-method complete. Work may continue as
1618: provisional co-evolution only when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, but
1619: the affected boundary may not be promoted, published or closed (P6).
1620: 
1621: ### Computational realisation projection (UP-019)
1622: 
1623: The three views project domain structure, execution and lifecycle. They
1624: deliberately show domain identities, so they do not reveal that two
1625: domain-distinct components rest on the same data structures and
1626: algorithms. Repeated machinery is therefore invisible to a domain-only
1627: reading, and each occurrence looks correctly owned and correctly named
1628: within its own entity (P1;
1629: rc.2 #computational-realization-projection-stdo-up-019).
1630: 
1631: Component role sets. Every material realisation component has an explicit
1632: set of semantic and operational roles. Technology capability does not
1633: confer authority (an instance of
1634: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
1635: creates no authority). A component's declared role set is design authority;
1636: where a role carries authority, composition and use preserve the
1637: applicable authority relation under IDENTITY §6, which is supporting law
1638: here rather than the owner of the role model (P6). A component may
1639: lawfully hold several roles. Three cases are distinguished: behaviour
1640: already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation; a new
1641: operational responsibility and a new semantic or authoritative role are
1642: each design changes, and only those two require re-entry. Use of a
1643: component outside its declared role set does not silently establish
1644: identity, admission, lifecycle, ordering, closure or projection truth (P6,
1645: P3).
1646: 
1647: The projection. At a material semantic boundary, the design projects the
1648: domain design into its computational realisation: abstract data types,
1649: identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and
1650: effect boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational
1651: mappings. The cross-view evaluation extends to prove that the domain views
1652: and this projection describe one system (P1). For a material
1653: producer-to-consumer path, the projection identifies fact establishment,
1654: consuming operations, applicable basis and invalidators, effect
1655: boundaries, retained alternatives and accumulated work, using the validity
1656: and reuse relation of ACTIVATION §4 (Complete enclosing-relation
1657: admission) and §7; method and assurance operations are included where
1658: material. Component-local success cannot establish the complete-path
1659: claim, and different names do not establish different computational
1660: responsibilities (P4b, P6; ASSURANCE §13 Computational whole-path
1661: evaluation).
1662: 
1663: Operational assumptions. Material algorithmic work declares the supported
1664: input dimensions, workload and growth, and the operational assumptions
1665: needed for the selected outcome; the separation of material startup, framework
1666: processing, external computation, transport and assurance costs is
1667: ACTIVATION §6. Bind
1668: any acceptance limits and their owning authority before qualification;
1669: limits and workloads are Product-owned, not universal method constants.
1670: Challenge the assumptions on representative supported paths and material
1671: growth. Observe work directly where elapsed time cannot locate it, without
1672: repeating the operation merely to count it. Existing design and proof
1673: surfaces carry these relations; no additional accounting system or fixed
1674: algorithmic complexity is required (P2, P6).
1675: 
1676: The projection is subordinate. It reveals repeated implementation
1677: structure; it cannot decide semantic identity, ownership or authority
1678: (FOUNDATIONS §4 Shared machinery). The evaluation sequence (P1, P6):
1679: 
1680: ```text
1681: computational similarity
1682:   -> commonisation candidate
1683:   -> semantic and operational equivalence evaluation
1684:   -> reuse, parameterised common relation, or justified separation
1685: ```
1686: 
1687: Two components may share a map or an append-only sequence while differing
1688: in identity and key law, ownership, ordering, admissible mutation,
1689: consistency and concurrency, retention, failure semantics, access policy,
1690: lifecycle or authority over truth. A materially non-equivalent law among
1691: those dimensions requires separation. Other differences justify separation
1692: only when evaluation shows that parameterisation or adaptation would
1693: weaken ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational
1694: constraints. The existence of a difference does not by itself discharge
1695: Prime contraction or recurrence review (P3, P6).
1696: 
1697: Disposition is two-part. Each material algorithmic obligation in `M(B)`
1698: carries a semantic disposition (existing accepted relation, extension, or
1699: new candidate relation) and a realisation disposition (consume, implement
1700: locally, optimise, adapt, or deliberately duplicate under stated
1701: non-semantic constraints). Isolation, substrate, performance, security and
1702: dependency ownership are each lawful grounds for an independent
1703: implementation. The invariant is not that equivalent code is never
1704: rebuilt; it is that a local realisation does not present an existing
1705: accepted semantic or authoritative relation as newly owned local truth
1706: (P6, P4b).
1707: 
1708: This law is false if any of the following holds (P6, P3): two domain-named
1709: components implement materially equivalent abstract data types or
1710: algorithms without a semantic disposition; a generic building block
1711: becomes a new semantic authority; superficially similar operations are
1712: commonised despite different identity, ordering, failure, ownership or
1713: lifecycle law; or a local realisation presents an existing accepted
1714: relation as newly owned local truth.
1715: 


METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md member_sha256=9e2642d51d0b024a448fe7910dcb323fb3f3bb2a003ad33c27c39a5dda625220 lines=2057-2081
2057: ### Interface bleed prohibition
2058: 
2059: No interface should bleed semantic authority into another interface family
2060: (P6; rc.2 #12-interface-bleed-prohibition). Interface bleed exists when one
2061: interface reconstructs another interface's source truth; projection logic
2062: becomes closure logic; report or prompt logic becomes admission logic;
2063: public wrappers decide kernel semantics; or adapters invent meaning instead
2064: of translating boundaries. The required shape: each interface family has
2065: one authoritative source truth; downstream interfaces consume that truth;
2066: crossing an interface boundary does not create a new semantic centre. Low
2067: coupling requires semantic non-bleed, not only small functions.
2068: 
2069: ### Proxy interface prohibition
2070: 
2071: Projects using this profile do not use proxy or partial interface
2072: implementation as a substitute for real migration or real design
2073: completion (P6; rc.2 #13-proxy-interface-prohibition; SPEC_METHOD §7
2074: Bridge prohibition). A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that
2075: forwards to the old authority path, reconstructs missing truth from the
2076: old path, keeps the old path executable behind a new name, or allows
2077: proofs to stay green while the old law still governs. This is bridge debt,
2078: not progress. If compatibility is intentionally retained, it is treated as
2079: an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof; otherwise
2080: the proxy path is removed.

11: ## 1. Claims
12: 
13: A load-bearing claim names its exact subject, the property claimed, the
14: governing basis, the relation between witness and claim, the nearest weaker
15: property it excludes, and its falsifier, before a witness is selected.
16: Without these it is evidence discovery, not proof. Packaging, syntax,
17: compilation, presence, invocation or local behaviour never substitutes for a
18: semantic, authority-bearing, installed, release or end-to-end claim because
19: the weaker property is easier to measure (P6; conserves
20: [UP-001](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#proof-target-identity-and-adequacy-stdo-up-001)).
21: 
22: Where a claim about a construction concerns its recursive or repeated
23: work, it is one of the four kinds the construction relation keeps apart,
24: preservation, progress, termination and outcome satisfaction
25: ([ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation)), and states which.
26: Its witness is an assertion whose predicate is the full obligation, a
27: necessary condition of it or part of a sufficient conjunction, and the
28: claim states which. Its expected result has assertion provenance and its
29: execution has execution provenance, as
30: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation)
31: and [Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance)
32: define them; a passing check of a necessary condition establishes that
33: condition and no more (P1, P6).
34: 
35: Boundary congruence. A checker, validator, harness, reviewer or other
36: assurance surface supporting promotion or closure binds the exact claimed
37: subject and its authoritative composition relation. Evidence over one file
38: or carrier proves only that boundary; it cannot establish a multi-file or
39: carrier-set claim. Cross-carrier satisfaction and conflict are decided at
40: the declared composite boundary (P3, P6). A claim of mechanical enforcement
41: names an executable or reproducible predicate and a witness reachable
42: through the declared ordinary assurance path; a planned or
43: specification-only harness is planned evidence, not observed verification,
44: and until both the predicate and such a witness are observed the claim
45: remains open or is explicitly downgraded to the planned property (P6;
46: conserves
47: [UP-022](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#assurance-boundary-congruence-and-method-qualification-stdo-up-022),
48: first two paragraphs).
49: 
50: A claim's quantifier, population and scope cannot exceed its evaluated
51: evidence. Generalising a local defect or observation needs a declared
52: inference relation, the relevant comparable population, explicit
53: counterexample treatment and governing evidence. Later counterevidence
54: invalidates every dependent verdict until the claim-evidence relation is
55: superseded, withdrawn or requalified (UP-022). The quantifier rule and the
56: boundary rule are false if assurance observes a weaker or different
57: subject, if per-carrier evidence closes an unevaluated composite claim, if
58: mechanical enforcement lacks its predicate or a reachable witness, if
59: planned evidence is reported as observed verification, if a verdict outruns
60: its evaluated population or declared inference relation, or if dependent
61: verdicts survive material counterevidence without requalification.

132: ## 2. Separation
133: 
134: Three bases stay distinct (P6, P1): the semantic basis, the constitutional
135: and accepted-design relations that define what a claim means; the evidence
136: basis, the exact artifacts, events, logs, tests and observations used to
137: evaluate it; and the state projection, a current view derived from admitted
138: semantic and evidence bases. Semantic law defines what an evaluation means;
139: evidence supplies observations; the evaluator applies the declared
140: relation; decision authority disposes. One actor may lawfully perform
141: several; the record keeps them distinguishable. This section owns these
142: separations. [RF-007](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-007-semantic-evidence-and-verdict-separation)
143: binds them to a frame declaration and
144: [AC-018](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation)
145: to an a_c model; each adds only its domain binding.
146: 
147: An evidence change can invalidate a verdict without any change of law.
148: Whether a given change does so is decided by the reuse rule of
149: [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and where it
150: does, the invalidation is mandatory and takes effect before reliance. A
151: projection change can invalidate a view without changing semantic truth;
152: when a derived view is stale is decided by
153: [ACTIVATION §2, Staleness of derived surfaces](ACTIVATION.md#staleness-of-derived-surfaces).
154: A semantic change requires lawful re-entry and invalidates affected
155: downstream acceptance. A broad digest may conservatively
156: invalidate a review; it does not prove that every semantic relation
157: changed (conserves
158: [UP-008](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#semantic-evidence-and-projection-separation-stdo-up-008),
159: [RF-007](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-007-semantic-evidence-and-verdict-separation)).
160: 
161: Structural conformance decides closed syntax, types, identities, references,
162: bases and mechanically decidable predicates. Semantic fidelity decides
163: meaning and materiality. Structural success is evidence for semantic
164: review, not a substitute for it. A checker decides the structural subset; it claims a
165: semantic or authority subset only under an exact lawful decision contract
166: supplied by the model. For a_c models,
167: [AC-018](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation)
168: and [AC-019](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-019-valid-model) bind this rule to
169: the model's records and validity conditions (P1, P6; provenance rc.2
170: AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS #ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation,
171: #ac-019-valid-model).
172: A valid parse, a valid map, a green test and a historical judgment each
173: establish exactly their own claim. Evidence bound to a basis other than
174: the evaluated one is excluded by basis; it is not admitted with a narrower
175: scope (P3;
176: [RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)).
177: 
178: ## 3. Independent assessment
179: 
180: A constructor's self-review is construction output, not assessment. Where
181: promotion needs independent assessment, the assessor evaluates the exact
182: live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state, not the
183: constructor's summary (P6, and P0 with its premise that a step's output is
184: a candidate until evaluated; instance premise (c) of §1 Foundation to law;
185: conserves
186: [UP-007](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/TICKET_METHOD.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-stdo-up-007)).
187: This section decides what counts as independent assessment. Which
188: boundaries require it is a policy choice of the Spec Method, owned by
189: [TICKETS §7 Execution and verification authority separation](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007);
190: a governing basis may add boundaries.
191: 
192: Protocol: where method qualification applies
193: ([§7 Method self-qualification](#method-self-qualification)), the subject is
194: frozen by identity before material reference exposure; elsewhere it is
195: stabilised by an immutable identity or an equivalent exact-subject relation
196: sufficient for the claimed assessment. The assessor records its
197: expectations from the governing source before opening the candidate; it
198: reads the subject at that identity or relation, never a mutable working
199: tree; it makes no repair; it does not assess its
200: own authorship. Reusing the constructor's judgment does not satisfy
201: independence; shared mechanical evidence may be reused, judgment may not
202: (ACTIVATION §7). Binding a returned assessment to its producer, subject,
203: basis and evidence authenticates the result; it establishes neither the
204: assertion provenance of its expected answer nor the execution provenance
205: of its run, which
206: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance)
207: requires separately (P6, P3). Membership in a plan authenticates nothing,
208: an unauthenticated result satisfies no required assessment, and a result
209: bound to another subject satisfies no planned assessment
210: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results));
211: no cryptographic or transport protocol is prescribed for the binding (P6). Any post-exposure revision is a declared intervention: it
212: is either a method constituent with its own qualification boundary or a new
213: qualification subject, and it cannot retroactively make the original
214: frozen construction pass. This law prescribes no actor type or count,
215: review-round count, engine, prompt or orchestration (UP-022).
216: 
217: Author identity is the party responsible for the content of a realised
218: subject. It is distinct from actor identity, whoever performs one
219: operation, which is an identity and not an authority
220: ([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)).
221: Authorship is one of the conditions on
222: which the independence of an assessment rests; the evidence conditions are
223: the other (P6, P3; provenance: the definition moves here from the build
224: binding terms of SPEC_METHOD §11, which refers to it).
225: 
226: Independence rests on authorship and on the evidence conditions above, not
227: on a new context. The assessor may read the same governing sources as the
228: constructor. A fresh context alone establishes no independence, and it
229: supplies no review authority the author lacks: an author that opens a
230: fresh context to review its own candidate is still its author, and its
231: review is self-review, which stays construction output and cannot be
232: relabelled as independent assessment (P6; UP-007 applied to a fresh
233: context). A contribution received from another author stays that
234: author's wherever it is carried, and that author's reading of it supplies
235: no independent acceptance of it (P6).
236: 
237: Independence across actor families is declared, not assumed. Whether two
238: activations of one model family are independent for a semantic judgment is a
239: policy the governing basis states for the claim; the default where it is not
240: stated is that they are not independent.
241: 
242: ## 4. Review results
243: 
244: A review returns one core result
245: ([FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) for each declared
246: predicate it evaluated, with: the exact subject and basis, the evidence
247: consulted, the findings ranked by consequence, each finding's evidence and
248: the smallest bounded correction, the residual uncertainty, and the
249: invalidation conditions. A declared predicate the review planned and did
250: not evaluate has no result (FOUNDATIONS §4, Results). The review names it
251: as not performed and reports no core value for it, neither
252: `indeterminate` nor `falsified`, so that conjunction keeps it apart from
253: an undecided predicate and from required coverage that no planned
254: assessment addresses
255: ([FOUNDATIONS §4, Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results);
256: P5, P6). It may recommend a disposition
257: ([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)), which is
258: evidence only and never a disposition; it does not apply one. A finding
259: without evidence a consumer can chase is commentary.
260: 
261: ### Result and triage projection
262: 
263: Where a review returns findings with technical triage, the triage is the
264: assessor's evidence-bound assessment of each finding against the exact
265: evaluated claim and basis. Severity, the assessor's grade of consequence,
266: is evaluation evidence. Priority, the effect on the current promotion
267: boundary and the disposition are the decision owner's (ACTIVATION §1,
268: Roles and delegation; when a finding can block is
269: [§5, When a finding blocks promotion](#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion))
270: and stay distinct values even where a
271: Product-defined policy maps one to another. A recommended disposition
272: is evidence for the decision owner: it is not a disposition, a
273: priority or a boundary effect, and it is never adopted mechanically (P6,
274: RF-007). The fields of a triage are declared by the profile that adopts it, and
275: the scales it uses are bound by the adopting Product (P2, P6; provenance
276: [reviewer result and triage projection](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#reviewer-result-and-triage-projection)).
277: 
278: The projection of the finding-level triage payload is total over the core
279: values of [FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A predicate
280: not performed has no result and so no triage payload; the payload class
281: `indeterminate` never stands for it. The payload classes `complete`,
282: `indeterminate` and `not_applicable` classify the triage only; they are
283: not new results, dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states (P5, P1).
284: 
285: | Core result | Finding and triage payload | Decision-owner consumption constraint |
286: |---|---|---|
287: | satisfied | an explicit no-finding state; triage `not_applicable`; evidence, residuals and invalidation stay present | priority and boundary effect are `not_applicable` to this result unless another exact consumed result supplies a finding |
288: | falsified | one or more exact findings; triage `complete` where supported, keeping `indeterminate` fields where evidence cannot close them | apply the Product-owned priority and boundary policy without mapping severity mechanically to a disposition |
289: | indeterminate | a partial finding or observation state; triage `indeterminate`; the exact evidence gaps and residual uncertainty | keep the uncertainty or reactivate a capable evaluation; do not consume it as satisfaction or as a closed finding |
290: | out_of_frame | the evaluated claim needs an undeclared material relation or evaluator capability; triage `indeterminate`; the missing relation or capability and the exact reconfiguration pressure are named | refine or reconfigure a capable activation and keep the claim unresolved; do not consume the result as satisfaction or falsification |
291: | invalid_basis | a basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse to consume the result and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |
292: 
293: An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim does not replace the
294: claim-relative result. The assessor returns it separately, with triage
295: `not_applicable` to that claim and the exact repricing or re-entry
296: pressure; the decision owner returns it to its declared owner without
297: creating a claim-relative block, or another review round, from its
298: severity alone (P6, P2).
299: 
300: The assessor returns to the decision owner, not to the constructor. It does
301: not edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation (P6,
302: §3).
303: 
304: Purpose and material relation of this projection's generality: the
305: predecessor stated it for the Reviewer and the Executive only. Stating it
306: for any assessor and decision owner gives every configuration the same
307: separation of severity, priority, boundary effect and disposition, and
308: EXECUTIVE_BASELINE keeps the Reviewer and Executive instance (P6).
309: 
310: ## 5. Acceptance
311: 
312: Acceptance is the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject;
313: recording it cannot widen it, and it exhausts only the instance and interval
314: it names (P6, P2; conserves
315: [UP-013](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#product-outcome-conservation-stdo-up-013),
316: [AC-014](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-014-judgment-separation)).
317: A work item closes by the condition it stated, not by a reviewer's approval;
318: a reviewer result is an input to closure, never the closure. Green labels,
319: document counts, review counts and historical outcomes are not acceptance.
320: A human decision may be exercised directly or through an explicitly admitted
321: bounded proxy. What a proxy grant names is
322: [IDENTITY §6](IDENTITY.md#6-authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004)'s,
323: and what a proxy can never decide is
324: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)';
325: for acceptance, a change a proxy cannot make re-enters at its owning
326: relation (provenance rc.2 IDENTITY_METHOD
327: #authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004 and
328: [UP-020](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#agentic-construction-execution-stdo-up-020)).

340: ### When a finding blocks promotion
341: 
342: A finding is a defect a review reports against the exact claim it
343: evaluated (§4). Blocking current promotion is the decision owner's act
344: over that finding (§4, Result and triage projection). This section is the
345: one statement of when a finding can block; profiles and work carriers
346: refer to it and add only their domain triggers.
347: 
348: A review verdict is bounded by the exact reviewed claim and its applicable
349: hard stops ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement)). A
350: finding can block current promotion only when it:
351: 
352: 1. falsifies that claim;
353: 2. exposes competing or ambiguous authority on the claim's acceptance
354:    path;
355: 3. violates applicable active authority, safety or retained accepted
356:    behaviour; or
357: 4. establishes a material architectural decision with durable
358:    consequences that forecloses an admitted Product outcome.
359: 
360: These conditions are necessary. Which of them suffice is decided as
361: follows:
362: 
363: | Consumed condition | Effect on the current promotion boundary |
364: |---|---|
365: | a valid falsification of a mandatory claim governed by a non-waivable hard stop | the boundary blocks, whatever the assigned priority or the decision cutoff |
366: | any other finding meeting one of the four conditions | the decision owner decides blocking from the exact affected claim, the governed outcome or decision the work serves ([ACTIVATION §1, Intake](ACTIVATION.md#intake)), the applicable hard stops and the Product-owned cutoff policy; below that cutoff no block follows mechanically, and an accepted residual is retained explicitly |
367: | a finding meeting none of the four conditions | it does not block |
368: | an observation outside the exact reviewed claim | repricing or re-entry input, returned as §4 states: by itself it does not widen the reviewed subject, block its bounded claim, or require a new ticket, artifact, review round or implementation increment |
369: 
370: Severity selects neither priority nor a block mechanically, and priority
371: neither erases severity nor waives a hard stop. The decision cutoff is the
372: adopting Product's policy; this member sets no cutoff (P6, P2; conserves
373: [UP-007](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/TICKET_METHOD.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-stdo-up-007)'s
374: blocking conditions). The table is new tier-1 law: it states for the
375: decision owner of any promotion boundary the rule that the predecessor's
376: [Executive promotion constraint projection](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#executive-promotion-constraint-projection)
377: states for the Executive only, which
378: [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#promotion-constraint-projection)
379: keeps as its instance. Purpose and material
380: relation: the method stated these conditions in a work carrier, a design
381: profile and the Executive profile, so an actor reconciled three texts; one
382: statement gives every review consumer the same answer, and the conditions
383: keep a bounded review from blocking on observations outside its claim
384: while a non-waivable hard stop still blocks.

386: ## 6. Conformance of realisations
387: 
388: A realisation aⱼ conforms to a specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour
389: satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract (P1) and an independent
390: judgment (P6). Several realisations may conform to one Σ; sufficiency does
391: not require unique derivation or equality with an incumbent. A weak Σ that
392: admits materially different behaviours either declares the latitude or is
393: repaired before a decision-complete design is claimed.
394: 
395: Equivalence ladder. The ladder is the list of the four claims named next,
396: each a rung; the rungs are listed, not ordered, and no rung implies
397: another. Conformance, semantic equivalence, computational equivalence and
398: categorical equivalence are separate claims with separate evidence (P1,
399: P6). Conformance establishes neither identical behaviour outside Σ nor
400: equal cost. Semantic equivalence of realisations claims that two
401: realisations, or a realisation and a declared reference outcome, have
402: identical interpreted behaviour on a stated domain, behaviour outside Σ
403: included. In this member semantic equivalence is always this equivalence
404: of realisations, not the equivalence of concepts across bounded contexts
405: that
406: [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#5-bounded-context-semantic-resolution)
407: governs, and semantic conformance, in the comparison rule below, is
408: conformance with the governing semantic basis as Σ. Computational
409: equivalence claims that two realisations compute the same function at
410: equal cost for declared workloads on a declared architecture H.
411: Categorical equivalence is a claim about categories and the maps between
412: them: FOUNDATIONS §4, Formal fragment, owns what a category or functor
413: claim must show and defines the symbols 𝒜, ℐ and 𝒞_H used here, and a
414: map's preservation of identities and composition is a further claim
415: distinct from every rung.
416: For a proposed span 𝒜 → ℐ and 𝒜 → 𝒞_H, conformance to Σ, semantic
417: equivalence and computational equivalence remain different claims.
418: A claim of categorical equivalence meets each item of the Formal fragment
419: that applies to it, as that section states them. This rung adds one
420: requirement of its own to those items: a quasi-inverse functor, and
421: natural isomorphisms between each composite of the functor with its
422: quasi-inverse and the identity functor, on a stated domain. An analogy or matching result
423: is insufficient. Evidence for one claim is not reported as a result for
424: another (§1). The ladder is new law: it keeps a matching output, an analogy
425: or a passing conformance check from being read as equivalence or as
426: preserved structure (P1, P6).
427: 
428: Layered sufficiency. A specification arranged in layers is sufficient when
429: a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer from each layer; the
430: derivation need not be unique, since different realisations may satisfy the
431: same upper layer, and the test is sufficiency, not determinism. A failure
432: to derive at any boundary is a defect of the upper layer: unclear,
433: contradictory, underspecified, not concrete or decomposable enough, or
434: polluted with accidental lower-layer detail. A boundary that can be crossed
435: only by hiding a major unresolved ambiguity is not yet sufficient even if
436: some downstream artifact can be produced. For an already accepted relation,
437: reconstruction may reuse its exact current basis and sufficient evidence
438: after checking applicability and invalidation (ACTIVATION §7);
439: reconstructability requires a correct reconstruction route, not its
440: execution at every use, grants no restart authority and does not excuse
441: stale success. The claim determines the reconstruction span; a local
442: selected function does not require recreating the whole subject. New
443: material counterexamples still challenge the affected relation (P2, P1,
444: P0; conserves the
445: [Reconstruction Litmus](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#reconstruction-litmus),
446: whose application to the method's own chain, with the diagnosis per layer,
447: is SPEC_METHOD §2).
448: 
449: Comparison. After freeze the evaluator compares the frozen result against
450: the mandatory governing semantic basis for semantic conformance or
451: equivalence. A separately held expected or reference outcome, if one exists
452: and is applicable, is optional evidence and explicitly non-authoritative;
453: semantic equivalence to it is required only where the governing basis
454: requires it. A lawful alternative construction permitted by the basis
455: passes. Subjective similarity to the basis or the reference is insufficient
456: to establish conformance or equivalence. Byte or structural identity,
457: unique derivation, determinism and incumbent equality are not generic
458: comparison criteria. A construction outside the declared competence or
459: configuration envelope cannot indict generic method sufficiency (P6, P1;

547: ### Frame qualification
548: 
549: A candidate frame ([REFERENCE_FRAME](REFERENCE_FRAME.md)) is qualified in
550: proportion to its claims (P6, P2; provenance
551: `stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#frame-qualification`).
552: The minimum evaluation asks:
553: 
554: 1. Decision test: can a competent actor produce a result in the declared
555:    algebra for representative in-domain evaluations?
556: 2. Reconstruction test: can a fresh competent actor activate the frame
557:    from the declared packet without hidden history (RF-013)?
558: 3. Sensitivity test: do changes to declared material relations affect the
559:    result where expected?
560: 4. Irrelevance test: do excluded unrelated changes leave the result stable
561:    where expected?
562: 5. Basis test: does stale, mismatched or ambiguous basis information
563:    invalidate or refuse the evaluation?
564: 6. Authority test: does frame selection preserve semantic and decision
565:    authority and the exact inherited operation authority for every
566:    material construction, transformation, admission, publication or
567:    mutation?
568: 7. Counterexample test: does the frame detect the representative
569:    historical or constructed violations it claims to cover?
570: 8. Capability test: can the declared actor class hold and operate the
571:    frame within its envelope?
572: 9. Result-consumption test: can a declared consumer use the closed result
573:    without importing hidden frame context?
574: 
575: Qualification binds the exact frame revision, actor envelope, evaluation
576: family, basis class and evidence conditions evaluated. It does not
577: generalise to an unevaluated population by naming the frame generically
578: (§1, the quantifier rule).
579: 
580: Adequate attention. The capability test asks two questions, and they are
581: evaluated separately. Whether the declared actor class can hold the frame
582: is fit: for the context dimension, the size of the selected
583: representation, measured as ACTIVATION §2 step 3 measures it, against the
584: declared capacity; the envelope's other dimensions are fitted as RF-014
585: states. Whether the actor class
586: operates the frame adequately is adequate attention, and only actual-use
587: evidence establishes it: actors of the declared class apply the frame to
588: its declared tasks under its declared conditions, and the results are
589: judged against expectations recorded from the governing sources before the
590: results are opened, by an assessor under §3 where the claim needs
591: independent assessment. A size measurement, or any byte or token
592: threshold, establishes fit and nothing about attention; a frame that fits
593: is not thereby adequately attended. Actual-use evidence binds the frame
594: revision, actor class, tasks and conditions evaluated, like the
595: qualification above, and establishes no universal attention score (§1,
596: the quantifier rule). Time, spend and other resource limits are those of
597: the selected execution binding, under the resource-limit law of
598: [ACTIVATION §6](ACTIVATION.md#6-cost-and-proportionality), not of this
599: test. The separation is new law: finite attention makes fit necessary
600: (RF-002), and only use shows that a frame that fits is applied, so a frame
601: is never qualified for attention because it fits (P0, P6).
