409: ### Technical triage, severity, priority and boundary effect
410: 
411: Technical triage is the Reviewer's assessment of one finding against the
412: exact evaluated claim and basis. Where admissible evidence and the actor's
413: capability envelope support it, the triage records (P6, P5; rc.2
414: #technical-triage-severity-priority-and-boundary-effect):
415: 
416: - the affected claim and the observed failure;
417: - severity on the Product-selected severity scale;
418: - causal assessment and confidence, the confidence being a quantified
419:   claim under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Quantified assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#quantified-assurance);
420: - blast radius and the affected users, paths or relations;
421: - an available workaround or containment;
422: - repair complexity, regression risk and material dependencies; and
423: - residual uncertainty and the evidence that would reduce it.
424: 
425: Missing causal or repair evidence stays explicit. Where the missing
426: relation can change the evaluation, the Reviewer returns `indeterminate` or
427: `out_of_frame` pressure (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results); it does not invent precision and
428: does not send work sideways to the Worker (P5).
429: 
430: Severity grades the consequence if the finding manifests. Priority orders
431: the response relative to the complete Product outcome, likelihood and
432: exposure, the current MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies,
433: cost of delay and available capacity. The Reviewer grades severity; the
434: Executive assigns priority (P6, P2).
435: 
436: The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis binds the severity scale,
437: the priority scale and the current-boundary decision cutoff, and names
438: which conditions of the governed outcome are hard stops. What a hard stop
439: is, its classes, and that it holds whatever the priority, cutoff or risk
440: appetite, so that no decision waives it, are
441: [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement) Hard stops,
442: whose classes are typical, not closed; the basis names its own
443: non-waivable hard stops, each holding as that section states. "Non-waivable hard stop" in this
444: profile and in EVALUATION §5 means such a stop. This profile imposes no
445: universal numeric scale. Severity, priority, the frame result
446: (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results) and the current-boundary effect are four distinct
447: values. When a finding can block a promotion boundary is
448: [EVALUATION §5 When a finding blocks promotion](EVALUATION.md#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion),
449: and none of the four values alone decides it (P6, P1).
450: 
451: Current-boundary effect is the Executive's recorded determination of what
452: one finding does to the current promotion boundary: it blocks it, requires
453: narrowing it, or may remain an explicit residual. It is a decision
454: projection, a state this profile declares, not a result and not a
455: disposition (§8): it maps to no core value of its own and decides nothing
456: by itself. Where it is "blocks", a condition of EVALUATION §5 holds; the
457: decision it records returns through the core only through the one
458: existing disposition the Executive then applies (ACTIVATION §3,
459: Disposition). Purpose and material relation: the record keeps the
460: Executive's reading of each finding apart from severity, priority and the
461: disposition, so a consumer can see why a boundary was held, narrowed or
462: promoted with a residual, and no field other than the disposition decides
463: acceptance (P6, P2). A hard stop or a falsified mandatory claim cannot be
464: waived by lowering priority. An observation outside the exact claim
465: boundary cannot open another review round because it carries a severe
466: label (P6, P2). How each result member projects the triage payload and
467: constrains its consumption is EVALUATION §4 (Result and triage
468: projection).
469: 
470: ### Work result
471: 
472: A work result is the Worker's closed output to its declared consumer; in
473: the coordinated branch that consumer is the Executive. It exists only after
474: a successful Worker activation. An `activation_refusal`, with the cause and
475: core value that
476: [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions) gives it,
477: returns to the assigning authority or declared result carrier and creates
478: neither a Worker activation nor a Worker result. This applies to the
479: Worker the rule that
480: [ACTIVATION §3 Admission and activation](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation)
481: states for every step (P5, P6; rc.2 #work-result).
482: 
483: The work-result values are the five values of construction availability,
484: the refinement that
485: [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability) defines for the
486: predicate "a candidate is available". ACTIVATION §3 owns their grounds,
487: maps each to exactly one core value, and states that the mapping is total
488: and exclusive after lawful activation. In this profile they are carriers,
489: not new semantic dispositions, and none of them is an assessment or an
490: acceptance of the candidate (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results). The cause that
491: selects each value is the ground ACTIVATION §3 states; this profile states
492: no ground of its own. It binds only what the Worker reports and what its
493: consumer does with each value; the core value shown with each is
494: ACTIVATION §3's (P5, P6):
495: 
496: - `candidate_ready` (`satisfied`): the consumer receives the exact
497:   candidate and its transition evidence and decides whether independent
498:   review is required (§12 step 4); the value is not `accept`;
499: - `refused` (`falsified`): the work result names the prohibition or
500:   refusal that is the value's counterexample; the Executive verifies the
501:   basis and applies the existing authority relation (§12 step 4);
502: - `incomplete` (`falsified`): the Worker's residuals and stop basis name
503:   each evaluation it did not perform, which has no result, each it
504:   performed that its evidence could not decide, which keeps its own
505:   `indeterminate`, and whether bounded execution ended first. The work
506:   result is never read as `indeterminate`, as ACTIVATION §3 states, and
507:   the Executive reactivates work only where current authority already
508:   permits it (§12 step 4);
509: - `re_entry_requested(authority)` (`out_of_frame`): the Executive returns
510:   the question to the decision owner the value names; and
511: - `re_entry_requested(basis)` (`invalid_basis`): the Executive revalidates
512:   the basis lock (§6 Drift locks) before any further activation.
513: 
514: A capability, authority, stale-basis, ambiguous-basis or topology mismatch
515: known during activation is an `activation_refusal` with its cause, never a
516: synthetic Worker result (P5, P6). Consumers choose the representation;
517: ACTIVATION §1 and §3 stay the owners of the execution relation, its
518: results and its dispositions.
519: 
520: The result references the current computed classification, supporting
521: evidence, residual judgments and original rulings through their existing
522: carriers. It does not reconstruct unchanged C/J/O at each handoff. The
523: consumer checks applicability and concrete invalidators; changed evidence
524: revises only the affected results, preserving originals and supported
525: surviving claims (ACTIVATION §7; P4b).
526: 
527: ### Exact candidate
528: 
529: An exact candidate is the subject identity that the transition evidence of
530: ACTIVATION §7 and the traceability of EVALUATION §3 require. Where generic
531: method qualification applies (EVALUATION §7), its construction result is
532: frozen before material reference exposure as that clause requires.
533: Elsewhere this profile stabilises the review subject through an immutable
534: identity or an equivalent exact-subject relation sufficient for the claimed
535: assessment. The profile creates no new lifecycle state named `frozen` (P3,
536: P6; rc.2 #exact-candidate).


METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md member_sha256=e50b4ad70451fe84882053bc0dffef6f6c0c806a5dba68ac9933aa79029fb935 lines=548-720
548: ## 6. Executive attention, evaluation and action
549: 
550: ### The three duties
551: 
552: The Executive is the frame for three inseparable duties over one governed
553: outcome (P0, P6, P2; rc.2 #executive-attention-evaluation-and-action):
554: 
555: 1. attention management: it keeps the exact outcome and basis, the
556:    Product-role map, the evaluation inventory, the dependency relation, the
557:    unresolved frontier, the actor envelopes, the current MVP or release
558:    mandate, the applicable triage policy and the residual boundary, and it
559:    selects the smallest dependency-ready activation set sufficient for the
560:    next decision within the finite actor envelopes;
561: 2. evaluation orchestration: it activates capable Workers, Reviewers or
562:    specialists, keeps their exact subjects and bases, and consumes only
563:    closed results or declared translations; and
564: 3. authorised action selection: it assigns priority, determines the effect
565:    on the current promotion boundary, applies an existing disposition, and
566:    issues only the next already-authorised activation or action.
567: 
568: The Executive does not contain the complete workspace and does not perform
569: every evaluation. It acquires no Product meaning, implementation, mutation,
570: acceptance, publication or other operation authority from the role. A
571: material effect stays owned by the actor that carries its exact operation
572: grant (P6, RF-002).
573: 
574: ### No mutation while Executive
575: 
576: An actor occupying the Executive frame modifies no candidate, Product or
577: worktree bytes and performs no implementation effect. Filesystem or tool
578: access is no exception, and neither is an edit that is small, test-only,
579: reversible or apparently obvious. Mutation requires a separately activated
580: Worker or Writer relation carrying the exact operation grant, subject and
581: write territory. A same-actor role transition is explicit and is recorded in
582: the existing work carrier before the effect; for that effect the actor is no
583: longer acting as Executive. Recording or delegating after an Executive edit
584: cannot authorise the edit retroactively (P6, P3). This prohibition is this
585: profile's, and it applies wherever the executive configuration is selected
586: ([ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration), Example; §7);
587: an operation grant covering a construction, status and checkpoint sequence
588: does not lift it
589: ([ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)).
590: 
591: ### Attention cycle
592: 
593: ```text
594: U0 = every known material evaluation not closed on the current basis
595: 
596: while U is non-empty:
597:   select a finite dependency-ready subset M that fits the assigned actors
598:   activate each member of M against the exact outcome and basis
599:   keep assurance-independent evaluations free of unclosed peer results
600:   when no other authorised decision is ready:
601:     await decision-relevant input (event-driven attention, below)
602:   record every closed result, technical triage, residual and invalidation condition
603:   apply only declared conjunctions or translations
604:   assign priority and boundary effect only under the current Product mandate
605:   invalidate affected results when the subject or basis changes
606:   update U from coverage, dependencies, conflicts and discovered materiality
607: 
608: stop only when every mandatory evaluation is closed, or governing authority
609: has explicitly retained every remaining residual consistently with the claim
610: ```
611: 
612: The cycle needs no scheduler and no frame engine (RF-016). `M` may hold
613: parallel activations. Recursion follows declared evaluation dependencies and
614: bounded refinements; it does not nest or join undifferentiated copies of
615: every frame. The Executive holds the frontier and the closed-result ledger
616: in attention, not the undocumented working context of every evaluator (P0,
617: P4b, P2).
618: 
619: Severity supplied by the Reviewer is evaluation evidence. Priority,
620: current-boundary effect, disposition and the next action are Executive
621: decisions. They stay distinct ledger entries even where a Product-defined
622: policy maps one to another (P6, RF-007).
623: 
624: Every result returns to the Executive, to a declared conjunction or to
625: another frame through an explicit declared relation. That none of them
626: activates another frame or authorises continuation by itself is
627: [ACTIVATION §1 Admission](ACTIVATION.md#admission), applied here. A consumer receives the
628: closed result and its source routes, not the child's hidden reasoning
629: context (P6, P4a; ACTIVATION §7).
630: 
631: ### Event-driven attention
632: 
633: Executive attention is event-driven by default. The Executive re-enters the
634: attention cycle for a decision-relevant closed result, a material exception
635: or changed basis, an owner request, or a declared deadline or checkpoint.
636: While Workers carry out their bounded grants and no other authorised
637: decision is ready, it waits. It does not repeatedly inspect unfinished work,
638: replay unchanged judgments or request status without a decision need (P0,
639: P2; rc.2 #event-driven-executive-attention).
640: 
641: It keeps the frontier, the return conditions and the valid evidence and
642: judgments. It refreshes affected support when a material observation
643: changes its basis, and revalidates the drift locks (below) before activation
644: and before disposition. Waiting waives no current-workspace verification,
645: evidence validity, required independent assessment, closed-result
646: consumption, or authority or closure duty (P6, P4b).
647: 
648: Where notification is unavailable or unreliable, or an actual supervision
649: obligation requires observation, the Executive uses bounded fallback
650: observation with a declared purpose, cadence or checkpoint, evidence target,
651: and stop or escalation condition. Silence proves neither progress nor
652: failure. A genuine blocker or material risk is investigated, with
653: intervention where required, within existing grants; unknown status alone
654: does not establish a stalled Worker (P5, P6).
655: 
656: Repeated no-progress observations, or returns with no new decision-relevant
657: evidence, require a bounded reassessment of the frame, grant, dependency or
658: evidence gap and a decision under existing authority. The Executive does not
659: keep polling or repeat the same repair on an unchanged basis (ACTIVATION §3,
660: Disposition). Reduced reasoning churn is not a lower-assurance path and is
661: no permission to reduce required actor capability; it introduces no
662: universal cost, budget or accounting gate (P2, P0; ACTIVATION §6).
663: 
664: ### Drift locks
665: 
666: Before activation and before disposition, the Executive revalidates five
667: locks (P3, P6, P2; rc.2 #executive-drift-locks):
668: 
669: | Lock | Holds when |
670: |---|---|
671: | outcome lock | the selected Goal, Product outcome, boundary and lawful re-entry class, the current MVP or release mandate, and the triage policy are unchanged |
672: | basis lock | the subject, authority, dependency, configuration, topology, evidence, time and candidate coordinates are exact and current |
673: | Product-role lock | the mutable Source Project, Product Definition, Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact and dependent Product identities stay distinct, and every Development Product role stays bound to its exact underlying Install |
674: | authority lock | the semantic, evaluation, operation, decision, acceptance and publication owners and grants are unchanged |
675: | coverage-and-return lock | every material evaluation and interaction is closed or an explicit residual, and every consumed result followed its declared return relation |
676: 
677: A failed lock takes the value or move its owner gives the case; this
678: profile adds none (P5, P6):
679: 
680: | Failed lock | Value or move, and its owner |
681: |---|---|
682: | changed Product meaning (outcome lock) | `re_enter` to the owning relation ([ACTIVATION §3 Disposition](ACTIVATION.md#disposition)) |
683: | stale or substituted basis, before activation (basis lock) | the activation refuses: `activation_refusal(basis)`, `invalid_basis` ([REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions)) |
684: | stale or substituted basis of an evaluation performed on it | that evaluation's own result is `invalid_basis`, or it is reactivated on the current basis ([RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)) |
685: | stale basis of a held result, before disposition | for the disposition's conjunction the component has no applicable closed result: a gap, never relabelled `invalid_basis` and never counted as returned ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results), Stale results) |
686: | missing material scope | `out_of_frame`: at activation, as [ACTIVATION §3 Admission and activation](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation) states; for an evaluation, on the ground [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) gives, an undeclared material relation or capability |
687: | missing operation authority (authority lock) | the activation refuses, `activation_refusal(authority)` (REFERENCE_FRAME §5), or the effect is refused |
688: | an unresolved mandatory conflict (coverage-and-return lock) | the conjunction is not `satisfied`; the conflict survives every join (FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results, Survival) |
689: 
690: The Executive repairs none of these by making its own frame larger (P5,
691: P6).
692: 
693: ### Product-chain basis
694: 
695: A governed outcome may concern one Product or an explicit directed chain of
696: Products. Its basis records the distinct role of every mutable Source
697: Project, current Product Definition, exact candidate checkpoint, Release
698: Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, Development Product, dependent Product and
699: composition edge. Each Development Product role binds one exact underlying
700: Install identity. Each edge names its source and target roles, its governing
701: authority and contracts, its lifecycle, its evidence boundary, its refusal
702: and its invalidation (P3, P6; rc.2 #product-chain-basis; the Product-role
703: map in the basis is PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7, the lineage objects FOUNDATIONS
704: §2).
705: 
706: An installed Product may lawfully build its own successor or another
707: Product. That Development Product stays distinct from the mutable Source
708: Project and from the Product being authored. Directory nesting, shared code,
709: shared actors, source imports, tool reachability, matching labels or equal
710: outputs create no Product identity, composition edge or authority transfer
711: (P3, P1).
712: 
713: Exact basis does not make a Source Project immutable. A Worker may
714: cumulatively mutate the exact Source Project and write territory named by
715: its operation grant. A Reviewer evaluates an exact candidate checkpoint
716: produced from that workspace. A repair advances the workspace, creates a new
717: candidate and invalidates the affected results. A released Product, Release
718: Cut or exact Install stays immutable under its own lifecycle law and imposes
719: no immutability on the Source Project constructing a successor (P3, P4b).

843: ## 8. Derived Executive frame
844: 
845: The Executive frame, in the shape of a frame declaration (REFERENCE_FRAME
846: §13; P6, P0; rc.2 #derived-executive-frame):
847: 
848: | Frame element | Executive |
849: |---|---|
850: | evaluation family | Is the bounded outcome and execution basis authorised? Which frames and actors are capable? Is a returned result exact and current? Which priority, current-boundary effect, disposition and next action follow from the current Product mandate? |
851: | subject and basis | the complete selected method cut; the exact Goals, Product, requirements, design and work authority; the current MVP or release mandate; the current workspace and checkpoint; open findings and their technical triage; the Product-selected triage policy; the proxy grant where one is used |
852: | material manifold | outcome, mandate, affected causal cone, evaluation inventory, frame configuration, actor envelopes, evidence obligations, returned results and technical triage, priority, boundary effect, re-entry owners and the boundary of already-authorised continuation |
853: | coordinates | exact method, project, outcome, mandate, authority, checkpoint, candidate, evidence, finding, triage-policy and actor identities |
854: | governing invariants | RF-001 to RF-017 (REFERENCE_FRAME §3); the execution relation and intake of ACTIVATION §1 with the design profile's bounded-frame conservation laws; applicable identity, carrier, assurance and release law |
855: | authority | the existing Product or work frame-set and decision authority, or its admitted bounded proxy; no operation or other authority arises from the label |
856: | evidence | live authority surfaces, frame results, Reviewer technical triage, exact candidate identity, transition evidence, coverage residuals and specialist results |
857: | capability envelope | enough method, Product, release or MVP, authority, workspace, triage and actor-selection competence to configure, prioritise and dispose the bounded evaluation; implementation expertise may be delegated to specialist frames |
858: | exclusions | candidate, Product or worktree byte mutation and implementation effects while occupying the frame; implementation ownership; silently rewriting Reviewer evidence or severity; claiming independent review without a qualifying activation; semantic reconstruction owned elsewhere; disposition outside the admitted grant |
859: | result | one core result (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results), the assigned priority and current-boundary effect, and one existing disposition (ACTIVATION §3 Disposition) where the basis is decidable |
860: | invalidation | a material change of method, authority, outcome, mandate, triage policy, checkpoint, candidate, evidence, finding, capability or topology |
861: 
862: The frame adds no `authorize` or `no_action` disposition. Activation is the
863: `activate` function of REFERENCE_FRAME §5; candidate disposition stays
864: exactly `accept`, `local_repair`, `re_enter` or `reject` (ACTIVATION §3,
865: Disposition). Priority and current-boundary effect are decision
866: projections, neither core results nor dispositions. If the Executive cannot
867: rely on a supplied severity or technical assessment, it reactivates a
868: capable evaluation or keeps the uncertainty; it never silently rewrites the
869: Reviewer result (P5, P6).
870: 
871: ### Steel-thread delivery
872: 
873: The Executive sequences delivery around a steel thread: the smallest real,
874: runnable path from a supported Product entry to a material outcome through
875: the selected composition. The path is established early and widened in
876: bounded increments; where it already exists, the affected thread is extended
877: or revalidated. Increments are chosen for consequential uncertainty,
878: dependency and interface reach, and failure impact (P2; rc.2
879: #steel-thread-delivery; the generic sequencing heuristic is SPEC_METHOD §8).
880: The steel thread is this profile's selected strategy under the
881: construction relation ([ACTIVATION §1 Strategy](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation)):
882: its rationale is early feedback on the end-to-end composition at the cost
883: of later widening; other strategies remain lawful for other
884: configurations; no superiority over them is claimed, and the rationale
885: states the objective the selection serves and its cost (P2, P6).
886: 
887: Early end-to-end and integration evidence prunes incompatible construction
888: choices before they spread; it settles the exercised interfaces, keeps
889: working composition, and concentrates construction on unresolved
890: obligations. Each passing thread establishes only the relations and
891: conditions actually exercised; untested branches, interaction combinations,
892: and refusal and recovery paths keep their material proof obligations.
893: Settled construction decisions are revisited when material counterevidence
894: invalidates their basis (P6, P4b).
895: 
896: During construction, focused deterministic regression and targeted
897: judgment probes resolve material uncertainty, and unit evidence covers
898: module-owned laws under the testing frames (ASSURANCE §7). Substantial,
899: resource-intensive user-acceptance cycles are scheduled near release or
900: when a bounded capability is complete enough to qualify; an early focused
901: user probe stays appropriate where it decides a material outcome
902: uncertainty (P2, ACTIVATION §7 proof cadence).
903: 
904: The product testing frames keep their distinct claims and govern the
905: necessary scenarios, independent assessments and repetitions. Qualified
906: results are reused while their exact subject and basis stay valid; affected
907: assurance is rerun when a material change invalidates it. The Executive
908: selects this sequence under the existing mandate and activates construction
909: only through the existing operation grants (P6, P4b).

912: 
913: (P6, P0; rc.2 #derived-worker-frame)
914: 
915: | Frame element | Worker |
916: |---|---|
917: | evaluation family | Can the exact authorised outcome be constructed through the smallest coherent causal cone while preserving every affected governing relation and disposing of competing paths? |
918: | subject and basis | the sufficient execution intake of ACTIVATION §1, with the accepted design-to-execution basis of the design profile where it applies |
919: | material manifold | affected entities, lifecycles, transformations, authorities, capabilities, algorithms, inputs, outputs, dependencies, interaction seams, failure boundaries and proof obligations |
920: | coordinates | exact activation, source checkpoint, workspace, inputs, dependencies, configuration, actor envelope, outputs, candidate and evidence identities |
921: | governing invariants | the complete selected method and project relations material to the affected cone; ACTIVATION §1 owns construction and self-review |
922: | authority | inherited bounded construction or transformation authority and self-review only; mutation only where the exact inherited owner grant names the subject and write territory; no admission, publication, independent acceptance, frame-set revision or inferred next action |
923: | evidence | live implementation, tests and test source, analysis, generated artifacts, installed or operational behaviour where claimed, reconstruction, mutations and exact transition evidence |
924: | capability envelope | the declared method, domain, implementation, tool, access and finite-context competence the causal cone requires |
925: | exclusions | upstream semantic change, unauthorised cone expansion, self-acceptance, hidden competing paths, and advancing after returning the work result |
926: | result | exactly one work-result value, which carries the one core value ACTIVATION §3 maps it to for "a candidate is available" (§5 Work result); each evaluation the Worker performed keeps its own core result (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results) |
927: | invalidation | a material change of intake, basis, checkpoint, dependency, configuration, capability or topology |
928: 
929: `candidate_ready` binds the exact candidate and the transition evidence of
930: ACTIVATION §7. It is not `accept`. Green tests are evidence only for the
931: relations their production and test semantics actually exercise (P6;
932: EVALUATION §1).
933: 
934: The Worker label grants no mutation authority. An effectful Worker may
935: mutate only the exact subject and write territory named by its inherited
936: construction or transformation grant; missing, ambiguous or out-of-territory
937: mutation authority refuses the effect (P6).
938: 
939: Read scope follows the complete causal cone and may exceed write territory
940: within the declared access grant. A narrow mutation grant does not justify
941: omitting a material producer, consumer or governing owner from inspection.
942: A repair needed outside the territory is returned to its owner;
943: understanding a relation grants no cross-boundary effect (P0, P6;
944: ACTIVATION §1, Execution unit).

946: ## 10. Derived Reviewer frame
947: 
948: (P6, P5; rc.2 #derived-reviewer-frame)
949: 
950: | Frame element | Reviewer |
951: |---|---|
952: | evaluation family | Is this the exact claimed subject and basis? Does it satisfy the applicable method and project relations without competing authority, proof masking or an unevaluated composition boundary? For each finding, which evidence-bound severity and technical implications follow? |
953: | subject and basis | exact candidate, claim, governing method and project authority, scope, exclusions, evidence population, Product-selected severity scale, review carrier and declared independence conditions |
954: | material manifold | claimed relations; causal producers and consumers; authority seams; competing paths; failure, recovery, installed and reconstruction surfaces where claimed; test and fixture semantics; historical counterexamples; a finding's cause, blast radius, workaround, repair complexity, regression risk and uncertainty where supportable |
955: | coordinates | exact candidate, source basis, authority revision, configuration, dependency, evidence population, severity scale, installed subject, review time and Reviewer identity |
956: | governing invariants | RF-001 to RF-017; the execution relation (ACTIVATION §1 and §3); independence and traceability (EVALUATION §3); assurance boundary and qualification freeze (EVALUATION §1, §3 and §7); applicable Product, design, identity and release law |
957: | authority | bounded evaluation only; review access yields no construction, transformation, admission, publication, mutation, decision, disposition or next-activation authority |
958: | evidence | independently acquired live authority, candidate implementation, tests, artifacts, history, operational evidence, mutations, replay or reconstruction, and reproduced observations material to the claim and the technical triage |
959: | capability envelope | declared method, domain, implementation, assurance, technical-triage, tool, access, context, counterexample-search and independence competence |
960: | exclusions | editing the candidate, implementing a repair, assigning priority, disposing the release or MVP boundary, selecting the next action, substituting the Worker's summary, assurance-owned semantic reconstruction, flattening unbound evidence, silent scope expansion |
961: | result | one core result with findings, counterexamples, evidence-bound technical triage and residuals sufficient for the Executive to assign priority and apply the existing disposition where the basis is decidable |
962: | invalidation | a material change of candidate, authority, basis, evidence population, severity scale, dependency, configuration, scope or independence |
963: 
964: When independent review is required, and what makes a claimed review
965: traceable, are
966: [TICKETS UP-007](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007),
967: with the further boundaries a governing basis adds; what counts as
968: independent is [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment);
969: EVALUATION §1, §3 and §7 decide the exact assurance boundary and the
970: qualification freeze. This profile adds no universal review round and no
971: new independence test (P6).
972: 
973: ACTIVATION §1 and §3 stay the owners of assessment and disposition. This
974: profile uses an activated Reviewer result as independent live-surface
975: evaluation input and, in the coordinated branch, the Executive as the
976: authorised assessor or proxy that applies the one existing disposition. It
977: creates no second verdict or disposition family (P6, P5).
978: 
979: The Reviewer may assess likely repair complexity and regression risk
980: without becoming the repair owner. Where cause, blast radius, workaround or
981: repair risk cannot be supported inside the activation, the result records
982: that uncertainty instead of manufacturing a complete triage (P5).
983: 
984: Tests are inside the Reviewer's manifold when their code, fixtures,
985: mutations, environment or interpretation can change the proof claim; a
986: passing result is not relied on in place of reviewing those semantics (P6,
987: EVALUATION §1).
988: 
989: Each finding binds a violated property, a supported entry or state, the
990: governing operating or threat model and a credible causal path. The same
991: conditions apply to retained guards and acceptance predicates as to new
992: findings. An excluded threat alone gives no retention claim; a proposed
993: wider threat model re-enters its owner. Internal location alone does not
994: establish trust, and hypothetical hostility alone does not establish
995: applicability. The actual untrusted-input, mutable-state, authority and
996: effect checks the supported model requires are retained. A suggested repair
997: becomes an obligation only through its proper owner (P6, P2, P5).

1116: ## 12. Complete engagement transition
1117: 
1118: The steps below describe the coordinated branch selected under §3. Direct
1119: Worker engagement keeps the same sufficient intake, work-result algebra,
1120: closure conditions and owner boundaries without inserting an Executive
1121: appointment, or a review that no applicable condition requires (P0, P6;
1122: rc.2 #complete-engagement-transition).
1123: 
1124: ### 1. Existing authority selects the basis
1125: 
1126: Goals, Product, requirements, accepted design, a ticket, release law or an
1127: admitted bounded proxy selects the outcome and the work authority under its
1128: existing owner. The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis
1129: (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7) projects that decision (P6; rc.2
1130: #1-existing-authority-selects-the-basis).
1131: 
1132: ### 2. Executive activates Worker
1133: 
1134: In the coordinated branch the Executive applies `activate` (REFERENCE_FRAME
1135: §5) to the sufficient execution intake of ACTIVATION §1. The packet is
1136: REFERENCE_FRAME §11; for this step it identifies (P0, P6; rc.2
1137: #2-executive-activates-worker):
1138: 
1139: - the selected complete method and project authority;
1140: - the exact governed outcome and checkpoint;
1141: - the affected causal relation set and the governing invariants;
1142: - the selected computational relations and specialist frames;
1143: - where testing evidence is required: the testing claims, exact subjects,
1144:   frame topology, material combination populations, ordinary paths,
1145:   oracles and forbidden-path exclusions (ASSURANCE §7 to §9);
1146: - the Worker's authority and capability envelope, and, where mutation is
1147:   authorised, the exact inherited operation grant, subject and write
1148:   territory;
1149: - the evidence and qualification obligations;
1150: - exclusions, prohibited competing paths, stop conditions and re-entry
1151:   conditions; and
1152: - the exact bounded action already authorised.
1153: 
1154: If activation detects a known capability, authority, subject, basis or
1155: topology mismatch, it returns `activation_refusal` directly to the
1156: Executive, with the cause and core value REFERENCE_FRAME §5 gives it. No
1157: Worker frame is active, no Worker evaluation occurs, and the
1158: Executive does not manufacture a Worker result to represent the failed
1159: activation (P5, P6).
1160: 
1161: ### 3. Worker returns to Executive
1162: 
1163: Every coordinated Worker activation ends in one closed work result sent to
1164: the Executive; direct work uses its declared result consumer (P5, P6; rc.2
1165: #3-worker-returns-to-executive):
1166: 
1167: ```text
1168: WorkerResult
1169:   = candidate_ready(exact_subject, transition_evidence, residuals)
1170:   | refused(reason, authority, evidence)
1171:   | incomplete(residuals, evidence, stop_basis)
1172:   | re_entry_requested(owner, material_relation, evidence)
1173: ```
1174: 
1175: The notation explains and mandates no schema. The material relation of
1176: `re_entry_requested` names its cause, authority or basis, which is part of
1177: the value. Each value maps to exactly one core value for "a candidate is
1178: available" under
1179: [ACTIVATION §3 Construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability),
1180: read as in §5 Work result; the mapping applies only after lawful
1181: activation. The Worker does not send a candidate directly into an
1182: implicitly active Reviewer. It stops after returning the result (P5,
1183: P6).
1184: 
1185: ### 4. Executive evaluates the work result
1186: 
1187: For `refused`, `incomplete` or `re_entry_requested`, the Executive verifies
1188: the exact basis and applies the existing authority relation. It records the
1189: applicable disposition, or reactivates work only where current authority
1190: already permits that action. None of these variants is accepted progress
1191: because work occurred (P6, P5; rc.2 #4-executive-evaluates-the-work-result).
1192: 
1193: Whatever the variant, an effect of uncertain completion, one the work
1194: result names `completion_unknown` or names `not_effected` with its end not
1195: established ([ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects)), is
1196: reconciled under
1197: [ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart), sufficiently for
1198: the next dependent action, before work is reactivated, the effect is
1199: repeated or any action that depends on it is taken (P5, P6).
1200: 
1201: For `candidate_ready`, the Executive verifies the exact subject and decides
1202: whether independent assessment is required. It applies the boundaries at
1203: which this method requires it,
1204: [TICKETS UP-007](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007);
1205: the execution relation's assessment where required (ACTIVATION §1); method
1206: qualification ([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#7-qualification-of-frames-and-of-the-method));
1207: and the further boundaries the governing basis adds, as
1208: [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment) permits: Product,
1209: release, risk or the admitted work contract. What counts as independent is
1210: EVALUATION §3's. Green aggregate status cannot satisfy this step when a
1211: required user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration, unit or negative-path
1212: result is missing, bound to another subject, or contradicted by a material
1213: frame result (P6; ASSURANCE §10).

1216:

1219: transition evidence and any mandatory specialist results, and applies the
1220: disposition within its decision envelope. Self-review stays Worker
1221: evidence; the disposition does not relabel it as independent (P6; rc.2
1222: #5a-candidate-does-not-require-independent-review).

1234:   combinatorial and negative-path frame results, with their exact claims and
1235:   populations;

1237: - the Reviewer's capability and independence envelope; and
1238: - invalidation and stop conditions.
1239:

1263: assessor there is the Reviewer and the decision owner is the Executive. The
1264: Reviewer returns to the Executive, not to the Worker, and returns no
1265: disposition; a recommendation is evidence only (EVALUATION §4). It does not
1266: edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation (P6; rc.2

1270: 
1271: The Executive verifies that every consumed result is still bound to the

1291: read with the Executive as the decision owner; this profile restates none

1414: ## 16. Adoption or project-defined configuration
1415: 
1416: ### Existing authority selects the configuration
1417: 
1418: Two relations stay apart here. Adopting this profile for a Product is
1419: the Product authority's act, recorded in its Project Reference-Frame Basis:
1420: inclusion in a method cut makes the profile available, and only Product
1421: authority adopts it
1422: ([PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis)).
1423: Admitting a frame configuration, this profile's executive configuration or
1424: another, for the decisions it makes follows the rule of
1425: [ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration), Admission of a
1426: configuration: the smallest existing authority that owns each material
1427: decision admits it, and admission creates no new authority over it. That
1428: rule leaves to the profile which authority owns which decision; this
1429: section is that binding for the executive configuration (P6, P2; rc.2
1430: #existing-authority-selects-the-configuration):
1431: 
1432: - Goals or admitted work authority own bounded work selection;
1433: - Product owns Product-wide capability or acceptance meaning;
1434: - requirements own constitutional behaviour;
1435: - accepted design owns realisation structure and specialist design frames;
1436: - identity and release owners keep their declared decisions; and
1437: - an explicitly bounded proxy acts only inside its existing grant
1438:   ([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), Proxy
1439:   limit).
1440: 
1441: The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7)
1442: cites every material source of the configuration and does not collapse
1443: them into a new local-axiom authority (P6).
1444: 
1445: ### Adopt this baseline
1446: 
1447: A baseline-adoption projection records inside that Product-owned basis
1448: (P6, P3; rc.2 #adopt-this-baseline):
1449: 
1450: - the exact selected complete method, REFERENCE_FRAME and profile
1451:   identities;
1452: - the existing authority admitting adoption;
1453: - the governed workspace, Product scope, outcome, basis and time;
1454: - local Executive, Worker and Reviewer capability envelopes and
1455:   actor-binding rules;
1456: - generic family declarations or authoritative acquisition paths, with an
1457:   authority-bound non-material or explicit residual disposition for each of
1458:   the twelve families of §11;
1459: - specialist-frame declarations or authoritative acquisition paths;
1460: - where testing evidence is material: testing-frame declarations, exact
1461:   Product and module claims, ordinary-path identities, combinatorial
1462:   populations, the scenario matrix, oracles and the forbidden-path
1463:   inventory (ASSURANCE §7 to §9);
1464: - local subject, evidence, checkpoint and review-result coordinates;
1465: - the coverage ledger and the accepted residual boundary; and
1466: - invalidation and frame-set revision conditions.
1467: 
1468: ### Define a project configuration
1469: 
1470: A project may define different frames, names, overlaps, sequences and actor
1471: bindings. The defining Product, requirement, Goals or accepted-design
1472: authority records (P6, P2; rc.2 #define-a-project-configuration;
1473: REFERENCE_FRAME §4):
1474: 
1475: - the exact method and project basis;
1476: - the known evaluation inventory;
1477: - each frame declaration and capability envelope;
1478: - semantic, evaluation, operation where material, and decision authority;
1479: - intentional overlap, separately activated evaluations and required
1480:   assurance independence;
1481: - the conjunction, translation and composition actually used;
1482: - the explanation of the allocation, with its material resource limits and
1483:   failure assumptions, that ACTIVATION §1 Configuration requires of every
1484:   configuration;
1485: - the mapping to the applicable construction, assessment, disposition,
1486:   identity and release obligations;
1487: - coverage and residual uncertainty; and
1488: - re-entry, invalidation and revision conditions.
1489: 
1490: A project configuration need not keep the labels Executive, Worker and
1491: Reviewer or map one local frame to each. It keeps every applicable method
1492: relation and identifies how its evaluations cover the claims it makes. It
1493: is evaluated against its task, its dependencies, its actors' limits, the
1494: authority it applies and the required assurance, as ACTIVATION §1
1495: Configuration states, never by its labels, its topology or its difference
1496: from this profile. A local axioms document may carry the accepted
1497: configuration; its authority is the cited Goals, Product, requirement or
1498: accepted-design decision, not the document's category (P6, P1).
1499: 
1500: ### Extension versus replacement
1501: 
1502: Adding domain or specialist frames, additional separately activated or
1503: assurance-independent coverage, or local evidence coordinates extends this
1504: profile. Changing the material Executive, Worker, Reviewer, handoff,
1505: independence or disposition configuration creates a project-defined
1506: profile (P6; rc.2 #extension-versus-replacement).
1507: 
1508: Neither choice amends the method's execution law. A project that
1509: intentionally departs from that law records a separate method basis or a
1510: non-conformance; it does not describe the departure as local frame
1511: selection (P6, EVALUATION §6).
1512: 
1513: ## 17. Actor binding and independence
1514: 
1515: Frames and actors are separate identities: activation binds an actor to
1516: a frame ([ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration)). In
1517: this configuration, as
1518: [ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)
1519: permits for any configuration, one actor may occupy several frames across
1520: different activations where authority and any claimed independence are
1521: preserved. Humans, agents, deterministic tools or mixed configurations may
1522: occupy them. The profile prescribes no actor count (P3, P6, RF-016; rc.2
1523: #actor-binding-and-independence).
1524: 
1525: Where independent review is required, the activation records the exact
1526: subject and verdict carrier, which
1527: [TICKETS UP-007](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007)
1528: requires for a traceable verdict, and
1529: [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment) decides what
1530: counts as independent: the Reviewer is not the author of that subject,
1531: and a fresh context of the author is still the author. For generic method
1532: qualification,
1533: EVALUATION §7 adds its declared capability, configuration, comparison
1534: basis, reference-exposure and freeze conditions (P6).
1535: 
1536: An Executive may inspect a subject to adjudicate a result. That inspection
1537: does not become an additional independent Reviewer result because the actor
1538: used reviewer-like tools (P6, P1).

52: ## 2. Ontology
53: 
54: | Term | Definition | Requires |
55: |---|---|---|
56: | Subject | the thing a claim, representation or transformation is about; exact, with inventory and bytes or semantic addresses | P3 |
57: | Representation | bytes, text, a model or a program standing for a subject; equal representations do not establish equal meaning | P1 |
58: | Interpretation | a declared contract from representation to meaning within a context; says which distinctions a consumer may rely on and which are residual | P1 |
59: | Context | the declared scope under which an interpretation holds: subject, definitions, basis, admissible observations | P1 |
60: | Outcome U | a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval; adequacy of a transformation is judged against it | P2 |
61: | Object O | a subject with scoped identity (authority, kind, value), a boundary, current state and declared material relations; identity survives admissible state and encoding change | P3 |
62: | Actor | whoever performs a step within a declared capability envelope (context, attention, time, capability); a role is a relation an actor occupies, not a kind of actor, and which roles exist is set by a configuration ([ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration)), not by this definition | P0, P6 |
63: | Step | one bounded unit of work: intake, selected context, grant, execution, output | P0 |
64: | Step-produced fact | a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be re-acquired from declared sources; an observation reproducible from declared sources is re-acquirable and is not one | P0, P4b |
65: | Claim | an assertion with subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier | P6 |
66: | Evidence | the exact observations or artifacts admitted to evaluate a claim on a basis; each carries provenance, subject identity, basis and scope; evidence becomes neither semantic truth nor decision authority by being available inside a frame ([What creates no authority](#authority-kinds)) | P6 |
67: | Judgment | a recorded evaluation over an unchanged subject, with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation | P6 |
68: | Authority | an identity-bearing permission to operate or to dispose acceptance within a scope; its kinds, and what creates none, are defined under Authority kinds below | P6 |
69: | Residual | a material uncertainty, omission, loss or unproven relation that remains until an authorised disposition | P4b |
70: | Basis | the exact state a step, claim, result or evaluation binds: every version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration or evidence coordinate whose change can alter it; immutable, or moving with a declared way of detecting advancement and a declared condition for reevaluation; mixed bases need an explicit composite relation | P6, P3 |
71: | Material | of a relation: its lawful change can change an evaluation's result, invalidate its basis, change the admissible evidence, change who may perform a material operation, or change who may decide the evaluation or a material operation; of an uncertainty or closure: likewise; materiality is evaluation-relative, so a relation material in one frame may be irrelevant in another; the relation family of ACTIVATION §2 is the material relations of a step | P2, P6 |


METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md member_sha256=fd2d895f90eb39bda0950c1c7ff02057ef5d8ae73fcbc5b3203f7e99081d6e3f lines=101-227
101: ### Frame objects
102: 
103: The reference frame and the objects it binds are first-class in this
104: corpus. Each is defined here once; [REFERENCE_FRAME](REFERENCE_FRAME.md)
105: states the laws over them and [ACTIVATION](ACTIVATION.md) the step that
106: activates one. Provenance for this subsection and the three that follow is
107: `stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#definitions`
108: and its child sections.
109: 
110: | Term | Definition | Requires |
111: |---|---|---|
112: | Evaluation | a declared question whose admissible result family, evidence basis, decision authority and, where it performs a material action, operation authority are known; it may ask for a judgment, prediction, construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification or action recommendation | P6, P2 |
113: | Evaluation family | evaluations that need the same material-relation manifold, authority basis and result algebra; similar wording does not prove that two evaluations share a family | P1, P2 |
114: | Workspace | the bounded body of material reasoned over or acted upon, which may include constitutional sources, domain assets, designs, implementations, tools, runtime state, evidence, historical records, external dependencies and human decisions; broader than a repository, which is one possible carrier | P3 |
115: | Material-relation manifold | the finite, jointly interpretable set of variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities, observations and exclusions an evaluation family needs; a bounded relation space whose coordinate charts may overlap; no geometric mathematics or runtime abstraction is implied | P0, P2 |
116: | Coordinate | the complete local position from which a value, event, decision, observation or action is interpreted: the basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority information the evaluation requires; equal names, values, shapes, locations or apparent topology positions do not establish coordinate equality, which follows a declared relation | P1, P3 |
117: | Topology | the relation structure among the material entities, capabilities, authorities, lifecycle state spaces, adjacencies and seams visible to a frame at one basis; a frame need not hold the workspace's complete topology; a state-value change preserves the frame topology only when it preserves every such entity, relation, lifecycle, authority, capability, adjacency and seam, and a transition that changes any of them is a topology mutation that may invalidate the frame's coordinates | P3 |
118: | Capability envelope | the competence, context capacity, tools, access, applicable evaluation- or assurance-independence conditions and configuration required to activate a frame and perform its evaluations; the same frame may be usable by one actor and unusable by another; actor capability may justify a different frame size or activation sequence and can neither waive an invariant nor widen authority | P0, P6 |
119: | Reference frame | a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations required to perform one declared evaluation family over a stated basis; its components are the frame tuple below | P0 |
120: | Activated frame | one frame declaration bound to an exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; a reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct | P3, P6 |
121: | Frame set | the human-declared family of frames available for a governed outcome or workspace; it may intentionally hold overlaps, alternatives, specialist frames, broad exploratory frames and separately activated assurance frames; it is not required to be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology | P6 |
122: | Active frame configuration | the set of frame activations and declared result relations used for one evaluation or decision; one frame, or several disjoint, overlapping or composed frames; separately activated evaluations may be disjoint or overlapping | P4a |
123: | Lens | a reusable family of questions applied across a frame configuration; authority, capability and reuse, temporal behaviour, transport and proof are lenses when named abstractly; a lens becomes a frame only when instantiated with a bounded evaluation, basis, material manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra and capability envelope | P2 |
124: | Role, persona, abstraction, component | a role allocates responsibility or authority, and the authority comes only from an admitted grant: naming a role or a frame grants none (Authority kinds below, What creates no authority); a persona alters an actor's approach or salience; an abstraction hides or contracts detail; a component is a structural part of a subject; each may help construct or activate a frame and none is a reference frame by identity alone; one component may appear in several frames and one frame may cross several components | P3, P6 |
125: 
126: ### Authority kinds
127: 
128: Authority takes these kinds (P6): frame-set authority, the human authority
129: that declares or accepts a project frame set; semantic authority, the
130: owner of meaning for a material relation; evaluation authority, the role
131: permitted to perform an evaluation; operation authority, the owner-issued
132: grant to construct, transform, admit, publish or mutate a material subject
133: where an evaluation performs such an operation; decision authority, the
134: role permitted to accept, reject or otherwise dispose a result; and actor
135: identity, the human, agent, tool or process performing the work, which is
136: an identity and not an authority. These may coincide in a lawful case and
137: never collapse by default. A read-only evaluation declares no operation
138: authority; an effectful evaluation inherits the exact operation grant from
139: its existing owner, and the frame does not create that grant (P6, P3).
140: 
141: What creates no authority. Authority of any kind exists only by an
142: admitted grant or an explicit authority decision of its owner, with an
143: identifiable basis. None of the following mints, widens, transfers or
144: reconstructs semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority (P6,
145: P3):
146: 
147: - actor identity, an actor's capability, its tools or its access;
148: - a name, label, display label, status label, role name, capability
149:   string, locator, file name or path;
150: - declaring, naming, selecting, activating or executing a frame, or
151:   occupying a role;
152: - implementation reachability, a reachable code path or an available
153:   operation;
154: - the shape of evidence or of a payload, or the availability of evidence
155:   inside a frame;
156: - a passing check, a successful step, a completed review or a count of
157:   any of them;
158: - copying, interpreting, encoding, evaluating, transporting, projecting,
159:   compressing, importing or acquiring material;
160: - drafting, admitting or retaining a work contract, beyond what its owner
161:   has admitted;
162: - composition, delegation, adapters, wrappers and registries, which may
163:   restrict admitted authority or carry it faithfully, and never widen its
164:   scope, add a role, increase its cardinality or change its kind.
165: 
166: Elevation, transfer, split, merge, proxy grant, revocation and retirement
167: each need an explicit authority decision with an identifiable basis. A
168: member that names an instance of this list for its own domain cites this
169: paragraph and adds only the instance.
170: 
171: Proxy limit. Human authority may act directly, or through an explicitly
172: admitted bounded proxy where the governing identity and authority law
173: permits it; proxy identity and human-authority identity stay distinct
174: (P6, P3). A proxy acts only inside its existing grant. It cannot change
175: the governing outcome's meaning, the requirements, the governing authority
176: or the accepted design; such a change re-enters at its owning relation.
177: Proxy authority does not make a constructor's self-review independent,
178: confers no unrelated runtime or domain authority, and does not replace
179: direct human acceptance where the governing product or release law
180: requires it. The contents of a proxy grant are
181: [IDENTITY §6](IDENTITY.md#6-authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004)'s,
182: and the decisions a proxy may take inside a step are
183: [ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)'s.
184: 
185: Purpose and material relation of the list and the proxy limit: each
186: member that names what cannot create authority decides the same question,
187: so one list keeps the answer the same in every member, and a capability,
188: a label or a passing check can never be read as a permission (P6).
189: 
190: ### Disjointness and independence
191: 
192: Three relations stay distinct (P6, P1). Frame disjointness is structural:
193: two frames share no material variable, coordinate, evidence or result
194: dependency for the declared evaluations. Evaluation independence is
195: procedural: separately activated evaluations neither consume nor influence
196: one another's unclosed working results, although they may inspect the same
197: subject, overlap in their manifolds and later supply closed results to one
198: conjunction. Assurance independence is claim-relative: the governing
199: assurance law states the non-authorship, evidence-acquisition,
200: reference-exposure, actor and configuration separation a verdict needs to
201: count as independent assurance (EVALUATION §3). Disjoint frames need not
202: be independently evaluated; independently activated evaluations need not
203: be disjoint; and the unqualified word "independent" establishes none of
204: the three.
205: 
206: ### The frame tuple
207: 
208: A reference frame F is the tuple ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩
209: (P0): Q the evaluation family; B the workspace and topology basis; M the
210: material-relation manifold; C the coordinate and equality law; I the
211: applicable invariant set; A the authority relation; E the admissible
212: evidence and provenance law; X the exclusion and prohibited-assumption set;
213: R the closed result algebra (§4 [Results](#results), or a refinement mapped
214: into it); J the invalidation and rechart
215: condition; K the actor capability envelope; and D the optional set of
216: declared dependencies, overlaps, inputs and outputs involving other frames.
217: The tuple specifies the relation; it is not a required schema or runtime
218: carrier (P2). Operationally a frame is an evaluation contract that defines
219: the finite attention scope one evaluation family requires. A prompt, a
220: context packet, a symbolic program or any other representation is a
221: projection of an activated frame, not the frame (P1). A frame is bound
222: when every material coordinate above resolves to an exact source, subject,
223: basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and
224: invalidation condition; the binding may be expressed entirely in
225: source-linked prose, and representation cannot create, widen or replace it
226: (P3, P6).

251: The governing rules: a mutable source workspace is not called a product;
252: when a released product acts as builder substrate, the exact install is
253: bound as a development product without confusing it with the product being
254: authored; an immutable release cut or installed product is not confused
255: with the mutable source project building the next cut; the product
256: definition is the surface of a source project, not the released product
257: artifact; products may depend on other products; installed products may
258: build the next version of themselves or other products. The compiler
259: analogy is the intended model: bootstrap source, release P0, install P0,
260: use P0 to build the source for P1, release P1. The taxonomy is load-bearing:
261: blurred, dependency and self-hosting errors compound quickly and are
262: expensive to unwind. SPEC_METHOD §6 applies these objects to lineage and
263: release.

267: `stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/RELEASE_METHOD.md#release-identities`).

269: possible successor; it is non-operative for released consumers. A release

271: release cut binds, described by that cut's release-scoped claims; a
272: carrier that holds it does not thereby make co-located material a
273: member. A version-line selector is a mutable
274: alias naming the highest-ordinal published release cut on one version
275: line of one project; it is convenient discovery, not immutable identity,
276: and not sufficient as an exact basis ([RELEASE §1](RELEASE.md#1-context-and-position)
277: states which).
278: Equal version text does not collapse these objects. A selector or a
279: mutable carrier may move; a release cut never moves. RELEASE §2 realises

METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md member_sha256=fd2d895f90eb39bda0950c1c7ff02057ef5d8ae73fcbc5b3203f7e99081d6e3f lines=790-940
790: ### Results
791: 
792: Every performed evaluation returns one value of the core result algebra,
793: directly or as a refined value mapped into it (P5):
794: 
795: | Value | Meaning |
796: |---|---|
797: | `satisfied` | the declared predicate holds on the exact basis |
798: | `falsified` | a declared counterexample defeats it |
799: | `indeterminate` | the available admissible evidence cannot decide it |
800: | `out_of_frame` | the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or capability |
801: | `invalid_basis` | the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation |
802: 
803: This core is the only one. Results of constraints, judgments, frame
804: evaluations, stops, work steps and effects are stated in it or in a
805: refinement mapped into it, so that results from any members combine under
806: one rule ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)). Purpose and
807: material relation: no combination can report success while a failure, an
808: undecided question, an unperformed evaluation or an uncertain effect
809: remains, and none of these can be mistaken for another (P5, P6).
810: 
811: Recording. A result records its core value together with the predicate
812: evaluated and the original domain outcome, which is the refined value
813: where a refinement produced it. A mapping into the core never owns domain
814: meaning: the member, profile or adopting Product that defines the refined
815: value keeps it, and a consumer that needs the domain distinction reads the
816: domain outcome, never the core value alone (P1, P6).
817: 
818: Standing. The standing of a result is what it establishes about its
819: predicate; it is distinct from the standing of a commitment (§1). Only
820: `satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
821: predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
822: `out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
823: would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
824: owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
825: predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
826: are not ordered among themselves.
827: 
828: No refinement or mapping raises a result's standing (P5, P6):
829: 
830: - a falsified or failed result never maps to a satisfied or successful one;
831: - a result that admissible evidence cannot decide never maps to
832:   `satisfied`;
833: - an evaluation that was not performed stays distinct from one whose
834:   evidence cannot decide: it has no
835:   [closed result](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and it is never mapped
836:   to `indeterminate` or to any other core value;
837: - an effect whose completion is unknown never maps to no effect or to
838:   completed.
839: 
840: Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
841: performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it
842: did not perform (P6). Nothing is coerced to success: a failed,
843: indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
844: the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
845: `satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
846: conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result
847: where an assessment was planned, and uncovered coverage where none was.
848: This
849: conserves
850: [RF-012](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-012-closed-results),
851: whose five values the table restates unchanged, and
852: [AC-007](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal),
853: whose rule that a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
854: invalid-basis result follows the declared algebra rather than being
855: coerced to success is the sentence before; both are restated here once.
856: [REFERENCE_FRAME §3](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-012-closed-results) states
857: RF-012 as a law over frames and
858: [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal)
859: states AC-007 as a law over constraints; each uses this core and neither
860: defines it again.
861: 
862: Refinements. A member, profile or adopting Product that needs finer
863: outcomes defines a refinement. The refinement names the question it
864: answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps every refined value
865: to exactly one core value. No outcome exists outside the core; a
866: refinement adds no core value and keeps the pressure of `indeterminate`,
867: `out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` explicit. Where a refined value would
868: map to one of two core values according to its cause, the cause is part of
869: the refined value and each resulting value maps once (P5, P1). A further
870: refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
871: refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:
872: each child value names its parent value and its cause and keeps its
873: parent's core value; a child that needs a different core value needs a
874: different parent value, which only the owner of the parent declares; and
875: no child takes `satisfied` from a parent that is not `satisfied`. No
876: further refinement raises a result's standing (P5, P6, P1). Purpose and
877: material relation: a consumer that reads a parent value reads the same
878: core value from each of its children, so a split by cause adds a domain
879: distinction and never changes what the parent establishes (P5, P6). The
880: refinements for admission, activation and steps are
881: [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition); each other
882: member, profile and adopting Product states its mapping where it defines
883: its values.
884: 
885: Availability, assessment and acceptance are separate results, each with its
886: own predicate: that a step produced a candidate; that the candidate meets
887: its declared criteria; and that the
888: [decision owner](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation) accepts it at its
889: boundary. A step having produced a candidate never maps to the candidate's
890: fitness or acceptance, and acceptance is never inferred from a successful
891: step (P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition),
892: [EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results) and
893: [§5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance)).
894: 
895: Out of frame or indeterminate. The boundary between these values is drawn
896: on what the activated frame declares and on what the step did with it (P5,
897: finite capacity and graceful total handling; the material relation drawn
898: is the three-way out_of_frame boundary: capability not declared, capability
899: declared and exercised, capability declared and not exercised; rc.2 RF
900: #rf-012-closed-results). Three cases; the first two name core values, and
901: the third names none:
902: 
903: - `out_of_frame` when the claim requires a material relation or an
904:   evaluator capability that the activated frame does not declare. The
905:   result names the missing relation or capability, its owner where the
906:   subject gives one, and the reconfiguration pressure it creates
907:   ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement); rc.2 RF
908:   #reconfigure-when-necessary). A term the claim depends on and the frame
909:   leaves undefined is an undeclared material relation: its meaning can
910:   alter the result and it enters through no declared input (rc.2 RF
911:   #material-relation, RF-003; P1). Whether the step exercised anything is
912:   irrelevant to this value; the ground is the missing declaration.
913: - `indeterminate` when the available admissible evidence cannot decide the
914:   claim (rc.2 RF-012). The result names the evidence that would decide, as
915:   its residual uncertainty (rc.2 RF #return-a-closed-result). Where the
916:   claim also depends on an undeclared relation or capability,
917:   `out_of_frame` and `indeterminate` each have a lawful ground; the result
918:   names the value it returns and that ground, and this boundary excludes
919:   neither (P5).
920: - no value of its own when the step did not exercise a declared capability
921:   the evaluation requires. A result is returned wherever a sufficient
922:   evaluation or an applicable judgment exists without that capability,
923:   identifying its evidence, verdict and residual uncertainty like any
924:   closed result (rc.2 RF #rf-012-closed-results, #return-a-closed-result):
925:   a counterexample found by what was exercised, as when source inspection
926:   falsifies A in a claim of A and B, returns `falsified`, and common
927:   agreement cannot discard it (rc.2 RF #result-conjunction). Where none
928:   exists because the capability was not exercised, the evaluation was not
929:   performed and has no result: the step's stop state carries it,
930:   `incomplete` under
931:   [construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability), and
932:   its work state ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart))
933:   carries the unexercised capability as a residual (P6). In either case
934:   the unexercised part, B above, has no result: in every conjunction over
935:   it, it is a planned assessment without a closed result, and the known
936:   failure A survives with it ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)).
937:   The evaluation's result and the step's stop state answer different
938:   questions, so the step's stop value never becomes the evaluation's
939:   result.
