METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md member_sha256=fd2d895f90eb39bda0950c1c7ff02057ef5d8ae73fcbc5b3203f7e99081d6e3f lines=1008-1130
1008: ### Conjunction of results
1009: 
1010: Conjunction combines results into one result for a composite predicate: a
1011: claim made of component claims, a decision over several evaluations, or
1012: the outer contract of composed steps. It is defined here once, over the
1013: core. A member or profile that combines results applies this rule and
1014: declares only the choices it leaves open (P4a, P4b, P5, P6). Purpose and
1015: material relation: failure, undecidability, non-performance and uncertain
1016: effects stay distinct after combination, so a composite can neither report
1017: success nor hide which kind of gap it has while one of them remains in
1018: what it requires.
1019: 
1020: A conjunction takes three inputs and keeps them apart:
1021: 
1022: 1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
1023:    domain outcome;
1024: 2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the
1025:    composite: evaluations the composite requires that were not performed,
1026:    or whose result is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or
1027:    incapable of establishing its claim;
1028: 3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
1029:    required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
1030:    assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.
1031: 
1032: Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
1033: `satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
1034: uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
1035: reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
1036: assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
1037: `indeterminate` component.
1038: 
1039: Stale results. A held result is stale for a composite when the basis it
1040: binds is not the basis the composite requires of that component, because
1041: a later state has superseded or advanced it or because it binds another
1042: subject or basis (§2, Basis). Two questions stay apart, so that one
1043: composite has one reported value (P3, P5, P6):
1044: 
1045: - an evaluation performed on a subject or basis that is stale, advanced,
1046:   ambiguous or mismatched against the one it must bind returns
1047:   `invalid_basis` for its own predicate, or is reactivated on the current
1048:   basis; [RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)
1049:   states this law over frames, and a conjunction that receives that
1050:   `invalid_basis` holds it as a returned result;
1051: - a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
1052:   applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
1053:   evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
1054:   closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
1055:   neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
1056:   the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;
1057: - the declared basis relations disagree (Reported value below) only among
1058:   returned results, each bound to the basis the composite requires of it,
1059:   whose bases the declared rule requires to agree or to join in a coherent
1060:   composite basis, and which do not.
1061: 
1062: A stale `satisfied` never counts toward the composite. Purpose and
1063: material relation: answering one stale component as a gap in one place and
1064: as `invalid_basis` in another would give one composite two reported
1065: values; keeping the evaluation's own value apart from the composite's gap
1066: keeps the reported value unique and the stale result visible.
1067: 
1068: Survival. Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
1069: counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
1070: every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
1071: join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
1072: planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
1073: coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
1074: either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
1075: cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
1076: contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
1077: mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule, and aggregate
1078: satisfied status cannot replace it (P4b, P5).
1079: 
1080: Predicates travel. Each component keeps its predicate and domain outcome
1081: through every join, so an uncertain effect stays distinct from a failure
1082: and from an undecided claim, and a `satisfied` for one predicate never
1083: counts toward another: a step's `satisfied` for "a candidate is available"
1084: never counts toward the candidate's fitness or acceptance.
1085: 
1086: Reported value. The conjunction is `satisfied` only when every mandatory
1087: result is `satisfied` with valid applicable evidence, the declared basis
1088: relations agree, and the second and third inputs are empty. A composite
1089: with a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint or an uncovered
1090: required obligation cannot project success. Where a mandatory result is
1091: not `satisfied`, the conjunction
1092: reports a non-satisfied value chosen by its declared rule from those
1093: returned; no universal order among the non-satisfied values exists, and
1094: the member or profile that applies the conjunction declares its own in
1095: its declared rule. Where every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`
1096: and the declared basis relations disagree, the conjunction reports
1097: `invalid_basis`, because no coherent composite basis supports the
1098: composite predicate (§2, Basis); any gaps stay recorded by kind. Where
1099: every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`, the declared basis
1100: relations agree and a gap remains, the conjunction reports
1101: `indeterminate`, because the results it holds cannot decide the composite
1102: predicate; that value is the conjunction's own, and the gaps stay
1103: recorded by kind. A `falsified` result that is not mandatory stays in the
1104: conjunction's record with its predicate and is never discarded. Where
1105: every mandatory result is `satisfied`, the declared basis relations agree
1106: and no gap remains, a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint
1107: falsifies the conjunction whichever contributor found it, and without one
1108: the conjunction's value is the one its declared rule gives over the
1109: mandatory results.
1110: 
1111: The declared rule. A conjunction declares which results are mandatory; how
1112: conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree,
1113: results on different bases combining only under a declared coherent
1114: composite basis (§2, Basis); which decision authority owns the
1115: conjunction; how results that are not mandatory count; and whether any
1116: result may veto or defer the decision.
1117: Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing
1118: evaluation (P6, P4a).
1119: 
1120: Composition of results. The result of composed steps for the outer
1121: predicate is the conjunction of the steps' results, with the outer
1122: contract's obligations as the required coverage. That each step returned
1123: `satisfied` supports the outer predicate only where the refinement's
1124: premises hold ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement),
1125: Refinement).
1126: 
1127: Provenance: rc.2 RF #result-conjunction and
1128: #applicability-and-required-results, and the combination rule of
1129: conservation accounting.

METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md member_sha256=fd2d895f90eb39bda0950c1c7ff02057ef5d8ae73fcbc5b3203f7e99081d6e3f lines=1230-1356
1230: ### Assertions and observation
1231: 
1232: For a selected source obligation r, let `Q_r = interpret(r, Γ, Ω)` be its
1233: required predicate over the declared domain Ω of cases. The interpretation
1234: retains the obligation's scope, conditions, exceptions and permitted
1235: alternatives. A source identifier or digest authenticates the selected
1236: text; it does not prove the interpretation faithful (P1, P3).
1237: 
1238: An assertion targets a predicate `q_t` and states whether that predicate
1239: is the full obligation or a narrower claim. The directions differ:
1240: 
1241: ```text
1242: Q_r implies q_t                   : q_t is a necessary condition of Q_r.
1243: q_t implies Q_r                   : establishing q_t is sufficient for Q_r.
1244: (q_1 and ... and q_n) implies Q_r : the stated conjunction is sufficient.
1245: ```
1246: 
1247: These implications are conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a check of a
1248: necessary condition does not establish the full obligation. A conjunction
1249: requires its own coverage and compatibility argument; a collection of
1250: passing tests does not supply it by its count (P1, P6, P5).
1251: 
1252: Let `π: Ω → O` describe the observations available to a checker and
1253: `T ⊆ O × R` its admitted evaluation relation, where R is the core result
1254: algebra of Results above. A deterministic checker is a functional special
1255: case. A human or probabilistic checker can admit different conclusions on
1256: the same observations; a universal soundness claim covers all admitted
1257: conclusions, not a favourable selected run. `indeterminate` is the core
1258: judgment whose admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate (Results).
1259: It is distinct from an evaluation that was not performed, and from work
1260: or coverage that remains unresolved, which is a state of the work
1261: ([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition),
1262: [§5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)) and not a judgment value.
1263: Writing `sat` and `fal` for the satisfied and falsified judgments about
1264: `q_t`, not new execution states:
1265: 
1266: ```text
1267: For every s in Ω:
1268:   (π(s), sat) in T  implies  q_t(s).
1269:   (π(s), fal) in T  implies  not q_t(s).
1270: ```
1271: 
1272: The candidate identifies what supports each claimed direction and where
1273: it is unresolved. A relation admitting both a sound satisfied judgment
1274: and an indeterminate judgment need not always decide the case. A
1275: restricted deterministic model retains its scope, and an actual checker
1276: requires its own conformance account. An observed test pass remains an
1277: observation while the oracle's fidelity is unestablished; it does not
1278: become established satisfaction of the source obligation, and a reported
1279: failure is treated the same way. The observation binding itself needs
1280: support: an idealised π does not establish that the instrument, actor or
1281: execution acquired the required facts correctly. A probabilistic claim
1282: uses its declared distribution over outcomes under Quantified assurance
1283: below; the relation alone supplies no probabilities (P6, P5, P1).
1284: 
1285: Observation sufficiency. A checker that always decides `q_t` correctly
1286: from π alone requires:
1287: 
1288: ```text
1289: For all s, s' in Ω:
1290:   π(s) = π(s')  implies  q_t(s) = q_t(s').
1291: ```
1292: 
1293: If two admissible cases have the same observation but opposite truth
1294: values, that observation cannot support a sound complete decision between
1295: them; further evidence, a justified narrower scope or an indeterminate
1296: judgment is required. In a classical set model this condition permits a
1297: predicate on the image of π; it establishes neither an executable decision
1298: procedure nor its cost. Unknown effects and unavailable observations
1299: retain their distinctions from falsehood and from an evaluation that was
1300: not performed (Results) (P3, P1, P5, P6).
1301: 
1302: ### Parallel derivation and mutual assurance
1303: 
1304: Construction and assurance can follow different paths from a common
1305: obligation. For `requirement → refinement → realisation`, assertions
1306: derived from the requirement check its applicable conditions in the
1307: realisation; assertions derived from the refinement check its more
1308: detailed obligations there. Acceptance tests and build-level tests can
1309: instantiate these paths
1310: ([ASSURANCE §14](ASSURANCE.md#14-design-to-module-evidence-route)); the
1311: roles identify the selected sources and subject in this example and
1312: prescribe no stage names or test classes (P1, P6).
1313: 
1314: An expected result or acceptance predicate has assertion provenance: the
1315: owning obligation, its interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared
1316: dependencies, which give it meaning. An execution has execution
1317: provenance: the actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment,
1318: inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they
1319: support; execution records alone cannot establish that the expected
1320: answer follows from the requirement. Authentication of a returned
1321: assessment, which binds a result to its producer, subject, basis and
1322: evidence ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), is a
1323: third thing and establishes neither provenance (P6, P3).
1324: 
1325: An implementation-derived test can be useful for regression or a stated
1326: local property. Repeating the implementation's decision supplies no
1327: independent justification of its fidelity to an upstream obligation. A
1328: shorter assertion path can be easier to inspect and execute than
1329: construction; that is a supported design claim for the selected path, not
1330: a guarantee of correctness, coverage or independence. Valid distinct
1331: implementations can produce different outputs within the same acceptable
1332: relation; equality of outputs is not always the oracle (P1, P6).
1333: 
1334: Mutual assurance compares independently justified constructions or
1335: assertions within their stated scope. Agreement is compatible with both
1336: being correct and with a shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis
1337: ([ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation))
1338: and does not identify the faulty party by itself. Assurance accounts for
1339: shared specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations,
1340: copied material and other material failure causes. Different actors,
1341: model families or codebases do not establish statistical independence.
1342: Porting retains authorship and common dependencies (EVALUATION §3 and the
1343: Cross-Synthesis rule of the Product that owns this corpus). Repeating
1344: evidence does not create a new independent observation. Agreement with
1345: an incorrect common model cannot validate that model against the desired
1346: real-world outcome; validation of the governing expectations uses its
1347: declared purpose and external observations through their owners, and
1348: proposed corrections preserve counterexamples and follow the applicable
1349: change authority ([SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#4-change-management))
1350: (P4a, P6, P1).
1351: 
1352: These relationships are recoverable from the existing sources, bindings
1353: and evidence carriers. Shared derivations can be recorded once and applied
1354: to a declared family. No new per-test document, parallel ledger, fixed
1355: number of reviewers or prescribed provenance format is required (P6).

1409: ### Change impact and evidence reuse
1410: 
1411: Assertion justification and evidence validity are related but distinct
1412: dependency relations. The former explains why a check expresses an
1413: obligation. The latter identifies what can affect the check's behaviour,
1414: conclusion or applicability: implementation, shared libraries, data,
1415: instruments, environments and governing assumptions. A
1416: requirements-to-test link alone is not a complete impact model (P3, P6).
1417: 
1418: Let Δ be a change to material facts or dependencies, including a newly
1419: discovered invalid assumption. Let `I(Δ)`, the impact cover, conservatively cover the changed
1420: facts and their affected dependents. For each check t, let `D*(t)` cover
1421: the transitive dependencies material to its assertion, execution and use
1422: of evidence. A candidate selection is:
1423: 
1424: ```text
1425: S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }.
1426: ```
1427: 
1428: The representation of these dependencies is the tenant's choice; no
1429: exhaustive graph database is required. Excluding a check requires
1430: supported coverage of its material dependencies and a reason the change
1431: cannot invalidate the intended reused claim; an absent edge is not
1432: evidence of non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves
1433: the dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations or cases create
1434: assessment work even when no existing check covers them. A mandatory
1435: gate, an assessment that the governing policy requires irrespective of
1436: selection ([RELEASE §8](RELEASE.md#8-acceptance)), remains applicable
1437: (P5, P6).
1438: 
1439: For a new subject and basis, let `E_old` be the existing evidence records,
1440: `E_reassessed` the evidence newly produced by reassessment, and `E_new`
1441: the resulting account. Reassessment includes the checks selected in
1442: `S_Δ`, the assessment of new obligations and the applicable mandatory
1443: gates. Selection alone produces no execution evidence; failed and
1444: indeterminate results retain their standing:
1445: 
1446: ```text
1447: E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.
1448: ```
1449: 
1450: Retention establishes the material validity conditions on the new
1451: subject: the claim and its scope still apply, its assertion and
1452: observation basis remain justified, and the affected dependencies are
1453: unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The
1454: original evidence keeps its original subject; a new applicability
1455: relation permits its use. A changed hash alone establishes neither
1456: invalidity nor equivalence. A corrected run is not an unchanged independent
1457: test of the correction: the corrected subject carries its own evidence.
1458: Known failures, unresolved coverage and their
1459: citations remain visible until a supported repair, a reassessment or an
1460: authorised change of obligation disposes of them (P3, P4b, P6).
1461: 
1462: If a governing requirement changes, dependent expectations may need
1463: authorised revision as well as new execution. A correction in a
1464: refinement revisits the affected obligations and their links to both the
1465: requirement and the realisation. A correction in the realisation
1466: reassesses the affected implementation and integration under the
1467: still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependency boundaries,
1468: not file or directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires current reality and
1469: invalidates affected claims; it need not erase valid work or rerun every
1470: check ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)) (P3, P6).
1471: 
1472: The governing assurance can be established from applicable retained
1473: evidence together with new evidence; the completeness of that account is
1474: distinct from the freshness of every execution. Selection considers
1475: impact-analysis, acquisition, execution and assessment costs together,
1476: with anticipated costs distinguished from measurements
1477: ([ACTIVATION §6](ACTIVATION.md#6-cost-and-proportionality)). The
1478: required assurance, risk policy and mandatory gates constrain that
1479: optimisation; a cheap selection that leaves a required obligation
1480: uncovered is insufficient. Broad or
1481: uncertain impact, a change to the selection model, an applicable release
1482: rule or evidence that selection missed a dependency can justify wider
1483: testing; full-suite execution remains available and may itself have
1484: coverage gaps. No universal full-suite cadence follows, and no
1485: optimisation removes a separately required gate. Failures enter diagnosis
1486: and an authorised response
1487: ([ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation));
1488: the next selected action may acquire evidence before any repair is
1489: justified. [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse)
1490: applies this relation to closed results and handoffs; its three
1491: invalidators are kinds of change Δ, and a closed result is affected when
1492: its `D*(t)` meets `I(Δ)` (P5, P6).

233: ## 4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager
234: 
235: Within the product-definition-routing context an Installed Release Basis
236: is the pair (P3; rc.2
237: #shared-installed-release-basis-and-toolchain-manager):
238: 
239: ```text
240: (immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI, installed-manifest SHA-256)
241: ```
242: 
243: The URI identifies one immutable annotated RC cut. The digest identifies
244: the deterministic installed-release manifest, which binds the cut's tag
245: object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards
246: inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. The manifest shape
247: is owned by `schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json`. The manifest
248: is transport and integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution (P6).
249: 
250: An Adoption Plan is the read-only, deterministic acceptance object that
251: binds one current Product Definition's identity and bytes to its current
252: basis and to one resolved immutable target's cut, annotated tag object,
253: commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is the
254: operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants
255: no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the
256: subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised
257: fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests
258: under the same law.

647: ## 7. Collective reference-frame basis
648: 
649: A Project Reference-Frame Basis is the Product-owned accepted declaration
650: of the shared frame set through which finite actors collectively engage one
651: governed Product scope or outcome (P0, P6; rc.2
652: #collective-reference-frame-basis). It binds:
653: 
654: ```text
655: Project Reference-Frame Basis
656:   = exact reference-frame law and optional profile basis
657:   + admitting authorities and governed scopes
658:   + frame declarations and evaluation inventory
659:   + actor-binding rules and capability envelopes
660:   + semantic, evaluation, operation and decision grants
661:   + result, conjunction, translation and coverage relations
662:   + lifecycle activation triggers and invalidation law
663: ```
664: 
665: [REFERENCE_FRAME](REFERENCE_FRAME.md) supplies frame principles only, and
666: its §4 the shape of a frame-set declaration; a profile member (the
667: Executive baseline, tier 3) supplies one optional profile only. Neither
668: selects, adopts or owns a Product binding. The adopting Product's existing
669: authority owns the concrete declaration and every grant it contains (P6).
670: 
671: `reference_frame_bases` is the non-empty locator set for the accepted
672: frame bases through which finite actors collectively engage the governed
673: Product and its work. Each entry names (P6, P3):
674: 
675: - the URI carrying one accepted frame-basis declaration;
676: - every existing Goals, Product, requirement, accepted-design or other
677:   lawful authority that admits the declaration; and
678: - the exact Product, bounded context, build tenant, outcome or other
679:   governed scope to which it applies.
680: 
681: The referenced declaration owns the selected frame set, the method or
682: profile basis, the governed outcome, the actor-binding rules, the
683: capability envelopes, the grant requirements, the triggers, the coverage,
684: the result relations and the invalidation law. It may adopt an available
685: profile or define a project configuration. The JSON entry locates that
686: declaration and its authority relation; it does not contain the binding,
687: adopt the profile, restate the frames or create frame-set authority (P6).
688: 
689: Profile availability, Product adoption and execution-scoped activation are
690: three distinct relations. Inclusion in a selected method cut makes a
691: profile available; only Product authority may adopt it; only an exact
692: authorised work instruction may activate one bound frame for an actor and
693: subject (P6, P3).
694: 
695: The collective basis and an actor activation are distinct. An Agent Frame
696: Activation is the execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable
697: frame declaration or active configuration, an exact evaluation, subject,
698: basis, evidence boundary and capability envelope; what the agent receives
699: is the activation packet of REFERENCE_FRAME §11, and the step it performs
700: is ACTIVATION §1. The Product Definition records the durable shared basis;
701: a ticket or other authorised work instruction carries the activation
702: packet. An Agent Frame Activation does not mutate the overlay, and the overlay
703: registers no agents, assigns no permanent frames and persists no temporary
704: active frame configuration (P3, P0).
705: 
706: Frames and actors keep separate identities. Several agents may activate
707: overlapping subsets of one frame set; one agent may activate different
708: frames over time. Neither an actor name nor a broad frame grants semantic,
709: operation, review, acceptance or disposition authority beyond the cited
710: owners and the exact activation (P6, P3).

883: ## 11. One constitutional surface and version boundary
884: 
885: STDO-SURFACE-001. The shared methodology is modular in authorship and
886: singular in authority. Each law has one owning member; other members
887: consume it by reference. The members become operative only as one complete
888: released version of the method (P6, P3; rc.2
889: #one-constitutional-surface-and-version-boundary-stdo-surface-001).
890: 
891: A released cut identifies its exact member set, member digests, review
892: basis, human acceptance and immutable identity. Compressions, templates,
893: comments, candidate work, installed copies and mutable source are derived,
894: evidential or authoring surfaces. They cannot become a selectable partial
895: constitution and cannot reinterpret the owning members (P3, P6).
896: 
897: Within their declared scope, derived instructions preserve the owning
898: clauses' applicability, obligations, permissions, exclusions, decision
899: owners and invalidators. A projected prohibition cannot lose its condition
900: or its lawful alternative, even when every source digest is correct. A
901: summary, bootstrap or index cannot require a stricter or weaker relation by
902: compression. Its references are resolvable within the declared actor's
903: access; otherwise the required meaning is supplied directly (P4b, P1;
904: FOUNDATIONS §4, reference versus body).

906: Staleness binding. What a derived surface is, when it is stale, and
907: what an actor uses in its place are
908: [ACTIVATION §2 Staleness of derived surfaces](ACTIVATION.md#staleness-of-derived-surfaces);
909: which questions a derived surface decides on its own is ACTIVATION §2,
910: Standalone scope. This member refines that law for the derived surfaces
911: a released cut or an installation carries, among them compressions,
912: templates, bootstraps, indexes and projected frames. Each carries the
913: path and digest of each deciding source it was derived from, and of each
914: index it watches (GLOSSARY §2). A change to any of those digests is the
915: source change that makes it stale under that law, and it must be
916: regenerated or explicitly re-accepted before an installation treats it
917: as current. What a matching digest establishes is stated above
918: (EVALUATION §7). The raw owning members of the same
919: selected cut remain the deciding authority: a question that a stale or
920: insufficient carrier cannot decide is decided from them, as ACTIVATION
921: §2 states (P3, P5, P6; provenance rc.2
922: authority_compressions/README.md and stdo_bootstrap.md step 5, a claim no
923: rc.2 body states).

926: abstract state and transition laws, admissibility conditions, necessary
927: causal order and evidence invariants. Consumers own concrete Product
928: realisation: instantiated types and schemas, files, tools, runtime and
929: orchestration machinery, tests and executable conformance implementation.
930: A concrete form is method law only when the method explicitly accepts it
931: as an interoperability boundary, as §1 does for the definition schema and

933:

955: 
956: - a shared versioned STDO store, addressed through the exact
957:   `constitution.stdo.basis`, as the installed distribution of the selected
958:   process constitution;
959: - `specification/GOALS.md` as current work-wave orientation;
960: - `specification/INTENT.md` as domain direction;
961: - `specification/PRODUCT.md` as the current product-definition surface;
962: - `specification/requirements/` as the live requirement surface;
963: - `build_tenants/` as the root for shared and tenant-local realisation
964:   surfaces; and
965: - `.ai-workspace/` as the sprint, ticket and comment carrier root.
966: 
967: These are template defaults, not universal path law; the definition's URI
968: bindings select the actual project carriers (P2).
969: 
970: The authority split is (P6, P3):
971: 
972: - mutable methodology authoring lives in the method's own source workspace
973:   (the standards of its source project) and governs only a future
974:   candidate cut;
975: - released methodology authority is the exact immutable STDO version
976:   selected by the consumer;
977: - installed methodology distribution lives in the toolchain manager's
978:   shared versioned store by default and matches the basis URI and manifest
979:   digest;
980: - project-owned constitutional surfaces live at the definition's `what`
981:   bindings; and
982: - project-owned realisation and work surfaces live at its `how` and
983:   `ticketing` bindings.
984: 
985: A project creates no competing local methodology root, such as a default
986: `specification/standards/`, and binds no mutable or partial method source
987: as if it were the selected immutable release (P6).
988: 
989: Method authority is singular: the selected immutable STDO release
990: authority, projected into the installed distribution located by the
991: overlay; and the project constitutional authority at the definition's
992: bound WHAT surfaces (P6). When editing or repricing methodology, the
993: mutable source path is authoring authority for the candidate being
994: constructed; it is not operative consumer law before release and explicit
995: selection (P3, P6). When operating inside a governed workspace, the
996: resolved installed basis is the operative distribution of the selected
997: immutable release until the consumer explicitly adopts another cut. A
998: project-local exact copy stays lawful when explicitly bound and verified;
999: it is not the default, and file proximity cannot select it (P6, P3).


METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md member_sha256=d64ee5c05aaefac346116c2e43eabf193dd84123f1d461070ecd378ce5e9b551 lines=281-458
281: ### RF-001 Evaluation relativity
282: 
283: Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
284: declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary (P2; rc.2
285: #rf-001-evaluation-relativity).
286: 
287: ### RF-002 Finite attention
288: 
289: An activated frame contains a finite attention surface that fits the
290: selected actor's declared capability envelope. A frame that needs
291: undeclared ambient memory, conversation history or an effectively global
292: workspace context is not reconstructable for that actor (P0; rc.2
293: #rf-002-finite-attention). The fit is tested in
294: [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
295: which owns the measurement of the context's size and when it applies.
296: Whether the actor attends adequately to a frame that fits is a separate
297: question, answered by actual-use evidence under
298: [EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification); a size measurement
299: does not answer it (P0, P6).
300: 
301: ### RF-003 Material sufficiency
302: 
303: Every known relation whose lawful change can alter the evaluation result,
304: the validity of the basis, the sufficiency of evidence, operation authority
305: or decision authority appears in the frame or enters through a declared
306: authoritative input. Omitting a material relation makes the frame
307: insufficient. The law does not require proving that no undiscovered
308: material relation exists (P2; P0 with the open-world premise; rc.2
309: #rf-003-material-sufficiency).
310: 
311: ### RF-004 Irrelevance exclusion
312: 
313: Relations that cannot affect the declared evaluation stay outside active
314: attention unless they are needed to establish that irrelevance. A frame
315: does not expand because adjacent workspace material exists (P2; rc.2
316: #rf-004-irrelevance-exclusion).
317: 
318: ### RF-005 Exact basis and coordinates
319: 
320: Every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence
321: scope. A stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns
322: `invalid_basis` or requires reactivation. Apparent equality never
323: substitutes for declared coordinate equality (P3, P1; rc.2
324: #rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates).
325: 
326: ### RF-006 Authority conservation
327: 
328: A frame carries and applies admitted authority. It does not mint, widen,
329: transfer or reconstruct semantic, evaluation, operation or decision
330: authority from anything that creates none. That list is
331: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)'; its
332: instances in a frame include actor identity, available capability,
333: evidence shape, implementation reachability and frame selection (P6;
334: rc.2 #rf-006-authority-conservation).
335: 
336: ### RF-007 Semantic, evidence and verdict separation
337: 
338: The separation of semantic law, evidence, the evaluator's application
339: and the disposing decision authority is
340: [EVALUATION §2](EVALUATION.md#2-separation)'s. This law binds it to a
341: frame: a frame declaration keeps these roles distinguishable even when
342: one actor lawfully performs several of them, and where the evaluation
343: performs a material operation, the existing operation owner supplies the
344: exact grant as a further role the declaration keeps apart (P6; rc.2
345: #rf-007-semantic-evidence-and-verdict-separation).
346: 
347: ### RF-008 Overlap without identity collapse
348: 
349: Frames may share entities, variables, evidence or coordinates. Shared
350: material establishes neither identical meaning nor identical basis,
351: authority or result. Every cross-frame equality or translation an
352: evaluation uses is declared where it is used (P1, P3; rc.2
353: #rf-008-overlap-without-identity-collapse).
354: 
355: ### RF-009 No assumed hierarchy
356: 
357: Frames may relate through disjointness, overlap, refinement, restriction,
358: translation, temporal succession, composition or governance (§7). Parent
359: and child relations apply only where explicitly declared. Functional
360: decomposition, communication, authority precedence, frame configuration,
361: subject topology and evaluation dependency are distinct relation
362: structures; a consumer may align them where the governed subject warrants
363: it and may not silently treat them as one hierarchy (P3, P1; rc.2
364: #rf-009-no-assumed-hierarchy). Communication is the exchange of
365: information between frames, or between the actors activated on them. An
366: exchange by itself grants no authority, an instance of
367: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
368: creates no authority, and establishes neither a decomposition nor an
369: evaluation dependency (P6, P1). Communication is new
370: in this list. Purpose and material relation: a configuration assigns
371: information exchanges as well as responsibilities
372: ([ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#configuration)), and an exchange read as a
373: grant or as a dependency would move authority or change a result without a
374: declared relation.
375: 
376: ### RF-010 Composition on demand
377: 
378: Using several frames does not require composing their internal manifolds.
379: Composition law is required only when the governing evaluation combines
380: their internal variables, transports evidence or values across them, or
381: treats their operations as one material execution relation. Independently
382: activated evaluations may instead return closed results to one declared
383: conjunction or decision rule (P4a; §6; rc.2
384: #rf-010-composition-on-demand).
385: 
386: ### RF-011 Topology mutation and recharting
387: 
388: An activated frame declares the topology changes capable of invalidating
389: its coordinates or its materiality judgment. A detected material topology
390: mutation causes reevaluation, frame revision or recharting before the
391: previous result is reused. Material revision of the frame itself
392: invalidates for reuse every result bound to the prior revision coordinate;
393: §10 Revision actions states that rule (P3, P4b; rc.2
394: #rf-011-topology-mutation-and-recharting).
395: 
396: ### RF-012 Closed results
397: 
398: Every performed evaluation of a frame returns one closed result in the
399: frame's declared result algebra: the core algebra of
400: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), or a refinement mapped
401: into it under that section. That section owns the five core values
402: (`satisfied`, `falsified`, `indeterminate`, `out_of_frame` and
403: `invalid_basis`), their meanings and the rules over them: that nothing is
404: coerced to success; that a refinement adds no core value, keeps
405: indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure explicit and raises
406: no result's standing; and that an evaluation not performed has no result,
407: its stop state being
408: [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition). This law
409: applies them to every frame and defines none of them (P5; rc.2
410: #rf-012-closed-results).
411: 
412: ### RF-013 Reconstructable activation
413: 
414: A fresh competent actor inside the declared capability envelope can
415: reconstruct the activated evaluation from the frame declaration, the exact
416: subject, the basis and the admissible inputs, without undocumented
417: conversational or historical context (P0 with the actor-change premise;
418: rc.2 #rf-013-reconstructable-activation).
419: 
420: ### RF-014 Capability fit
421: 
422: Frame adequacy includes actor usability. When the material manifold
423: exceeds an actor's capability envelope, the remedies are those of
424: [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)
425: step 3, which owns the list: among them selecting another actor, refining
426: the frame into steps, sequencing activations and a lawful compression
427: (RF-017). Choosing among them is human authority's, exercised directly or
428: in advance through the grant; ACTIVATION §2 says which of them a step
429: selects itself and which re-enter the grant's owner. The actor may not
430: silently omit material relations to fit its context (P0, P5; rc.2
431: #rf-014-capability-fit).
432: 
433: ### RF-015 Residual uncertainty
434: 
435: Coverage and evaluation results retain known uncertainty. Unresolved
436: relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability
437: stay explicit. Absence of a recorded counterexample is not evidence of
438: universal completeness (P4b, P6; open-world premise; rc.2
439: #rf-015-residual-uncertainty).
440: 
441: ### RF-016 Implementation neutrality
442: 
443: This member requires the declared relations and the observable outcomes.
444: It requires no frame runtime, universal carrier, registry, controller,
445: prompt format, repository layout, collaboration topology, worker count or
446: software framework (P2; rc.2 #rf-016-implementation-neutrality).
447: 
448: ### RF-017 Proportional compression
449: 
450: A frame compresses accumulated practice when its declaration preserves the
451: material distinctions and failure detections its evaluation family requires
452: while fitting its capability envelope. Compression does not require a
453: unique smallest frame. Intentional overlap is retained where it supplies
454: independently activated evaluation, different capability fit, different
455: evidence altitude or useful fault detection. Frames are merged only when
456: the merged frame preserves evaluation meaning, authority, capability fit
457: and proportional reasoning cost (P2, P0; rc.2
458: #rf-017-proportional-compression).

525: ## 5. Method functions
526: 
527: The frame and the functions over it remain distinct. An application may
528: realise the following relations in any conforming form; the signatures
529: describe relations, not callable software interfaces (P2; RF-016; rc.2
530: #method-functions):
531: 
532: ```text
533: declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities)
534:   -> frame_set
535: 
536: activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor)
537:   -> activated_frame | activation_refusal
538: 
539: evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence)
540:   -> result + evidence + residuals
541: 
542: conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results)
543:   -> decision | conflict | indeterminate
544: 
545: translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping)
546:   -> translated_value | declared_loss | refusal
547: 
548: audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set)
549:   -> coverage_ledger
550: 
551: revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change)
552:   -> proposed_frame_set_delta
553: ```
554: 
555: `declare` is §4; `activate` and `evaluate` are ACTIVATION §1 and §2;
556: `evaluate` returns its result under RF-012, and the closed result is
557: returned and reused under ACTIVATION §7; `conjoin` and `translate` are §6;
558: `audit_coverage` is §8, which maps the statuses of its ledger to the core;
559: `revise` is §10. EVALUATION §7 qualifies each.
560: 
561: The outcomes of `activate`, `conjoin` and `translate` form a refinement of
562: the core algebra, stated under the refinement rule of
563: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): each outcome below maps
564: to exactly one core value for the predicate its function names, the value
565: travels with that predicate and with the outcome, whose meaning stays here,
566: and an outcome named in the signatures above that would map to more than
567: one core value according to its cause carries the cause in its name, as in
568: `activation_refusal(basis)` (P5, P6). The refinement is new in this
569: corpus. Purpose and material relation: a consumer that combines these
570: outcomes with other results reads them in the one core, so a refusal, a
571: conflict or a loss outside the accepted loss is neither mistaken for
572: success nor merged with an evaluation that was not performed.
573: 
574: | Function and predicate | Outcome | Cause | Core value |
575: |---|---|---|---|
576: | `activate`: the frame is activated for this evaluation, subject, basis and actor | `activated_frame` | the frame declaration is bound to the exact evaluation, subject, basis and actor | `satisfied` |
577: | | `activation_refusal(capability)` | the frame declares a capability the evaluation needs, and the selected actor's declared envelope lacks it; the refusal names that capability and its owner where the subject gives one | `out_of_frame` |
578: | | `activation_refusal(authority)` | the activation needs semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority that is not admitted to it; the refusal names that authority's owner | `out_of_frame` |
579: | | `activation_refusal(basis)` | the subject or basis is stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched (RF-005), a topology mismatch included: the subject's topology is not the topology basis the frame declares (RF-011) | `invalid_basis` |
580: | `conjoin`: the composite predicate holds under the declared decision rule | `decision(holds)` | the conjunction of FOUNDATIONS §4 reports `satisfied` | `satisfied` |
581: | | `decision(fails)` | the conjunction reports `falsified`, and no mandatory result for the same claim is `satisfied` | `falsified` |
582: | | `conflict` | the conjunction reports `falsified` while mandatory results for the same claim disagree, one `satisfied` and another `falsified`; the counterexample survives the join, and the disagreement stays unresolved for the decision authority | `falsified` |
583: | | `indeterminate` | the conjunction reports `indeterminate` | `indeterminate` |
584: | `translate`: the value or evidence enters the target frame as the declared translation states | `translated_value` | the value or evidence is carried into the target coordinates with its declared meaning | `satisfied` |
585: | | `declared_loss` | the value or evidence is carried with a loss inside the declared accepted loss; the loss travels with it as a residual (P4b) | `satisfied` |
586: | | `refusal(condition)` | a refusal condition the translation declares holds, a loss outside the accepted loss included; or the value or evidence fails identity or equality under the translation's declared equality law | `falsified` |
587: | | `refusal(authority)` | an authority mismatch the translation does not declare: the value or evidence carries semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority whose relation to the target frame's authority the translation states neither as preserved nor as a refusal condition; the refusal names that authority's owner | `out_of_frame` |
588: | | `refusal(basis)` | the source value or evidence binds a stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis or coordinate (RF-005) | `invalid_basis` |
589: 
590: Where no frame the actor can use declares a material relation or
591: capability the evaluation needs, `activate` returns `out_of_frame` itself
592: ([ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
593: Activation). Where the conjunction reports `out_of_frame` or
594: `invalid_basis`, `conjoin` returns that value; the signatures name no
595: outcome for either case, and a basis mismatch is this returned
596: `invalid_basis`, as EVALUATION §7 names it for `conjoin`. Under a
597: declared veto or deferral, `conjoin` returns the outcome above whose cause
598: holds for the value the conjunction reports
599: ([FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)), or that value
600: itself where it is `out_of_frame` or `invalid_basis`. A planned
601: assessment without a closed result, and required coverage that no planned
602: assessment addresses, are no outcome of `conjoin`:
603: [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results) records them
604: beside the reported value, and they map to no core value. The outcomes of
605: `activate` answer whether a frame was activated, never the
606: evaluation's claim: a refused activation performs no evaluation.
607: `decision(holds)` assesses the composite predicate and is not its
608: acceptance, which is a separate result
609: ([FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)).
610: 
611: ## 6. Frames in conjunction
612: 
613: Frames act together through four distinct relations, and only where the
614: evaluation requires one (P4a; RF-010; rc.2 #using-frames-in-conjunction).
615: 
616: ### Independently activated co-evaluation
617: 
618: Several frames may evaluate the same subject through separate activations
619: and return closed results. They may overlap in subject, manifold or
620: evidence sources; neither evaluation consumes or influences the other's
621: unclosed working result. This serves assurance independence, different
622: evidence altitudes and distinct failure perspectives (P6; FOUNDATIONS §2,
623: evaluation independence; rc.2 #independently-activated-co-evaluation).
624: 
625: ### Result conjunction
626: 
627: A declared decision rule consumes the closed results of several frames.
628: The rule, what it must state, and the conjunction it computes are
629: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
630: over the core values of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results);
631: this member defines no conjunction of its own. The outcomes of `conjoin`
632: map to the core as §5 states (P4a, P5, P6; rc.2 #result-conjunction).
633: 
634: ### Evidence or coordinate translation
635: 
636: One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another. The
637: translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning,
638: accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions (P1, P4b;
639: rc.2 #evidence-or-coordinate-translation). What a statement of preserved
640: meaning and accepted loss must show, and the law that licenses the
641: step, are
642: [ACTIVATION §4, Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement), and where the
643: translation is represented in `a_c` it is recorded in the preservation,
644: introduced, removed and residual fields of
645: [AC-013](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-013-transformation). This section adds
646: only the frame fields: the source and target coordinates, the
647: provenance, the equality law and the refusal conditions.
648: 
649: ### Material composition
650: 
651: Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning
652: relation. The owning application declares the composition, the shared
653: invariants, the effect or decision order where material, closure, failure,
654: and the conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority.
655: Composition is introduced only when the evaluation requires it; a possible
656: future interaction does not require a general composition law in every
657: frame (P4a, P6, P2; rc.2 #material-composition).
658:

686: ### Coverage basis
687: 
688: Coverage is evaluated against the tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): the
689: workspace W, the governed outcome G, the exact basis B, the known
690: evaluation inventory E, the declared frame set S and the time or immutable
691: checkpoint T of the claim. Changing any material member may invalidate the
692: coverage result; whether a change does is decided by
693: [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse): it does when it
694: could change that result, as a material input change or a changed basis
695: (P3, P6; rc.2 #coverage-basis).

METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md member_sha256=d64ee5c05aaefac346116c2e43eabf193dd84123f1d461070ecd378ce5e9b551 lines=726-806
726: ### Coverage ledger
727: 
728: The ledger holds at least, for each evaluation (P4b, P6; rc.2
729: #coverage-ledger):
730: 
731: | Field | Meaning |
732: |---|---|
733: | evaluation | the exact question or predicate |
734: | provenance | the source establishing materiality |
735: | subject and basis | the exact workspace coordinate |
736: | selected frames | the frames capable of evaluating it |
737: | actor envelope | the competence and context required |
738: | semantic authority | the owner of the evaluated meaning |
739: | operation authority | the existing owner grant for construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation where the evaluation performs one; otherwise none |
740: | decision authority | the owner of the disposition |
741: | evidence | the required observations and their provenance |
742: | dependencies | material frame or seam relations |
743: | status | the coverage disposition |
744: | residual | uncertainty, exclusion or re-entry condition |
745: 
746: The baseline coverage statuses are `covered`, `separately_covered`,
747: `conditionally_covered`, `conflicted`, `uncovered`, `unknown` and
748: `excluded_by_authority`.
749: 
750: The statuses form a refinement of the core, stated under the refinement
751: rule of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). They answer
752: whether a row's coverage obligation is met, for the predicate "on the
753: declared coverage tuple, a capable frame of S covers the evaluation with
754: no unresolved conflict among the frames, results or authorities that
755: cover it, or a governing authority the row cites excludes it". Each status
756: maps to exactly one core value, and the value travels with that predicate
757: and with the status, whose meaning stays here (P5, P6):
758: 
759: | Status | Cause | Core value |
760: |---|---|---|
761: | `covered` | a capable frame of S evaluates it on the tuple, with no unresolved conflict among what covers it | `satisfied` |
762: | `separately_covered` | separately activated frames of S each evaluate it on the tuple, with no unresolved conflict among them (High-risk separately activated coverage) | `satisfied` |
763: | `excluded_by_authority` | the governing authority the row cites excludes the evaluation from the claim (Operational full coverage, item 7) | `satisfied` |
764: | `conditionally_covered` | a capable frame of S covers it only under a condition the audit has not established; the residual names the condition and the evidence that would decide it | `indeterminate` |
765: | `conflicted` | the frames, results or authorities that cover it conflict, and the conflict is unresolved; the conflict is the counterexample and stays unresolved for the decision authority (Operational full coverage, item 6) | `falsified` |
766: | `uncovered` | no capable frame of S evaluates it, and no cited authority excludes it; that absence is the counterexample | `falsified` |
767: | `unknown` | the admissible evidence cannot decide whether a capable frame of S covers it, as where the actor capability or the materiality is unknown | `indeterminate` |
768: 
769: These values are results of `audit_coverage` for this predicate, never
770: results of the covered evaluation itself. `satisfied` for an excluded row
771: establishes that the obligation is met by the cited exclusion, never that
772: the evaluation is covered or was performed; the status keeps that
773: distinction (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Recording). In a conjunction over the
774: governed claim, an evaluation whose row is `uncovered` is required
775: coverage that no planned assessment addresses
776: ([FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)), never a
777: `falsified` component. Where the coverage tuple itself is stale, advanced,
778: ambiguous or mismatched, the audit returns `invalid_basis` (RF-005) and
779: assigns no status. The mapping is new in this corpus. Purpose and material
780: relation: a coverage claim combined with other results is read in the one
781: core, so a conditional, conflicted, unknown or uncovered row is never read
782: as covered, and a cited exclusion is never read as a failure (P5, P6).
783: 
784: ### Interaction coverage
785: 
786: Evaluation-row coverage is insufficient when two covered relations interact
787: in a way capable of changing the governed outcome. Every material
788: interaction is covered by one frame, a declared conjunction, a translation
789: or a material composition evaluation (P4a, P2; rc.2
790: #interaction-coverage).
791: 
792: ### Authority coverage
793: 
794: Every material evaluation identifies semantic and decision authority.
795: Every material operation also identifies its existing construction,
796: transformation, admission, publication or mutation authority. A frame set
797: with broad observational reach, an unresolved decision owner or an
798: effectful path without operation authority is not closed (P6; rc.2
799: #authority-coverage).
800: 
801: ### Failure coverage
802: 
803: Coverage includes known success, refusal, boundary, integration, recovery,
804: reconstruction and competing-path cases where they are material.
805: Historical failures stay first-class coverage inputs until a declared frame
806: detects or excludes their recurrence (P4b, P5; rc.2 #failure-coverage).


METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md member_sha256=d64ee5c05aaefac346116c2e43eabf193dd84123f1d461070ecd378ce5e9b551 lines=817-839
817: ### Operational full coverage
818: 
819: A frame set has operational full coverage for its declared tuple when
820: (rc.2 #operational-full-coverage):
821: 
822: 1. every known material evaluation is covered by at least one capable
823:    frame;
824: 2. every material interaction has a declared evaluation, conjunction,
825:    translation or composition relation;
826: 3. every evaluation has semantic and decision authority, and every
827:    material operation has its inherited operation authority;
828: 4. every mandatory claim has an admissible evidence path and a refusal
829:    path;
830: 5. the required independently activated overlaps and
831:    assurance-independence conditions are present;
832: 6. no unresolved frame-result conflict is hidden by aggregation;
833: 7. excluded evaluations cite their governing authority; and
834: 8. uncovered and unknown residuals are explicit and compatible with the
835:    claim.
836: 
837: Operational full coverage is relative to its tuple. It is not a claim that
838: no undiscovered evaluation exists (P6; P0 with the open-world premise).

880: ### Diagnostic order
881: 
882: Diagnosis asks, in this order (P2; rc.2 #diagnostic-order):
883: 
884: 1. Was the correct declared frame activated?
885: 2. Were the subject and basis exact?
886: 3. Was the actor inside the capability envelope?
887: 4. Was admissible evidence available?
888: 5. Is a material variable or invariant missing from the frame?
889: 6. Is a required conjunction or translation missing?
890: 7. Is the evaluation family itself wrong or incomplete?
891: 8. Is another frame required?
892: 
893: Question 1 is answered by family inclusion, not by set membership. An
894: evaluation is within a frame's family when the question it decides is one
895: the frame's declared evaluation family states, at the frame's declared
896: coordinates (RF-001). Membership of the frame in the frame set, the frame's
897: name, a role label or similar wording of the question does not place an
898: evaluation in the frame's family; an activation of a frame on an evaluation
899: outside its family answers question 1 no, whatever the frame's standing in
900: the set. The test is a tightening the predecessor implies and does not
901: state (P2, the evaluations determine the attention surface; P1, a name
902: carries no meaning; the material relation drawn is evaluation-to-family
903: inclusion; rc.2 #diagnostic-order, #evaluation, where similar wording
904: proves no shared family, #rf-001-evaluation-relativity and
905: #applicability-and-required-results, where a frame name or listed family is
906: no activation trigger by itself).
907: 
908: The order prevents every difficult evaluation from creating another frame.
909: 
910: ### Revision actions
911: 
912: A revision may (P4b; rc.2 #revision-actions): clarify activation or
913: evidence acquisition; change the capability envelope; add or remove a
914: material relation; split an overloaded frame; merge duplicative frames
915: where capability and authority stay sound; add intentional overlap; add or
916: revise a conjunction or translation; retire a frame whose evaluation family
917: is no longer material; or revise the project evaluation inventory. Every
918: material revision changes frame identity or revision coordinates and states
919: which prior activations, results and coverage claims require reevaluation
920: (P3, P4b).
921: 
922: Stated plainly: a material revision of a frame produces a new frame
923: revision coordinate. Every prior closed result bound to the previous
924: revision of a materially revised frame is bound to a mismatched coordinate
925: (RF-005) and is invalidated for reuse until it is re-checked against the
926: new revision (RF-011; ACTIVATION §7). The revision record lists those
927: results as reopened; a result leaves that list only by a recorded re-check
928: that finds it demonstrably independent of the change, or by re-evaluation
929: on the new revision. A material revision does not select which of the
930: results bound to the prior revision it reopens, and silence does not keep
931: a result closed. The reopening by default is a tightening the predecessor
932: implies and does not state (P3, P4b; rc.2 #revision-actions, which makes
933: the revision state the results that require reevaluation,
934: #rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates, #rf-011-topology-mutation-and-recharting
935: and #return-a-closed-result, whose demonstrably independent surviving
936: results are the re-check's one survival route).
937: 
938: Whether a revision needs a new frame revision coordinate turns on the
939: frame's declarations; whether a result already closed stays valid is a
940: separate question. A revision is material when it changes a frame
941: declaration in a way that is material under
942: [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology). A revision that changes no
943: declaration of the frame needs no new coordinate. That answer decides
944: nothing about any result: an unchanged declaration is no ground for
945: keeping a result closed. Whether a closed result stays valid is decided
946: by the reuse rule of
947: [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), with materiality
948: as [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology) defines it, and that rule
949: can reopen results although no declaration changed; results it reopens
950: without a material revision are recorded as reopened in the work state
951: ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)). For example, a
952: clarification that finds a recorded activation outside its frame's family,
953: so that the result fails the exact applicability check of ACTIVATION §7
954: ([RF-001](#rf-001-evaluation-relativity);
955: [Diagnostic order](#diagnostic-order) question 1), or newly acquired
956: admissible evidence that is material to a closed result, a material
957: input change under ACTIVATION §7, reopens that result
958: and every coverage ledger row and coverage claim that consumed it, and
959: preserves every demonstrably independent surviving result. A harmless
960: explanatory clarification, which changes no material input and is no
961: revising observation, invalidates no result by itself;
962: reuse still requires the consumer's exact applicability check (P3, P6;

965: ## 11. The activation packet
966: 
967: An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame
968: configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete
969: workspace from ambient context (P0; rc.2 #agentic-use). The minimum
970: activation packet contains:
971: 
972: - frame identity and revision;
973: - the evaluation and its result algebra;
974: - the exact subject and basis;
975: - the material relations and applicable invariants;
976: - semantic, evaluation, operation where material, and decision authority;
977: - admissible evidence and tools;
978: - the capability and context envelope;
979: - exclusions and prohibited assumptions;
980: - declared frame dependencies or conjunction outputs; and
981: - invalidation, stop and reconfiguration conditions.
982: 
983: The actor may own its internal reasoning and search where the governing
984: method permits. It returns through the declared result relation. Hidden
985: internal reasoning is no substitute for required evidence, provenance or
986: authority (P6). Frame size is optimised for reliable evaluation, not for
987: maximum context loading: a more capable actor may activate a broader frame
988: and a less capable one may use a lawful refinement sequence, and both
989: preserve the same material invariants and authority relations (P0, P2;
990: RF-014).
991:

METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md member_sha256=b4b8cafae7da0885f4177e9114d5effc21637ed5a44deb31c3791be658a77a24 lines=825-874
825: ### Universal intake triage
826: 
827: There is one front door for substantive change. The intake label does not
828: determine the process class: a reported bug, feature request, issue,
829: regression, operator finding, release blocker or scenario failure all enter
830: through the same intake triage (P2, P6; rc.2 #universal-intake-triage).
831: 
832: Intake triage determines six things: whether the report represents a
833: substantive change at all; the affected product boundary and intended
834: scope; the lawful change class; the lawful re-entry point into the
835: constitutional chain; the downstream surfaces and evidence that must be
836: repriced, re-derived or re-proved, a determination whose evidence part is
837: the selection `S_Δ` over the impact cover `I(Δ)` of the affected surfaces
838: ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse));
839: and whether the work remains within the
840: currently declared release scope or requires repricing of that release
841: plan. No bug, feature, issue or other intake bypasses this triage by going
842: straight to code, tests or release handling. The purpose is not a separate
843: tracking bureaucracy; it is to classify impact correctly so the change
844: enters the method at the right constitutional boundary.
845: 
846: Triage diagnoses among the four causes of
847: [ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation),
848: a defective realisation, an inadequate governing requirement or design, an
849: inaccurate predictive model, and insufficient observation, and routes each
850: supported repair to the owner of its cause rather than inferring it from
851: the intake label; severity and priority follow the policies that
852: [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) owns; a bug list projects existing work state. This
853: paragraph applies ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis and states no
854: second relation (P2, P6).
855: 
856: Triage triangulates a failure across the applicable reference frames over
857: the same subject and basis. Each frame tests candidate diagnoses against
858: its material workspace variables, governing relations and evidence; their
859: combined results constrain the supported cause, preserve unresolved
860: alternatives and uncertainty, and identify the smallest sufficient lawful
861: scope of repair. The frame that exposes a failure need not contain its
862: cause. Repeating the same analysis under different frame names supplies no
863: additional causal evidence. The smallest sufficient applicable frame
864: configuration is used, under frame applicability and frames in conjunction
865: (REFERENCE_FRAME §5 and §6). The frames' results combine under the one
866: [conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results): each
867: keeps the diagnosis it evaluated as its predicate, a counterexample that
868: one frame finds survives the join, and a frame planned and not applied
869: leaves its diagnosis open, never ruled out. Counterexample localisation
870: applies where required (ASSURANCE; provenance rc.2 STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE
871: #counterexample-localization). This prescribes no reviewer count and no new
872: review round; required independence stays intact. A diagnosis grants no
873: repair effects and does not establish that governing meaning must change: a
874: candidate may instead need correction under sufficient existing law (P6).

911: ### Computed classification and treatment
912: 
913: Intake supplies one reusable classification result rather than requiring
914: each role to reconstruct the same facts (P4b, P6, P1; rc.2
915: #computed-classification-and-treatment). Three annotations keep the kinds
916: of determination apart: C denotes reproducible facts and declared rule
917: application; J denotes residual semantic or materiality judgment; O denotes
918: a ruling reserved to its actual owner. The annotations grant no authority,
919: an instance of
920: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
921: creates no authority, and introduce no calculus kind, runtime, classifier interface or mandatory
922: document.
923: 
924: The explicitly selected source, worksite or qualification capability
925: produces C over the exact request and desired outcome, the known targets
926: and effects, the operation grant and work lifetime, the product definition
927: and governing basis, the baseline and the available candidate, the declared
928: relations, the accepted design and trace bindings, the evidence and the
929: applicable rules. Its output identifies the producer and procedure
930: revision, the inputs, the result, the scope, the source routes, the
931: reproduction relation, the unknowns and the invalidators. A missing
932: candidate or missing evidence is an input state, not a claim that nothing
933: changed.
934: 
935: The computed result exposes four things, in this order:
936: 
937: 1. Authority traversal. Follow the explicit source, ownership, dependency,
938:    composition and projection declarations from the affected targets and
939:    effects. Identify each reached layer and owner, its exact basis and its
940:    changed, unchanged or unknown relation, the traversed edges and the
941:    unresolved frontier. Include root, authority and grant changes even when
942:    public bytes are equal. An absent edge does not prove irrelevance;
943:    undeclared or semantically uncertain materiality remains J.
944: 2. Public delta. Enumerate the complete relevant serialised member universe
945:    under its owning declaration and applicable projection, including helper
946:    and generated dependencies. Report added and removed identities and
947:    every retained member with changed typed value or bytes, with exact
948:    before and after values. A rename is removal plus addition unless its
949:    owner supplies an identity-preserving relation. A missing candidate,
950:    incomplete enumeration, ambiguous identity or unavailable projection
951:    leaves the affected delta unknown; membership equality alone proves no
952:    value equality (P3).
953: 3. Accepted-design coverage. Join changed bytes and relations to explicit
954:    accepted scope, traces and acceptance evidence. Distinguish covered,
955:    missing, stale, ambiguous and outside-scope evidence. A filename, listed
956:    artifact or digest alone establishes no accepted coverage. Current trace
957:    coverage is a computed fact; residual semantic sufficiency remains J.
958: 4. Rule-determined treatment. Apply only declared rules with sufficient
959:    input facts, recording their owners, matched predicates and
960:    consequences. Expose the smallest lawful re-entry, the next action, the
961:    applicable evidence or assessment, the reserved ruling and the carrier
962:    lifetime, with any conflict or missing premise still unresolved. A label
963:    or filename cannot select the route. When rules settle the question, no
964:    residual judgment is invented.
965: 
966: The values these steps assign, a relation changed, unchanged or unknown,
967: an identity added, removed or retained with a changed value, and evidence
968: covered, missing, stale, ambiguous or outside scope, are facts of the
969: computed result. They are not results of an evaluation and map to no core
970: value. An evaluation that consumes them returns its own core value with
971: its predicate under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), and
972: an unknown it consumes stays unknown. Purpose and material relation: a
973: classification fact is never combined as an evaluation result, so
974: evidence classified covered, or a relation classified unchanged, cannot
975: stand in for a `satisfied` result (P5, P1).
976: 
977: A public delta or other nonconformance does not itself require changing
978: the governing contract. If that contract remains sufficient for the
979: authorised outcome, the candidate is rejected or locally repaired within
980: its grant. The actual governing owner is re-entered when the explicitly
981: selected desired outcome requires changed meaning or an applicable
982: assessment establishes governing insufficiency. C determines that
983: consequence only from sufficient declared premises; unresolved intended
984: meaning or necessity is J, and any reserved decision remains O. Candidate
985: behaviour cannot author its own target law (P6).
986: 
987: Unknown treatment withholds dependent reliance or promotion, not unrelated
988: authorised work. An existing bounded construction or evidence grant may
989: permit the cheapest useful discriminator, including obtaining the first
990: candidate, without asserting that the candidate is conformant; it carries
991: its own exact subject, territory, operations and stop conditions. The
992: affected C result is updated before dependent effects or promotion rely on
993: newly available evidence. A mistaken route is corrected at its smallest
994: affected owner, preserving the original cause, the attempted subject, the
995: observed effect state and valid progress. Retry requires the applicable
996: outcome, authority and safe-recovery conditions; an effect of uncertain
997: completion (`completion_unknown`, or `not_effected` with its end not
998: established, under [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects)) cannot
999: be silently treated
1000: as no effect, and is reconciled as ACTIVATION §5 states before any retry
1001: or dependent action (P5).
1002: 
1003: A new role, conversation or resumption reuses valid C after checking exact
1004: applicability; reuse and invalidation are
1005: [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), which this
1006: paragraph applies to C. The material inputs of C, whose change is that
1007: rule's material input change and invalidates the affected claims of C
1008: before reliance, are by name: the request, the candidate, an owner or
1009: root relation, a projection, a design trace or acceptance, a rule
1010: applied, the configuration and the material evidence. A changed basis
1011: and a declared revising observation, that rule's other two
1012: invalidators, invalidate likewise. Predecessor and
1013: successor identities, changed inputs, surviving facts and affected J
1014: dependencies are preserved; the wider frontier is recomputed where
1015: independence is unproved (ACTIVATION §7).
1016: [TICKETS §7](TICKETS.md#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity) owns
1017: the existing carrier and the recorded J and O continuity rules (provenance
1018: rc.2 TICKET_METHOD #recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity).
