1782: ## 11. Build-tenant binding
1783: 
1784: This section owns the relation between a product's WHAT and the build
1785: tenants that realise it: what a tenant binds, what stays fixed while it
1786: chooses, and what its evidence shows. It applies to every product built
1787: with this method (P2, P1, P6).
1788: 
1789: Terms used in this section:
1790: 
1791: - A build tenant is one independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a
1792:   product's WHAT. The build-tenancy context of
1793:   [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#8-what-how-and-work-carriers)
1794:   names it, and the product definition's tenant registry locates each one.
1795: - The requirements calculus of a product is the set of obligations its
1796:   WHAT states, the outcomes it permits, and its rules for refining and
1797:   composing the work that realises it.
1798: - A computational calculus is a declared set of executable operations,
1799:   with the laws by which they compose, the transformations they permit,
1800:   and their effects and resource behaviour, as far as these are material
1801:   to the obligations.
1802: - An execution environment is the concrete means that performs those
1803:   operations: a technology stack; a human process, made of people, roles,
1804:   documents, communication channels and decision procedures; or a
1805:   combination of the two.
1806: - A tenant's build-tenant binding has two parts: its calculus binding,
1807:   from the requirements calculus to its computational calculus, and its
1808:   execution binding, from that computational calculus to its execution
1809:   environment. A tenant's registry entry locates the tenant; it is not the
1810:   binding.
1811: - A generic procedure is a method procedure whose scope is independent of
1812:   the selected execution environment. It and its projections preserve the
1813:   bindings Rule 2 permits: code, an event stream or reconstruction from a
1814:   complete history is required only where the governing obligations or
1815:   the selected execution binding require it, and an adequate human
1816:   process using current records and direct observation is a permitted
1817:   execution binding of a generic procedure that requires none of them
1818:   (P1, P6; law carried from the common binding requirement).
1819: - Author identity and actor identity are as
1820:   [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment) defines them:
1821:   authorship is one condition of an assessment's independence there, and
1822:   an actor's identity is not an authority.
1823:   Operation kind is what an operation does, such as construct, assess,
1824:   relay, record, measure or decide, together with the authority that kind
1825:   of operation requires.
1826: 
1827: Rules:
1828: 
1829: 1. Realisations of one WHAT. One WHAT is realised by one or more
1830:    independent build tenants, whatever the physical layout. The WHAT is
1831:    constitutional and each tenant's realisation is HOW; a tenant-local
1832:    realisation stays derivative until its governing truth is ratified in
1833:    specification (§2). Each tenant binds the product's requirements
1834:    calculus to a declared computational calculus and binds that calculus
1835:    to a concrete execution environment. Both bindings are that tenant's
1836:    design and realisation: they are declared in its existing design and
1837:    realisation surfaces, chosen under the Design rule (§2) and recorded as
1838:    design decisions (§10), and the method requires no further carrier. The
1839:    tenant owns its binding, its realisation and their evidence; the WHAT
1840:    keeps its meaning (P2, P6).
1841: 2. Selection. The execution environment may be a technology stack, a
1842:    human process or a combination. Its selection stays within the
1843:    requirements calculus, including every human decision that calculus
1844:    requires: no choice of environment removes a required human decision or
1845:    a required independent assessment. Author identity, actor identity and
1846:    operation kind stay distinct, and none determines another. Who authored
1847:    a tenant does not select its environment; one actor may perform
1848:    operations of several kinds, each under its own grant; and an actor's
1849:    identity neither decides the kind of an operation nor grants authority
1850:    for it. A person performing an operation does not by that make it human
1851:    adjudication: §5 states the admission that makes an operation human
1852:    adjudication and how a person who decides under policy without it is
1853:    governed. The same holds for every decision the requirements reserve to
1854:    a human: the person the governing authority admits for it takes it, and
1855:    a person's part elsewhere in the process does not (P6, P1).
1856: 3. Material content. For the obligations it serves, the binding
1857:    identifies:
1858:    - the operations, each with its inputs, outputs, effects and outcome
1859:      values; each outcome value maps to exactly one core value under
1860:      [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), and an intended
1861:      external effect, one of uncertain completion included, is recorded as
1862:      [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects) states;
1863:    - the composition laws, and the transformations the calculus permits;
1864:    - the resource measures;
1865:    - the operational assumptions on which conformance depends, among them
1866:      those about actors, tools, availability and failure.
1867: 
1868:    Human effort, elapsed time, communication and machine resources are
1869:    measured where a selected obligation needs them. Each measure states its
1870:    unit and its boundary: what is counted, and where measurement starts and
1871:    stops. A resource claim without its unit or its boundary supports no
1872:    conformance claim. The size of a selected context is measured as
1873:    [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)
1874:    step 3 measures it, against the capacity the binding declares for the
1875:    actor. The law for declaring, measuring and honouring resource limits
1876:    is [ACTIVATION §6 Resource limits](ACTIVATION.md#resource-limits), and
1877:    this rule binds it: the values of a step's time, spend and other
1878:    resource limits, and the units and boundaries the environment can
1879:    measure, are those of the execution binding, stated before the
1880:    activation they limit. Where a configuration states its resource limits
1881:    and its assumptions about failure
1882:    ([ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration)), it takes
1883:    them from this binding (P0, P2, P5).
1884: 4. Conformance evidence. The obligations of the requirements calculus
1885:    decide fitness; the kind of executor alone neither accepts nor rejects a
1886:    realisation. Evidence establishes how the bound realisation satisfies
1887:    the required meaning and constraints, including the applicable
1888:    authority, independence, failure and recovery conditions. Conformance is
1889:    judged under
1890:    [EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations), and two
1891:    conforming tenants need not behave identically outside the contract.
1892:    Each assessment returns a core value for its predicate, and the tenant's
1893:    conformance is their
1894:    [conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results), with the
1895:    obligations of the requirements calculus as its required coverage. A
1896:    convenient stack never weakens an obligation. An execution plan that
1897:    merges two required independent assessments, or substitutes an
1898:    automated result for a required human decision, is a counterexample to
1899:    the obligation it weakens, so the binding's conformance for that
1900:    obligation is `falsified`; in any run under such a plan the lost
1901:    assessment or decision has no applicable closed result. Matching
1902:    outputs, lower cost or a faster run do not discharge the lost
1903:    independence or authority. A claim that a binding preserves categorical
1904:    structure is a further claim: it meets the Formal fragment of
1905:    [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra) and stays distinct from
1906:    conformance on the equivalence ladder of EVALUATION §6 (P6, P1, P4b).
1907: 5. Reuse. A computational calculus may be reused across tenants and
1908:    execution environments wherever each binding satisfies its laws, and
1909:    each binding shows that it does. A different language, tool, team or
1910:    person does not by itself require a different calculus: replacing the
1911:    executor of an operation while the calculus's laws hold changes the
1912:    execution binding, not the calculus (P1, P4a).
1913: 6. Representation. A representation of the requirements calculus or of a
1914:    binding in a_c, the axiomatic calculus of
1915:    [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md), prescribes no executor and
1916:    does not establish execution conformance by structural validation alone
1917:    ([AC-018](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation)).
1918:    An a_c model of a human process that passes structural validation
1919:    neither selects an automated executor nor shows that the process meets
1920:    its requirements; execution conformance needs its own evidence under
1921:    rule 4 (P1, P6).
1922: 7. Three accounts. The algorithmic, informational and computational
1923:    accounts of a construction, which
1924:    [FOUNDATIONS §2 Accounts of a construction](FOUNDATIONS.md#accounts-of-a-construction)
1925:    defines, apply across the binding, from the requirements calculus
1926:    through the computational calculus to the execution environment. The
1927:    binding keeps the three accounts apart. A mapping from one account to
1928:    another is a transformation: what it preserves, the law that licenses
1929:    it, and whether it is exact or approximate with its adequacy relation
1930:    and end-to-end bound, are stated and discharged under
1931:    [ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement), and where it is
1932:    recorded in a_c its record is
1933:    [AC-013](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-013-transformation). The binding adds
1934:    only which accounts the mapping joins and the evidence, in its
1935:    execution environment, that discharges the preservation (P1, P0, P4a,
1936:    P6).

METHOD SOURCE c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3:specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/claude/standards/TICKETS.md member_sha256=8d244a16b11f17a9e1a85ecf8d7e1dfb3686ea79a09b885321727d620659c43e lines=627-749
627: ### Carrier selection
628: 
629: Every execution governed by this method uses one run-scoped execution
630: contract. The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the
631: smallest lawful source carrier: first establish the applicable upstream
632: work authority, then select the first matching row below. For work inside
633: an admitted sprint the local carrier boundary is that sprint; otherwise it
634: is the current run (P2, P4b, P6; rc.2 #work-carrier-to-execution-rule).
635: 
636: | Condition | Execution-contract source | Durable-ticket decision |
637: |---|---|---|
638: | no applicable upstream work authority exists | no execution contract is admitted | do not create a ticket as substitute authority; stop or re-enter |
639: | applicable authority exists and an existing admitted ticket covers the exact work | derive the run-scoped contract from that ticket | reuse it; do not create another ticket |
640: | applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and the work or an open obligation needs independent state beyond the local carrier boundary | one durable ticket plus the run-scoped contract | create or update the ticket only under ticket-state authority |
641: | applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and the work stays inside one admitted sprint with no state required after sprint close | the sprint manifest plus one manifest-local iteration entry | do not create a durable ticket |
642: | applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket or sprint covers the work, and the work ends in the current run with no independent surviving state | an intake-drafted run-scoped contract | do not create a durable ticket |
643: 
644: "Ticket-shaped" describes the categorisation, closure criteria, proof
645: surface, non-closure conditions and the other required execution-contract
646: fields (§4, Required fields). It creates no durable ticket identity and no
647: ticket-lane state (P3).
648: 
649: Absence of a durable ticket neither requires nor authorises creating one.
650: An exact product-authorised work instruction may supply the upstream work
651: authority for a one-run contract; a generic request or a model-widened
652: scope cannot. A durable ticket is created or updated only when the table
653: requires surviving state and the actor holds ticket-state authority. An
654: explicit instruction from ticket-state authority to create a durable record
655: selects that durability; it does not admit an execution contract or widen
656: its upstream work authority (P6, P2).
657: 
658: The step side of admission is [ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#admission) and
659: is defined there once: drafting versus admission inside one invocation, the
660: condition under which execution may begin, what admission may never be
661: inferred from (including ticket or sprint presence, lane placement and
662: `active` status), the coordinates an admitted result carries, the recording
663: of every result, withheld closure and residual obligation before return,
664: and refusal when no durable result and evidence surface is available. This
665: member adds the carrier side (P6, P4b). The admission mechanism and the
666: durable result and evidence surface are the ones the product definition
667: binds. When that surface is the ticket or the sprint manifest, the admitted
668: result with its coordinates is recorded there. A carrier's lane, status or
669: prose that asserts admission without those coordinates is not admission
670: evidence, and the contract it describes remains drafted or rejected.
671: 
672: When admission is absent or rejected, ACTIVATION §1 returns the missing
673: work authority without execution. Before that return, an obligation that
674: must survive the run is carried as follows (P4b, P6): it becomes a
675: sprint-local entry when its lifetime stays inside the admitted sprint;
676: otherwise it is recorded as a durable ticket, only under ticket-state
677: authority; where that authority is absent, it is retained in the
678: contract's named durable result and evidence surface or in an
679: already-authorised enclosing carrier, closure is marked withheld on
680: ticket-state authority, and the required re-entry is returned.
681: 
682: Execution and closure use the same admitted categorisation, criteria,
683: proof surface and non-closure conditions. The resulting state still flows
684: through proof, gap analysis and repricing (P6, P2).
685: 
686: ### Execution contract admission
687: 
688: The runtime execution flow should treat a ticket, a sprint entry or a
689: drafted work contract as an admission candidate, never as automatic truth;
690: the contract carries at minimum the states named in ACTIVATION §1
691: (drafted, admitted, rejected, superseded). An admitted execution contract
692: should be logged in runtime and event truth, available to prompt assembly,
693: and available to later closure checking, so that execution and closure
694: read the same admitted basis (P6,
695: P4b; rc.2 #execution-contract-admission). The refusal of self-certification
696: is ACTIVATION §1.
697: 
698: Admission validates a contract against its cited product outcome,
699: prerequisite or experiment basis and does not admit that basis (ACTIVATION
700: §1). Admission or renewal of the basis belongs to the authority owning the
701: selected goals work wave, or its explicitly bounded proxy, and stays
702: durably legible in the existing goals or ticket authority
703: ([SPEC_METHOD §3](SPEC_METHOD.md#3-outcome-conservation)). A ticket's
704: `active` status, its lane, or an admitted or retained contract is therefore
705: never the admission of a growth basis (P6, P2).
706: 
707: ### Evaluation criteria and non-closure conditions
708: 
709: An execution contract should expose both what counts as progress or
710: completion and what still counts as failure even when some local proof is
711: green. At minimum it should make `evaluation_criteria` and
712: `non_closure_conditions` visible. These are the local gain function for
713: the work (P6, P2; rc.2
714: #evaluation-criteria-and-non-closure-conditions).
715: 
716: For implementation migrations, typical non-closure conditions are: the old
717: authoritative path still passes in normal execution within the declared
718: affected scope; mixed old and new proof is still accepted; a proxy or
719: partial interface implementation still stands in the acceptance path;
720: competing or ambiguous executable authority remains reachable on the
721: claimed product acceptance path; ticket wording, product wording and proof
722: wording are not reconciled. These conditions are not optional commentary;
723: they are the anti-self-deception surface for execution (P6).
724: 
725: Residual implementation debt outside the claimed acceptance path is not by
726: itself a non-closure condition. It may be deferred only under the
727: path-relative authority and explicit disposition rules of
728: [SPEC_METHOD §7](SPEC_METHOD.md#constitutional-migration-options) (P2).
729: 
730: ### Bounded-context term binding
731: 
732: Ticket and work-instruction terms resolve under the bounded-context
733: semantic resolution of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5. A ticket may use an
734: unqualified term when its cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis
735: and affected scope select exactly one bounded-context meaning (P1, P3;
736: rc.2 #bounded-context-term-binding).
737: 
738: When a ticket spans contexts, or a material term has competing meanings,
739: the ticket cites the applicable product-definition disambiguation or the
740: owner-authorised import, translation, equivalence or disambiguation
741: carrier; it may reference that relation rather than duplicate it. Ticket
742: prose, actor familiarity, a matching glossary heading, tenant placement or
743: comment context cannot select meaning or transfer authority (P1, P6).
744: 
745: An unresolved or multiply resolved material term blocks execution-contract
746: admission and closure for the affected claim. Opening or updating the
747: ticket records the pressure and does not cure it; resolution re-enters at
748: the authority that owns the missing context or semantic relation (P1, P5).

1036: ## 7. Authority, judgment, closure and state
1037: 
1038: The generic law is tier 1: a constructor's self-review is construction
1039: output and the independent-assessment protocol is
1040: [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment); acceptance as the
1041: decision owner's disposition, and closure by stated condition rather than
1042: by reviewer approval, is [EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance); reuse
1043: of a closed result is [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse).
1044: This section states what those laws require of work carriers.
1045: 
1046: ### Execution and verification authority separation (UP-007)
1047: 
1048: Authority to author or implement a change is not independent authority to
1049: verify it. What counts as independent, including that the reviewer is
1050: not the author of the reviewed subject, and the protocol an independent
1051: assessment follows are
1052: [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment). Where
1053: independent review is required, the reviewer identifies the exact
1054: subject, basis, scope, exclusions, evidence, verdict and unresolved
1055: findings (P6; rc.2
1056: #execution-and-verification-authority-separation-stdo-up-007). Review
1057: findings must cite current authority and the code or proof paths they
1058: rest on, not only historical commentary (P6, P1; provenance rc.2
1059: authority_compressions/ticket_method.compressed.md, a claim no rc.2 body
1060: states).
1061: 
1062: Self-review remains useful authoring evidence and cannot be relabelled as
1063: independent. Human authority may accept or reject the claim; it does not
1064: make implementer self-review independent. The boundaries at which this
1065: method requires independent assessment are this member's policy, which
1066: EVALUATION §3 names; a governing basis may add others, as that section
1067: states. Independent review is required at
1068: product, qualification, release and explicitly risk-bearing boundaries that
1069: claim it, not for every local implementation step (P6, P2).
1070: 
1071: A claimed independent review may support promotion or closure only when its
1072: exact subject and verdict are durably traceable through an existing ticket,
1073: commentary, qualification or release-evidence carrier. A statement that
1074: review occurred, an unbound conversation summary or an unavailable draft is
1075: not the review verdict. This rule requires no separate receipt, carrier or
1076: review round (P6, P4b).
1077: 
1078: A ticket's review verdict is bounded by the exact reviewed claim and its
1079: applicable hard stops. When a finding blocks current promotion, and what a
1080: valid observation outside that boundary does, are stated once at
1081: [EVALUATION §5 When a finding blocks promotion](EVALUATION.md#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion);
1082: this carrier applies that section to a ticket's review and adds no
1083: trigger (P2, P6).
1084: 
1085: A direct or lawfully proxied human ruling receives a durable disposition
1086: before the next affected acceptance boundary. Its source wording stays
1087: distinct from agent interpretation. Opening a ticket records the
1088: obligation and does not satisfy it, and an agent cannot widen the ruling
1089: while recording it (P6, P4b).
1090: 
1091: Where the agentic construction relation applies (ACTIVATION §1, bound to
1092: this method by [SPEC_METHOD §8](SPEC_METHOD.md#8-bounded-execution-in-this-method)),
1093: the active work item identifies the selected execution basis, the bounded
1094: affected relation set, the delegated construction and assessment authority,
1095: and the re-entry conditions. It may point to accepted design and existing
1096: evidence carriers rather than restate them. Ticket state, ticket prose or
1097: an admitted execution contract cannot widen that basis or substitute for
1098: the live-surface assessment the relation requires (P6, P0).
1099: 
1100: The reviewable transition (ACTIVATION §7, Transition evidence) may be
1101: carried by an existing ticket, commentary, commit, qualification or
1102: release-evidence surface. No new ticket state, document type, review round
1103: or approval ceremony is required. This member carries selection and
1104: traceability; ACTIVATION §1 and SPEC_METHOD §8 own the execution semantics
1105: (P2, P6).
1106: 
1107: ### Recorded judgment and owner-ruling continuity
1108: 
1109: A residual judgment that another activation needs is recorded once, with
1110: its owning work, in the existing carrier selected under §5. The record
1111: identifies the question; the exact subject and governing basis; the
1112: supporting computed facts and evidence; the responsible actor and its
1113: authority; the conclusion and its scope; the uncertainty; and a concrete
1114: revising observation that lets a consumer determine whether the conclusion
1115: still applies. A question settled by rule needs no invented J record (P4b,
1116: P6; rc.2 #recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity; C, J and O are
1117: the annotations of [SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#computed-classification-and-treatment)).
1118: 
1119: Later roles and resumed runs recover the result and check its
1120: applicability rather than re-author unchanged judgment. Reuse and
1121: invalidation are
1122: [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse): changed material
1123: inputs, a declared revising observation or a changed basis invalidate
1124: the affected result, preserving the original result and its successor
1125: relation and keeping only demonstrably independent results, and a new
1126: role or conversation alone invalidates nothing. For a recorded judgment
1127: the material inputs include its supporting computed facts and evidence,
1128: and its declared revising observation is the one the record states;
1129: reassessment covers what the change affects. The result may reference
1130: current C outputs; reuse cannot silently turn unknown facts into
1131: established premises (P4b, P5). Required independent assessment may consume valid C, but
1132: its assessor acquires sufficient exact evidence and supplies its own
1133: judgment under the actual independence condition; reusing the author's J
1134: cannot satisfy that condition (P6; EVALUATION §3).
1135: 
1136: A direct or lawfully proxied owner ruling is recorded in its original
1137: wording, with its owner, exact subject and basis, permitted scope and
1138: effects, conditions and source, separately from agent interpretation. Later
1139: work consumes that same ruling while it applies; it neither widens the
1140: ruling nor requests unchanged authority again. New ambiguity or a
1141: materially changed decision returns only the affected question to its
1142: owner. J is not O, and recording either cannot create admission,
1143: acceptance, effects or continuation beyond the original grant (P6, P3).
1144: 
1145: These results follow the lifetime of the existing run, sprint or durable
1146: ticket and its named result and evidence surface. They require no separate
1147: judgment registry, no ticket per judgment and no additional approval
1148: ceremony (P2).
1149: 
1150: Repricing gives each affected obligation a disposition in that same
1151: carrier: retained, superseded, deferred or withdrawn, with its owning
1152: authority and applicable evidence links. Surviving work is preserved and
1153: changed dependencies are explained; unaffected history is not copied into
1154: a parallel ledger. An owner decision is presented as the short consequence
1155: delta needed to decide it, with the original ruling preserved separately.
1156: A general instruction to continue does not accept an undisclosed
1157: architectural or scope change (P4b, P6, P2).
1158: 
1159: The four repricing dispositions are recorded states of the obligation,
1160: set by its owning authority; they are not results and map to no core
1161: value. Each records the standing the obligation keeps after repricing,
1162: as the lifecycle statuses of
1163: [SPEC_METHOD §2](SPEC_METHOD.md#requirement-categories-and-classification)
1164: record a requirement's, and answers no predicate that an evaluation
1165: decides on evidence. They differ from the disposition of an assessed
1166: candidate ([ACTIVATION §3 Disposition](ACTIVATION.md#disposition)), which
1167: is the acceptance result that FOUNDATIONS §4 Results places in the core,
1168: because a repricing disposition accepts no candidate; and from the
1169: disposition of a predecessor claim
1170: ([RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)),
1171: which is a claim that qualification evaluates. An evaluation that reads
1172: them returns its own core value with its predicate under
1173: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). Purpose and material
1174: relation: a recorded disposition is never combined as an evaluation
1175: result, so a retained obligation is never read as satisfied, and a
1176: superseded, deferred or withdrawn one never as discharged (P5, P1, P6).
1177: 
1178: ### Condition-based closure and reuse
1179: 
1180: A work claim is complete only when every applicable declared obligation is
1181: satisfied by valid evidence for its exact subject, basis and scope; every
1182: required judgment and owner ruling is present and applicable; and no active
1183: non-closure condition remains. A mandatory obligation whose applicability is
1184: unknown, or whose evidence is insufficient, withholds the dependent claim;
1185: evidence presence alone is not satisfaction. The existing owner decides any
1186: reserved acceptance (P6, P5; rc.2 #condition-based-closure-and-reuse).
1187: This condition is the
1188: [conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results) with the
1189: declared obligations as required coverage. This section owns the
1190: closure condition of a work claim;
1191: [SPEC_METHOD §4 Consistency gate](SPEC_METHOD.md#consistency-gate)
1192: applies it as the gate over a declared change span.
1193: 
1194: Review evaluates these conditions; its occurrence is not the closing event.
1195: Where applicable law requires no independent review or reserved
1196: acceptance, a work claim is recorded as
1197: [ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)
1198: states in Recording a result without review, with the ticket as the
1199: existing carrier. The conditions that still apply include sprint-close
1200: law (§3) and the design profile's law (P6, P2).
1201: 
1202: An unchanged obligation reuses valid applicable evidence and recorded J
1203: and O under the reuse rule of
1204: [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse). For a work
1205: claim, the changed material inputs and revising observations that rule
1206: names include a material counterexample, changed evidence and a stated
1207: revising observation of a recorded J; with a changed basis, each
1208: invalidates the affected claim and its dependent results before further
1209: reliance. An unrelated observation is retained as bounded repricing input;
1210: it does not reopen a satisfied claim or expand the work automatically.
1211: Closure recording preserves the exact evaluated scope, the satisfied
1212: conditions, the evidence and the remaining residuals (P4b, P2).
1213: 
1214: ### Test case authority
1215: 
1216: Tests are proof projections from admitted work authority. Every
1217: substantive test case should derive along this chain (P6, P2; rc.2
1218: #test-case-authority):
1219: 
1220: ```text
1221: ticket -> intake triage -> lawful re-entry point -> governing requirement,
1222: design, module, published function, carrier, or closure surface -> test expectation
1223: ```
1224: 
1225: Tests do not derive authority from the current implementation. An
1226: acceptance predicate also needs an applicable supported entry or state and
1227: an obligation under the governing operating or threat model. Existing test
1228: presence cannot authorise an excluded threat or retain a superseded guard.
1229: When that responsibility changes, the affected predicates are audited, and
1230: unsupported expectations are retired under the owning basis without
1231: inventing a replacement guard. An actual conflict in live authority
1232: requires re-entry, not a test-only waiver (P6, P2).
1233: 
1234: Implementation behaviour is evidence. The code is never the arbiter of a
1235: test's expected result when code and test disagree (P6). When a ticket is
1236: fixed and a mismatch appears between implementation behaviour and test
1237: expectation, review reconciles the mismatch in this order:
1238: 
1239: 1. the ticket's `change_intent`, `change_class`, `re_entry_point`,
1240:    `target_truth`, `superseded_truth`, `closure_law`,
1241:    `evaluation_criteria` and `non_closure_conditions`;
1242: 2. the ticket's intake triage and lawful owning re-entry;
1243: 3. the governing requirement, design, module, published-function, carrier
1244:    or other cited authority surface;
1245: 4. the test case expectation;
1246: 5. the implementation.
1247: 
1248: The implementation may show that a test is stale, incomplete or too
1249: narrow; it cannot by itself authorise changing the expected result.
1250: Changing a test only because the current code behaves differently is a
1251: ticket-method defect. A test that predates a lawful ticket repricing is
1252: updated or removed only after naming the governing ticket and the authority
1253: change that superseded the old expectation. If the ticket is stale,
1254: ambiguous or missing the authority needed to decide the expectation, the
1255: work re-enters triage (§4) before either the code or the test is treated as
1256: correct. A passing test is closure evidence only when its expectation
1257: traces back to the admitted ticket and its governing authority chain (P6,
1258: P4b). The general test authority law is ASSURANCE §3; this clause is its
1259: ticket-local rule.
1260: 
1261: ### One-truth state projection and drift refusal (UP-009)
1262: 
1263: Work state has one authority chain: goals own the bounded work wave, the
1264: ticket owns ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone
1265: state (§1), and accepted design owns realisation decisions. Comments,
1266: dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections
1267: (P6, P3; rc.2 #one-truth-state-projection-and-drift-refusal-stdo-up-009).
1268: 
1269: Recency, visibility or repetition does not turn a projection into truth.
1270: Contradiction between the owning ticket, its required milestones, the
1271: current goals or the cited acceptance evidence blocks closure. Superseded
1272: evidence remains history and cannot be projected as current acceptance
1273: (P6, P4b).

# Intent

Provide concrete implementations of the STDO axiomatic calculus that preserve
source-owned identities, constraints, permitted variation and unresolved meaning
while making declared symbolic models easier to inspect and acquire.

Provide deterministic support tools for F_P Executives, Workers and Reviewers
using the source-owned contracts of Specification Methodology. Make their
selected inputs, acquired context, declared checks and execution/evidence
exchanges inspectable without taking ownership of the method or F_P judgment.

The shared specification defines the required behavior independently of a graph
library, authoring format, model provider or execution stack. A build tenant
chooses its computational realization and demonstrates the required preservation.
The first tenant uses Graphify's graph representation and tools. F_P remains
responsible for semantic interpretation; mechanical tools check only declared
properties and retain the evidence needed for further judgment.


WHAT/GOVERNING PREIMAGE SOURCE c2f67fec8154028d45d7cd7a2832dd4fade4d94b:a_c/specification/PRODUCT.md sha256=9ebc8342affe8c5e0afb08ebe22f3f98f73f7bdc64db00eee17674c47274bef7
# Axiomatic Calculus Implementations

## Product boundary

This source project constructs implementations of the **axiomatic calculus**,
`a_c`, identified by `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c`. Its bounded context
is `urn:a-c-implementations:bounded-context:realization`.

The exact selected published STDO `AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md` owns calculus meaning.
The shared requirements here own implementation obligations. A tenant's design
owns its computational calculus, representation, operations, concrete stack and
demonstrated fragment. Neither an implementation nor its successful use amends
the calculus or accepts a subject interpretation.

## Capability

A realization consumes an explicitly authored symbolic model and its exact
signature and basis. It checks a declared structural fragment, preserves the
model through its representation, and supports source-reenterable inspection
and bounded acquisition. It keeps constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals,
transformations and judgments distinguishable from ordinary objects and edges.

The initial Graphify realization carries all eight fundamental record families
and their exact content. Its mechanical checks and acquisition operations have
an explicitly bounded contract. It does not execute arbitrary predicates,
transform models, select applicable frames, infer logical truth or supply
semantic acceptance. Unsupported operations refuse rather than silently pass.

A tenant may also facilitate creation of that model from an exact source
corpus through a declared F_P authoring workflow. Graphify extraction and
discovery may supply authoring context inside this workflow; an existing
native interpretation is not a prerequisite. The workflow retains exact source
grounding, authoring provenance, coverage dispositions and unresolved meaning.
Authoring, mechanical validation, carrier generation and external semantic
assessment remain separate claims. A generated model starts as a proposal.

An unaccepted model may have a clearly identified **proposal view**. That view
is not `a_c.X.C` admission. An encoding represented as the calculus's accepted-
interpretation carrier relation requires a separate semantic judgment over the
exact unchanged model. Tooling checks the supplied coordinates; decision
authority and semantic fitness remain external judgments. Carrier admission is
a separate judgment over unchanged carrier bytes; creating bytes or passing a
partial check does not itself issue that judgment. Its declared assessment may
be mechanical, as in `F_D[v_carrier_admission]`.

## F_D support for F_P development actors

The Product additionally provides deterministic support tools for F_P
Executives, Workers and Reviewers building in a Specification Methodology
workspace. STDO3.0 owns the methodology and consequently the contracts these
tools support: lifecycle, role duties, triage/re-entry, frame/activation,
applicability, admission, results/conjunction, review/independence and acceptance.
The tools consume those contracts through an exact caller-selected method/profile
binding. a_c owns their supplied inputs, outputs, checked properties, public use
and qualification; it does not create a second lifecycle or coordinate F_P work.

| Deterministic support | Use by F_P actors |
|---|---|
| Discover tool contracts; bind/observe exact Product, method and current workspace | Executive, Worker and Reviewer identify supported operations, input identities, current material bytes and explicit unsupported contracts. |
| Resolve records/raw source/grounding; query authored dependencies, impact and coverage | All three acquire deciding content and declared relationships. Executive uses them for its selections; Workers inspect the affected implementation/proof; Reviewers acquire source and evidence independently. |
| Assemble/check caller-selected reference-frame context; preflight execution contracts | Render the method-owned activation from supplied selections and exact content; check the declared closure, envelope, bindings and Product-bound admission evidence without inventing authority. |
| Dispatch through a selected executor; retain observations and notifications | Supply exact context/settings and the existing grant, and expose acknowledgment, output, observed effects, partial evidence and exceptions to the declared consumer. |
| Capture/check closed returns; prepare review comparisons; execute declared checks and joins | Preserve actor outputs and their provenance; inspect exact candidate/source/proof, detect binding errors, and evaluate only supported supplied predicates or method-owned operators. |
| Project/record existing work and evidence; prepare affected refresh/handoff; retain usage | Read existing owned carriers and apply already-authorized records through named Writer interfaces; preserve actual support, unresolved impact/effects and measured attempt costs across sessions. |

These are tools available at the points where the selected method and F_P actor
need them, not an a_c stage sequence, task-state store or agent topology.
Public interfaces must support direct Worker and Reviewer source/context/proof
access as well as Executive use. Commands, MCP/protocols, storage, executor,
provider and concrete schemas remain tenant HOW. Existing work/evidence owners
remain authoritative; a tool view or recorded recommendation is not a decision.

In the target calculus, `F_D[v]` is deterministic evaluation/proof over declared
properties and returns a judgment. Source acquisition, context rendering,
serialization, dispatch and authorized recording are named domain operations
with their own contracts; the `F_D` label does not merge their identities or
confer effects. The deterministic wrapper may invoke an F_P actor, but its
semantic output remains F_P. Qualified deterministic evaluation of an already-
declared predicate or method-owned conjunction is supported only within its
explicit checked fragment; F_P supplies semantic selection and unresolved
judgment. Existing source-to-model F_P authoring remains a separate capability,
not one of these new deterministic evaluations.

## Method ownership and basis roles

The [source-owner map](requirements/fd-source-owner-map.md) binds provisional
STDO3.0 derivation reference commit
`494451522072ec34381c644f1ccfa2331f2b1e27`, package
`specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/common/`, tree
`082df4ea2b7b3658aab528bbfbcfe81234ccc810`, with exact member digests and deciding
clauses for each tool requirement. That common candidate is not accepted,
released or installed. It identifies the contracts from which the requested
toolset is derived; it is not an operative a_c constitution or a published v3
release identity.

This implementation's builder remains the exact installed STDO v2.5.1-rc.2
selected in `stdo_a_c.json`. A consumer workspace's exact selected operative
method/profile is a separate input, and represented subject versions are another
basis role. A supported binding or explicitly qualified translation must resolve
those inputs; label equality, file presence and co-location do not compose them.
No implicit latest adoption, V3 runtime dependency, sibling Product composition,
method acceptance or frozen-model regeneration follows from this source work.

## Delivery and qualification boundary

The [deterministic support requirements](requirements/fd-support-tools.md) and
[qualification scenarios](requirements/fd-support-verification.md) specify the
requested Product outcome. Their status is Deferred because owning design and
realization are pending, not because the outcome is withdrawn. Current codecs,
projections, source-generation scripts and worker launch facilities are building
blocks; this increment does not claim the new public toolset, general contract
binding/admission support or a maintained whole-workspace representation exists.
Current frozen dogfood models represent selected methodology corpora.

Qualification separates deterministic checked properties, actual acquisition
and executor effects, ordinary actor usability, independent semantic assessment
and owner disposition under the selected method. Benefit requires matched
accepted-result quality/cost evidence, including acquisition, F_P authoring,
refresh, invocation, retries, repair and review; graph use or fewer calls alone
establishes no improvement. Implementation, qualification, acceptance and
release remain downstream work.

## Independence

Graphify is a build tenant of this common WHAT. It is not a separately composed
Axiom Indexer Product. The Product Definition's composition is empty. This
project neither changes nor waits for v3, and has no membership in the existing
STDO release-matched cohort. Any later consumer adoption is separately selected.
Upstream software used by a tenant is part of that tenant's HOW.

## Product disposition authority

Jim, the Product owner, retains scope, meaning, acceptance and release decisions.
T-001 authorizes its bounded implementation/verification work. The current
[T-007 instruction](../.ai-workspace/tickets/active/T-007-executive-lifecycle-tooling.md#owner-instruction)
authorizes Product and requirement authoring for the additional F_D support
tools. Neither instruction asserts semantic acceptance of fixtures, complete
calculus conformance, release readiness or measured efficiency improvement.
Design/implementation requires a subsequent bounded work selection.
Construction and independent assessment do not accept their own subjects.

# Common Realization Requirements

The authoritative calculus is
`stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md`, SHA-256
`cbe2edb928d3e75e23446f6d525baea664966e8d5920e6fa389cbaa4af8f1f8d`.
These requirements select implementation obligations without redefining it.
Physical file layout and Graphify-specific record grammar belong to tenant HOW.

| ID | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| AC-R-001 | Bind the exact calculus, subject basis, signature, interpretation contract, semantic-selection ledger and content identity. Mutable locators alone do not establish identity. |
| AC-R-002 | Preserve all eight core populations as distinct families. Every local identity occurs exactly once. Empty populations are explicit and signature-permitted. Unknown fields, kinds and unsupported domains refuse within the declared checked fragment. |
| AC-R-003 | Preserve every record's content, context, owner, scope and basis. Typed references have explicit cardinality and target domains; local/external collisions, dangling references and wrong-family/sort targets refuse. |
| AC-R-004 | Retain the exact external-resolution coordinates separately from local populations. No inferred relationship, payload equality or same-spelled identifier supplies semantic identity or authority. |
| AC-R-005 | Preserve directed relation identity, distinct parallel relations, self-relations, qualifications, ordered content and repeated occurrences through representation and recovery. No carrier optimization silently merges or discards them. |
| AC-R-006 | A representation has an exact versioned profile and deterministic content identity. Recovering it preserves the complete declared model; malformed, stale, incomplete or contradictory representations refuse. |
| AC-R-007 | Distinguish a proposed-model view from the accepted-interpretation encoding relation. The latter requires an external accepted judgment with exact model identity/digest and declared decision contract, authority, evidence and provenance. A consistency check does not prove the judgment's legitimacy or semantic correctness. |
| AC-R-008 | Acquisition binds exact seeds and authored/signature-declared governing dependency roles. Compute complete finite closure, preserving constraints, governing conditions, latitude and residuals required by those exact roles. Cycles terminate. A budget cannot silently truncate required content. |
| AC-R-009 | A projection identifies the exact parent, selection, included/excluded records and external/unresolved boundaries. Discovery and provenance links remain inspectable without automatically becoming governing dependencies. A projection is not a complete replacement model or an acceptance decision. |
| AC-R-010 | Search and path results report their structural scope. Connectivity, ranking and extraction confidence do not establish implication, semantic truth, safe execution or authority. |
| AC-R-011 | Mechanical validation returns only the properties actually checked. F_P interpretation, F_D assessment, F_H adjudication and domain operations retain distinct identities and claims. Do not report full calculus admission from shape, digests, round trips or path traversal. |
| AC-R-012 | Declare unsupported operations and return an explicit refusal when requested. In particular, retaining transformation records does not establish AC-013 transformation execution or preservation proofs. |
| AC-R-013 | The realization is usable independently of v3, Axiom Indexer and STDO Representation. Its concrete stack, upstream identity, commands and qualification evidence are tenant-owned. |
| AC-R-014 | Qualify preservation with adversarial cases and an actual boundary trial. Measure discovery, context sufficiency, correction and total accepted-result cost before claiming efficiency improvement. |
| AC-R-015 | A tenant offering source-to-model creation declares its F_P authoring contract, exact input corpus and source coverage, preserves qualifications and residuals, and retains generation provenance. Discovery confidence, inferred graph links, shape checks and source processing do not by themselves establish normative relationships, semantic fidelity, completeness or acceptance. Existing authored models are not required inputs to that creation path. |

Interpretation fidelity, representation preservation, actual use, semantic
acceptance and release are separate deciding questions. Their evidence and
residuals remain explicit even when a mechanical check succeeds.

# Deterministic Support Tools for F_P Actors

**Family**: REQ-AC-FD-*
**Status**: Deferred
**Category**: Capability

This family specifies additional tools supporting F_P Executives, Workers and
Reviewers. Deferred means owning design and realization are pending; the Product
outcome is retained. STDO3.0 owns the methodology and its contracts. The
[source-owner map](fd-source-owner-map.md) binds the exact provisional derivation
reference and the owner clauses cited below. Runtime use consumes the caller's
exact selected method/profile through a declared supported binding, without
adopting that provisional candidate or changing a_c's installed builder basis.

Every operation has an exact versioned input/output contract and reproducible
checks over its supplied inputs. External observations retain their identity,
scope and time. A named source/carrier/dispatch/write operation is distinct from
an `F_D[v]` evaluation/proof returning a judgment; neither makes the invoked
F_P operation or its semantic answer deterministic. Existing AC-R-001..015 and
the separate F_P source-to-model authoring capability remain applicable.

### REQ-AC-FD-001 — Discover supported tool contracts

**Input:** an optional requested operation, exact method/profile and capability
query. **Output/checks:** a versioned inventory of public operations, input/output
contracts, compatible method/profile bindings, supported representations,
checked fragments, effect/access prerequisites, qualification scope and explicit
unsupported cases. Unknown or unsupported requests return their exact reason
and unmet contract. **Limit:** availability selects no method, frame, role,
workflow or next action; the interface must be usable by all three F_P actors
without private study knowledge. Protocol, CLI/MCP, schema and provider are HOW.
Owners: [PDEF](fd-source-owner-map.md#pdef) §8/11;
[RF](fd-source-owner-map.md#rf) RF-016;
[ASSURE](fd-source-owner-map.md#assure) §13.

### REQ-AC-FD-002 — Bind and observe exact workspace inputs

**Input:** caller-selected Product scope/definition, exact operative method and
optional profile, declared material observation scope and access grant.
**Output/checks:** resolved identities/content digests and observation evidence
for the selected definition, method, subject, configuration/dependencies and
current relevant workspace bytes, including dirty/untracked content. Distinguish
the tool's builder basis, consumer operating basis and represented subject cuts;
report ambiguous, inaccessible, changed or unsupported bindings without
substitution. Reobservation compares the supplied material preconditions before
a dependent tool effect. **Limit:** branch/HEAD alone is not mutable state;
observation establishes only the acquired scope/time and neither adopts latest
nor composes sibling Products/bases. Owners:
[PDEF](fd-source-owner-map.md#pdef) §4/12;
[RF](fd-source-owner-map.md#rf) RF-005;
[ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §5/7.

### REQ-AC-FD-003 — Resolve records, source and grounding

**Input:** exact model/record/source identities, selected mappings or search
scope and permitted acquisition routes. **Output/checks:** found record payloads,
actual source content and their exact routes/digests, original grounding,
owner/mapping coordinates, coverage dispositions and unresolved boundaries.
Literal/structural searches identify their scope; missing, ambiguous, stale,
wrong-basis or ungrounded references return the relevant gap. Workers and
Reviewers can acquire raw deciding source directly rather than relying on an
Executive/author summary. **Limit:** a locator or manifest is distinct from
acquired content. Search, code edges and extraction confidence cannot author
semantic/governing mappings or establish fidelity. Owners:
[ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §2 Acquisition/Standalone scope;
[PDEF](fd-source-owner-map.md#pdef) §11;
[EVAL](fd-source-owner-map.md#eval) §1–3.

### REQ-AC-FD-004 — Query declared dependencies, impact and coverage

**Input:** exact selected model(s), caller-selected seeds, authored typed
dependency/impact/coverage relations, conditional predicates or already-recorded
applicability, and explicit cross-model identity/translation rules where used.
**Output/checks:** reproducible closure/path/impact/coverage results, included
and missing declared obligations/dependencies, predicate results only for the
supported supplied decidable contract, and qualifications/residuals/boundaries.
Show computed facts separately from supplied F_P judgments and owner rulings.
**Limit:** F_P selects material relations and interprets unresolved applicability;
the tool does not infer semantic edges, prescribe re-entry or select a frontier.
An absent path in incomplete coverage cannot establish non-influence. Owners:
[FOUND](fd-source-owner-map.md#found) Change impact and evidence reuse;
[RF](fd-source-owner-map.md#rf) §6/8/10;
[ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §1 Applicability;
[SPEC](fd-source-owner-map.md#spec) §4.

### REQ-AC-FD-005 — Assemble and check selected actor context

**Input:** caller-selected frame/configuration and exact method packet contract,
subject/basis, seeds and governing dependency semantics, allowed acquisition
routes, supplied role/authority and actor envelope. **Output/checks:** an exact
projection of the supplied binding with actual acquired record/source content,
source references, declared closure and boundaries; a manifest of what was
supplied versus still to be acquired; and scoped completeness/identity/fit
checks under the selected contract. Where context capacity is declared, measure
its stated boundary/unit before read, retaining any unmeasured/unknown host
context. Preserve the selected method's qualifications, result relation and
stop/refusal semantics. **Limit:** do not invent packet fields as a second method,
silently truncate required content or claim semantic sufficiency from closure,
size or schema. Exact late acquisition is visible and follows the supplied
method contract. Owners: [RF](fd-source-owner-map.md#rf) §11, RF-013/014;
[ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §2;
[EXEC](fd-source-owner-map.md#exec) §19 only when that profile is selected.

### REQ-AC-FD-006 — Preflight a Product-bound execution contract

**Input:** caller-supplied work contract, governing outcome/grant, exact admission
binding/checks and any existing admission or permitted override evidence,
operation/tools/territory/envelope and named durable result/evidence surface.
**Output/checks:** deterministic preflight findings over those inputs and
admission evidence obtained from the selected Product-bound mechanism where
invoked, bound to exact contract identity and decision authority. Report missing
or mismatched required support before dispatch; retain draft and admitted
coordinates separately under the method's own contract. **Limit:** a successful
shape/context check, role name, ticket state or tool invocation cannot mint
admission or work authority. The tool neither drafts a new grant nor admits the
upstream outcome. Owners: [ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §1 Admission;
[TICK](fd-source-owner-map.md#tick) §5.

### REQ-AC-FD-007 — Dispatch, notify and observe under a supplied grant

**Input:** exact preflighted activation/admission, selected executor operation,
existing grant, permitted tools/territory, material preconditions, effective
context/settings and selected attempt/resource/observation conditions.
**Output/checks:** invocation identity, actual supplied payload/settings,
acknowledgments, output/partial-output and effect/termination observations with
scope/time, retained attempts and decision-relevant return/exception/basis-change
notifications. Check material bindings before the named effect and expose
changed preconditions without silent rebase. **Limit:** the deterministic
wrapper does not make F_P output deterministic or semantic evidence of success.
Requests, delivery, evaluation, intended effects and their observed end remain
separate under the selected method; timeout/cancel/interruption preserve its
unknown-effect semantics. Fallback observation is bounded by supplied conditions,
not a mandatory polling controller. Owners: [ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act)
§1/3 Effects/5; [EXEC](fd-source-owner-map.md#exec) §6 if selected.

### REQ-AC-FD-008 — Capture and check a closed return

**Input:** returned payload/transport evidence, original activation and return
contract, expected consumer, exact subject/basis and supplied currentness,
dependency and independence predicates/evidence. **Output/checks:** preserved raw
return and provenance, deterministic binding/format/currentness findings and
the exact declared evaluations, predicates, domain outcomes and residuals that
were actually returned. Identify stale/wrong-subject/wrong-basis, missing,
duplicate and conflicting evidence without dropping it; expose non-consumable
support/gaps to the declared consumer. **Limit:** do not relabel a historical
verdict as a new verdict, manufacture a result for an unperformed evaluation or
treat schema validity as semantic assessment/acceptance. A transport failure is
reported separately using the selected method contract. Owners:
[FOUND](fd-source-owner-map.md#found) Results/Conjunction of results;
[RF](fd-source-owner-map.md#rf) RF-012;
[ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §3/7;
[EVAL](fd-source-owner-map.md#eval) §4.

### REQ-AC-FD-009 — Prepare independently acquirable review evidence

**Input:** exact review claim/candidate and composition boundary, caller-selected
source, comparison subjects, proof/evidence population and method-owned
independence/exposure contract. **Output/checks:** independently resolvable raw
authority/candidate/proof acquisition routes, acquired content where requested,
exact byte/record comparisons, and separate assertion/expected-result versus
execution provenance. Support expectation recording before candidate exposure
and preserve the actual acquisition/exposure record under the supplied contract.
Workers can acquire their implementation/proof context; Reviewers can inspect
the actual candidate, tests/fixtures and source without author-only privileges.
**Limit:** diffs and trace/binding checks are not semantic findings, an independent
verdict or adoption of a review recommendation as disposition. Owners:
[EVAL](fd-source-owner-map.md#eval) §1–4/6;
[ASSURE](fd-source-owner-map.md#assure) §3/10/13–16;
[EXEC](fd-source-owner-map.md#exec) §9/10/17/19 if selected.

### REQ-AC-FD-010 — Execute declared checks and method-owned joins

**Input:** exact subject/observations, selected executable or reproducible
decidable predicate/proof contract and its provenance/domain/limits, or a
selected method-owned conjunction/translation with required coverage and inputs.
**Output/checks:** reproducible `F_D[v]` judgments for the properties actually
evaluated, counterexamples/gaps, and joins computed only under the supplied
qualified operator. Preserve source predicate, original domain outcomes,
not-performed assessments, uncovered obligations and incompatibilities as the
owner contract requires. Retain assertion/observation and execution identities.
**Limit:** do not invent an algebra or stronger claim, turn a necessary-condition
pass into full satisfaction, execute an unsupported arbitrary calculus operation
or replace F_P/owner judgment. Owners: [AC](fd-source-owner-map.md#ac) §5;
[FOUND](fd-source-owner-map.md#found) Results/Conjunction of results/Assertions
and observation; [EVAL](fd-source-owner-map.md#eval) §1/2;
[ASSURE](fd-source-owner-map.md#assure) §10.

### REQ-AC-FD-011 — Project and record existing work/evidence facts

**Input:** selected authoritative work/evidence carriers, caller-selected view,
or an already-authorized actor/owner record and exact named Writer interface,
grant, target preimage and update conditions. **Output/checks:** source-linked
projections of existing work, progress/support, residuals and next-action
scope/support/owner; for an authorized write, the exact applied record and
observed effect/result identity or refusal. Preserve original owner wording
separately from interpretation and method-owned distinctions among verdict,
recommendation, disposition, checkpoint, closure and release. **Limit:** create
no rival task ledger, owner decision, role transition or continuation grant;
the tool records a supplied decision, never mechanically adopts a review
recommendation or mutates as an F_P Executive/Reviewer. Owners:
[PDEF](fd-source-owner-map.md#pdef) §8;
[TICK](fd-source-owner-map.md#tick) §7;
[ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §5;
[EVAL](fd-source-owner-map.md#eval) §4;
[EXEC](fd-source-owner-map.md#exec) §6 if selected.

### REQ-AC-FD-012 — Compute affected refresh and prepare reusable handoff

**Input:** old/current source observations, exact dependency/impact declarations,
declared invalidators, existing results/rulings and caller-selected recovery or
reuse contract. **Output/checks:** source/derived differences, affected projection
and evidence candidates, missing dependency coverage, method-prescribed
invalidation/applicability check results where decidable, and a reconstructable
handoff of still-applicable support, original records/successors, residuals and
unreconciled effects. Reacquire named current inputs for the next dependent
action; retain partial writes rather than assuming a reset. **Limit:** do not
erase history/frozen studies, rewrite old judgments onto new subjects, infer
unaffectedness from absent edges, or require replay/rebuild of valid unchanged
support merely because a session/role changed. F_P resolves unsupported semantic
impact or preservation premises. Owners: [FOUND](fd-source-owner-map.md#found)
Change impact and evidence reuse; [RF](fd-source-owner-map.md#rf) §10;
[ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §5/7;
[TICK](fd-source-owner-map.md#tick) §7.

### REQ-AC-FD-013 — Retain attempt, usage and uncertainty evidence

**Input:** invocation/acquisition/check/refresh/repair/review attempt observations
and selected accounting/resource contract. **Output/checks:** bound attempt and
cost records with units, measured scope, elapsed versus summed actor intervals,
available usage/cache counters, partial/failed calls, unknown counters and any
declared limit-check result. Aggregation is reproducible without double counting;
anticipated costs remain separate from observations. **Limit:** unavailable
backend usage stays unknown, selected limits are not universal quotas, and
fewer calls or faster deterministic checks do not prove lower accepted-result
cost or improved F_P quality. Owners: [ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §6;
[EVAL](fd-source-owner-map.md#eval) §1;
[SPEC](fd-source-owner-map.md#spec) §8.


WHAT/GOVERNING PREIMAGE SOURCE c2f67fec8154028d45d7cd7a2832dd4fade4d94b:a_c/specification/requirements/fd-support-verification.md sha256=3746e614a5ddc3f0a551e926998f16d6101cc037c5c43b879b4447b017a8dbdf
# Deterministic Support Tool Qualification

**Family**: REQ-AC-FDV-*
**Status**: Deferred
**Category**: Verification

This family qualifies the [additional tools](fd-support-tools.md), not the
STDO3.0 methodology or F_P actor judgments. Design, implementation and executed
qualification remain pending. Owners are the exact provisional clauses in the
[source-owner map](fd-source-owner-map.md), consumed through the caller-selected
operative method rather than adopted as a new a_c builder basis.

### REQ-AC-FDV-001 — Qualify observable tool contracts on a real use path

For each claimed operation, bind exact inputs, deterministic output/check
predicate, scope, expected counterexample and method-owner contract. Verify
reproducibility over frozen inputs and preserve the scope/time of external
observations. Exercise the documented ordinary interfaces with F_P Executive,
Worker and Reviewer callers on one real bounded development task, including
actual context/source acquisition, executor boundary, proof/review evidence
and durable return/recording routes selected for that task. Distinguish
contract sufficiency, actual boundary exchanges, runnable path and actor
usability; do not substitute private study success or fixture knowledge. F_P
assessment, required independence and owner disposition are provided by their
existing owners, not by the tools. Each unexercised operation/variant remains
an explicit qualification gap. Owners: [EVAL](fd-source-owner-map.md#eval)
§1/3/6; [ASSURE](fd-source-owner-map.md#assure) §3/13–16.

### REQ-AC-FDV-002 — Qualify refusal, unknown and recovery discriminators

Execute positive and relevant negative/control cases for the inventory below,
with exact tool/method/profile/candidate identities, assertion and execution
provenance, actual supplied context/settings, raw attempts, expected observable
checks/refusals and retained unknowns. Different source conditions must yield
the owner-contract distinctions; an always-refuse or always-pass implementation
cannot qualify them. Demonstrate handoff/resumption from named durable sources
without hidden actor context. These scenarios test the tool response to supplied
rules and observations, not an a_c-owned workflow or semantic truth oracle.
An independent tenant can apply the same carrier-neutral contract without
Graphify, a V3 runtime dependency or study-private machinery. Owners:
[ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §1 Applicability/2/3/5/7;
[FOUND](fd-source-owner-map.md#found) Results/Conjunction of results;
[ASSURE](fd-source-owner-map.md#assure) §3/13.

### REQ-AC-FDV-003 — Evaluate accepted-result benefit separately

Before claiming improved discovery, quality, consistency or efficiency, compare
matched real tasks with/without the declared tool support under exact
source/method, actor/envelope/settings and outcome/acceptance criteria. Retain
semantic/coverage/acceptance evidence and all material acquisition, F_P authoring,
context preparation, refresh, invocation, failed attempts/retries, repair,
review and decision effort, with measurement boundaries and unknowns. Report
observed differences and limitations rather than inferring a general benefit
from count, graph size, fit or structural success. Owners:
[ACT](fd-source-owner-map.md#act) §6;
[EVAL](fd-source-owner-map.md#eval) §1;
[FOUND](fd-source-owner-map.md#found) Assertions and observation/Change impact
and evidence reuse.

## Scenario and requirement trace

The following is written test-case authority, not executed evidence. FD-nnn
expands to `REQ-AC-FD-nnn`; FDV-nnn expands to `REQ-AC-FDV-nnn`. Each case supplies
the exact applicable upstream contract; the table does not redefine its states,
role duties, result values, applicability or admission policy.

| Scenario | Supplied input/variation and required observable tool response | Trace |
|---|---|---|
| SC-AC-FD-001 Real actor use | One actual bounded task uses ordinary documented operations for Executive preparation/dispatch, Worker source/proof acquisition and Reviewer independent candidate/source/proof access, then captures supplied actor/owner results through the selected carrier. All effective inputs and effect evidence are traceable; no tool-generated semantic/owner verdict appears. | FD-001..013; FDV-001 |
| SC-AC-FD-002 Contract discovery/bases | Exact supported request returns its contract/checked fragment. Unknown operation, unsupported method/profile and ambiguous Product selection refuse with reasons. Tool builder, consumer method and represented v3 subject stay distinct; equal model labels do not create a join. | FD-001,002,004; FDV-002 |
| SC-AC-FD-003 Dirty current state | Relevant dirty/untracked bytes or dependency/configuration change after observation without changing HEAD. A dependent preflight detects the changed supplied precondition; a branch/commit match cannot hide it or silently rebase the request. | FD-002,006,007; FDV-002 |
| SC-AC-FD-004 Grounding and incomplete coverage | Give exact source/record references plus a missing mapping, inferred code edge and methodology-only model. Return actual payload/content or a named gap and coverage boundaries. No inferred governing relation, complete-workspace claim or unaffectedness conclusion follows. | FD-003,004; FDV-002 |
| SC-AC-FD-005 Supplied conditional predicates | Evaluate a declared supported applicability predicate on true, false and missing-premise inputs, plus missing/wrong-subject prerequisite evidence. Preserve the method's exact distinction and F_P judgments separately; no semantic frontier/re-entry choice is made by the query. | FD-004,008,010; FDV-002 |
| SC-AC-FD-006 Context and envelope | Supply locator-only versus acquired records/source, governing closure with qualifications/residuals, exact permitted late reads, denied acquisition, exceeded capacity and unknown host context. Assemble/check the selected packet, measure only the declared boundary and preserve gaps/owner refusals without silent trimming or sufficiency claims. | FD-003,005; FDV-002 |
| SC-AC-FD-007 Admission and grants | Candidate packet/ticket/role without the selected admission evidence or granted effect refuses dispatch. Exact Product-bound mechanism/allowed override and supplied grant permit only the named tools/territory. Unauthorized recording/Executive or Reviewer mutation refuses under the selected role contract. | FD-006,007,011; FDV-002 |
| SC-AC-FD-008 Transport and uncertain effect | Distinguish receipt, schema-valid output, F_P return, observed effect and observed end. Lost response/timeout/cancel/interruption with partial write preserves upstream unknown-effect evidence and material retry preconditions. A termination request never proves completion/rollback. | FD-007,008,012,013; FDV-002 |
| SC-AC-FD-009 Closed return binding | Capture exact valid, stale, wrong-subject/basis, duplicate and conflicting returns. Preserve raw original predicates/domain outcomes; report consumer-binding errors and gaps without rewriting old verdicts, counting duplicate independence or fabricating unperformed results. | FD-008,010; FDV-002 |
| SC-AC-FD-010 Independent review acquisition | Under supplied exposure/independence conditions, record source-derived expectations before candidate exposure and permit a nonauthor Reviewer to acquire exact candidate, tests/fixtures, governing source and comparisons directly. Author summary/new session is not certified independent. The tool returns acquisition/diff facts, never review severity or disposition. | FD-003,005,009; FDV-001,002 |
| SC-AC-FD-011 Declared checks/conjunction | Execute a qualified supplied structural/proof predicate and method-owned operator. Preserve wrong-basis inputs, missing planned assessments, uncovered obligations, original domain outcomes and conflicts exactly.
