COMPARISON PREIMAGE c2f67fec8154028d45d7cd7a2832dd4fade4d94b:a_c/build_tenants/graphify/design/README.md sha256=50972dd5793d9bb17e4db2ff2d8f7989c3af3e7ebdbb56250fbfb05dedf654c2; exact committed comparison only, not complete pre-effect workspace or accepted qualification baseline
# Graphify realization design

Status: construction design for the independent `a_c` Product, not semantic
acceptance, carrier admission or release. This design precedes its implementation.

## Declared fragment

The versioned `a_c.graphify.model/1` family represents all eight exact core
record shapes in the selected STDO calculus. A model has one exact calculus and
subject basis, one context/owner/scope, an explicit signature, interpretation
contract and selection ledger, a closed identity universe and exact external
resolution tuples. Composite bases and signature migrations are unsupported.

The signature owns closed sort/kind populations and schemas for every field.
The small schema language supports null, Boolean, integer, string, enum, closed
object, array and typed identity reference. Floating-point numbers, unknown
fields/types, implicit optional fields and arbitrary executable predicates are
unsupported. Identity references declare their local family/sort domains,
external target kinds, reference-domain identity and required basis relation.
Scalar/array schema structure supplies explicit reference cardinality. Every
reference schema also declares a Boolean governing role; provenance, evidence
and source re-entry references are not automatically acquisition dependencies.
Sort/kind specializations declare the value, endpoint, predicate and uncertainty
domains used by their records. This is a finite structural fragment, not a
generic proof that a signature or interpretation satisfies the whole calculus.

Signature specialization cannot retarget fixed core record links. In this
profile a transformation's traversal resolves locally to `traversals`, a
constraint's latitude reference resolves locally to `latitude`, and a
transformation's residual references resolve locally to `residuals`. Complete
model identities and external-resolution delta/witness coordinates are external
coordinates, rather than local fundamental records. These are structural
domain restrictions; no transformation application or delta proof is implied.

All eight population keys are mandatory. Required populations are signature-
declared. Record identity uniqueness is global. Every declared reference is
resolved once, with explicit local/external separation; record basis and scoped
coordinates must match the model. Exact external resolution coordinates remain
distinct from the local record populations. A reference coordinate is checked
for consistency; its external evidence is not independently authenticated.
Every external tuple, including an unused one, must match a reference-domain,
external-target-kind and basis-relation contract declared by at least one
signature schema. Collection includes nested and kind-specialized schemas.
Unused external identities remain lawful when that complete contract is declared.

The canonical grammar is UTF-8 JSON with sorted object keys, no whitespace,
Unicode unescaped, integer numbers only, and array order preserved. It is a
tenant-specific byte grammar, **not** RFC 8785/JCS. SHA-256 binds these bytes.
The model's supplied identity and calculated digest are distinct coordinates.

## Graph encoding

`materialize` creates a clearly marked unaccepted proposal view. `encode`
requires a separately supplied accepted semantic judgment naming the unchanged
model identity and digest, exact decision contract, authority, evidence and
provenance. It only checks those supplied coordinates; it does not establish
issuer authority, semantic correctness or carrier admission.

The graph uses Graphify-compatible node-link JSON and reifies each semantic
record as a node. Each identity-reference occurrence has its own node with
record identity and exact JSON field path, and separate owner/target edges.
Each occurrence has a separate endpoint-role node so an owner that is also its
own target cannot collapse two edges in the undirected simple graph.
Occurrences preserve direction, ordering, parallel relations, self-relations
and repeated arguments even through Graphify's undirected simple graph.
External targets have distinct nodes. The metadata node is deliberately
isolated rather than creating a global membership hub. `file_type=document` avoids upstream's
isolated-code-node pruning. Extraction confidence describes representation
provenance, not semantic validity.

A metadata node carries envelope coordinates, signature and external map,
without an embedded full model/population snapshot. Record nodes carry exact
record payloads. Decode reconstructs the model and independently regenerates
the expected semantic nodes, occurrence nodes and edges. Missing, added,
contradictory, tampered or collapsed graph content refuses. Incidental upstream
node/edge attributes may be added; all tenant-owned attributes must survive.
The graph supports `links` node-link input and Graphify extraction `edges`.
When present, the container's `directed` and `multigraph` declarations must be
exact Boolean false, and `graph.ac_profile` must identify this exact profile.
Flagless extraction input and incidental upstream graph annotations remain
supported; a contradictory container declaration is not an annotation.
Per-family record ordinals conserve population-array order independently of
graph iteration order. Unique record labels and deterministic authored-field
excerpts in Graphify's native `attributes` support native discovery. The decoder
checks these derived display fields as well as the full payload. Excerpts are
bounded display aids, not substitute semantic content.

The graph's canonical semantic identity excludes external judgment evidence.
`encode` places supplied evidence under the distinct `ac_evidence` envelope;
matching judgments never change the unchanged semantic subject. Upstream
build/export may omit this envelope, so retain the original judgment separately.
Finite numeric upstream annotations (such as confidence_score=1.0) are accepted
only outside tenant-owned semantic fields. Raw export bytes and their digest
are distinct from the normalized semantic representation identity.

Upstream target: Graphify-Labs/graphify commit
`fe085cedddde3a18554f8749b230bfe47f3dcce7`. Actual upstream compatibility is
separately tested against that exact revision. The CLI itself uses Python 3
stdlib and imports neither Axiom Indexer nor v3.

## Inspection and acquisition

`find` is literal text discovery over exact record payloads; `inspect` returns
one exact record and its typed references. Neither result proves implication.
`project` computes finite least closure over declared governing relation kinds,
retaining those relation records and endpoint records, recursively retaining
attached constraints, latitude and residuals and their signature-declared
governing local references. Non-governing typed references remain boundary
coordinates, including re-entry and provenance routes.
Explicit non-governing provenance/discovery relations do not force their other
endpoint into the view. A projection names parent identity/digest, exact seeds
and dependency declaration, all included/excluded identities, external and
unresolved boundaries, and crossing relations. It is a view rather than a
replacement complete model. Insufficient record budgets refuse without partial
success. No token or semantic-cost minimum is claimed.

The Python `project_many(model, selections)` API accepts an ordered sequence of
`(seeds, budget_records)` pairs and returns projections in that order. It checks
model freshness once and builds governing-reference and attachment indexes once
for the operation. Every selection has the same closure, boundary and budget
semantics as `project`; a refusal aborts the batch without a partial return. An
empty batch still checks freshness and returns an empty list. Indexes are local
to the operation, so later calls revalidate mutable model input rather than reuse
stale cached authority. Population ordinals are indexed in one pass during
materialization. These mechanics preserve existing model/carrier/profile bytes
and acquisition results; they do not establish semantic or cost qualification.

`transform`, `overlay`, `execute` and `evaluate-predicate` explicitly refuse.
Retained traversal/transformation/judgment records remain inert authored data;
their presence is not proof of execution, preservation or decision authority.

## Qualification

Adversarial tests cover cross-family duplicates, unknown grammar, stale basis,
wrong sort/family, ambiguous external identities, dangling references, graph
tampering, repeated and reversed relations, governing/residual closure, cycles
and insufficient budgets. A separate actual-upstream build/read/decode trial
qualifies the representation boundary. Semantic fidelity, complete calculus
conformance, issuer authority, efficiency and Product acceptance remain open.

00001: # Graphify realization design
00002: 
00003: Status: construction design for the independent `a_c` Product, not semantic
00004: acceptance, carrier admission or release. This design precedes its implementation.
00005: 
00006: ## Declared fragment
00007: 
00008: The versioned `a_c.graphify.model/1` family represents all eight exact core
00009: record shapes in the selected STDO calculus. A model has one exact calculus and
00010: subject basis, one context/owner/scope, an explicit signature, interpretation
00011: contract and selection ledger, a closed identity universe and exact external
00012: resolution tuples. Composite bases and signature migrations are unsupported.
00013: 
00014: The signature owns closed sort/kind populations and schemas for every field.
00015: The small schema language supports null, Boolean, integer, string, enum, closed
00016: object, array and typed identity reference. Floating-point numbers, unknown
00017: fields/types, implicit optional fields and arbitrary executable predicates are
00018: unsupported. Identity references declare their local family/sort domains,
00019: external target kinds, reference-domain identity and required basis relation.
00020: Scalar/array schema structure supplies explicit reference cardinality. Every
00021: reference schema also declares a Boolean governing role; provenance, evidence
00022: and source re-entry references are not automatically acquisition dependencies.
00023: Sort/kind specializations declare the value, endpoint, predicate and uncertainty
00024: domains used by their records. This is a finite structural fragment, not a
00025: generic proof that a signature or interpretation satisfies the whole calculus.
00026: 
00027: Signature specialization cannot retarget fixed core record links. In this
00028: profile a transformation's traversal resolves locally to `traversals`, a
00029: constraint's latitude reference resolves locally to `latitude`, and a
00030: transformation's residual references resolve locally to `residuals`. Complete
00031: model identities and external-resolution delta/witness coordinates are external
00032: coordinates, rather than local fundamental records. These are structural
00033: domain restrictions; no transformation application or delta proof is implied.
00034: 
00035: All eight population keys are mandatory. Required populations are signature-
00036: declared. Record identity uniqueness is global. Every declared reference is
00037: resolved once, with explicit local/external separation; record basis and scoped
00038: coordinates must match the model. Exact external resolution coordinates remain
00039: distinct from the local record populations. A reference coordinate is checked
00040: for consistency; its external evidence is not independently authenticated.
00041: Every external tuple, including an unused one, must match a reference-domain,
00042: external-target-kind and basis-relation contract declared by at least one
00043: signature schema. Collection includes nested and kind-specialized schemas.
00044: Unused external identities remain lawful when that complete contract is declared.
00045: 
00046: The canonical grammar is UTF-8 JSON with sorted object keys, no whitespace,
00047: Unicode unescaped, integer numbers only, and array order preserved. It is a
00048: tenant-specific byte grammar, **not** RFC 8785/JCS. SHA-256 binds these bytes.
00049: The model's supplied identity and calculated digest are distinct coordinates.
00050: 
00051: ## Graph encoding
00052: 
00053: `materialize` creates a clearly marked unaccepted proposal view. `encode`
00054: requires a separately supplied accepted semantic judgment naming the unchanged
00055: model identity and digest, exact decision contract, authority, evidence and
00056: provenance. It only checks those supplied coordinates; it does not establish
00057: issuer authority, semantic correctness or carrier admission.
00058: 
00059: The graph uses Graphify-compatible node-link JSON and reifies each semantic
00060: record as a node. Each identity-reference occurrence has its own node with
00061: record identity and exact JSON field path, and separate owner/target edges.
00062: Each occurrence has a separate endpoint-role node so an owner that is also its
00063: own target cannot collapse two edges in the undirected simple graph.
00064: Occurrences preserve direction, ordering, parallel relations, self-relations
00065: and repeated arguments even through Graphify's undirected simple graph.
00066: External targets have distinct nodes. The metadata node is deliberately
00067: isolated rather than creating a global membership hub. `file_type=document` avoids upstream's
00068: isolated-code-node pruning. Extraction confidence describes representation
00069: provenance, not semantic validity.
00070: 
00071: A metadata node carries envelope coordinates, signature and external map,
00072: without an embedded full model/population snapshot. Record nodes carry exact
00073: record payloads. Decode reconstructs the model and independently regenerates
00074: the expected semantic nodes, occurrence nodes and edges. Missing, added,
00075: contradictory, tampered or collapsed graph content refuses. Incidental upstream
00076: node/edge attributes may be added; all tenant-owned attributes must survive.
00077: The graph supports `links` node-link input and Graphify extraction `edges`.
00078: When present, the container's `directed` and `multigraph` declarations must be
00079: exact Boolean false, and `graph.ac_profile` must identify this exact profile.
00080: Flagless extraction input and incidental upstream graph annotations remain
00081: supported; a contradictory container declaration is not an annotation.
00082: Per-family record ordinals conserve population-array order independently of
00083: graph iteration order. Unique record labels and deterministic authored-field
00084: excerpts in Graphify's native `attributes` support native discovery. The decoder
00085: checks these derived display fields as well as the full payload. Excerpts are
00086: bounded display aids, not substitute semantic content.
00087: 
00088: The graph's canonical semantic identity excludes external judgment evidence.
00089: `encode` places supplied evidence under the distinct `ac_evidence` envelope;
00090: matching judgments never change the unchanged semantic subject. Upstream
00091: build/export may omit this envelope, so retain the original judgment separately.
00092: Finite numeric upstream annotations (such as confidence_score=1.0) are accepted
00093: only outside tenant-owned semantic fields. Raw export bytes and their digest
00094: are distinct from the normalized semantic representation identity.
00095: 
00096: Upstream target: Graphify-Labs/graphify commit
00097: `fe085cedddde3a18554f8749b230bfe47f3dcce7`. Actual upstream compatibility is
00098: separately tested against that exact revision. The CLI itself uses Python 3
00099: stdlib and imports neither Axiom Indexer nor v3.
00100: 
00101: ## Inspection and acquisition
00102: 
00103: `find` is literal text discovery over exact record payloads; `inspect` returns
00104: one exact record and its typed references. Neither result proves implication.
00105: `project` computes finite least closure over declared governing relation kinds,
00106: retaining those relation records and endpoint records, recursively retaining
00107: attached constraints, latitude and residuals and their signature-declared
00108: governing local references. Non-governing typed references remain boundary
00109: coordinates, including re-entry and provenance routes.
00110: Explicit non-governing provenance/discovery relations do not force their other
00111: endpoint into the view. A projection names parent identity/digest, exact seeds
00112: and dependency declaration, all included/excluded identities, external and
00113: unresolved boundaries, and crossing relations. It is a view rather than a
00114: replacement complete model. Insufficient record budgets refuse without partial
00115: success. No token or semantic-cost minimum is claimed.
00116: 
00117: The Python `project_many(model, selections)` API accepts an ordered sequence of
00118: `(seeds, budget_records)` pairs and returns projections in that order. It checks
00119: model freshness once and builds governing-reference and attachment indexes once
00120: for the operation. Every selection has the same closure, boundary and budget
00121: semantics as `project`; a refusal aborts the batch without a partial return. An
00122: empty batch still checks freshness and returns an empty list. Indexes are local
00123: to the operation, so later calls revalidate mutable model input rather than reuse
00124: stale cached authority. Population ordinals are indexed in one pass during
00125: materialization. These mechanics preserve existing model/carrier/profile bytes
00126: and acquisition results; they do not establish semantic or cost qualification.
00127: 
00128: `transform`, `overlay`, `execute` and `evaluate-predicate` explicitly refuse.
00129: Retained traversal/transformation/judgment records remain inert authored data;
00130: their presence is not proof of execution, preservation or decision authority.
00131: 
00132: ## Qualification
00133: 
00134: Adversarial tests cover cross-family duplicates, unknown grammar, stale basis,
00135: wrong sort/family, ambiguous external identities, dangling references, graph
00136: tampering, repeated and reversed relations, governing/residual closure, cycles
00137: and insufficient budgets. A separate actual-upstream build/read/decode trial
00138: qualifies the representation boundary. Semantic fidelity, complete calculus
00139: conformance, issuer authority, efficiency and Product acceptance remain open.
00140: 
00141: ## F_D support increment
00142: 
00143: The [T-008 support design](fd-support.md) extends this existing tenant with
00144: ordinary deterministic tools for F_P Executives, Workers and Reviewers. The
00145: [exact Claude RC9 support binding](fd-method-claude-rc9.json) names method owners
00146: for the owner's work-scoped execution selection. The method remains external
00147: source authority; no replacement lifecycle, installed V3 basis, sibling runtime
00148: composition or change to the codec/source-authoring fragment is introduced.
00149: This additional design is a candidate; public implementation, operational
00150: qualification, accepted-result benefit and Product acceptance remain pending.

00001: # Deterministic support for F_P development actors
00002: 
00003: Status: **design candidate v3 for T-008** (A–G seams and selected F1–F5 repairs). This is tenant HOW for
00004: [REQ-AC-FD-001..013](../../../specification/requirements/fd-support-tools.md)
00005: and the [qualification obligations](../../../specification/requirements/fd-support-verification.md).
00006: No executable support-tool behavior, semantic acceptance or benefit is claimed
00007: by this document. The unchanged codec and source-generation designs retain
00008: their existing checked scopes.
00009: 
00010: ## Boundary and method binding
00011: 
00012: The Product is `urn:stdo:product-definition:a-c-implementations`; Graphify is
00013: its existing registered tenant. The increment adds tools to that tenant, not
00014: an Executive, scheduler, independent Product, graph-owned workflow, work ledger
00015: or method. F_P actors select work, frames, material relations, meaning,
00016: assurance claims and already-authorized actions. Named operations acquire,
00017: render, dispatch, retain and record. `F_D[v]` checks evaluate only declared
00018: supported predicates. An executor invoking F_P does not make its answer F_D.
00019: 
00020: [T-008](../../../.ai-workspace/tickets/active/T-008-fd-tenant-implementation.md)
00021: records the owner's instruction, exact design activation and external bootstrap
00022: admission. The installed construction constitution stays STDO v2.5.1-rc.2,
00023: manifest `3d860ff4c1746f06ac25295a9e205cffb8e7725869615ac77cf2304b70ff2782`.
00024: The owner selects Claude RC9 for this bounded work's execution, including its
00025: Executive and software-design profiles. This does not rewrite the installed
00026: constitution or assert a published/accepted V3 install.
00027: 
00028: The [RC9 binding](fd-method-claude-rc9.json) pins source commit
00029: `c2cfa9b908d1722ae3f26c32fa4ece691083bdc3`, custody
00030: `3a2097137c3588ba44b98e3ea801ac7f2be1daf0`, standards tree
00031: `98de394b352179c25dfa63b0b59a9b6bdd43632d` and exact deciding members. The
00032: same profile is the first finite consumer contract supported by the toolset.
00033: The source-owner map from T-007 remains the prior common-candidate derivation,
00034: not a substituted execution basis. Exact model subjects remain a third basis
00035: role. Runtime imports no V3 code, native compiler, sibling Product, study MCP
00036: or generated study model. Method content is supplied through verified source
00037: references; its source repository need not be mutable or colocated.
00038: 
00039: ### Deciding owners and translation scope
00040: 
00041: | Tool relation | Exact RC9 deciding owner |
00042: |---|---|
00043: | Activation carrier and source/identity relations | REFERENCE_FRAME §11 and RF-005/006/012/013/014 |
00044: | Contract admission, intake, context/fit, actor duties, effects and recovery | ACTIVATION §§1–3, 5 and 7; TICKETS §5 |
00045: | Result predicates, original domain outcomes, gaps, conjunction and reuse | FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Conjunction of results, Change impact and evidence reuse |
00046: | Evidence versus semantic law, source-first expectations and independence | EVALUATION §§1–4; ASSURANCE §§3, 10, 13–16 |
00047: | Selected role additions, no Executive mutation and event-driven attention | EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §§6, 8–10, 12, 17 and 19 |
00048: | Work/evidence ownership and recorded decisions | TICKETS §7; PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8 |
00049: | This source-to-module gate | DESIGN_MODULE §5 Decision-complete symbolic design and §7 three-view gate |
00050: 
00051: These routes retain source conditions and exclusions. A profile describes a
00052: finite serialization/check binding; it supplies no new method rule. An unknown
00053: cut, optional-profile selection, vocabulary, predicate primitive, translation
00054: or executor contract refuses specifically. A matching label or hash establishes
00055: neither applicability nor authority. No arbitrary cross-method join is supported.
00056: 
00057: ## Operating model and trust boundary
00058: 
00059: A trusted local Product operator starts the CLI/server with an exact policy
00060: file, its expected SHA-256 and one fixed principal identity. The operator
00061: selects the Product, source roots/repositories, method profile, owner records,
00062: existing work grants, roles, predicate/operator definitions, executors and
00063: protected evidence root. The API caller is untrusted with respect to these
00064: choices. A request cannot create or replace policy, change its principal,
00065: register an executor, grant territory or declare itself owner. Policy bytes
00066: are acquired and checked again before effects. Their digest checks continuity;
00067: it does not authenticate whoever wrote them. Authority rests on the trusted
00068: operator's separately established Product/owner binding.
00069: 
00070: The supported deployment is a cooperative local development account: the
00071: operator and registered executor programs are trusted to honor their declared
00072: operation contracts. Requests, workspace content and F_P output are untrusted
00073: input to the tool. Same-account actors able to rewrite protected policy,
00074: executables or retained evidence behind the server are outside this boundary;
00075: the tool provides no OS credential isolation, signing or adversarial concurrent
00076: filesystem sandbox. It still detects ordinary dirty state, dependency drift,
00077: conflicting tool writes, missing evidence and incorrect request boundaries.
00078: No internal path is trusted merely because it is internal.
00079: 
00080: A registered process is **not OS-confined**. Preflight and dispatch enforce
00081: its exact invocation, input and configuration, check its registered dependency
00082: preimages, and observe declared effect surfaces. They do not prove that an
00083: arbitrary child cannot write elsewhere or create descendants. An executor's
00084: qualified contract must honestly declare its tools, local-effect behavior,
00085: dependency population, termination observations and unobserved host conditions.
00086: Unsupported enforcement requirements refuse; no `sandboxed` guarantee appears.
00087: 
00088: Policy/source roots and the protected evidence root cannot be in any permitted
00089: Writer territory. All API-relative paths reject absolute paths, `..`, empty or
00090: ambiguous components and symlink components, including a symlink leaf; regular
00091: file opens use non-following checks. Immutable Git acquisition resolves an
00092: exact full object/revision and member, checks regular-blob mode and hash, then
00093: reads blob bytes without checkout, hooks, filters or a moving branch. Product
00094: read roots may exceed write territory only where explicitly configured. A
00095: missing or inaccessible root is a gap, never permission to search elsewhere.
00096: 
00097: ## Ontology and invariants
00098: 
00099: The irreducible domain carriers are the selected policy/binding, exact acquired
00100: content/observations, activated context, one execution attempt, original return
00101: and downstream operation evidence. Files, CLI messages and MCP results are
00102: representations of those carriers. No separate mutable task object is needed.
00103: 
00104: | Carrier | Identity, ownership and relationship |
00105: |---|---|
00106: | `OwnerPolicy` | One exact operator-selected id/digest per Runtime, binding one Product definition id/digest and fixed principal. Contains existing grants and approved operation/executor/predicate references. External authority, never public-tool output. |
00107: | `MethodBinding` | One exact registered profile id/digest and method cut plus member hashes. References owners; maps their packet/result contracts to tenant serialization. |
00108: | `SourceRef` | One engine, registered root/repository, exact relative path/object and whole-content SHA-256. One optional selector narrows acquisition, never changes parent identity. |
00109: | `Observation` | One named acquisition scope/time, enumerated path population, existence/mode/byte hashes and relevant configuration/dependency preconditions. Dirty/untracked bytes participate. |
00110: | `ModelRef` | One exact raw input digest, model id/digest, codec/profile and subject basis; source grounding is separately supplied. Model and carrier identities stay distinct. |
00111: | `Context` | One caller-selected method packet plus actual record/source payloads, late-acquisition manifest, projection boundaries, rendered stdin bytes and scoped fit evidence. |
00112: | `Preflight` | One exact activation/context/grant/executor/result-surface tuple, policy and source preimages, finite admission findings and receipt. It does not admit its cited outcome. |
00113: | `Attempt` | One protected identity/reservation, exact invocation/payload/settings, ordered retained observations, stdout/stderr and named result surface. May have predecessor attempt; never an inferred continuation. |
00114: | `ClosedReturn` | One original raw payload and producer/activation/subject/basis/consumer bindings, original predicates/domain values, provenance, residuals and invalidators. Checks do not rewrite it. |
00115: | `OperationEvidence` | One immutable request/response/content manifest and hash-linked observations. Reconstructable downstream evidence, not a work-state authority. |
00116: | `ExistingCarrier` | An externally owned work/evidence source. Projection does not own its state. Only a named, separately granted Writer operation changes it. |
00117: 
00118: Cross-carrier invariants:
00119: 
00120: 1. Full semantic identities and content digests remain separate. No equality of
00121:    labels or payloads creates a join or grants authority.
00122: 2. Acquired payload is distinct from a locator. Derived projections preserve
00123:    parent identity, all required closure records, qualifications and boundaries.
00124: 3. Every dependency-sensitive effect rechecks its exact material preconditions,
00125:    policy, Product definition, method/profile and executor dependencies. It does
00126:    not silently rebase on new bytes. Effects are recorded before returning.
00127: 4. Admission comes from the protected selected mechanism and existing policy
00128:    authority. A request's alleged grant/receipt is not trusted evidence.
00129: 5. Role is startup-bound. Executive/Reviewer cannot call a candidate/work-carrier
00130:    Writer operation or receive mutation authority from a role label. Automatic
00131:    tool evidence stays outside the Product/worktree; it is not such a mutation.
00132: 6. Receipt, evaluation, output, intended effect and observed end are independent
00133:    facts. Lost response, timeout, cancellation and process exit do not alone
00134:    establish external completion or rollback.
00135: 7. Historical returns retain original subject, basis, predicate and verdict.
00136:    Current applicability is a new check/relation. Duplicate evidence is not an
00137:    additional assessment; inconsistent evidence remains visible.
00138: 8. Unsupported/missing premises remain gaps. Negative reachability in incomplete
00139:    coverage proves no non-influence, fit proves no attention, and a necessary
00140:    condition proves no stronger claim.
00141: 9. Evidence retention never creates a disposition, acceptance, release, role
00142:    transition, work-state ledger or next-action grant.
00143: 
00144: ## Public wire grammar
00145: 
00146: All public operations use integer-only JSON, UTF-8, duplicate-key rejection,
00147: finite strings/arrays/objects, no NaN/infinity and a closed versioned request.
00148: Tenant canonical JSON uses the existing sorted-key compact UTF-8 grammar;
00149: array order is significant. It is not asserted to be JCS. `id` is a nonempty
00150: caller request identity; exact retries of an effect reuse its reservation,
00151: while the same id with different effective inputs refuses.
00152: 
00153: ```json
00154: {
00155:   "schema": "a_c.fd-support.request/1",
00156:   "id": "request-001",
00157:   "operation": "tools.describe",
00158:   "arguments": {}
00159: }
00160: ```
00161: 
00162: ```json
00163: {
00164:   "schema": "a_c.fd-support.response/1",
00165:   "id": "request-001",
00166:   "operation": "tools.describe",
00167:   "status": "ok",
00168:   "result": {"artifact": null, "value": {}},
00169:   "refusal": null,
00170:   "operation_outcome": {
00171:     "predicate": "B(tools.describe): the declared exact inventory output is available",
00172:     "value": "returned",
00173:     "cause": "declared output available",
00174:     "core_value": "satisfied",
00175:     "source_parent": {
00176:       "member": "FOUNDATIONS.md",
00177:       "sha256": "fd2d895f90eb39bda0950c1c7ff02057ef5d8ae73fcbc5b3203f7e99081d6e3f",
00178:       "clause": "results"
00179:     },
00180:     "evidence": [],
00181:     "limits": ["output availability only"]
00182:   },
00183:   "evidence": {"id": "operation-evidence-id", "sha256": "64 hex characters"}
00184: }
00185: ```
00186: 
00187: `status` is `ok`, `refused` or `error`, a transport distinction, never
00188: a semantic result algebra. The distinct operation-boundary outcome below has
00189: its own availability predicate and source-bound core mapping. Refusal contains exactly `code`, `reason`, `gaps`
00190: and `source_refs`; `result` may retain partial observations but cannot pretend
00191: that the refused effect occurred. `error` preserves caught external failure and
00192: unknown effects. An `F_D[v]` result appears separately under `result.value.judgment`
00193: with predicate, original domain outcome, core value, subject/basis, evidence
00194: and limits. An unperformed evaluation has no such judgment. Refusals name the
00195: unmet supported contract; they never fabricate a Worker work result.
00196: 
00197: The boundary-to-wire map is closed and shared by CLI/MCP and persist_outcome:
00198: 
00199: | Bound operation outcome | response.status / CLI exit | response.refusal |
00200: |---|---|---|
00201: | returned | ok / 0 | null; this includes a truthful available negative or unknown inner judgment/observation, and a completely available rejected-admission receipt. |
00202: | refused(constraint), refused(basis), refused(authority), refused(capability) | refused / 2 | Required exact code/reason/gaps/source_refs; code must map to that cause in the closed code table. The denied dependent effect has not begun. |
00203: | held(observation), held(effect) | error / 1 | Required exact held-cause code/reason/gaps/source_refs; retain any actual partial output, effect and publication uncertainty. |
00204: | no bound operation (parse/startup/protocol failure) | refused / 2 for a known guard violation; error / 1 for a caught observation/internal/publication failure | Exact applicable diagnostic code; operation_outcome is null, and no named evaluation is fabricated. |
00205: 
00206: A timeout returning its contracted current unknown observation is returned/ok;
00207: an interrupted operation unable to provide its contracted output is held/error.
00208: The difference is output availability under that exact operation contract,
00209: not the inner effect value. A caught error cannot be relabeled returned merely
00210: because it has a diagnostic. Inner method/F_P results are never rewritten to
00211: match status. MCP isError is true exactly for refused/error tool responses;
00212: protocol parse/invalid-request/method/params failures use JSON-RPC errors and
00213: have no named operation outcome. A trusted store failure may leave evidence
00214: null with its exact publication gap as already specified; no false durable ref.
00215: 
00216: `SourceRef` has the exact keys below. `object` is null for workspace files and
00217: retained evidence, and an exact full Git revision/object for Git sources.
00218: `selector` is null, `{"lines":[first,last]}` (inclusive 1-based, UTF-8 text) or
00219: `{"json_pointer":"/path"}`. `sha256` always binds whole parent content.
00220: 
00221: ```json
00222: {
00223:   "engine": "workspace-regular-file",
00224:   "root": "registered-read-root",
00225:   "path": "relative/member.md",
00226:   "object": null,
00227:   "sha256": "64 lowercase hex characters",
00228:   "selector": null
00229: }
00230: ```
00231: 
00232: `ArtifactRef` is exactly `{"id":"protected-artifact-id","sha256":"..."}`.
00233: It resolves only in the Runtime's evidence store and checks the complete retained
00234: artifact envelope bytes below; it is not an arbitrary filesystem path. Raw blobs
00235: may share storage, but their provenance-bearing acquisition/return records do not
00236: share identity merely because their payload bytes match. `ModelRef` is exactly `{"source":SourceRef,
00237: "format":"model|carrier","model_id":"...","model_sha256":"..."}`.
00238: The `format` value is the enum `model` or `carrier`, not the literal string
00239: containing a vertical bar. A Writer target uses the same SourceRef fields;
00240: only there `sha256:null` denotes a required absent preimage for exclusive
00241: creation. Source reads never accept a null digest.
00242: Inputs requiring currentness take retained Observation refs, not a caller's
00243: unverified assertion that HEAD matches. Unknown fields and enum variants refuse.
00244: 
00245: The inventory below is the closed operation family for this increment. All
00246: listed keys are required unless marked optional. Empty lists are explicit;
00247: semantically required nonempty populations are checked. Discovery publishes
00248: these same contracts and limits, including JSON Schemas; CLI/MCP do not have
00249: independent schemas or dispatch implementations.
00250: 
00251: | Operation | `arguments` keys | Result payload |
00252: |---|---|---|
00253: | `tools.describe` | optional `operation`, optional `method_profile` | Inventory or exact contract, effect prerequisites, checked fragment, supported profile, qualification status and unsupported variants. |
00254: | `workspace.observe` | `scope` (registered file/directory scopes), optional `previous` (Observation ref) | Exact enumerated current observation, additions/removals/byte/config changes against previous, acquisition limits and current Git metadata as supplementary data. |
00255: | `source.read` | `source` (SourceRef), `encoding` (`utf8` or `base64`), optional `max_content_bytes` | Actual content, parent/selected hashes and routes, original line coordinates; no locator-only substitution. |
00256: | `records.find` | `model`, `text` | Exact literal matches and model scope, via `ac_graph.find`. |
00257: | `records.read` | `model`, `ids` | Exact payloads and typed references via `ac_graph.inspect`; unknown ids refuse the batch. |
00258: | `graph.project` | `model`, `selections` (ordered `seeds`, optional `budget_records`) | `ac_graph.project_many` views with complete governing closure and untouched boundary/population semantics. |
00259: | `relations.query` | `model`, `declarations` (SourceRef), `query` (`dependencies`, `path`, `impact`, `coverage`), `seeds` | Paths/closure/coverage from explicitly authored typed declarations, supplied applicability separated, incomplete-coverage boundaries. |
00260: | `context.assemble` | `packet`, `models` (ModelRef plus selections), `sources` (SourceRefs), `late_acquisition` (SourceRefs), `envelope` | Protected Context artifact, actual acquisition manifest, exact bytes and selected-capacity measurement/fit judgment (unperformed when no such gate is selected). Does not emit over-capacity content to an actor. |
